transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 2

transcript_json.text: Good evening.
transcript_json.translation: 晚上好。

transcript_json.text: In 1959, on the day that I was born, a headline in Life magazine proclaimed "Target Venus: There May be Life There!
transcript_json.translation: 1959 年，在我出生的那天，《生活》杂志的一个标题宣告：“目标金星：那里可能有生命！

transcript_json.text: " It told of how scientists rode a balloon to an altitude of 80,000 feet to make telescope observations of Venus's atmosphere, and how their discovery of water raised hopes that there could be living things there.
transcript_json.translation: ”文章讲述了科学家如何乘气球升到 8 万英尺高空，用望远镜观测金星大气，以及他们发现水如何燃起了那里可能存在生命的希望。

transcript_json.text: For many of my peers though, Venus quickly lost its romance.
transcript_json.translation: 不过对我的许多同龄人来说，金星很快就失去了它的浪漫色彩。

transcript_json.text: The very first thing that scientists discovered with a mission to another planet was that Venus was not at all the earthly paradise that fiction had portrayed.
transcript_json.translation: 科学家借助飞向另一颗行星的探测器最先发现的一件事就是：金星根本不是小说里描绘的那种人间天堂。

transcript_json.text: It is nearly identical to our own planet in bulk properties such as mass, density and size.
transcript_json.translation: 在质量、密度和体积等总体性质上，它几乎与地球一模一样。

transcript_json.text: But its surface has been cooked and dried by an ocean of carbon dioxide trapped in the burning death grip of a runaway greenhouse effect.
transcript_json.translation: 但它的表面被失控温室效应牢牢困住的二氧化碳海洋烘烤得焦灼干裂。

transcript_json.text: Venus has long been held up as a cautionary tale for everything that could go wrong on a planet like Earth.
transcript_json.translation: 金星长期以来都被当作反面教材，警示像地球这样的行星可能出问题的所有情形。

transcript_json.text: As a possible home for alien life, it has been voted the planet least likely to succeed.
transcript_json.translation: 作为外星生命的潜在家园，它被评为最不可能获得成功的一颗行星。

transcript_json.text: But I have refused to give up on Venus.
transcript_json.translation: 但我一直拒绝放弃金星。

transcript_json.text: And over the years, my stubborn loyalty has been justified.
transcript_json.translation: 而这么多年过去，我的固执守候得到了回报。

transcript_json.text: The rocky views glimpsed by Venera 9 and other Russian landers suggested a tortured, cloud-shrouded, volcanic history,
transcript_json.translation: 金星九号和其他俄罗斯着陆器瞥见的岩石景象，揭示出一段饱经摧残、云雾笼罩的火山历史，

transcript_json.text: that was confirmed in the early 1990s by the American Magellan orbiter, which used radar to peer through the planet's thick clouds
transcript_json.translation: 这一点在二十世纪九十年代初得到了美国麦哲伦号轨道器的证实——它用雷达穿透了金星厚厚的云层，

transcript_json.text: and map out a rich, varied and dynamic surface.
transcript_json.translation: 并绘制出一幅丰富多样、充满活力的表面地图。

transcript_json.text: The surface formed mostly in the last billion years, which makes it fresher and more recently active than any rocky planet other than Earth.
transcript_json.translation: 金星表面主要形成于最近的十亿年内，这使它成为除地球以外最年轻、地质活动最晚近的岩石行星。

transcript_json.text: Russian and American spacecraft also found hints that its ancient climate might have been wetter, cooler and possibly even friendly to life.
transcript_json.translation: 俄美两国的航天器还发现了线索：金星远古的气候可能更湿润、更凉爽，甚至也许适宜生命。

transcript_json.text: Measurements of density and composition imply that Venus originally formed out of basically the same stuff as Earth.
transcript_json.translation: 对密度和成分的测量表明，金星最初基本上是由与地球相同的物质形成的。

transcript_json.text: That presumably included much more water than the tiny trace we find blowing in the thick air today.
transcript_json.translation: 这些物质所含的水，想必比如今在其浓密大气中飘散的微量水汽要多得多。

transcript_json.text: Thus our picture of Venus at around the time life was getting started on Earth
transcript_json.translation: 因此，当地球上的生命刚刚起步时，我们眼中的金星

transcript_json.text: is one of warm oceans, probably rich with organic molecules, splashing around rocky shores and cloud-shrouded volcanic vents.
transcript_json.translation: 是一片温暖的海洋，里面很可能富含有机分子，在岩石海岸和云雾缭绕的火山口周围翻涌。

transcript_json.text: The sun was considerably less bright back then, so Venus was arguably a cosier habitat for life than Earth.
transcript_json.translation: 当时的太阳远不如现在明亮，所以金星很可能是比地球更宜居的生命家园。

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 3
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: I'm a psychology professor at the University of British Columbia.
transcript_json.translation: 我是英属哥伦比亚大学的心理学教授。

transcript_json.text: I specialize in cultural psychology, examining similarities and differences between East Asians and North Americans.
transcript_json.translation: 我的专业方向是文化心理学，研究东亚人和北美人之间的异同。

transcript_json.text: Our research team has been looking at cultural differences in self-enhancing motivation, helping people have positive feelings towards not only themselves but things connected to themselves.
transcript_json.translation: 我们的研究团队一直在研究自我提升动机方面的文化差异，也就是人们对自身以及与自己相关的事物产生的积极情感。

transcript_json.text: For example, when you own something, you view it as more valuable than when you don't own it.
transcript_json.translation: 比如说，你拥有的东西，在你眼里会比不属于你时更有价值。

transcript_json.text: It's called the endowment effect.
transcript_json.translation: 这叫作禀赋效应。

transcript_json.text: The strength of that effect is stronger in Western cultures than in East Asian cultures.
transcript_json.translation: 这种效应在西方文化中比在东亚文化中更强烈。

transcript_json.text: So we've been looking at other ways of seeing whether this motivation to view oneself positively is shaped by cultural experiences.
transcript_json.translation: 所以我们一直在用其他方式研究，这种积极看待自己的动机是否由文化经历塑造。

transcript_json.text: We've also started to look at how culture shapes sleep.
transcript_json.translation: 我们还开始研究文化如何影响睡眠。

transcript_json.text: We are still in the exploratory stages of this project, although what's noteworthy is that East Asians on average sleep about an hour and a half less each night than North Americans do.
transcript_json.translation: 这个项目仍处于探索阶段，不过值得注意的是，东亚人平均每晚的睡眠时间比北美人少大约一个半小时。

transcript_json.text: And it's not a more efficient sleep, not like they're compressing relatively more value out of their hours.
transcript_json.translation: 而且他们的睡眠并非更高效，并不是说他们从同样的小时数里榨取了更多价值。

transcript_json.text: Studies have found that even infants in East Asia sleep about an hour less than European infants.
transcript_json.translation: 研究发现，就连东亚的婴儿也比欧洲的婴儿少睡约一个小时。

transcript_json.text: So we're trying to figure out how culture shapes the way you sleep.
transcript_json.translation: 所以我们想弄清楚文化是如何塑造睡眠方式的。

transcript_json.text: Our experiment does not take place in a sleep lab.
transcript_json.translation: 我们的实验不在睡眠实验室进行。

transcript_json.text: Instead, we lend people motion-detecting watches and they wear them for a week at a time, whenever they are not having a shower or swimming.
transcript_json.translation: 而是把运动监测手表借给参与者，他们每次戴一周，洗澡或游泳时除外。

transcript_json.text: These kinds of watches are used in sleep studies as a way of measuring how long people are sleeping, how efficient their sleep is, and whether they are waking up in the night.
transcript_json.translation: 这类手表在睡眠研究中被用来测量人们的睡眠时长、睡眠效率，以及夜里是否会醒来。

transcript_json.text: Ideally, I'd like to take this into a controlled lab environment.
transcript_json.translation: 理想情况下，我希望把研究搬进受控的实验室环境。

transcript_json.text: We'll see where the research points us.
transcript_json.translation: 我们再看研究会把我们引向何方。

transcript_json.text: We usually start off with the more affordable methods.
transcript_json.translation: 我们通常从成本较低的方法入手。

transcript_json.text: And if everything looks promising, then it'll justify trying to build a sleep lab and study sleep across cultures that way.
transcript_json.translation: 如果各项结果都很有希望，那就值得尝试建立睡眠实验室，用那种方式研究跨文化的睡眠。

transcript_json.text: Why do we study sleep?
transcript_json.translation: 我们为什么要研究睡眠？

transcript_json.text: Sleep is something that has really been an unexplored topic cross-culturally.
transcript_json.translation: 从跨文化的角度看，睡眠其实一直是个未被充分探索的话题。

transcript_json.text: I'm attracted to it because culture isn't something that only shapes the way our minds operate.
transcript_json.translation: 我被它吸引，是因为文化并不仅仅塑造我们思维的运作方式。

transcript_json.text: It shapes the way our bodies operate too. And sleep is at the intersection of those.
transcript_json.translation: 它也塑造我们身体的运作方式，而睡眠正处在这两者的交汇点上。

transcript_json.text: M: Today our guest is Rosie Melinda who works as a features editor for Fashion magazine.
transcript_json.translation: M: 今天的嘉宾是罗茜·梅琳达，她是《时尚》杂志的专题编辑。

transcript_json.text: Hi Rosie, you're a features editor at one of the most widely read women's magazines in the U. K.
transcript_json.translation: 嗨，罗茜，你是英国发行量最大的女性杂志之一的专题编辑。

transcript_json.text: What kind of responsibilities does that job entail?
transcript_json.translation: 这份工作需要承担哪些职责？

transcript_json.text: W: We spend our days looking at ideas from journalists, writing copy for the magazine and website and editing.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我们每天的工作就是审看记者的选题、为杂志和网站撰稿并进行编辑。

transcript_json.text: We do random things like asking people in the street questions and testing sports clothing.
transcript_json.translation: 我们还会做些五花八门的事，比如在街上向路人提问、试穿运动服装。

transcript_json.text: We also do less tangible things like understanding what our readers want.
transcript_json.translation: 我们也会做些不那么具体的工作，比如了解读者想要什么。

transcript_json.text: It's certainly varied and sometimes bizarre.
transcript_json.translation: 这份工作确实花样繁多，有时还很离奇。

transcript_json.text: M: During your working day what kind of work might you typically do?
transcript_json.translation: M: 在你的工作日里，你通常要做哪类工作？

transcript_json.text: W: My day mainly incorporates responding to emails, writing and editing stories and coming up with new feature ideas.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我的一天主要包括回复邮件、写稿改稿，以及想出新的专题点子。

transcript_json.text: M: How does the job of features editor differ from that of fashion editor or other editorial positions?
transcript_json.translation: M: 专题编辑的工作与时尚编辑或其他编辑职位有何不同？

transcript_json.text: W: The feature's team deals with articles such as careers, reports, confidence and confessions.
transcript_json.translation: W: 专题团队负责诸如职业、报道、自信、倾诉之类的文章。

transcript_json.text: Everything except to fashion and beauty.
transcript_json.translation: 除了时尚和美妆之外的都归我们管。

transcript_json.text: M: A lot of people believe that working at a magazine is a glamorous job.
transcript_json.translation: M: 许多人认为在杂志社工作是一份光鲜亮丽的工作。

transcript_json.text: Is this an accurate representation of what you do?
transcript_json.translation: 这能准确反映你的工作吗？

transcript_json.text: W: I'd say it's glamorous to an extent, but not in the way it's portrayed in films.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我想说，在一定程度上确实光鲜，但不是电影里演的那样。

transcript_json.text: We do have our moments such as interviewing celebrities and attending parties which is a huge thrill.
transcript_json.translation: 我们确实有高光时刻，比如采访名人、出席派对，那是非常令人兴奋的。

transcript_json.text: Ultimately though, we're the same as our readers.
transcript_json.translation: 但归根结底，我们和读者没什么两样。

transcript_json.text: But working in a job we're all very lucky to have.
transcript_json.translation: 只是干着一份我们都觉得非常幸运才能拥有的工作。

transcript_json.text: M: Did you have to overcome any difficulties to reach this point in your career?
transcript_json.translation: M: 走到职业生涯的今天，你有没有必须克服的困难？

transcript_json.text: How did you manage to do this?
transcript_json.translation: 你是怎么做到的？

transcript_json.text: W: I had to be really persistent and it was very hard work.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我必须非常执着，而且过程非常辛苦。

transcript_json.text: After three years of working in a petrol station and doing unpaid work I still hadn't managed to get an entry level job.
transcript_json.translation: 在加油站打了三年工、又做了三年无偿工作之后，我仍然没能得到一份入门级的工作。

transcript_json.text: I was lucky that my last desperate attempt led to a job.
transcript_json.translation: 幸运的是，我最后一次孤注一掷的尝试为我换来了一份工作。

transcript_json.text: I told myself that all experiences make you a better journalist in the long run and luckily, I was right.
transcript_json.translation: 我告诉自己，从长远看，所有经历都会让你成为更好的记者，幸运的是，我是对的。

transcript_json.text: Related to the 'use-it-or-lose-it law' is the 'keep-moving principle'.
transcript_json.translation: 与"不用即废定律"相关的是"保持运动原则"。

transcript_json.text: We learned about stagnation from nature.
transcript_json.translation: 我们从大自然中懂得了什么是停滞。

transcript_json.text: A river that stops moving gets smelly.
transcript_json.translation: 停止流动的河水会发臭。

transcript_json.text: The same thing happens to people who stop moving, either mentally or physically.
transcript_json.translation: 停止运动的人——无论脑力上还是体力上——也会发生同样的事。

transcript_json.text: Those who play contact sports know that the player who usually gets hurt the most is the one who is standing still.
transcript_json.translation: 玩过对抗性运动的人都知道，通常受伤最重的，是站着不动的那个球员。

transcript_json.text: Of course, you'll need some time to catch your breath every so often, but the essential massage is keep moving, extending and learning.
transcript_json.translation: 当然，你偶尔也需要时间喘口气，但最重要的信息是：保持运动、不断拓展、不断学习。

transcript_json.text: Ships last a lot longer when they go to sea than when they stay in the harbor.
transcript_json.translation: 船出海远航，比停泊在港口里寿命长得多。

transcript_json.text: The same is true for the airplanes.
transcript_json.translation: 飞机也是同样道理。

transcript_json.text: You don't preserve an airplane by keeping it on the ground, you preserve it by keeping it in service.
transcript_json.translation: 保养飞机不是把它停在地面，而是让它持续服役。

transcript_json.text: We also get to live a long healthy life by staying in service.
transcript_json.translation: 我们也是靠持续"服役"才能活得长久健康。

transcript_json.text: Longevity statistics reveal that the average person doesn't last very long after retirement.
transcript_json.translation: 寿命统计数据显示，普通人退休后活不了太久。

transcript_json.text: The more we'll hear is don't retire.
transcript_json.translation: 我们更多听到的是：别退休。

transcript_json.text: If a fellow says "I'm 94 years old and I worked all my life", we need to realize, that is how he got to be 94, by staying involved.
transcript_json.translation: 如果一位老先生说"我 94 岁了，干了一辈子活"，我们要明白，他正是靠一直参与其中才活到 94 岁的。

transcript_json.text: George Bernard Shaw won a Nobel Prize when he was nearly 70.
transcript_json.translation: 萧伯纳年近 70 岁时获得诺贝尔奖。

transcript_json.text: Benjamin Franklin produced some of his best writings at the age of 84, and Pablo Picasso put brush to canvas right through his eighties.
transcript_json.translation: 本杰明·富兰克林 84 岁时还在写出他最好的作品，巴勃罗·毕加索整个八十多岁仍在挥笔作画。

transcript_json.text: Isn't the issue how old we think we are?
transcript_json.translation: 问题的关键，难道不是我们自认为多老吗？

transcript_json.text: A bonus with the 'keep-moving principle' is that while we keep moving, we don't have a chance to worry.
transcript_json.translation: "保持运动原则"的一个附带好处是：只要我们一直在动，就没工夫去忧虑。

transcript_json.text: Hence we avoid the dreaded paralyses by analysis.
transcript_json.translation: 由此我们避开了可怕的"分析瘫痪"。

transcript_json.text: In 2014, one in sixteen Americans visited the hospital emergency room for home injuries.
transcript_json.translation: 2014 年，每 16 个美国人中就有一个因家中受伤去了医院急诊室。

transcript_json.text: One of the main causes of these accidents?
transcript_json.translation: 这些事故的主要原因之一是什么？

transcript_json.text: A wandering mind!
transcript_json.translation: 心不在焉！

transcript_json.text: By one estimate, people daydream through nearly half of their waking hours.
transcript_json.translation: 据一项估计，人们在醒着的时间里近一半都在走神。

transcript_json.text: Psychologists have recently focused on the tendency to think about something other than the task one is doing.
transcript_json.translation: 心理学家最近关注的是人们想与手头任务无关之事的倾向。

transcript_json.text: For one experiment, researchers developed an app to analyze the relationship between daydreaming and happiness.
transcript_json.translation: 在一项实验中，研究人员开发了一款应用，用来分析走神与幸福感之间的关系。

transcript_json.text: They found that the average person's mind wandered most frequently about 65% of the time during personal activities, such as brushing their teeth and combing their hair.
transcript_json.translation: 他们发现，普通人在刷牙、梳头等私人活动时走神最频繁，约有 65% 的时间。

transcript_json.text: Respondents' minds tended to wander more when they felt upset rather than happy.
transcript_json.translation: 受访者心情低落时比心情愉快时更容易走神。

transcript_json.text: They were more likely to wander toward pleasant topics than unpleasant ones.
transcript_json.translation: 他们的思绪更容易飘向令人愉快的话题，而不是不愉快的。

transcript_json.text: How do daydreams affect daydreamers?
transcript_json.translation: 白日梦对爱做梦的人有什么影响？

transcript_json.text: A wandering mind leaves us vulnerable when driving.
transcript_json.translation: 开车时走神会让我们处于危险之中。

transcript_json.text: In one study, researchers interview 955 people involved in traffic accidents, the majority of them reported having daydream just before the accident.
transcript_json.translation: 在一项研究中，研究人员访谈了 955 名交通事故当事人，其中大多数人报告说事故前刚好在走神。

transcript_json.text: Yet other research suggests that daydreaming has benefits.
transcript_json.translation: 然而其他研究表明，走神也有好处。

transcript_json.text: Researches have found that it gives us a chance to think about our goals and it also seems to increase creativity.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员发现，走神让我们有机会思考自己的目标，似乎还能提高创造力。

transcript_json.text: In one experiment, 145 undergraduates completed four unusual uses tasks, each requiring them to list as many uses as possible for everyday object.
transcript_json.translation: 在一项实验中，145 名本科生完成了四项"非常规用途"任务，每项都要求他们尽可能多地列出一件日常物品的用途。

transcript_json.text: After the first pair of tasks was completed, one group of participants was assigned an undemanding activity intended to cause their minds to wander.
transcript_json.translation: 完成前两项任务后，其中一组参与者被安排做一项轻松的活动，意在让他们的思绪游离。

transcript_json.text: When all the participants proceeded to the second pair of tasks, the daydreamers performed 40% better than the others.
transcript_json.translation: 当所有参与者进入后两项任务时，那些走过神的参与者比其他人表现得好了 40%。

transcript_json.text: Dating from as far back as the 12th century, they are claimed to be the rarest historic buildings in western Europe.
transcript_json.translation: 它们的历史最早可追溯到 12 世纪，据称是西欧最罕见的历史建筑。

transcript_json.text: These buildings offer vital insight into Scandinavia's Viking past.
transcript_json.translation: 这些建筑为了解斯堪的纳维亚的维京历史提供了重要视角。

transcript_json.text: But now, with only 30 wooden churches remaining and their condition deteriorating, experts are working to preserve the structures for future generations.
transcript_json.translation: 但如今，仅存 30 座木教堂，且状况不断恶化，专家们正在努力为子孙后代保护这些建筑。

transcript_json.text: Some of these spectacular churches are no more than small buildings, barely 4 meters wide and 6 meters tall.
transcript_json.translation: 这些壮观的教堂中，有些不过是小小的建筑，宽仅 4 米、高仅 6 米。

transcript_json.text: Others are much larger structures.
transcript_json.translation: 另一些则是大得多的建筑。

transcript_json.text: They soar up to 40 meters into the cold air.
transcript_json.translation: 它们高达 40 米，直插寒冷的空中。

transcript_json.text: Most consist of timber frames that rest on stone blocks.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数由架在石块上的木构架构成。

transcript_json.text: This means that they have no foundations.
transcript_json.translation: 这意味着它们没有地基。

transcript_json.text: Although many of the churches appear from the outside to be complex structures, they normally feature only a single storey but numerous different roof levels.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然许多教堂从外面看结构复杂，但它们通常只有单层，却有着许多高低不同的屋顶层级。

transcript_json.text: Staff from the Norwegian government have carried out conservation work on 10 of the churches over the past two years.
transcript_json.translation: 过去两年，挪威政府的工作人员已对其中 10 座教堂开展了保护修缮工作。

transcript_json.text: Most of these churches date from between the 12th and 14th centuries.
transcript_json.translation: 这些教堂大多建于 12 至 14 世纪之间。

transcript_json.text: Other churches were conserved in previous years.
transcript_json.translation: 其他教堂则在前些年完成过保护修缮。

transcript_json.text: So far, specialists have worked to add preservative materials to the churches' exteriors.
transcript_json.translation: 到目前为止，专家们一直致力于给教堂外墙添加防腐材料。

transcript_json.text: They also replaced rotting roots and halted the sinking of the churches into the ground.
transcript_json.translation: 他们还更换了腐朽的木根，并遏制了教堂向地下沉降的趋势。

transcript_json.text: In two cases, huge machines have been used to lift the buildings up to 30 centimeters into the air.
transcript_json.translation: 有两处还动用了大型机械，把建筑整体抬高了多达 30 厘米。

transcript_json.text: This was accomplished so that the team could examine and repair the churches' original medieval stone blocks.
transcript_json.translation: 这样做是为了让团队能检查并修复教堂最初的中世纪石块。

transcript_json.text: The team plans to return to around a dozen of the buildings to assess progress and consider further action.
transcript_json.translation: 团队计划重返约 12 座建筑，评估进展并考虑进一步行动。

transcript_json.text: The earliest free-standing wooden church was probably built in Norway in around 1080.
transcript_json.translation: 最早的独立式木教堂大概是 1080 年前后在挪威建造的。

transcript_json.text: However, the largest known wooden churches were built from the 1130s onwards.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，已知最大的木教堂是 1130 年代以后建造的。

transcript_json.text: This period was one of inter-elite rivalry, in which nobles sought to increase their influence by funding the construction of churches and other buildings.
transcript_json.translation: 那个时期是精英之间相互角力的时代，贵族们通过出资建造教堂和其他建筑来扩大自己的影响力。

transcript_json.text: The reason for constructing the buildings from wood is probably that ideally proportioned straight and slender timber was available in large quantities in Scandinavia's vast pine forests.
transcript_json.translation: 用木材建造这些建筑的原因，很可能是斯堪的纳维亚广袤的松林里能大量获得比例匀称、笔直修长的木料。

transcript_json.text: As wood was so plentiful, it was cheaper to use than the stone used in the buildings of other European cultures.
transcript_json.translation: 由于木材如此充足，用它比其他欧洲文化在建筑中使用的石头更便宜。

transcript_json.text: The area's ship building tradition, partly established by the Vikings, also meant that sophisticated carpentry was a major aspect of the local culture.
transcript_json.translation: 该地区的造船传统——部分由维京人奠定——也意味着精湛的木工技艺是当地文化的一大支柱。

transcript_json.text: The complex style of the medieval wooden church carvings and the skills used to make them almost certainly to derive from the ancient Viking tradition.
transcript_json.translation: 中世纪木教堂雕刻的复杂风格及其制作技艺，几乎可以肯定源自古老的维京传统。

transcript_json.text: In last week's lecture, we discussed the characteristics of the newly born offspring of several mammals.
transcript_json.translation: 上周的课上，我们讨论了几种哺乳动物新生幼崽的特征。

transcript_json.text: You probably remember that human infants are less developed physically than other mammals of the same age.
transcript_json.translation: 大家也许还记得，人类婴儿的身体发育程度不及同龄的其他哺乳动物。

transcript_json.text: But in today's lecture, we'll look at three very interesting studies that hint at surprising abilities of human babies.
transcript_json.translation: 但在今天的课上，我们将看三项非常有趣的研究，它们揭示了人类婴儿令人惊讶的能力。

transcript_json.text: In the first study, three-year-olds watch two videos shown side by side.
transcript_json.translation: 在第一项研究中，三岁儿童并排观看两段视频。

transcript_json.text: Each featuring a different researcher, one of whom they'd met once two years earlier.
transcript_json.translation: 两段视频分别由不同的研究人员出镜，其中一位他们在两年前见过一次。

transcript_json.text: The children spend longer watching the video showing the researcher they hadn't met.
transcript_json.translation: 孩子们观看没见过那位研究人员的视频时间更长。

transcript_json.text: This is consistent with young children's usual tendency to look longer at things that aren't familiar.
transcript_json.translation: 这与幼儿通常更长时间注视陌生事物的倾向一致。

transcript_json.text: And really this is amazing.
transcript_json.translation: 而这实在令人惊叹。

transcript_json.text: It suggests the children remember the researcher they've met just one time when they were only one-year-olds.
transcript_json.translation: 这说明，孩子们记得那位只在只有一岁时见过一次的研究人员。

transcript_json.text: Of course, as most of us forget memories from our first few years as we grow older, this early long-term memories will likely be lost in subsequent years.
transcript_json.translation: 当然，我们大多数人长大后都会忘掉最初几年的记忆，这种早期长时记忆很可能在之后几年里消失。

transcript_json.text: Our second study is about music. For this study researchers play music to babies through speakers located on either side of a human face. They waited until the babies got bored and inverted their gaze from the face.
transcript_json.translation: 我们的第二项研究关于音乐。在这项研究中，研究人员通过人脸两侧的扬声器给婴儿播放音乐。他们一直等到婴儿感到厌烦、把目光从那张脸上移开。

transcript_json.text: And then they change the mood in the music either from sad to happy or the other way around.
transcript_json.translation: 然后他们改变音乐的情绪，或从悲伤变欢快，或从欢快变悲伤。

transcript_json.text: This mood switch made no difference to the three-month-olds; but for the nine-month-olds, it was enough to renew their interest and they started looking again in the direction of the face.
transcript_json.translation: 这种情绪切换对三个月大的婴儿毫无影响；但对九个月大的婴儿来说，足以重新唤起他们的兴趣，他们又开始朝人脸的方向看去。

transcript_json.text: This suggests that babies of that age can tell the difference between a happy melody and a sad tune.
transcript_json.translation: 这表明这个月龄的婴儿能分辨欢快的旋律与悲伤的曲调。

transcript_json.text: Our final study is from 1980, but it's still relevant today.
transcript_json.translation: 我们的最后一项研究来自 1980 年，但至今仍有现实意义。

transcript_json.text: In fact, it's one of the most famous pieces of research about infant emotion ever published.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，它是迄今发表的关于婴儿情绪最著名的研究之一。

transcript_json.text: The study involved ordinary adults watching video clips of babies nine months or younger.
transcript_json.translation: 该研究让普通成年人观看九个月及以下婴儿的视频片段。

transcript_json.text: In the video clips, the babies made various facial expressions in response to real life events including playful interactions and painful ones.
transcript_json.translation: 在视频片段中，婴儿们对真实生活事件做出各种面部表情，包括玩耍互动和疼痛刺激。

transcript_json.text: The adult observers were able to reliably discern an assortment of emotions on the babies faces.
transcript_json.translation: 成年观察者能够可靠地分辨出婴儿脸上的多种情绪。

transcript_json.text: These emotions included interest, joy, surprise, sadness, anger, disgust, contempt, and fear.
transcript_json.translation: 这些情绪包括兴趣、喜悦、惊讶、悲伤、愤怒、厌恶、轻蔑和恐惧。

transcript_json.text: Next week, we'll be looking at this last study more closely.
transcript_json.translation: 下周，我们将更仔细地研究最后一项研究。

transcript_json.text: In fact, we will be viewing some of the video clips from that study.
transcript_json.translation: 实际上，我们将观看那项研究中的一些视频片段。

transcript_json.text: And together, see how well we do in discerning the babies' emotions.
transcript_json.translation: 一起看看我们分辨婴儿情绪的本事如何。

transcript_json.text: Today I'd like to talk about the dangers of being too collaborative.
transcript_json.translation: 今天我想谈谈过度协作的危险。

transcript_json.text: However, placing too much emphasis on being a good team player can negatively affect your career growth.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，过分强调"团队合作者"身份可能会对你的职业发展产生负面影响。

transcript_json.text: Being a good team player is a central skill in our modern workplace.
transcript_json.translation: 做一名好的团队合作者是现代职场的核心技能。

transcript_json.text: The ability to work well with others and collaborate on projects is a sought-after ability in nearly every position.
transcript_json.translation: 善于与他人合作、协同推进项目的能力，几乎在任何一个职位上都广受欢迎。

transcript_json.text: Don't be overly focused on gaining consensus.
transcript_json.translation: 不要过分专注于达成共识。

transcript_json.text: Don't be too concerned with the opinions of others.
transcript_json.translation: 不要太在意别人的看法。

transcript_json.text: This can hinder your ability to make decisions, speak up and gain recognition for your individual skills and strengths.
transcript_json.translation: 这会妨碍你做决策、大胆发声，以及让你的个人技能和长处获得认可。

transcript_json.text: Some people are too subordinate to others' opinions, too focused on decision consensus, too silent about their own point of view, too agreeable to take things on when they don't have time or energy.
transcript_json.translation: 有些人过于屈从别人的意见，过于在意决策共识，对自己的观点过于沉默，明明没有时间精力却因为太好说话而接下任务。

transcript_json.text: This leads to building a brand of underconfident, submissive, low-impact non-leaders and hampers their growth and career advancement.
transcript_json.translation: 这会让人打上不自信、顺从、影响力低的"非领导者"标签，妨碍其成长和职业晋升。

transcript_json.text: Collaboration certainly makes your individual competencies and contributions more difficult for outsiders to identify.
transcript_json.translation: 协作无疑会让外人更难辨识你个人的能力和贡献。

transcript_json.text: Collaborative projects mean you're sharing the spotlight with others.
transcript_json.translation: 协作项目意味着你要与他人分享聚光灯。

transcript_json.text: Outsiders may then find it difficult to determine your contributions and strengths.
transcript_json.translation: 外人于是可能难以判定你的贡献和长处。

transcript_json.text: This may end up costing you opportunities for promotions or pay raises.
transcript_json.translation: 这可能最终让你失去晋升或加薪的机会。

transcript_json.text: You certainly shouldn't ditch teamwork, but how can you avoid the hazards of being an over-collaborator?
transcript_json.translation: 你当然不该抛弃团队合作，但要如何避免过度协作者的隐患呢？

transcript_json.text: Working in a team can have huge benefits.
transcript_json.translation: 在团队中工作可能有巨大的好处。

transcript_json.text: Your team may have repeated successes and often gain recognition.
transcript_json.translation: 你的团队可能接连取得成功，并常常获得认可。

transcript_json.text: You then have more opportunities to expand your professional network than if you worked alone.
transcript_json.translation: 与单打独斗相比，你就有更多机会拓展职业人脉。

transcript_json.text: However, finding a balance between team efforts and individual projects that give you independent recognition is important for making a name for yourself and providing opportunities for advancement.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，在团队努力和能让你获得独立认可的个人项目之间找到平衡，对于打出个人名声、获得晋升机会很重要。

transcript_json.text: Be selective in who you work with.
transcript_json.translation: 挑选合作对象时要有所取舍。

transcript_json.text: This will maximize the benefits and minimize the downsides of being a team player.
transcript_json.translation: 这能把做团队合作者的好处最大化、坏处最小化。

transcript_json.text: Collaborate with people who have complementary expertise.
transcript_json.translation: 与拥有互补专长的人合作。

transcript_json.text: Select projects where there's potential for mutual benefit.
transcript_json.translation: 选择有互惠潜力的项目。

transcript_json.text: Perhaps you're bringing your unique knowledge and gaining access to someone else's professional network, or maybe you're able to learn a new skill by working with someone.
transcript_json.translation: 也许你带来了自己独特的知识，同时获得接触他人职业人脉的机会；也许你能通过与某人共事学到一项新技能。

transcript_json.text: Seek out your teammates purposefully rather than jumping on every new group project opportunity.
transcript_json.translation: 要有目的地寻找队友，而不是每个新的小组项目机会都一拥而上。

transcript_json.text: When we're too collaborative, we want everyone to agree with a decision before we proceed.
transcript_json.translation: 当我们过度协作时，总希望每个人都对决定表示同意后再推进。

transcript_json.text: This can create unnecessary delays as you hold meetings trying to achieve consensus.
transcript_json.translation: 这会造成不必要的拖延，因为你得不停开会试图达成共识。

transcript_json.text: It's fine to be collaborative when seeking input.
transcript_json.translation: 在征求意见时保持协作没问题。

transcript_json.text: But put a deadline on the input stage and arrive at a decision, even if it's a decision that doesn't have consensus.
transcript_json.translation: 但要让意见征集阶段有截止时间并做出决定，哪怕是一个没有达成共识的决定。

transcript_json.text: M: Excuse me.

transcript_json.text: Where's your rock music section?
transcript_json.translation: 你们的摇滚乐区在哪儿？

transcript_json.text: W: Rock music?
transcript_json.translation: W: 摇滚乐？

transcript_json.text: I'm sorry, we're a Jazz store.
transcript_json.translation: 抱歉，我们是一家爵士乐店。

transcript_json.text: We don't have any rock and roll.
transcript_json.translation: 我们不卖摇滚乐。

transcript_json.text: M: Oh, you only have Jazz music, nothing else.
transcript_json.translation: M: 哦，你们只有爵士乐，没有别的？

transcript_json.text: W: That's right.
transcript_json.translation: W: 对。

transcript_json.text: We're the only record store in London dedicated exclusively to Jazz.
transcript_json.translation: 我们是伦敦唯一一家专营爵士乐的唱片店。

transcript_json.text: Actually, we're more than just a record store.
transcript_json.translation: 其实，我们不只是一家唱片店。

transcript_json.text: We have a cafe and library upstairs and a ticket office down the hall where you can buy tickets to all the major Jazz concerts in the city.
transcript_json.translation: 楼上有咖啡馆和图书馆，走廊那头还有一个售票处，城里所有大型爵士音乐会的票都能在那儿买。

transcript_json.text: Also we have our own studio next door where reproduce albums for up and coming artists.
transcript_json.translation: 隔壁还有我们自己的录音棚，为崭露头角的艺人制作专辑。

transcript_json.text: We are committed to fostering new music talent.
transcript_json.translation: 我们致力于培养新的音乐人才。

transcript_json.text: M: Wow, that's so cool.
transcript_json.translation: M: 哇，太酷了。

transcript_json.text: I guess there's not much of a Jazz scene anymore.
transcript_json.translation: 我猜如今爵士乐的氛围已经大不如前了。

transcript_json.text: Not like they used to be.
transcript_json.translation: 不像从前那样了。

transcript_json.text: But here you're trying to promote this great music genre.
transcript_json.translation: 但你们在这里努力推广这种了不起的音乐类型。

transcript_json.text: W: Yes.
transcript_json.translation: W: 是啊。

transcript_json.text: Indeed, nowadays most people like to listen to pop and rock music.
transcript_json.translation: 确实，如今大多数人喜欢听流行乐和摇滚乐。

transcript_json.text: Hip hop music from America is also getting more and more popular.
transcript_json.translation: 来自美国的嘻哈音乐也越来越流行。

transcript_json.text: So as a result, there are fewer listeners of Jazz, which is a great shame because it's an incredibly rich genre.
transcript_json.translation: 所以听爵士乐的人越来越少，这很可惜，因为它是一种极其丰富的音乐类型。

transcript_json.text: But that's not to say there isn't any good new Jazz music being made out there anymore.
transcript_json.translation: 但这并不是说外面就没有新的优秀爵士乐了。

transcript_json.text: Far from it.
transcript_json.translation: 远非如此。

transcript_json.text: It's just a much smaller market today.
transcript_json.translation: 只是如今市场小得多罢了。

transcript_json.text: M: So how would you define Jazz?
transcript_json.translation: M: 那你怎么定义爵士乐？

transcript_json.text: W: Interestingly enough, there's no agreed upon definition of Jazz.
transcript_json.translation: W: 有意思的是，爵士乐并没有一个公认的定义。

transcript_json.text: Indeed, there are many different styles of Jazz, some have singing, but most don't.
transcript_json.translation: 的确，爵士乐有很多不同的风格，有的带演唱，但大多数没有。

transcript_json.text: Some are electric and some aren't.
transcript_json.translation: 有的用电声乐器，有的不用。

transcript_json.text: Some contain live experimentation, but not always.
transcript_json.translation: 有的包含现场即兴实验，但也不一定。

transcript_json.text: While there's no simple definition for it.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然它没有一个简单的定义。

transcript_json.text: Allow, there are many different styles of Jazz.
transcript_json.translation: 毕竟，爵士乐有很多不同的风格。

transcript_json.text: You simply know it when you hear it.
transcript_json.translation: 你一听到它自然就知道了。

transcript_json.text: Honestly.
transcript_json.translation: 说真的。

transcript_json.text: The only way to know what Jazz is, listen to it yourself.
transcript_json.translation: 想知道爵士乐是什么，唯一的办法就是自己去听。

transcript_json.text: As the great trumpet player.
transcript_json.translation: 正如伟大的小号手

transcript_json.text: Louis Armstrong said, if you've got to ask, you'll never know.
transcript_json.translation: 路易斯·阿姆斯特朗所说：如果你还要问，你就永远不会懂。

transcript_json.text: M: How did it go at the bank this morning?
transcript_json.translation: M: 今天上午去银行办得怎么样？

transcript_json.text: W: Not well.
transcript_json.translation: W: 不顺利。

transcript_json.text: My proposal was rejected.
transcript_json.translation: 我的申请被拒了。

transcript_json.text: M: Really?
transcript_json.translation: M: 真的？

transcript_json.text: But why?
transcript_json.translation: 为什么呀？

transcript_json.text: W: Bunch of reasons.
transcript_json.translation: W: 原因一大堆。

transcript_json.text: For starters, they said my credit history was not good enough.
transcript_json.translation: 首先，他们说我的信用记录不够好。

transcript_json.text: M: Did they say how you could improve that?
transcript_json.translation: M: 他们说没说怎么改善？

transcript_json.text: W: Yes, they said that after five more years of paying my mortgage, then I will become a more viable candidate for a business loan.
transcript_json.translation: W: 说了。他们说再还五年房贷，我申请商业贷款的资质就会更好一些。

transcript_json.text: But right now it's too risky for them to lend me money.
transcript_json.translation: 但现在借钱给我风险太大。

transcript_json.text: They fear I will default on any business loan I'm given.
transcript_json.translation: 他们担心我贷了款会违约。

transcript_json.text: M: That doesn't sound fair.
transcript_json.translation: M: 这听起来不公平啊。

transcript_json.text: Your business idea is amazing.
transcript_json.translation: 你的创业点子很棒。

transcript_json.text: Did you show them your business plan?
transcript_json.translation: 你给他们看商业计划书了吗？

transcript_json.text: What did they say?
transcript_json.translation: 他们怎么说？

transcript_json.text: W: They didn't really articulate any position regarding the actual business plan.
transcript_json.translation: W: 他们其实对商业计划书本身没发表什么意见。

transcript_json.text: They simply looked at my credit history and determined it was not good enough.
transcript_json.translation: 只是看了看我的信用记录，就认定不够好。

transcript_json.text: They said the bank has strict guidelines and requirements as to who they can lend money to.
transcript_json.translation: 他们说银行对放贷对象有严格的准则和要求。

transcript_json.text: And I simply don't meet their financial threshold.
transcript_json.translation: 而我就是达不到他们的财务门槛。

transcript_json.text: M: What if you ask for a smaller amount?
transcript_json.translation: M: 那申请少一点呢？

transcript_json.text: Maybe you could gather capital from other sources, smaller loans from more lenders.
transcript_json.translation: 也许你可以从别的渠道筹钱，多找几家借小额贷款。

transcript_json.text: W: You don't get it.
transcript_json.translation: W: 你没明白。

transcript_json.text: It doesn't matter the size of the loan I ask for, or the type of business I propose.
transcript_json.translation: 我申请多少贷款、做什么生意都无所谓。

transcript_json.text: That's all inconsequential.
transcript_json.translation: 那些都不重要。

transcript_json.text: The first thing every bank will do is study how much money I have and how much debt I have before they decide whether or not to lend me any more money.
transcript_json.translation: 每家银行第一件事都是先查我有多少钱、欠多少债，然后才决定要不要再借钱给我。

transcript_json.text: If I want to continue ahead with this dream of only my own business, I have no other choice.
transcript_json.translation: 如果我想继续追逐自己创业的梦想，就没有别的路可走。

transcript_json.text: But to build up my own finances, I need around 20% more in personal savings and 50% less debt.
transcript_json.translation: 要想改善个人财务，我的个人储蓄还得增加20%左右，债务要减少50%。

transcript_json.text: That's all there is to it.
transcript_json.translation: 就是这么回事。

transcript_json.text: M: I see now.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我明白了。

transcript_json.text: Well, it's a huge pity that they rejected your request, but don't lose hope.
transcript_json.translation: 唉，他们拒绝了你的申请真可惜，但别灰心。

transcript_json.text: I still think that your idea is great and that you would turn it into a phenomenal success.
transcript_json.translation: 我还是觉得你的点子很棒，你一定能把它做成一番了不起的事业。

transcript_json.text: There's a lot about Leo Sanchez and his farm in Salinas, California.
transcript_json.translation: 利奥·桑切斯和他位于加利福尼亚州萨利纳斯的农场，有很多地方

transcript_json.text: That seems unusual.
transcript_json.translation: 听起来很不寻常。

transcript_json.text: The national average farm size is around 440 acres, but his is only one acre.
transcript_json.translation: 全国农场平均面积约为440英亩，而他的只有1英亩。

transcript_json.text: The average age of farmers hovers around 58 years old, but he is just 26.
transcript_json.translation: 农民的平均年龄在58岁上下，而他才26岁。

transcript_json.text: And Sanchez constantly attempts to improve everything from seeding techniques out in the field to the promotion and sale of his produce online.
transcript_json.translation: 桑切斯还在不断改进一切，从田间的播种技术，到在网上宣传和销售自己的农产品。

transcript_json.text: This is evidence of an experimental approach.
transcript_json.translation: 这正体现了一种试验性的做法。

transcript_json.text: It's an approach not dictated by the confines of conventional large scale agriculture lead by international corporations.
transcript_json.translation: 这种做法不受跨国公司主导的传统大规模农业的条条框框束缚。

transcript_json.text: While farming is often difficult for both the body and mind, Sanchez says he and many of his fellow young farmers are motivated by desire to set a new standard for agriculture.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然务农常常让人身心俱疲，但桑切斯说，他和许多年轻农民同行是怀着为农业设立新标准的愿望在做这件事。

transcript_json.text: Many of them are employing a multitude of technologies, some new and some not so new.
transcript_json.translation: 他们中有很多人在用各种各样的技术，有的很新，有的没那么新。

transcript_json.text: Recently, Sanchez bought a hand operated tool which pulls out weeds and loosen soil.
transcript_json.translation: 最近，桑切斯买了一件手动工具，能拔草和松土。

transcript_json.text: It actually dates back to at least 1701.
transcript_json.translation: 这工具其实最早可以追溯到1701年。

transcript_json.text: It stands in sharp contrast to Sanchez's other gadget, a gas powered flame rekiller, invented in 1997.
transcript_json.translation: 这和他另一件1997年发明的燃气火焰除草器形成了鲜明对比。

transcript_json.text: He simply doesn't discriminate when it comes to the newness of tools.
transcript_json.translation: 对工具的新旧，他完全不挑。

transcript_json.text: If it works, it works.
transcript_json.translation: 好用就行。

transcript_json.text: Farmers have a long history of invention and is no different today.
transcript_json.translation: 农民搞发明的历史由来已久，如今也一样。

transcript_json.text: Young farmers are guided by their love for agriculture and aided by their knowledge of technology to find inexpensive and appropriately sized tools.
transcript_json.translation: 年轻农民凭着对农业的热爱，借助自己的技术知识，寻找便宜又大小合适的工具。

transcript_json.text: They collaborate and innovate.
transcript_json.translation: 他们合作创新。

transcript_json.text: Sometimes the old stuff just works better or more efficiently.
transcript_json.translation: 有时候老物件反而更好用、效率更高。

transcript_json.text: Eat Grub is Britain's first new food company that breaks western food boundaries by introducing edible insects as a new source of food.
transcript_json.translation: Eat Grub是英国第一家新型食品公司，它把可食用昆虫作为新的食物来源引入，打破了西方饮食的界限。

transcript_json.text: And Sainz Breeze is the first UK supermarket to stock the company's crunchy roasted crickets.
transcript_json.translation: Sainz Breeze则是英国第一家上架该公司香脆烤蟋蟀的超市。

transcript_json.text: Sainz Breeze insist that such food is no joke and could be a new, sustainable source of protein.
transcript_json.translation: Sainz Breeze坚持认为，这种食品不是开玩笑，它可能是一种新的、可持续的蛋白质来源。

transcript_json.text: Out of curiosity, I paid a visit to Sainz Breeze as I put my hand into a packet of crickets with their tiny eyes and legs.
transcript_json.translation: 出于好奇，我去了一趟Sainz Breeze。当我把手伸进一袋蟋蟀，看着它们小小的眼睛和腿，

transcript_json.text: The idea of one going in my mouth made me feel a little sick.
transcript_json.translation: 一想到要把一只放进嘴里，我就有点恶心。

transcript_json.text: But the first bite was a pleasant surprise, a little dry and lacking of taste, but at least a wing didn't get stuck in my throat.
transcript_json.translation: 但咬下第一口是个惊喜：有点干、没什么味道，但至少翅膀没卡在喉咙里。

transcript_json.text: The roasted seasoning largely overpowered any other flavour, although there was slightly bitter after taste.
transcript_json.translation: 烤制的调味料基本盖过了其他所有味道，不过余味有点苦。

transcript_json.text: The texture is crunchy, but smelt a little of cat food.
transcript_json.translation: 口感很脆，但闻起来有点像猫粮。

transcript_json.text: Eat Grub also recommends the crickets as a topping for noodles, soups and salads.
transcript_json.translation: Eat Grub还推荐把蟋蟀撒在面条、汤和沙拉上当配料。

transcript_json.text: The company boasts that its dried crickets contain more protein than beef, chicken, and pork, as well as minerals like iron and calcium.
transcript_json.translation: 该公司夸口说，他们的蟋蟀干比牛肉、鸡肉和猪肉含更多蛋白质，还有铁、钙等矿物质。

transcript_json.text: Unlike the production of meat, bugs do not use up large amounts of land, water or feed.
transcript_json.translation: 和生产肉类不同，养虫子不会消耗大量土地、水或饲料。

transcript_json.text: And insect farming also produces far fewer greenhouse gases.
transcript_json.translation: 而且昆虫养殖产生的温室气体也少得多。

transcript_json.text: However, despite 2 billion people worldwide already supplementing their diet with insects, consumer disgust remains a large barrier in many western countries.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，尽管全球已有20亿人在饮食中搭配昆虫，在许多西方国家，消费者的反感仍是一大障碍。

transcript_json.text: I'm not sure bugs will become a popular snack anytime soon, but they're definitely food for fort.
transcript_json.translation: 我不敢说虫子会很快成为流行零食，但它们确实引人深思。

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 1
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 1

transcript_json.text: Have you ever had someone try to explain something to you a dozen times with no luck?
transcript_json.translation: 你有没有遇到过别人给你解释一件事解释了十几遍你还是不懂？

transcript_json.text: But then when you see a picture, the idea finally clicks.
transcript_json.translation: 可一看到图，你一下子就明白了。

transcript_json.text: If that sounds familiar, maybe you might consider yourself a visual learner.
transcript_json.translation: 如果这听着很熟悉，也许你可以把自己当成视觉型学习者。

transcript_json.text: Or if reading or listening does a trick, maybe you feel like you're a verbal learner.
transcript_json.translation: 或者读一读、听一听就管用，也许你觉得自己是语言型学习者。

transcript_json.text: We call these labels learning styles.
transcript_json.translation: 我们把这类标签叫作学习风格。

transcript_json.text: But is there really a way to categorize different types of students?
transcript_json.translation: 但真的有办法把学生分成不同类型吗？

transcript_json.text: Well, it actually seems that multiple presentation formats, especially if one of them is visual, help most people learn.
transcript_json.translation: 嗯，实际上，多种呈现方式——尤其是其中包含视觉方式——似乎有助于大多数人的学习。

transcript_json.text: When psychologists and educators test for learning styles, they're trying to figure out whether these are inherent traits that affect how well students learn instead of just a preference.
transcript_json.translation: 心理学家和教育工作者测试学习风格时，想弄清的是这些风格究竟是影响学习效果的先天特质，还是仅仅是一种偏好。

transcript_json.text: Usually they start by giving a survey to figure out what style a student favors, like visual or verbal learning.
transcript_json.translation: 通常他们先做问卷调查，弄清学生偏好哪种风格，比如视觉学习还是语言学习。

transcript_json.text: Then they try to teach the students something with a specific presentation style, like using visual aids, and do a follow up test to see how much they learned.
transcript_json.translation: 然后用特定的呈现方式教学生一些内容，比如使用视觉辅助，再做个后续测试，看他们学到了多少。

transcript_json.text: That way, the researchers can see if the self identified verbal learners really learned better when the information was just spoken aloud, for example.
transcript_json.translation: 这样，研究人员就能看出，比如自认的语言型学习者，在信息只用口头讲出来时是否真的学得更好。

transcript_json.text: But according to a 2008 review, only one study that followed this design found that students actually learned best with their preferred style.
transcript_json.translation: 但根据2008年的一篇综述，只有一项采用这种设计的研究发现学生确实用自己偏好的风格学得最好。

transcript_json.text: But the study had some big flaws.
transcript_json.translation: 但那项研究有重大缺陷。

transcript_json.text: The researchers excluded 2/3 of the original participants, because they didn't seem to have any clear learning style from the survey at the beginning.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员剔除了三分之二的原始被试，因为从最初的调查看，他们似乎没有任何明确的学习风格。

transcript_json.text: And they didn't even report the actual test scores in the final paper.
transcript_json.translation: 而且他们在最终论文里甚至没有报告实际测试分数。

transcript_json.text: So it doesn't really seem like learning styles are an inherited trait that we all have.
transcript_json.translation: 所以，学习风格似乎并不是我们人人都有的先天特质。

transcript_json.text: But that doesn't mean that all students will do amazingly, if they just spend all their time reading from a textbook.
transcript_json.translation: 但这并不意味着所有学生只要把时间全花在啃课本上就能表现惊人。

transcript_json.text: Instead, most people seem to learn better if they're taught in several ways, especially if one is visual.
transcript_json.translation: 相反，如果用多种方式教学，大多数人似乎学得更好，尤其是其中包含视觉方式。

transcript_json.text: In one study, researchers tested whether students remembered lists of words better if they heard them, saw them or both.
transcript_json.translation: 在一项研究中，研究人员测试了学生是听到、看到还是既听又看单词列表时记得更牢。

transcript_json.text: And everyone seemed to do better if they got to see the words in print.
transcript_json.translation: 结果只要能看到印刷出来的单词，所有人似乎都记得更好。

transcript_json.text: Even the self identified auditory learners, their preference didn't seem to matter.
transcript_json.translation: 就连自认的听觉型学习者也是如此，他们的偏好似乎不起作用。

transcript_json.text: Similar studies tested whether students learned basic physics and chemistry concepts better by reading plain text or viewing pictures to and everyone do better with the help of pictures.
transcript_json.translation: 类似的研究还测试了学生通过阅读纯文本还是看图片能更好地学习基础物理和化学概念，结果有了图片大家都学得更好。

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 2
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 2

transcript_json.text: Free market capitalism hasn't freed us.
transcript_json.translation: 自由市场资本主义并没有解放我们。

transcript_json.text: It has trapped us.
transcript_json.translation: 反而困住了我们。

transcript_json.text: It's imperative for us to embrace a workplace revolution.
transcript_json.translation: 我们迫切需要迎来一场职场革命。

transcript_json.text: We're unlikely to spend our last moments regretting that we didn't spend enough of our lives slaving away at work.
transcript_json.translation: 到了生命最后一刻，我们不太可能后悔这辈子没在工作上多卖命。

transcript_json.text: We may instead find ourselves feeling guilty about the time we didn't spend watching our children grow all with our loved ones, or travelling or on the cultural or leisure suits that bring us happiness.
transcript_json.translation: 相反，我们可能会因为没有花时间陪孩子长大、陪在爱人身边，或是去旅行、去享受带来快乐的文化休闲活动而心怀愧疚。

transcript_json.text: Unfortunately, the average full time employee in the world works 42 hours a week.
transcript_json.translation: 不幸的是，全世界全职员工平均每周工作42小时。

transcript_json.text: Over a 3rd of the time we're awake.
transcript_json.translation: 占我们清醒时间的三分之一还多。

transcript_json.text: Some of our all too precious time is being stolen.
transcript_json.translation: 我们极其宝贵的时间正在被偷走。

transcript_json.text: Office workers do around 2 billion hours of unpaid overtime each year.
transcript_json.translation: 上班族每年大约要加20亿小时的无偿班。

transcript_json.text: So it's extremely welcome that some government coalitions have started looking into potentially cutting the working week to four days.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，一些政府联盟已开始研究能否把每周工作日缩到四天，这让人非常欣慰。

transcript_json.text: The champions of free market capitalism promised their way of life would bring us freedom, but it wasn't freedom at all.
transcript_json.translation: 自由市场资本主义的鼓吹者曾承诺，他们的生活方式会带给我们自由，但这根本不是自由。

transcript_json.text: From the lack of secure, affordable housing to growing job insecurity and rising personal debt, the individual is trapped.
transcript_json.translation: 从缺乏安全、负担得起的住房，到工作越来越不稳定、个人债务不断攀升，个人被困住了。

transcript_json.text: Nine decades ago, leading economists predicted that technological advances and rising productivity would mean that would be working a 15-hour week by now.
transcript_json.translation: 九十年前，主流经济学家曾预测，技术进步和生产率提升意味着我们如今每周只需工作15小时。

transcript_json.text: That target has been somewhat missed.
transcript_json.translation: 这个目标多少是落空了。

transcript_json.text: Here is the most malignant threat to our personal freedom, particularly as the balance of power in the workplace has been shifted so dramatically from worker to boss: a huge portion of our lives involves the surrender of our freedom and personal autonomy.
transcript_json.translation: 这就是对我们个人自由最恶性的威胁——尤其当职场的权力平衡已急剧从劳动者滑向老板：我们生命中的很大一部分时间，都在交出自己的自由和个人自主权。

transcript_json.text: It's time in which we are directed by the needs and desires of others, and denied the right to make our own choices.
transcript_json.translation: 在这段时间里，我们被他人的需求和欲望所支配，被剥夺了自行选择的权利。

transcript_json.text: That's bad for us.
transcript_json.translation: 这对我们很不利。

transcript_json.text: Its hardly surprising that over half a million workers suffer from work-related mental health conditions each year.
transcript_json.translation: 每年有超过50万劳动者患上与工作相关的心理疾病，这一点也不奇怪。

transcript_json.text: All that 15.4 million working days were lost to work-related stress last year-a jump of nearly a quarter.
transcript_json.translation: 而且去年因工作压力损失了1540万个工作日——激增近四分之一。

transcript_json.text: Yes, there are those who, far from being overworked, actually seek more hours, but a shorter working week would enable us to redistribute hours from the overworked to the underworked.
transcript_json.translation: 没错，有些人远远谈不上过劳，反而还想要更多工时，但缩短工作周能让我们把工时从过劳者重新分配给干活不足的人。

transcript_json.text: We need to look at ways of cutting the working week without slashing living standards.
transcript_json.translation: 我们需要想办法缩短工作周，同时又不大幅拉低生活水平。

transcript_json.text: After all, the world's workers have already suffered the worst deduction in wages since the early 18 hundreds.
transcript_json.translation: 毕竟，全世界的劳动者已经经历了19世纪初以来最严重的工资削减。

transcript_json.text: And cutting the working week would be conducive to the individual, giving millions of workers more time to spend as they see fit.
transcript_json.translation: 而且缩短工作周对个人有益，能让数百万劳动者有更多时间按自己的意愿支配。

transcript_json.translation: 问题19到21基于你刚听到的录音。

transcript_json.translation: Q19. 按说话人的说法，人们常为什么感到内疚？

transcript_json.translation: Q20. 九十年前主流经济学家预测了什么？

transcript_json.text: Q21. What is the result of denying workers' right to make their own choices?
transcript_json.translation: Q21. 剥夺劳动者自行选择的权利会导致什么结果？

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 3
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: Today I'm going to talk about Germany's dream airport in Berlin.
transcript_json.translation: 今天我要讲的是德国位于柏林的梦想机场。

transcript_json.text: The airport looks exactly like every other major modern airport in Europe, except for one big problem.
transcript_json.translation: 这座机场看起来和其他欧洲大型现代机场一模一样，只是有一个大问题。

transcript_json.text: More than seven years after it was originally supposed to open, it still stands empty.
transcript_json.translation: 距原定启用时间已过去七年多，它依然空置着。

transcript_json.text: Germany is known for its efficiency and refined engineering, but when it comes to its new ghost airport, this reputation could not be further from the truth.
transcript_json.translation: 德国以高效和精良的工程著称，但说到这座新的幽灵机场，这个名声就完全不成立了。

transcript_json.text: Plagued by long delays, perpetual mismanagement, and ever soaring costs, the airport has become something of a joke among Germans and a source of frustration for local politicians, business leaders and residents alike.
transcript_json.translation: 由于长期拖延、管理混乱、成本不断飙升，这座机场已经成了德国人眼中的一个笑柄，也让当地政客、商界领袖和居民同样头疼不已。

transcript_json.text: Planning for the new airport began in 1989.
transcript_json.translation: 新机场的规划始于1989年。

transcript_json.text: At the time, it became clear that the newly reunified Berlin would need a modern airport with far greater capacity than its existing airports.
transcript_json.translation: 当时人们已清楚地看到，重新统一的柏林需要一个运力远超现有机场的现代化机场。

transcript_json.text: The city broke ground on the new airport in 2006.
transcript_json.translation: 柏林市于2006年为新机场动工。

transcript_json.text: The first major sign of problems came in summer 2010, when the construction corporation pushed the opening from October 2011 to June 2012.
transcript_json.translation: 问题的第一个重大信号出现在2010年夏天，建筑公司把启用时间从2011年10月推迟到2012年6月。

transcript_json.text: In 2012, the city planned an opening ceremony.
transcript_json.translation: 2012年，市里计划举行启用典礼。

transcript_json.text: But less than a month before hand, inspectors found significant problems with the fire safety system and push the opening back again to 2013.
transcript_json.translation: 但就在典礼前不到一个月，检查人员发现消防安全系统存在重大问题，启用时间又一次推迟到2013年。

transcript_json.text: It wasn't just the smoke system, many other major problems subsequently emerged.
transcript_json.translation: 问题不只是排烟系统，随后还暴露出许多其他重大问题。

transcript_json.text: More than 90 meters of cable were incorrectly installed. 4000 doors were wrongly numbered.
transcript_json.translation: 90多米长的电缆安装错误，4000扇门编号有误。

transcript_json.text: Escalators were too short.
transcript_json.translation: 扶梯太短。

transcript_json.text: And there was a shortage of check in desks.
transcript_json.translation: 值机柜台也不够。

transcript_json.text: So why were so many problems discovered?
transcript_json.translation: 那么，为什么会发现这么多问题？

transcript_json.text: Didn't the airport corporation decide to give up on the project and start over?
transcript_json.translation: 机场公司难道没想过放弃项目推倒重来吗？

transcript_json.text: The reason is simple.
transcript_json.translation: 原因很简单。

transcript_json.text: People are often hesitant to terminate a project when they've already invested time or resources into it, even if it might make logical sense to do so.
transcript_json.translation: 人们在一个项目上已经投入了时间或资源之后，往往就难以下决心终止它，哪怕从理性上讲终止才是明智之举。

transcript_json.text: The longer the delays continued, the more problems inspectors found.
transcript_json.translation: 拖延的时间越长，检查人员发现的问题就越多。

transcript_json.text: Leadership of the planning corporation has changed hands nearly as many times as the opening date has been pushed back.
transcript_json.translation: 规划公司的领导层换人的次数，几乎和启用日期推迟的次数一样多。

transcript_json.text: Initially, rather than appointing a general contractor to run the project, the corporation decided to manage it themselves.
transcript_json.translation: 最初，公司没有任命总承包商来管理项目，而是决定自己管理。

transcript_json.text: Despite lack of experience with an undertaking of that scale.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管他们并没有这种规模工程的经验。

transcript_json.text: To compound the delays, the unused airport is resulting in massive costs.
transcript_json.translation: 雪上加霜的是，闲置的机场还在产生巨额开支。

transcript_json.text: Every month it remains unopened costs between nine and 10 million euros.
transcript_json.translation: 每多闲置一个月，就要花掉900万到1000万欧元。

transcript_json.text: Assuming all goes well, the airport should open in October 2020, but the still empty airport stands as the biggest embarrassment to Germany's reputation for efficiency and a continuing drain on city and state resources.
transcript_json.translation: 如果一切顺利，机场应在2020年10月启用，但这座仍然空置的机场，已成为对德国高效名声的最大羞辱，也在持续消耗着城市和州的资源。

transcript_json.translation: 问题22到25基于你刚听到的录音。

transcript_json.translation: Q22. 关于柏林的梦想机场，说话人说了什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q23. 柏林为什么需要一座新机场？

transcript_json.translation: Q24. 柏林为什么一再推迟梦想机场的启用？

transcript_json.translation: Q25. 机场闲置期间发生了什么？

transcript_json.text: CONVERSATION 1
transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 1

transcript_json.text: M: Tonight, we have a very special guest.
transcript_json.translation: M: 今晚，我们有一位非常特别的嘉宾。

transcript_json.text: Mrs. Anna Sanchez is a three-time Olympic champion and author of the new book to the Edge.
transcript_json.translation: 安娜·桑切斯女士是三届奥运冠军，也是新书《至境边缘》的作者。

transcript_json.text: Mrs. Sanchez, thank you for joining us.
transcript_json.translation: 桑切斯女士，感谢您来到我们的节目。

transcript_json.text: W: Thank you for having me.
transcript_json.translation: W: 谢谢你们邀请我。

transcript_json.text: M: Let's start with your book.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我们先从您的书说起吧。

transcript_json.text: What does the title "To the Edge" mean? What are you referring to?
transcript_json.translation: 《走向边缘》这个书名是什么意思？指的是什么？

transcript_json.text: W: The book is about how science and technology has helped push humans to the edge of their physical abilities.
transcript_json.translation: W: 这本书讲的是科学技术如何把人类推向体能的极限边缘。

transcript_json.text: I argue that in the past 20 years, we have had the best athletes the world has ever seen.
transcript_json.translation: 我认为，在过去20年里，我们拥有了有史以来最优秀的运动员。

transcript_json.text: M: But is this a fair comparison?
transcript_json.translation: M: 但这样的比较公平吗？

transcript_json.text: How do you know how, say, a football player from 50 years ago would compare to one today?
transcript_json.translation: 您怎么知道，比如说，50年前的足球运动员和今天的比起来会是什么样？

transcript_json.text: W: Well, you are right.
transcript_json.translation: W: 嗯，你说得对。

transcript_json.text: That comparison would be perhaps impossible to make.
transcript_json.translation: 那样的比较也许根本做不了。

transcript_json.text: But the point is more about our knowledge today of human biochemistry, nutrition, and mechanics.
transcript_json.translation: 但重点更多在于我们今天对人类生物化学、营养学和运动力学的认识。

transcript_json.text: I believe that while our bodies have not changed in thousands of years, what has changed is the scientific knowledge.
transcript_json.translation: 我认为，虽然我们的身体几千年来并没有变化，但变化的是科学知识。

transcript_json.text: This has allowed athletes to push the limits of what was previously thought possible.
transcript_json.translation: 这让运动员得以突破以前被认为不可能的极限。

transcript_json.text: M: That's interesting.
transcript_json.translation: M: 真有意思。

transcript_json.text: Please tell us more about these perceived limits.
transcript_json.translation: 请再多讲讲这些所谓的极限。

transcript_json.text: W: The world is seeing sports records being broken that could only be broken with the aid of technology, whether this be the speed of a tennis serve or the fastest time in a hundred-meter dash or 200-meter swimming race.
transcript_json.translation: W: 世界正在见证一项项体育纪录被打破，而它们只有借助技术才能被打破，无论是网球发球的速度，还是百米短跑或200米游泳的最快时间。

transcript_json.text: M: Is there any concern that technology is giving some athletes an unfair advantage over others?
transcript_json.translation: M: 有没有人担心技术会让一些运动员获得比其他人不公平的优势？

transcript_json.text: W: That is an interesting question.
transcript_json.translation: W: 这是个有意思的问题。

transcript_json.text: And one that has to be considered very carefully.
transcript_json.translation: 也是必须非常慎重考虑的问题。

transcript_json.text: Skis, for example, went from being made of wood to a metal alloy which allows for better control and faster speed.
transcript_json.translation: 比如说，滑雪板已经从木质变成金属合金材质，操控性更好，速度更快。

transcript_json.text: There is no stopping technological progress.
transcript_json.translation: 技术进步是无法阻挡的。

transcript_json.text: But, as I said, each situation should be considered carefully on a case by case basis.
transcript_json.translation: 但正如我所说，每种情况都应当在个案基础上仔细考量。

transcript_json.translation: 问题1至4基于你刚刚听到的对话。

transcript_json.translation: Q1. 关于安娜·桑切斯，我们了解到什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q2. 女士的书主要讲什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q3. 过去几千年里发生了什么变化？

transcript_json.translation: Q4. 男士对在体育比赛中使用技术的担忧是什么？

transcript_json.text: CONVERSATION 2
transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 2

transcript_json.text: W: I've worked in international trade all my life.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我一辈子都在做国际贸易。

transcript_json.text: My father did so too before me.
transcript_json.translation: 我父亲在我之前也是做这一行的。

transcript_json.text: So I guess you could say it runs in the family.
transcript_json.translation: 所以我猜可以说这是家传的。

transcript_json.text: M: What products have you worked with?
transcript_json.translation: M: 您都做过哪些产品？

transcript_json.text: W: All sorts, really.
transcript_json.translation: W: 真的是五花八门。

transcript_json.text: I've imported textiles, machinery, toys, solar panels, all kinds of things over the years.
transcript_json.translation: 这些年我进口过纺织品、机械、玩具、太阳能板，各种东西。

transcript_json.text: Trends and demand come and go.
transcript_json.translation: 潮流和需求来来去去。

transcript_json.text: So one needs to be very flexible to succeed in this industry.
transcript_json.translation: 所以要想在这一行成功，必须非常灵活。

transcript_json.text: M: I see.
transcript_json.translation: M: 明白了。

transcript_json.text: What goods are you trading now?
transcript_json.translation: 您现在在做哪些货？

transcript_json.text: W: I now import furniture from China into Italy and foods from Italy into China.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我现在把家具从中国进口到意大利，把食品从意大利进口到中国。

transcript_json.text: I even use the same container.
transcript_json.translation: 我甚至用同一个集装箱。

transcript_json.text: It's a very efficient way of conducting trade.
transcript_json.translation: 这是一种非常高效的贸易方式。

transcript_json.text: M: The same container?
transcript_json.translation: M: 同一个集装箱？

transcript_json.text: You mean you own a 40-foot cargo container?
transcript_json.translation: 您的意思是您有一个40英尺的货柜？

transcript_json.text: W: Yeah, that's right.
transcript_json.translation: W: 对，没错。

transcript_json.text: I have a warehouse in Genoa, Italy and another in Shanghai.
transcript_json.translation: 我在意大利热那亚有一个仓库，在上海也有一个。

transcript_json.text: I source mid-century modern furniture from different factories in China.
transcript_json.translation: 我从中国不同的工厂采购世纪中期现代风格的家具。

transcript_json.text: It's very good value for money.
transcript_json.translation: 性价比非常高。

transcript_json.text: I collect it all in my warehouse and then dispatch it to my other warehouse in Italy.
transcript_json.translation: 我把它们全部集中到我的仓库，然后发往我在意大利的另一个仓库。

transcript_json.text: Over there I do the same, but with Italian foods instead of furniture, things like pasta, cheese, wine, chocolates.
transcript_json.translation: 在那边我做同样的事，只不过用意大利食品代替家具，比如意面、奶酪、葡萄酒、巧克力。

transcript_json.text: And I send all that to my warehouse in China in the same freight container I use for the furniture.
transcript_json.translation: 然后我用运家具的同一个货柜，把那些食品统统发到我在中国的仓库。

transcript_json.text: M: So I presume you sell both lines of products wholesale in each respective country.
transcript_json.translation: M: 所以我猜这两种产品您分别在各自的国家做批发。

transcript_json.text: W: Of course.
transcript_json.translation: W: 当然。

transcript_json.text: I possess a network of clients and partners in both countries.
transcript_json.translation: 我在两个国家都有客户和合作伙伴网络。

transcript_json.text: That's the main benefit of having done this for so long.
transcript_json.translation: 这是干这一行这么久的主要好处。

transcript_json.text: I've made great business contacts over time.
transcript_json.translation: 日积月累，我结识了很多重要的生意伙伴。

transcript_json.text: M: How many times do you ship?
transcript_json.translation: M: 您一年发货多少次？

transcript_json.text: W: I did 12 shipments last year, 18 this year, and I hope to grow to around 25 next year.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我去年发了12次货，今年18次，希望明年能增长到25次左右。

transcript_json.text: That's both ways, there and back again.
transcript_json.translation: 这是双向的，去程加回程。

transcript_json.text: Demand for authentic Italian food in China is growing rapidly.
transcript_json.translation: 中国对正宗意大利食品的需求正在迅速增长。

transcript_json.text: And similarly, sales of affordable, yet stylish wooden furniture are also increasing in Italy.
transcript_json.translation: 同样，价格实惠又不失格调的木质家具在意大利的销量也在增长。

transcript_json.text: Furniture is marginally more profitable, mostly because it enjoys lower customs duties.
transcript_json.translation: 家具的利润略高一些，主要因为它享受更低的关税。

transcript_json.translation: Q5. 女士认为要在国际贸易中取得成功需要什么？

transcript_json.text: Q6. What does the woman say is special about her way of doing trade?
transcript_json.translation: Q6. 女士说她的贸易方式有什么特别之处？

transcript_json.text: Q7. What does the woman have in both Italy and China?
transcript_json.translation: Q7. 女士在意大利和中国各拥有什么？

transcript_json.text: Q8. What does the woman say makes furniture marginally more profitable?
transcript_json.translation: Q8. 女士说什么让家具的利润略高一些？

transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 1

transcript_json.text: Too many people view their jobs as a five-day prison, which they are paroled every Friday, says Joel Goodman, founder of the Humor Project, a humor consulting group in Saratoga Springs, New York.
transcript_json.translation: 纽约萨拉托加斯普林斯幽默咨询机构"幽默项目"的创始人乔尔·古德曼说，太多人把自己的工作看作一座五天的监狱，每到周五才获假释。

transcript_json.text: Humor unlocks the office prison because it lets adults bring some of their childlike spirit to the job, according to Howard Pollio, professor of psychology at the University of Tennessee Knoxville.
transcript_json.translation: 田纳西大学诺克斯维尔分校心理学教授霍华德·波利奥认为，幽默能打开办公室这座监狱，因为它让成年人把一些孩子般的天性带到工作中。

transcript_json.text: An office with humor breaks is an office with satisfied and productive employees.
transcript_json.translation: 有幽默休息时间的办公室，就是一个员工满意、高产出的办公室。

transcript_json.text: Pollio conducted a study that proved humor can help workers excel at routine production tasks.
transcript_json.translation: 波利奥开展的一项研究证明，幽默能帮助员工在日常生产任务中表现出色。

transcript_json.text: Employees perform better when they have fun.
transcript_json.translation: 员工玩得开心时表现更好。

transcript_json.text: In large corporations with a hierarchy of power, there is often no outlet for stress.
transcript_json.translation: 在等级森严的大公司里，压力往往无处宣泄。

transcript_json.text: Every company needs underground ways of poking fun at the organization, says Lynn Mark, a speaker on workplace humor for Saint Mary's Health Center in St. Louis.
transcript_json.translation: 圣路易斯圣玛丽健康中心的职场幽默讲师琳恩·马克说，每家公司都需要一些地下的方式来调侃组织。

transcript_json.text: Kodak's Rochester, New York branch, discovered a way for its 20,000 employees to uncork their bottled-up resentments.
transcript_json.translation: 柯达位于纽约州罗切斯特的分公司找到了一个办法，让两万名员工把郁积的不满一吐为快。

transcript_json.text: Their 1,000 square foot humor room features a toy store.
transcript_json.translation: 他们那间1000平方英尺的幽默室里设有一个玩具店。

transcript_json.text: Among the room's many stress-reducing gadgets, the main attraction is a boss doll with detachable arms and legs.
transcript_json.translation: 在房间里众多减压小玩意中，最吸引人的是一个四肢可拆卸的老板玩偶。

transcript_json.text: Employees can take the doll apart as long as they put its arms and legs back in place.
transcript_json.translation: 员工可以把玩偶拆开，只要之后把它的胳膊腿装回原位就行。

transcript_json.text: Sandy Cohan, owner of a graphic print production business, created the quote board to document the bizarre phrases people say when under strict deadlines.
transcript_json.translation: 平面印刷制作公司老板桑迪·科恩创建了"名言板"，记录人们在紧迫的截止日期下说出的奇怪话语。

transcript_json.text: "When you're under stress, you say stupid things," says Cohen.
transcript_json.translation: "人在压力之下会说傻话，"科恩说。

transcript_json.text: "Now we just look at each other and say, that's one for the quote board."
transcript_json.translation: "现在我们只是相视一笑，说：这句该上名言板了。"

transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 2

transcript_json.text: Public interest was aroused by the latest discovery of a changed gene in obese mice.
transcript_json.translation: 最新发现的肥胖小鼠体内一种发生变异的基因引起了公众的兴趣。

transcript_json.text: The news was made known by Rockefeller University geneticist Jeffrey Friedman.
transcript_json.translation: 这一消息由洛克菲勒大学的遗传学家杰弗里·弗里德曼公布。

transcript_json.text: The researchers believe this gene influences development of a hormone that tells an organism how fat or full it is.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员认为，这种基因会影响一种激素的生成，这种激素告诉机体自己有多胖、有多饱。

transcript_json.text: Those with the changed gene may not sense when they have eaten enough or if they have sufficient fatty tissue, and thus can't tell when to stop eating.
transcript_json.translation: 携带这种变异基因的人可能感觉不到自己什么时候吃饱了、脂肪组织够不够，因此不知道什么时候该停止进食。

transcript_json.text: The researchers also reported finding a gene nearly identical to the mouse obesity gene in humans.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员还报告说，在人类身上发现了一个与小鼠肥胖基因几乎相同的基因。

transcript_json.text: The operation of this gene in humans has not yet been demonstrated, however.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，这个基因在人体内的作用机制尚未得到证实。

transcript_json.text: Still, professionals like University of Vermont psychologist Eyster Ross Bloom reacted enthusiastically.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管如此，像佛蒙特大学心理学家伊斯特·罗斯·布卢姆这样的专业人士仍然反应热烈。

transcript_json.text: This research indicates that people really are born with a tendency to have a certain weight, just as they are to have a particular skin color or height.
transcript_json.translation: 这项研究表明，人的确天生就有拥有某种体重的倾向，就像天生就有特定的肤色或身高一样。

transcript_json.text: Actually, behavioral geneticists believe that less than half of the total weight variation is programmed in the genes, while height is almost entirely genetically determined.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，行为遗传学家认为，总体体重变异中由基因决定的部分不到一半，而身高则几乎完全由基因决定。

transcript_json.text: Whatever role genes play, Americans are getting fatter.
transcript_json.translation: 不管基因起多大作用，美国人正在越来越胖。

transcript_json.text: A survey by the Center for Disease Control found that obesity has increased greatly over the last 10 years.
transcript_json.translation: 美国疾病控制中心的一项调查发现，过去10年间肥胖率大幅上升。

transcript_json.text: Such rapid change underlines the role of environmental factors like the abundance of rich foods in Americans' overeating.
transcript_json.translation: 如此迅速的变化凸显了环境因素在美国人暴饮暴食中的作用，比如丰盛食物的唾手可得。

transcript_json.text: The Center for Disease Control has also found that teens are far less physically active than they were even a decade ago.
transcript_json.translation: 疾病控制中心还发现，青少年的身体活动量甚至比十年前少得多。

transcript_json.text: Excepting that weight is predetermined can relieve guilt for overweight people.
transcript_json.translation: 接受体重是天生注定的观点，可以减轻超重者的负罪感。

transcript_json.text: But people's belief that they cannot control their weight can itself contribute to obesity.
transcript_json.translation: 但人们相信自己无法控制体重的想法，本身就可能导致肥胖。

transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 1

transcript_json.text: Qualities of a relationship such as openness, compassion and mental stimulation are of concern to most of us regardless of sex.
transcript_json.translation: 诸如坦诚、体谅和精神共鸣这类关系品质，无论男女，都是我们大多数人所关心的。

transcript_json.text: But judging from the questionnaire response, they are more important to women than to men.
transcript_json.translation: 但从问卷回答来看，这些品质对女性比对男性更重要。

transcript_json.text: Asked to consider the ingredients of close friendship, women rated these qualities above all others.
transcript_json.translation: 在被要求考虑亲密友谊的要素时，女性把这些品质排在所有其他要素之上。

transcript_json.text: Men assigned a lower priority to them in favor of similarity in interests, selected by 77% of men, and responsiveness in a crisis, chosen by 61% of male respondents.
transcript_json.translation: 男性对它们的重视程度较低，而更青睐兴趣相投（77%的男性选择）和危机时刻的可靠支援（61%的男性受访者选择）。

transcript_json.text: Mental stimulation ranked 3rd in popularity by men as well as women, the only area of overlap.
transcript_json.translation: 精神共鸣在男性和女性中都排第三，是唯一有交集的方面。

transcript_json.text: Among men, only 28% named openness as an important quality.
transcript_json.translation: 在男性中，只有28%的人把坦诚列为重要品质。

transcript_json.text: Caring was picked by just 23%.
transcript_json.translation: 选择体谅的只有23%。

transcript_json.text: It is evident by their selections that when women speak of close friendships, they are referring to emotional factors.
transcript_json.translation: 从她们的选择可以明显看出，女性谈到亲密友谊时，指的是情感因素。

transcript_json.text: While men emphasized the pleasure they find in a friend's company.
transcript_json.translation: 而男性强调的则是朋友陪伴带来的快乐。

transcript_json.text: That is, when a man speaks of a friend, he is likely to be talking about someone he does things with-a teammate, a fellow hobbyist, a drinking buddy.
transcript_json.translation: 也就是说，当一个男人谈到朋友时，他很可能会说的是一个一起做事的人——队友、同好，或者酒友。

transcript_json.text: These activities are the fabric of the friendship.
transcript_json.translation: 这些活动就是友谊的经纬。

transcript_json.text: It is a "doing" relationship in which similarity in interests is the key bond.
transcript_json.translation: 这是一种"共事"关系，兴趣相投是其中的关键纽带。

transcript_json.text: This factor was a consideration of less than 11% of women.
transcript_json.translation: 把这一因素纳入考量的女性不到11%。

transcript_json.text: Women opt for a warm, emotional atmosphere where communication flows freely.
transcript_json.translation: 女性偏爱温暖、有情感的氛围，交流在其中自由流淌。

transcript_json.text: Activity is mere background.
transcript_json.translation: 活动只是背景。

transcript_json.text: Lastly, men, as we have seen, have serious questions about each other's loyalty.
transcript_json.translation: 最后，正如我们所看到的，男性对彼此的忠诚心存严重的疑虑。

transcript_json.text: Perhaps this is why they placed such strong emphasis on responsiveness in a crisis-someone I can call on for help.
transcript_json.translation: 也许正因如此，他们才如此强调危机时刻的可靠支援——一个我打电话就能求助的人。

transcript_json.text: Women, as their testimonies indicate, are generally more secure with each other and consequently are more likely to treat this issue lightly.
transcript_json.translation: 正如她们的陈述所表明的，女性彼此之间通常更有安全感，因此更倾向于轻看这个问题。

transcript_json.text: In follow-up interviews, this was confirmed numerous times as woman after woman indicated that being there when needed was taken for granted.
transcript_json.translation: 在后续访谈中，这一点得到了多次证实：一个又一个女性表示，需要时对方一定会在，这是想当然的事。

transcript_json.text: As for the hazards of friendship, more than a few relationships have been shattered because of cutthroat competition and feelings of betrayal.
transcript_json.translation: 至于友谊的危险，不少关系都因为残酷竞争和被背叛感而破裂。

transcript_json.text: This applies to both men and women, but unequally.
transcript_json.translation: 这对男女都适用，但程度不对等。

transcript_json.text: In comparison, nearly twice as many men complained about these issues as women.
transcript_json.translation: 相比之下，抱怨这些问题的男性几乎是女性的两倍。

transcript_json.text: Further, while competition and betrayal are the main thorns to female friendship, men are plagued in almost equal amounts by two additional issues: lack of frankness and a fear of appearing unmanly.
transcript_json.translation: 此外，虽然竞争和背叛是女性友谊的主要刺，但男性还受到另外两个问题几乎同等程度的困扰：缺乏坦诚，以及害怕显得不够男子气概。

transcript_json.text: Obviously, for a man, a good friendship is hard to find.
transcript_json.translation: 显然，对一个男人来说，一段好的友谊难能可贵。
