transcript_json.text: RECORDING 2
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 2

transcript_json.text: The partial skeletons of more than 20 dinosaurs and scattered bones of about 300 more have been discovered in Utah and Colorado at what is now the Dinosaur National Monument.
transcript_json.translation: 在犹他州和科罗拉多州、如今的恐龙国家保护区，人们发现了20多具恐龙的部分骨架，以及另外约300具恐龙的散落骨骼。

transcript_json.text: Many of the best specimens may be seen today at museums of natural history in the larger cities of the United States and Canada.
transcript_json.translation: 如今，许多最好的标本可以在美国和加拿大较大城市的自然历史博物馆里看到。

transcript_json.text: This dinosaur pit is the largest and best-preserved deposit of dinosaurs known today.
transcript_json.translation: 这个恐龙坑是当今已知规模最大、保存最完好的恐龙埋藏地。

transcript_json.text: Many people get the idea from the mass of bones in the pit wall that some disaster, such as a volcanic explosion or a sudden flood, killed a whole herd of dinosaurs in this area.
transcript_json.translation: 许多人从坑壁上成堆的骨骼得出一个想法：某种灾难，比如火山爆发或突发洪水，在这个地区杀死了一整群恐龙。

transcript_json.text: This could have happened, but it probably did not.
transcript_json.translation: 这种情况有可能发生过，但多半不是这样。

transcript_json.text: The main reasons for thinking otherwise are the scattered bones and the thickness of the deposit.
transcript_json.translation: 不这么认为的主要理由是骨骼的散落分布和沉积层的厚度。

transcript_json.text: In other deposits where the animals were thought to have died together, the skeletons were usually complete and often all the bones were in their proper places.
transcript_json.translation: 在其他被认为动物是集体死亡的埋藏地，骨架通常是完整的，而且常常所有骨骼都在原位。

transcript_json.text: Rounded pieces of fossil bone have been found here.
transcript_json.translation: 这里发现了圆化的化石骨块。

transcript_json.text: These fragments got their smooth, round shape by rolling along the stream bottom.
transcript_json.translation: 这些碎块是沿河床滚动才获得光滑浑圆的形状的。

transcript_json.text: In a mass killing, the bones would have been left on the stream or lake bottom together at the same level.
transcript_json.translation: 如果是集体死亡，骨骼应该一起留在河底或湖底的同一层位上。

transcript_json.text: But in this deposit, the bones occur throughout a zone of sandstone about 12 feet thick.
transcript_json.translation: 但在这个埋藏地，骨骼分布在整个约12英尺厚的砂岩层中。

transcript_json.text: The mixture of swamp dwellers and dry land types also seems to indicate that the deposit is a mixture from different places.
transcript_json.translation: 沼泽栖息物种和干旱陆地物种混杂在一起，似乎也表明这个埋藏地是来自不同地方的混合物。

transcript_json.text: The pit area is a large dinosaur graveyard-not a place where they died.
transcript_json.translation: 这个坑区是一处大型恐龙墓地——而不是它们死去的地方。

transcript_json.text: Most of the remains probably floated down an eastward flowing river until they were left on a shallow sandbar.
transcript_json.translation: 大部分遗骸很可能是顺流向东的河水漂下，最后搁浅在一片浅沙洲上。

transcript_json.text: Some of them may have come from faraway dry land areas to the west.
transcript_json.translation: 其中一些可能来自西边遥远的干旱陆地区域。

transcript_json.text: Perhaps they drowned trying to cross a small stream, or were washed away during floods.
transcript_json.translation: 也许它们在试图渡过小溪时溺水，或者在洪水中被冲走。

transcript_json.text: Some of the swamp dwellers may have got stuck in the very sandbar that became their grave.
transcript_json.translation: 一些沼泽栖息物种也许就困在了那片后来成为它们坟墓的沙洲上。

transcript_json.text: Others may have floated for miles before being stranded.
transcript_json.translation: 其他的也许漂流了好几英里才搁浅。

transcript_json.text: Even today, similar events take place: When floods come in the spring, sheep, cattle, and deer are often trapped by rising waters and often drown.
transcript_json.translation: 即使今天，类似的事情也在发生：春天洪水来临时，绵羊、牛和鹿常被上涨的洪水困住，常常溺亡。

transcript_json.text: Their dead bodies float downstream until the flood recedes, and leaves them stranded on a bar or shore where they lie, half buried in the sand until they decay.
transcript_json.translation: 它们的尸体顺流漂下，直到洪水退去，把它们搁浅在沙洲或岸边，半埋在沙里，直到腐烂。

transcript_json.text: Early travelers on the Missouri River reported that shores and bars were often lined with the decaying bodies of buffalo that had died during spring floods.
transcript_json.translation: 早期在密苏里河上的旅人报告说，岸边和沙洲上常常排满在春季洪水中死去的野牛的腐尸。

transcript_json.translation: 问题19至21基于你刚刚听到的录音。

transcript_json.text: Q19. Where can many of the best dinosaur specimens be found in North America?
transcript_json.translation: Q19. 在北美哪里可以看到许多最好的恐龙标本？

transcript_json.translation: Q20. 许多人看到坑壁上的大量骨骼时会想到什么？

transcript_json.text: Q21. What does the speaker suggest about the large number of dinosaur bones found in the pit?
transcript_json.translation: Q21. 关于坑中发现的大量恐龙骨骼，说话人提出了什么看法？

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 3
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: I would like particularly to talk about the need to develop a new style of aging in our own society.
transcript_json.translation: 我想特别谈谈在我们的社会里发展一种新的养老方式的必要性。

transcript_json.text: Young people in this country have been accused of not caring for their parents the way they would have in the old country.
transcript_json.translation: 这个国家的年轻人被指责不像在老家时人们那样照顾父母。

transcript_json.text: And this is true.
transcript_json.translation: 这是事实。

transcript_json.text: But it is also true that old people have been influenced by an American ideal of independence and autonomy.
transcript_json.translation: 但同样的事实是，老人也受到了美国式独立自主理想的影响。

transcript_json.text: So we live alone, perhaps on the verge of starvation, in time without friends.
transcript_json.translation: 于是我们独居，或许在饥饿边缘，需要帮助时身边却没有朋友。

transcript_json.text: But we are independent.
transcript_json.translation: 但我们很独立。

transcript_json.text: This standard American style has been forced on every ethnic group.
transcript_json.translation: 这种标准的美国模式被强加给了每一个族群。

transcript_json.text: Although there are many groups for whom the ideal is not practical, it is a poor ideal and pursuing it does a great deal of harm.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然对许多族群来说这个理想并不现实，但它本就是个糟糕的理想，追求它危害极大。

transcript_json.text: This ideal of independence also contains a tremendous amount of unselfishness.
transcript_json.translation: 这种独立的理想还包含着大量的忘我克己。

transcript_json.text: In talking to today's young mothers, I have asked them what kind of grandmothers they think they are going to be.
transcript_json.translation: 在和如今的年轻母亲交谈时，我曾问她们觉得自己将来会是什么样的祖母。

transcript_json.text: I hear devoted loving mothers say that when they are through raising their children, they have no intention of becoming grandmothers.
transcript_json.translation: 我听到慈爱尽职的母亲们说，她们养大孩子之后，并不打算去当祖母。

transcript_json.text: They are astonished to hear that in most of the world, throughout most of its history, families have been three or four generation-families living under the same roof.
transcript_json.translation: 当听说在世界大部分地方、在历史的大部分时间里，家庭都是三四代人同住一个屋檐下时，她们感到惊讶。

transcript_json.text: We have over-emphasized the small family unit-father, mother, small children.
transcript_json.translation: 我们过分强调了小家庭单元——父亲、母亲、小孩。

transcript_json.text: We think it is wonderful if grandma and grandpa, if they're still alive, can live alone.
transcript_json.translation: 我们觉得，如果爷爷奶奶姥姥姥爷还健在，能独自生活就再好不过了。

transcript_json.text: We have reached the point where we think the only thing we can do for our children is to stay out of their way.
transcript_json.translation: 我们已经到了这种地步：认为我们能为孩子做的唯一一件事就是别挡他们的路。

transcript_json.text: The only thing we can do for our daughter-in-law is to see as little of her as possible.
transcript_json.translation: 我们能为儿媳做的唯一一件事就是尽量少见她。

transcript_json.text: Old people's nursing homes, even the best ones, are filled with older people who believe the only thing they can do for their children is to look cheerful when they come to visit.
transcript_json.translation: 养老院，哪怕是最好的养老院，也住满了这样的老人：他们相信，自己能为孩子做的唯一一件事，就是在孩子来看望时显得开开心心。

transcript_json.text: So in the end, older people have to devote all their energies to not being a burden.
transcript_json.translation: 于是到头来，老年人不得不把全部精力都用在"不成为负担"上。

transcript_json.text: We are beginning to see what a tremendous price we've paid for our emphasis on independence and autonomy.
transcript_json.translation: 我们开始看到，为强调独立自主，我们付出了何等巨大的代价。

transcript_json.text: We've isolated old people and we've cut off the children from their grandparents.
transcript_json.translation: 我们把老年人孤立起来，也让孩子们与祖辈断了联系。

transcript_json.text: One of the reasons we have as bad a generation gap today as we do is that grandparents have stepped out.
transcript_json.translation: 如今代沟之所以如此严重，一个原因就是祖辈退出了。

transcript_json.text: Young people are being deprived of the thing they need most: perspective-to know why their parents behave so peculiarly and why their grandparents say the things they do.
transcript_json.translation: 年轻人正被剥夺他们最需要的东西：视角——去了解父母为什么行为如此古怪、祖辈为什么说那些话。

transcript_json.translation: 问题22至25基于你刚刚听到的录音。

transcript_json.translation: Q22. 美国年轻人受到了什么指责？

transcript_json.translation: Q23. 关于美国的老人，说话人说了什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q24. 令受访的年轻母亲们惊讶的是什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q25. 说话人说老年人在尽力做什么？

transcript_json.translation: 对话和问题都只念一遍。

transcript_json.text: CONVERSATION 1
transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 1

transcript_json.text: M: You are a professor of physics at the University of Oxford.
transcript_json.translation: M: 你是牛津大学的物理学教授。

transcript_json.text: You're a senior advisor at the European Organization for Nuclear Research.
transcript_json.translation: 你还是欧洲核子研究组织的高级顾问。

transcript_json.text: You also seem to tour the globe tirelessly giving talks.
transcript_json.translation: 你似乎还不知疲倦地满世界奔波演讲。

transcript_json.text: And in addition, you have your own weekly TV show on science.
transcript_json.translation: 此外，你还主持一档自己的每周科学电视节目。

transcript_json.text: Where do you get the energy?
transcript_json.translation: 你的精力是从哪里来的？

transcript_json.text: W: Oh, well, I just love what I do.
transcript_json.translation: W: 哦，我只是热爱我所做的事情。

transcript_json.text: I am extremely fortunate to have this life doing what I love doing.
transcript_json.translation: 能过这样的生活、做自己热爱的事，我真是太幸运了。

transcript_json.text: M: Professor, what exactly is your goal?
transcript_json.translation: M: 教授，您的目标究竟是什么？

transcript_json.text: Why do you do all of this?
transcript_json.translation: 您为什么要做这一切？

transcript_json.text: W: Well, as you said, I do have different things going on.
transcript_json.translation: W: 嗯，正如你所说，我确实同时在做不同的事情。

transcript_json.text: But these, I think, can be divided into two groups: the education of science and the further understanding of science.
transcript_json.translation: 但我想，这些事情可以分为两类：科学教育和进一步理解科学。

transcript_json.text: M: Don't these two things get in the way of each other?
transcript_json.translation: M: 这两件事不会互相妨碍吗？

transcript_json.text: What I mean is, doesn't giving lectures take time away from the lab?
transcript_json.translation: 我的意思是，讲课不会占用实验室的时间吗？

transcript_json.text: W: Not really, no.
transcript_json.translation: W: 并不会。

transcript_json.text: I love teaching, and I don't mind spending more time doing that now than in the past.
transcript_json.translation: 我热爱教学，现在花在教书上的时间比过去多，我并不介意。

transcript_json.text: Also what I will say is that teaching a subject helps me comprehend it better myself.
transcript_json.translation: 我还要说，讲授一门学科能帮助我自己更好地理解它。

transcript_json.text: I find that it furthers my own knowledge when I have to explain something clearly, when I have to aid others in understanding it, and when I have to answer questions about it.
transcript_json.translation: 我发现，当我必须把一件事讲清楚、必须帮助别人理解它、必须回答关于它的问题时，这会加深我自己的知识。

transcript_json.text: Teaching at a high level can be very stimulating for anyone, no matter how much expertise they may already have in the field they are instructing.
transcript_json.translation: 高水平的教学对任何人来说都可能极具启发性，无论他们在所教的领域已有多少专业造诣。

transcript_json.text: M: Any scientific breakthroughs that you see on the near horizon?
transcript_json.translation: M: 近期有什么科学突破在向您招手吗？

transcript_json.text: A significant discovery or invention we can expect soon?
transcript_json.translation: 我们很快会迎来什么重大发现或发明吗？

transcript_json.text: W: The world is always conducting science and there are constantly new things being discovered.
transcript_json.translation: W: 全世界一直在搞科学研究，新发现源源不断。

transcript_json.text: In fact, right now we have too much data sitting in computers.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，现在有太多数据躺在我们的电脑里。

transcript_json.text: For example, we have thousands of photos of planet Mars taken by telescopes that nobody has ever seen.
transcript_json.translation: 比如，我们手头有数千张望远镜拍摄的火星照片，却从来没有人看过。

transcript_json.text: We have them, yet nobody has had time to look at them with their own eyes, let alone analyze them.
transcript_json.translation: 我们拥有这些照片，但没人腾出时间亲眼看一看，更不用说分析了。

transcript_json.translation: Q1. 女士说她为什么能这么精力充沛？

transcript_json.translation: Q2. 女士一直从事哪些工作？

transcript_json.translation: Q3. 关于教学给她带来的益处，女士说了什么？

transcript_json.text: CONVERSATION 2
transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 2

transcript_json.text: M: Do you think dreams have special meanings?
transcript_json.translation: M: 你觉得梦有特殊的含义吗？

transcript_json.text: W: No, I don't think they do.
transcript_json.translation: W: 不，我觉得没有。

transcript_json.text: M: Don't either.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我也不觉得。

transcript_json.text: But some people do.
transcript_json.translation: 但有些人觉得有。

transcript_json.text: I would say people who believe that dreams have meanings are superstitious, especially nowadays.
transcript_json.translation: 我认为，相信梦有含义的人是迷信的，如今尤其如此。

transcript_json.text: In the past, during the times of ancient Egypt, Greece or China, people used to believe that dreams could foresee the future.
transcript_json.translation: 在过去，在古埃及、古希腊或古代中国的时代，人们曾经相信梦能预见未来。

transcript_json.text: But today, with all the scientific knowledge that we have, I think it's much harder to believe in these sorts of things.
transcript_json.translation: 但今天，有了我们掌握的这些科学知识，我认为要相信这类事情就难得多了。

transcript_json.text: W: My grandmother is superstitious, and she thinks dreams can predict the future.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我的祖母就迷信，她认为梦能预知未来。

transcript_json.text: Once she dreamed that the flight she was due to take the following day crashed, can you guess what she did?
transcript_json.translation: 有一次，她梦见自己第二天要乘坐的航班坠毁了，你能猜到她做了什么吗？

transcript_json.text: She didn't take that flight.
transcript_json.translation: 她没坐那趟航班。

transcript_json.text: She didn't even bother to go to the airport the following day.
transcript_json.translation: 第二天她连机场都没去。

transcript_json.text: Instead she took the same flight but a week later, and everything was fine.
transcript_json.translation: 而是坐了一周后的同一趟航班，结果一切正常。

transcript_json.text: Of course, no plane ever crashed.
transcript_json.translation: 当然，那趟飞机从来没有坠毁。

transcript_json.text: M: How funny!
transcript_json.translation: M: 太逗了！

transcript_json.text: Did you know that flying is actually safer than any other mode of transport?
transcript_json.translation: 你知道吗，坐飞机其实比任何其他交通方式都安全？

transcript_json.text: It's been statistically proven.
transcript_json.translation: 这已经得到统计数据的证实。

transcript_json.text: People can be so irrational sometimes.
transcript_json.translation: 人有时候就是会这么不理性。

transcript_json.text: W: Yes, absolutely.
transcript_json.translation: W: 是啊，绝对是。

transcript_json.text: But even if we think they are ridiculous, emotions can be just as powerful as rational thinking.
transcript_json.translation: 但即使我们觉得情绪很荒唐，它的影响力也可能和理性思考一样强大。

transcript_json.text: M: Exactly.
transcript_json.translation: M: 没错。

transcript_json.text: People do all sorts of crazy things because of their irrational feelings.
transcript_json.translation: 人们会因为不理性的感受做出各种疯狂的事。

transcript_json.text: But in fact, some psychologists believe that our dreams are the result of our emotions and memories from that day.
transcript_json.translation: 但实际上，一些心理学家认为，梦是我们当天情绪和记忆共同作用的结果。

transcript_json.text: I think it was Sigmund Freud who said that children's dreams were usually simple representations of their wishes, things they wished would happen.
transcript_json.translation: 我记得是西格蒙德·弗洛伊德说过，儿童的梦通常只是他们愿望的简单呈现，也就是他们希望发生的事情。

transcript_json.text: But in adults, dreams are much more complicated reflections of their more sophisticated sentiments.
transcript_json.translation: 而在成年人身上，梦则复杂得多，反映的是他们更复杂的情感。

transcript_json.text: W: Isn't it interesting how psychologists try to understand using the scientific method something as bizarre as dreams?
transcript_json.translation: W: 心理学家试图用科学方法去理解梦这么离奇的东西，是不是很有意思？

transcript_json.text: Psychology is like the rational study of irrational feelings.
transcript_json.translation: 心理学就像是对非理性情感的理性研究。

transcript_json.translation: 问题 5 至 8 基于你刚听到的对话。

transcript_json.translation: Q5. 两位说话人都怎么看梦？

transcript_json.translation: Q6. 女士的祖母为什么没有乘坐原定的航班？

transcript_json.text: Q8. What did psychologist Sigmund Freud say about adults' dreams?
transcript_json.translation: Q8. 心理学家西格蒙德·弗洛伊德关于成年人的梦说了什么？

PASSAGE 1
transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 1

transcript_json.text: While some scientists explore the surface of Antarctica, others are learning more about a giant body of water four kilometres beneath the ice pack.
transcript_json.translation: 一些科学家在探索南极洲的表面，另一些科学家则在更多地了解冰盖之下四公里处的一大片水体。

transcript_json.text: Scientists first discovered Lake Vostok in the 1970s by using radio waves that penetrate the ice.
transcript_json.translation: 20 世纪 70 年代，科学家借助能穿透冰层的无线电波首次发现了沃斯托克湖。

transcript_json.text: Since then, they have used sound waves and even satellites to map this massive body of water.
transcript_json.translation: 从那以后，他们一直用声波甚至卫星来测绘这片巨大的水体。

transcript_json.text: How does the water in Lake Vostok remain liquid beneath an ice sheet?
transcript_json.translation: 沃斯托克湖的水在冰盖之下如何保持液态？

transcript_json.text: "The thick glacier above acts like an insulating blanket and keeps the water from freezing," says Martin Siegert, a glaciologist from the University of Wales.
transcript_json.translation: “上方厚厚的冰川像一条隔热毯，使湖水不会冻结，”威尔士大学的冰川学家马丁·西格特说。

transcript_json.text: In addition, geothermal heat from deep within the earth may warm the hidden lake.
transcript_json.translation: 此外，来自地球深处的地热也可能在给这个隐秘的湖泊加温。

transcript_json.text: The scientists suspect that microorganisms may be living in Lake Vostok, closed off from the outside world for more than 2 million years.
transcript_json.translation: 科学家怀疑，在与外界隔绝了两百多万年的沃斯托克湖中，可能生活着微生物。

transcript_json.text: "Anything found there will be totally alien to what's on the surface of the earth," says Siegert.
transcript_json.translation: “在那里发现的任何东西，都将与地球表面的东西完全不同，”西格特说。

transcript_json.text: Scientists are trying to find a way to drill into the ice and draw water samples without causing contamination.
transcript_json.translation: 科学家正在设法钻入冰层并提取水样，同时不造成污染。

transcript_json.text: Again, robots might be the solution.
transcript_json.translation: 这一次，机器人也许又是解决方案。

transcript_json.text: If all goes as planned, a drill-shaped robot will cut through the surface ice.
transcript_json.translation: 如果一切按计划进行，一台钻头形状的机器人将穿透表层冰。

transcript_json.text: When it reaches the lake, it will release another robot that can swim in the lake, take pictures, and look for signs of life.
transcript_json.translation: 到达湖中时，它将释放出另一台机器人，后者可以在湖里游动、拍照并寻找生命的迹象。

transcript_json.text: The scientists hope their discoveries will shed light on life in outer space, which might exist in similar dark and airless conditions.
transcript_json.translation: 科学家希望他们的发现能为了解外太空的生命带来启示——那些生命可能存在于类似的黑暗缺氧环境中。

transcript_json.text: Recently, close-up pictures of Jupiter's moon Europa show signs of water beneath its icy surface.
transcript_json.translation: 最近，木星卫星木卫二的特写照片显示，其冰面之下有水的迹象。

transcript_json.text: Once tested in Antarctica, robots could be sent to Europa to search for life there too.
transcript_json.translation: 一旦在南极洲完成测试，机器人就可以被送往木卫二，在那里也寻找生命。

transcript_json.text: The idea to study the American Indian tribe Tarahumaras came to James Copeland in 1984, when he discovered that very little research had been done on their language.
transcript_json.translation: 研究美洲印第安部落塔拉乌马拉人的念头，是詹姆斯·科普兰在 1984 年冒出来的，当时他发现对这个部落语言的研究少之又少。

transcript_json.text: He contacted a tribe member through a social worker who worked with the tribesmen in Mexico.
transcript_json.translation: 他通过一名与墨西哥部族民众打交道的社会工作者，联系上了一位部落成员。

transcript_json.text: At first, the tribe member named Gonzalez was very reluctant to cooperate.
transcript_json.translation: 起初，这位名叫冈萨雷斯的部落成员非常不愿意合作。

transcript_json.text: He told Copeland that no amount of money could buy his language.
transcript_json.translation: 他告诉科普兰，再多钱也买不到他的语言。

transcript_json.text: But after Copeland explained to him what he intended to do with his research and how it would benefit the Tarahumaras, Gonzalez agreed to help.
transcript_json.translation: 但在科普兰向他解释了自己打算用这项研究做什么、研究将如何使塔拉乌马拉人受益之后，冈萨雷斯同意提供帮助。

transcript_json.text: He took Copeland to his village and served as an intermediary.
transcript_json.translation: 他把科普兰带回自己的村子，并充当中间人。

transcript_json.text: Copeland says, "Thanks to him, the Tarahumaras understood what our mission was and started trusting us."
transcript_json.translation: 科普兰说：“多亏了他，塔拉乌马拉人才明白我们的使命是什么，并开始信任我们。”

transcript_json.text: Entering the world of the Tarahumaras has been a laborious project for Copeland.
transcript_json.translation: 对科普兰来说，走进塔拉乌马拉人的世界是一项费力的工程。

transcript_json.text: To reach their homeland, he must drive 2.5 days from Houston, Texas.
transcript_json.translation: 要到达他们的家园，他必须从得克萨斯州休斯敦开车两天半。

transcript_json.text: He loads up his vehicle with goods that the tribesmen can't easily get and gives the goods to them as a gesture of friendship.
transcript_json.translation: 他往车里装满部落人不容易弄到的物品，把这些东西送给他们，以示友谊。

transcript_json.text: The Tarahumaras, who don't believe in accumulating wealth, take the food and share it among themselves.
transcript_json.translation: 不相信积攒财富的塔拉乌马拉人接过食物，彼此分享。

transcript_json.text: For Copeland, the experience has not only been academically satisfying, but also has enriched his life in several ways.
transcript_json.translation: 对科普兰来说，这段经历不仅在学术上令人满足，还从多个方面丰富了他的人生。

transcript_json.text: "I see people rejecting technology and living a very hard, traditional life, which offers me another notion about the meaning of progress in the western tradition," he says.
transcript_json.translation: “我看到人们拒绝科技、过着非常艰苦的传统生活，这让我对西方传统中“进步”的含义有了另一种认识，”他说。

transcript_json.text: "I experience the simplicity of living in nature that I would otherwise only be able to read about.
transcript_json.translation: “我亲身体验了生活在自然中的那份简朴，否则我只能从书本上读到。

transcript_json.text: I see a lot of beauty in their sense of sharing and concern for each other."
transcript_json.translation: 我在他们彼此分享、互相关怀的情怀中看到了许多美好。”

transcript_json.text: What is a radical?
transcript_json.translation: 什么是激进分子？

transcript_json.text: It seems today that people are terrified of the term, particularly of having the label attached to them.
transcript_json.translation: 如今，人们似乎很怕这个词，尤其怕被贴上这样的标签。

transcript_json.text: Accusing individuals or groups of being radical often serves to silence them into submission, thereby maintaining the existing state of affairs, and more important, preserving the power of a select minority who are mostly wealthy white males in western society.
transcript_json.translation: 指责个人或团体激进，往往能使他们噤声屈服，从而维持现状，更重要的是，保住一小撮人的权力——在西方社会，他们大多是富有的白人男性。

transcript_json.text: Feminism is a perfect example of this phenomenon.
transcript_json.translation: 女权主义就是这种现象的绝佳例证。

transcript_json.text: The women's movement has been plagued by stereotypes, misrepresentations by the media, and accusations of man-hating and radicalism.
transcript_json.translation: 妇女运动一直饱受刻板印象、媒体歪曲报道以及“仇恨男性”“激进主义”等指责的困扰。

transcript_json.text: When the basic foundation of feminism is simply that women deserve equal rights in all facets of life.
transcript_json.translation: 可女权主义的基本出发点，不过是女性在生活的方方面面都应享有平等的权利。

transcript_json.text: When faced with a threat of being labeled radical, women back down from their worthy cause and consequently participate in their own oppression.
transcript_json.translation: 面对被贴上“激进”标签的威胁，女性从自己的正当事业中退缩，结果反而参与了对自身的压迫。

transcript_json.text: It has gotten to the point that many women are afraid to call themselves feminists because of the stigma attached to the word.
transcript_json.translation: 事态已经发展到：由于这个词所附带的污名，许多女性都不敢自称女权主义者。

transcript_json.text: If people refuse to be controlled and intimidated by stigmas, the stigmas lose all their power.
transcript_json.translation: 如果人们拒绝被污名控制和恐吓，这些污名就会失去全部威力。

transcript_json.text: Without fear on which to feed, such stigmas can only die.
transcript_json.translation: 没有恐惧可供它们吞噬，这样的污名只能消亡。

transcript_json.text: To me, a radical is simply someone who rebels against the norm, who advocates a change in the existing state of affairs.
transcript_json.translation: 在我看来，激进分子就是反抗常规、主张改变现状的人。

transcript_json.text: On closer inspection, it becomes clear that the norm is constantly evolving and therefore is not a constant entity.
transcript_json.translation: 仔细审视就会发现，“常规”本身在不断演变，因此并非一成不变的存在。

transcript_json.text: So why is deviation from the present situation such a threat when the state of affairs itself is unstable and subject to relentless transformation?
transcript_json.translation: 既然现状本身就不稳定、处在无休止的转变之中，偏离现状又为什么会构成如此大的威胁呢？

transcript_json.text: It all goes back to maintaining the power of those who have it and preventing the rise of those who don't.
transcript_json.translation: 说到底，还是为了保住当权者的权力，并阻止无权者的崛起。

transcript_json.text: In fact, when we look at the word "radical" in a historical context, nearly every figure we now hold up as a hero was considered a radical in his or her time.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，从历史背景来看“激进”这个词，我们如今奉为英雄的人物，几乎每一位在当时都被视为激进分子。

transcript_json.text: Radicals are people who affect change.
transcript_json.translation: 激进分子是推动变革的人。

transcript_json.text: They are the people about whom history is written.
transcript_json.translation: 历史书写的正是这些人。

transcript_json.text: Abolitionists were radicals.
transcript_json.translation: 废奴主义者曾是激进分子。

transcript_json.text: Civil rights activists were radicals.
transcript_json.translation: 民权运动活动家曾是激进分子。

transcript_json.text: Even the founders of our country in their fight to win independence from England were radicals.
transcript_json.translation: 甚至我们国家的缔造者在为摆脱英国赢得独立而斗争时，也曾是激进分子。

transcript_json.text: Their presence in history has changed the way our society functions, mainly by shifting the balance of power that previously existed.
transcript_json.translation: 他们在历史上的存在改变了我们社会的运转方式，主要是改变了原有的权力平衡。

transcript_json.text: There are some radicals who have made a negative impact on humanity, but undeniably, there would simply be no progress without radicals.
transcript_json.translation: 有些激进分子确实给人类带来了负面影响，但不可否认，没有激进分子，就根本没有进步。

transcript_json.text: That being said, next time someone calls me a radical, I will accept that label with pride.
transcript_json.translation: 话虽如此，下次有人叫我激进分子时，我会自豪地接受这个标签。

transcript_json.text: We are very susceptible to the influence of the people around us.
transcript_json.translation: 我们很容易受身边人的影响。

transcript_json.text: For instance, you may have known somebody who has gone overseas for a year or so and has returned with an accent perhaps.
transcript_json.translation: 比如，你可能认识某人，出国一年左右，回来时也许还带上了口音。

transcript_json.text: We become part of our immediate environment.
transcript_json.translation: 我们会融入自己身边的环境。

transcript_json.text: None of us are immune to the influences of our own world.
transcript_json.translation: 没有人能对我们所处世界的影响免疫。

transcript_json.text: And let us not kid ourselves that we are untouched by the things and the people in our life.
transcript_json.translation: 我们也别自欺欺人，以为自己不受生活中人和事的影响。

transcript_json.text: Fred goes off to his new job at a factory.
transcript_json.translation: 弗雷德去工厂开始他的新工作。

transcript_json.text: Fred takes his 10-minute coffee break, but the other workers take a half an hour.
transcript_json.translation: 弗雷德喝 10 分钟的咖啡休息，可其他工人要休息半个小时。

transcript_json.text: Fred says, "What's the matter with you guys?" Two weeks later, Fred is taking 20-minute breaks.
transcript_json.translation: 弗雷德说：“你们这些人怎么回事？”两周后，弗雷德开始休息 20 分钟。

transcript_json.text: A month later, Fred takes his half hour.
transcript_json.translation: 一个月后，弗雷德也休息起了半个小时。

transcript_json.text: Fred is saying, "If you can't beat them, join them.
transcript_json.translation: 弗雷德心想：“打不过他们，就加入他们。

transcript_json.text: Why should I work any harder than the next guy?"
transcript_json.translation: 我凭什么要比别人干得更卖力？”

transcript_json.text: The fascinating thing about being human is that generally we are unaware that there are changes taking place in our mentality.
transcript_json.translation: 作为人，有趣的一点在于：我们通常意识不到自己的心态正在发生变化。

transcript_json.text: It is like returning to the city smog after some weeks in the fresh air.
transcript_json.translation: 这就像在新鲜空气中待了几周后，重新回到雾霾笼罩的城市。

transcript_json.text: Only then do we realize that we have become accustomed to the nasty smells.
transcript_json.translation: 只有那时我们才意识到，自己已经习惯了那些难闻的气味。

transcript_json.text: Mix with critical people and we learn to criticize.
transcript_json.translation: 与爱挑剔的人相处，我们就学会挑剔。

transcript_json.text: Mix with happy people and we learn about happiness.
transcript_json.translation: 与快乐的人相处，我们就学会快乐。

transcript_json.text: What this means is that we need to decide what we want from life and then choose our company accordingly.
transcript_json.translation: 这意味着，我们需要确定自己想从生活中得到什么，然后据此选择自己的交往对象。

transcript_json.text: You may well say, "That is going to take some effort.
transcript_json.translation: 你完全可以说：“那得费些力气。

transcript_json.text: It may not be comfortable.
transcript_json.translation: 可能不好受。

transcript_json.text: I may offend some of my present company." Right?
transcript_json.translation: 我可能得罪现在的一些朋友。”对吧？

transcript_json.text: But it is your life.
transcript_json.translation: 但这是你的人生。

transcript_json.text: Fred may say, "I'm always broke, frequently depressed.
transcript_json.translation: 弗雷德可能会说：“我总是缺钱，常常郁闷。

transcript_json.text: I'm going nowhere and I never do anything exciting." Then we discover that Fred's best friends are always broke, frequently depressed, going nowhere and wishing that life was more exciting.
transcript_json.translation: 我毫无长进，也从来不做什么刺激的事。”这时我们会发现，弗雷德最好的朋友们也总是缺钱、常常郁闷、毫无长进，还盼着生活更刺激一些。

transcript_json.text: This is not coincidence.
transcript_json.translation: 这绝非巧合。

transcript_json.text: Nor is it our business to stand in judgment of Fred.
transcript_json.translation: 我们也犯不着对弗雷德评头论足。

transcript_json.text: However, if Fred ever wants to improve his quality of life, the first thing he'll need to do is recognize what has been going on all these years.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，如果弗雷德真想改善自己的生活质量，他首先要做的是认清这些年来一直发生着什么。

transcript_json.text: It's no surprise that doctors as a profession suffer a lot of ill health because they spend their lives around sick people.
transcript_json.translation: 医生这个职业健康状况不佳的比例很高，这并不奇怪，因为他们一辈子都在病人身边度过。

transcript_json.text: Psychiatrists have a higher incidence of suicide in their profession for related reasons.
transcript_json.translation: 出于类似的原因，精神科医生这个职业群体的自杀率更高。

transcript_json.text: Traditionally, nine out of ten children whose parents smoke smoke themselves.
transcript_json.translation: 按惯常的说法，父母吸烟的孩子十有八九自己也吸烟。

transcript_json.text: Obesity is in part an environmental problem.
transcript_json.translation: 肥胖在某种程度上也是一个环境问题。

transcript_json.text: Successful people have successful friends.
transcript_json.translation: 成功人士有成功的朋友。

transcript_json.text: And so the story goes on.
transcript_json.translation: 这样的故事还在继续。

transcript_json.text: Virtually every American can recognize a dollar bill at a mere glance.
transcript_json.translation: 几乎每个美国人都能一眼认出一美元纸币。

transcript_json.text: Many can identify it by its sound or texture, but few people indeed can accurately describe the world's most powerful, important currency.
transcript_json.translation: 许多人凭声音或质感就能认出它，但真正能准确描述这种世界上最强有力、最重要货币的人，却寥寥无几。

transcript_json.text: The American dollar bill is colored with black ink on one side and green on the other.
transcript_json.translation: 美元纸币一面用黑色油墨印制，另一面用绿色。

transcript_json.text: The exact composition of the paper and ink is a closely guarded government secret.
transcript_json.translation: 纸张和油墨的确切成分是政府严守的机密。

transcript_json.text: Despite its weighty importance, the dollar bill actually weighs little.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管分量举足轻重，美元纸币实际却很轻。

transcript_json.text: It requires nearly 500 bills to tip the scales at a pound.
transcript_json.translation: 要凑够一磅重，得将近 500 张纸币。

transcript_json.text: Not only is the dollar bill lightweight, but it also has a brief lifespan.
transcript_json.translation: 美元纸币不仅轻，寿命也很短。

transcript_json.text: Few dollar bills survive longer than 18 months.
transcript_json.translation: 很少有美元纸币能撑过 18 个月。

transcript_json.text: The word "dollar" is taken from the German word "taler," the name for the world's most important currency in the 16th century.
transcript_json.translation: “dollar（美元）”一词源自德语“taler（塔勒）”，那是 16 世纪世界上最重要货币的名称。

transcript_json.text: The taler was a silver coin first minted in 1518 under the reign of Charles V, Emperor of Germany.
transcript_json.translation: 塔勒是一种银币，1518 年首次铸造，时值德意志皇帝查理五世在位。

transcript_json.text: The concept of paper money is a relatively recent innovation in the history of American currency.
transcript_json.translation: 纸币的概念在美国货币史上是相对晚近的发明。

transcript_json.text: When the Constitution was signed, people had little regard for paper money because of its steadily decreasing value during the colonial era.
transcript_json.translation: 宪法签署时，人们并不看重纸币，因为殖民时期纸币的价值不断下跌。

transcript_json.text: Because of this lack of faith, the new American government minted only coins for common currency.
transcript_json.translation: 由于这种不信任，新的美国政府只铸造硬币作为流通货币。

transcript_json.text: Interest-bearing bank notes were issued at the same time, but their purpose was limited to providing money for urgent government crises, such as American involvement in the War of 1812.
transcript_json.translation: 带息钞票也同时发行，但它们的用途仅限于为紧急的政府危机提供资金，比如美国卷入 1812 年战争。

transcript_json.text: The first noninterest-bearing paper currency was authorized by Congress in 1862, at the height of the Civil War.
transcript_json.translation: 第一种无息纸币于 1862 年、南北战争最激烈时获得国会批准。

transcript_json.text: At this point, citizens' old fears of devalued paper currency had calmed, and the dollar bill was born.
transcript_json.translation: 到这时，民众对纸币贬值的旧有恐惧已经平息，美元纸币就此诞生。

transcript_json.text: The new green-colored paper money quickly earned the nickname "greenback."
transcript_json.translation: 这种绿色的新纸币很快赢得了“绿钞”的绰号。

transcript_json.text: Today, the American dollar bill is a product of the Federal Reserve and is issued from the 12 Federal Reserve banks around the United States.
transcript_json.translation: 如今，美元纸币是美联储的产品，由美国各地的 12 家联邦储备银行发行。

transcript_json.text: The government keeps a steady supply of approximately 2 billion bills in circulation at all times.
transcript_json.translation: 政府始终维持约 20 亿张纸币的稳定流通量。

transcript_json.text: Controversy continues to surround the true value of the dollar bill.
transcript_json.translation: 围绕美元纸币真正价值的争议仍在继续。

transcript_json.text: American history has seen generations of politicians argue in favor of a gold standard for American currency.
transcript_json.translation: 美国历史上，一代代政治家都主张美国货币应采用金本位。

transcript_json.text: However, for the present, the American dollar bill holds the value that is printed on it and little more.
transcript_json.translation: 然而就目前而言，美元纸币所具有的价值就是它上面印的面额，仅此而已。

transcript_json.text: The only other guarantee on the bill is a Federal Reserve pledge as a confirmation in the form of government securities.
transcript_json.translation: 纸币上唯一的另一重保障，是美联储以政府证券形式作出确认的一项承诺。

transcript_json.text: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

transcript_json.text: To achieve financial security, how much you save is always more important than the amount you earn or how shrewdly you invest.
transcript_json.translation: 要实现财务保障，你存多少钱总是比你挣多少、投资多么精明更重要。

transcript_json.text: If you're under 30 years old, your goal should be to save 20% of your monthly income after tax deductions.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你不到 30 岁，你的目标应该是把扣税后月收入的 20% 存下来。

transcript_json.text: This is irrespective of how much you earn.
transcript_json.translation: 不管你挣多少钱都应如此。

transcript_json.text: Approximately 50% should be reserved for essentials like food and accommodation.
transcript_json.translation: 大约 50% 应留作食物、住房等必需开支。

transcript_json.text: The remaining 30% is for recreation and entertainment.
transcript_json.translation: 剩下的 30% 用于休闲娱乐。

transcript_json.text: But for many young people, it'll be difficult to designate such a large proportion of their income for savings.
transcript_json.translation: 但对许多年轻人来说，把这么大比例的收入划作储蓄会很困难。

transcript_json.text: If you find it hard to save any money at all, start by cutting all unnecessary spending.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你发现连一点钱都存不下来，那就从砍掉一切不必要的花销开始。

transcript_json.text: Allocate a tiny amount of 1 or 2 percent for savings and gradually increase that amount.
transcript_json.translation: 先拿出 1% 或 2% 这么小的比例用于储蓄，再逐步提高。

transcript_json.text: Always keep that 20% goal in mind to prevents yourself from becoming complacent.
transcript_json.translation: 始终把 20% 的目标记在心里，防止自己变得懈怠自满。

transcript_json.text: It can be challenging to stick to such a strict plan.
transcript_json.translation: 坚持如此严格的计划可能很有挑战。

transcript_json.text: But if you adopt the right mindset, you should be apt to make it work for you.
transcript_json.translation: 但只要摆正心态，你应该能让它为你所用。

transcript_json.text: So, what should you be doing with the money that you're saving?
transcript_json.translation: 那么，你存下的钱该怎么打理？

transcript_json.text: Some must be kept easily accessible in case you need some cash in an emergency.
transcript_json.translation: 有一部分必须放在随时可取的地方，以备急用。

transcript_json.text: The largest proportion should be invested in retirement plans, either through your employer or privately.
transcript_json.translation: 最大的一笔应投入退休计划，可通过雇主，也可自行办理。

transcript_json.text: And you can keep some money for high-risk but potentially lucrative investments.
transcript_json.translation: 你还可以留出一部分钱，用于高风险但可能高回报的投资。

transcript_json.text: Dividends can be reinvested or used to purchase something you like.
transcript_json.translation: 分红可以再投资，也可以用来买你喜欢的东西。

transcript_json.text: By following this plan, you should hopefully be able to enjoy your life now, and still be financially secure in the future.
transcript_json.translation: 按照这个计划来，你就有望既享受当下生活，又在未来保有财务保障。

transcript_json.translation: 这一现象导致了巨额的信用卡债务和巨大的环境足迹，而也许并非巧合的是，在同一个半世纪里，我们的幸福感并没有提升。

transcript_json.text: I'm here to suggest an alternative that having less might actually be a preferable decision.
transcript_json.translation: 我在这里想提出另一种选择：拥有更少，也许反而是更好的决定。

transcript_json.text: Many of us have experienced, at some stage, the pleasure of possessing less.
transcript_json.translation: 我们许多人都曾在某个阶段体会过拥有更少的乐趣。

transcript_json.text: I propose that less stuff and less space can not only help you economize, but also simplify your life.
transcript_json.translation: 我认为，更少的物品和更小的空间不仅能帮你省钱，还能简化你的生活。

transcript_json.text: I recently started an innovative project to discover some creative solutions that offered me everything I required.
transcript_json.translation: 我最近启动了一个创新项目，寻找一些有创意的解决方案，让我所需的一切都能得到满足。

transcript_json.text: By purchasing an apartment that was 40 square meters, instead of 60, I immediately saved $200,000.
transcript_json.translation: 买 40 平方米的公寓而不是 60 平方米，我一下子省下了 20 万美元。

transcript_json.text: Smaller space leads to reduced utility bills, and also a smaller carbon footprint.
transcript_json.translation: 更小的空间意味着更低的水电账单，也更小的碳足迹。

transcript_json.text: Because it is designed around an edited collection of possessions, limited to my favorite stuff, I'm really excited to live there.
transcript_json.translation: 因为它围绕精心筛选的物品来设计，只保留我最心爱的东西，能在那里生活让我兴奋不已。

transcript_json.text: How can we live more basically?
transcript_json.translation: 我们怎样才能过得更简约？

transcript_json.text: Firstly, we must ruthlessly cut the unnecessary objects out of our lives.
transcript_json.translation: 首先，我们必须毫不留情地把不必要的物品从生活中清除。

transcript_json.text: To stem consumption, we should think before we buy and ask ourselves, “Will it truly make me happier?” Obviously, we should possess some great stuff.
transcript_json.translation: 要遏制消费，我们应该三思而后买，问问自己：“它真的会让我更快乐吗？”显然，我们应该拥有一些好东西。

transcript_json.text: But we want belongings that we're going to love for years.
transcript_json.translation: 但我们要的是那些多年后仍会喜爱的物品。

transcript_json.text: Secondly, we require space efficiency.
transcript_json.translation: 其次，我们需要空间效率。

transcript_json.text: We want appliances that are designed for use most of the time, not for occasional use.
transcript_json.translation: 我们要的是为日常高频使用而设计的电器，而不是偶尔才用一次的。

transcript_json.text: Why own a six-burner stove when you rarely use even three burners?
transcript_json.translation: 连三个灶眼都很少用，何必要一个六灶眼的炉子？

transcript_json.text: Finally, we need multifunctional spaces and housewares.
transcript_json.translation: 最后，我们需要多功能的空间和家居用品。

transcript_json.text: I combined a moveable wall with transforming furniture to get more out of my limited space.
transcript_json.translation: 我把可移动隔墙与变形家具结合起来，从有限的空间里榨出更多用途。

transcript_json.text: Consider my coffee table.
transcript_json.translation: 拿我的咖啡桌来说。

transcript_json.text: It increases in size to accommodate ten.
transcript_json.translation: 它可以扩大到容纳十人。

transcript_json.text: My office is tucked away, easily hidden.
transcript_json.translation: 我的办公室藏在里面，很容易收起。

transcript_json.text: My bed simply pops out of the wall.
transcript_json.translation: 我的床直接从墙里翻出来。

transcript_json.text: For guests, I can relocate the moveable wall and utilize the foldable guest beds I installed.
transcript_json.translation: 来客人时，我可以挪动隔墙，用上我安装的折叠客床。

transcript_json.text: I'm not saying we should all live in tiny apartments, but consider the benefits of an edited life.
transcript_json.translation: 我不是说我们都该住迷你公寓，而是请想一想"删繁就简的生活"的好处。

transcript_json.text: When you return home and walk through your front door, take a moment to ask yourself, “Could I do with a little life editing?
transcript_json.translation: 当你回家走进前门时，不妨花点时间问问自己："我的生活是否也该删减一点？

transcript_json.text: Would that give me more freedom and more time?”
transcript_json.translation: 它能给我更多自由和更多时间吗？”

transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 2

transcript_json.text: Now, believe it or not, people sometimes lie in order to maintain a good, honest reputation—even if it hurts them to do so.
transcript_json.translation: 信不信由你，人们有时撒谎是为了维持诚实守信的好名声——哪怕这么做会让自己吃亏。

transcript_json.text: At least, this is what a team of scientists is suggesting, with evidence to prove it.
transcript_json.translation: 至少，这是一个科学家团队的观点，而且有证据佐证。

transcript_json.text: Picture this scenario: You often drive for work and can be compensated for up to 400 miles per month.
transcript_json.translation: 想象这样一个场景：你经常因公开车，每月最多可以报销 400 英里。

transcript_json.text: Most people at your company drive about 300 miles each month.
transcript_json.translation: 你们公司的大多数人每月开车约 300 英里。

transcript_json.text: But this month, you drove 400 miles.
transcript_json.translation: 但这个月，你开了 400 英里。

transcript_json.text: How many miles do you think you'd claim in your expense report?
transcript_json.translation: 你觉得你会在报销单上报多少英里？

transcript_json.text: The scientists asked this exact question as part of the study we're discussing today.
transcript_json.translation: 作为我们今天讨论的这项研究的一部分，科学家们问的正是这个问题。

transcript_json.text: With surprising results, they found that 12% of respondents reported the distance they drove as less than the actual figure, giving an average answer of 384 miles.
transcript_json.translation: 结果令人惊讶：他们发现12%的受访者申报的行驶里程低于实际数字，平均答案是384英里。

transcript_json.text: In other words, they lied about the number of miles, even though they would forfeit money they were owed.
transcript_json.translation: 换句话说，他们在英里数上撒了谎，尽管这样他们会损失本该拿到的钱。

transcript_json.text: The researchers believe this was to seem honest, with the assumption being that others would be suspicious of a high expense claim.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员认为，这是为了显得诚实——默认别人会对高额报销起疑。

transcript_json.text: But why would people fabricate numbers to their own detriment?
transcript_json.translation: 但人们为什么会编造数字、损害自己的利益呢？

transcript_json.text: The researchers explain that many people care a great deal about their reputation and how they'll be judged by others.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员解释说，许多人非常在意自己的名声以及别人对自己的评价。

transcript_json.text: If they care enough, their concern about appearing honest and not losing the respect of others may be greater than their desire to actually be honest.
transcript_json.translation: 如果在意到一定程度，他们对于"显得诚实"和"不失去他人尊重"的关切，可能会超过对实际诚实的渴望。

transcript_json.text: The researchers assert that the findings suggest that when people obtain very favorable outcomes, they anticipate other people's suspicious reactions and prefer lying and appearing honest to telling the truth and appearing as selfish liars.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员断言，研究结果表明：当人们获得非常有利的結果时，他们会预判别人的怀疑反应，宁可撒谎、显得诚实，也不愿讲真话、显得自私又爱撒谎。

transcript_json.text: So why is this research important?
transcript_json.translation: 那么，这项研究为什么重要？

transcript_json.text: Well, experts generally agree there are two main types of lie: selfish lies and lies that are meant to benefit others.
transcript_json.translation: 是这样的，专家们普遍认为谎言主要有两类：自私的谎言和旨在利他的谎言。

transcript_json.text: The first, as you may predict, is for selfish gain, such as submitting a fraudulent claim to an insurance company, while the second involves lying to help others or not offend others, for example, telling a friend whose outfit you don't like that they look great.
transcript_json.translation: 第一类如你所料是为私利，比如向保险公司提交虚假索赔；第二类则是为了帮助别人或不冒犯别人而撒谎，比如对一个你并不喜欢其穿着的朋友说她好看。

transcript_json.text: But the researchers are suggesting a third type of lying—lying to maintain a good reputation.
transcript_json.translation: 但研究人员提出了第三种谎言——为了维持好名声而撒谎。

transcript_json.text: Now this hypothesis is new and some skeptics argue that this isn't a whole new category of lie.
transcript_json.translation: 这个假设还比较新，一些怀疑者认为这并不算一个全新的谎言类别。

transcript_json.text: But the findings seem intuitive to me.
transcript_json.translation: 但在我看来，这些发现很符合直觉。

transcript_json.text: After all, one of the main motivations for lying is to increase our worth in the eyes of others, so it seems highly likely that people will lie to seem honest.
transcript_json.translation: 毕竟，撒谎的主要动机之一就是提升自己在他人眼中的价值，所以人们为了显得诚实而撒谎，看来是非常可能的。

transcript_json.text: Why do old people dislike new music?
transcript_json.translation: 为什么老年人不喜欢新音乐？

transcript_json.text: As I've grown older, I often hear people my age say things like “They just don't make good music like they used to.” Why does this happen?
transcript_json.translation: 随着年纪渐长，我常听到同龄人这样说：“现在的歌再也不像从前那样好听了。

transcript_json.text: Luckily, psychology can give us some insights into this puzzle.
transcript_json.translation: ”为什么会这样？幸运的是，心理学能帮我们洞悉这

transcript_json.text: Musical tastes begin to crystallize as early as age 13 or 14.
transcript_json.translation: 个谜题。音乐品味最早在十三四岁时就开始定型。

transcript_json.text: By the time we're in our early 20s, these tastes get locked into place pretty firmly.
transcript_json.translation: 到二十岁出头时，这些品味就已经相当牢固地固定下来了。

transcript_json.text: In fact, studies have found that by the time we turn 33, most of us have stopped listening to new music.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，研究发现，到 33 岁时，我们大多数人已经不再听新音乐了。

transcript_json.text: Meanwhile, popular songs released when you're in your early teens are likely to remain quite popular among your age group through the rest of your life.
transcript_json.translation: 与此同时，在你十三四岁时发行的流行歌曲，很可能在你这个年龄群里流行一辈子。

transcript_json.text: There could be a biological explanation for this, as there is evidence that the brain's ability to make subtle distinctions between different chords, rhythms and melodies deteriorates with age.
transcript_json.translation: 这可能有一种生物学上的解释：有证据表明，大脑对不同和弦、节奏和旋律作出细微区分的能力会随年龄退化。

transcript_json.text: So to older people, newer, less familiar songs might all “sound the same. ”
transcript_json.translation: 所以对上了年纪的人来说，较新、较陌生的歌可能都"听起来一个样"。

transcript_json.text: But there may be some simpler reasons for older people's aversion to newer music.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，老年人排斥新音乐也许有一些更简单的理由。

transcript_json.text: One of the most researched laws of social psychology is something called the “mere exposure effect,” which, in essence, means that the more we're exposed to something, the more we tend to like it.
transcript_json.translation: 社会心理学中被研究最多的定律之一是"曝光效应"，其要义是：我们对某样东西接触得越多，往往就越喜欢它。

transcript_json.text: This happens with people we know, the advertisements we see and the songs we listen to.
transcript_json.translation: 我们认识的人、看到的广告、听的歌曲都是如此。

transcript_json.text: When you're in your early teens, you probably spend a fair amount of time listening to music or watching music videos.
transcript_json.translation: 在十三四岁时，你大概会花不少时间听音乐或看音乐视频。

transcript_json.text: Your favorite songs and artists become familiar, comforting parts of your routine.
transcript_json.translation: 你喜欢的歌曲和歌手成为你日常生活中熟悉而令人安心的组成部分。

transcript_json.text: For many people over 30, job and family obligations increase, so there's less time to spend discovering new music.
transcript_json.translation: 对许多 30 岁以上的人来说，工作和家庭责任增多，用来发掘新音乐的时间更少了。

transcript_json.text: Instead, many will simply listen to old, familiar favorites from that period of their lives when they had more free time.
transcript_json.translation: 许多人干脆听那些人生中空闲较多时期的老歌、熟悉的旧爱。

transcript_json.text: Of course those teen years weren't necessarily carefree.
transcript_json.translation: 当然，青少年时期未必无忧无虑。

transcript_json.text: They're famously confusing, which is why so many TV shows and movies revolve around high school turmoil.
transcript_json.translation: 那是出了名的迷茫期，这也是那么多影视剧围绕高中风波展开的原因。

transcript_json.text: Psychology research has shown that the emotions that we experience as teens seem more intense than those that come later.
transcript_json.translation: 心理学研究表明，我们在青春期体验到的情绪似乎比之后的更强烈。

transcript_json.text: And we also know that intense emotions are associated with stronger memories and preferences.
transcript_json.translation: 我们还知道，强烈情绪与更深的记忆和偏好相关。

transcript_json.text: Both of these might explain why the songs we listen to during this period become so memorable and beloved.
transcript_json.translation: 这两点或许都能解释，为什么我们在这段时期听的歌曲会如此难忘、如此受喜爱。

transcript_json.text: So there's nothing wrong with your parents because they don't like your music.
transcript_json.translation: 所以，你父母不喜欢你的音乐，他们没什么毛病。

transcript_json.text: Rather it's all part of the natural order of things.
transcript_json.translation: 相反，这完全是事物的自然规律。

transcript_json.text: M: There are obvious benefits, though I don't seem to have the freedom I anticipated as I just don't seem able to decline work offers.
transcript_json.translation: M: 好处很明显，不过我似乎并没有得到预期的那种自由，因为我就是没办法拒绝送上门的活儿。

transcript_json.text: And working alone, there have been times when I've found that money alone provides insufficient motivation.
transcript_json.translation: 而且一个人单干，有时候我发现光靠钱不足以提供动力。

transcript_json.text: Have you experienced the same since you began working for yourself?
transcript_json.translation: 你开始自己干之后也有同样的感受吗？

transcript_json.text: W: Sometimes, yes.
transcript_json.translation: W: 有时候是。

transcript_json.text: Unlike the rest of the workforce who have managers to prompt motivation whenever they're feeling lazy or bored, we self-employed workers perform our jobs without a manager to lift our spirits.
transcript_json.translation: 其他上班族一犯懒或一觉得无聊，就有经理来给他们鼓劲，而我们这些自由职业者干活时没有经理来提振精神。

transcript_json.text: There's no one around to offer praise or initiate collaboration, no one to make greater use of our interests and talents.
transcript_json.translation: 身边没有人夸奖我们或发起合作，也没有人进一步发掘我们的兴趣和才能。

transcript_json.text: M: That's a fact.
transcript_json.translation: M: 确实如此。

transcript_json.text: Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care, of course.
transcript_json.translation: 当然，并不是每个经理都有这样的意识和关怀。

transcript_json.text: And certainly not all managers have a clue how to motivate people.
transcript_json.translation: 而且肯定不是所有经理都懂得怎么激励人。

transcript_json.text: Still, having a manager nearby at least indicates there's an opportunity they'll be decent enough to look out for you when your energy and focus begin to deplete.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，身边有个经理至少意味着，当你的精力和专注开始耗尽时，他们有可能会好心照应你一下。

transcript_json.text: W: The motivator I value most is autonomy.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我最看重的动力是自主权。

transcript_json.text: I've learned not to sacrifice my prized autonomy by working all hours of the day and by saying yes to every client request.
transcript_json.translation: 我已经学会不再牺牲我珍视的自主权——不再没日没夜地干活，也不再对客户的每个要求都一口答应。

transcript_json.text: M: Yes.
transcript_json.translation: M: 是啊。

transcript_json.text: I need to remind myself that I selected this lifestyle for the independence.
transcript_json.translation: 我得提醒自己，我选择这种生活方式就是为了独立。

transcript_json.text: I don't miss aspects of permanent full-time employment I disliked, such as the office politics, job insecurity, inflexible hours and so on.
transcript_json.translation: 全职固定工作里那些我不喜欢的东西，比如办公室政治、工作没保障、时间不灵活等等，我一点都不想念。

transcript_json.text: I wouldn't mind a bit more in the form of praise though, praise which is on the record.
transcript_json.translation: 不过要是能多得到些表扬，特别是有据可查的表扬，我也不介意。

transcript_json.text: W: That'll come with time.
transcript_json.translation: W: 时间久了自然会有。

transcript_json.text: Relatedness is inevitably cultivated via human interaction.
transcript_json.translation: 归属感必然是在人与人的交往中培养起来的。

transcript_json.text: Engaging with clients, getting written testimony and recommendations, staying in contact with clients afterwards, these are things you'll find will come in due course and provide you with motivation.
transcript_json.translation: 与客户互动、拿到书面证言和推荐、之后与客户保持联系，你会发现这些到时自然而然就有了，而且会给你提供动力。

transcript_json.text: M: You're right.
transcript_json.translation: M: 你说得对。

transcript_json.text: That's an area I do need to put some more effort into-building closer relationships with those who engage my services and skills.
transcript_json.translation: 这方面我确实需要多下功夫——跟那些聘用我、用我技能的客户建立更紧密的关系。

Weather is a constant force in our lives, but there is little marketing research on how it affects businesses.
transcript_json.translation: 天气是我们生活中一股持续不断的力量，但关于它如何影响企业的市场研究却很少。

transcript_json.text: Now, a new study reveals how sunny and snowy conditions influence consumer behavior.
transcript_json.translation: 如今，一项新研究揭示了晴天和雪天会如何影响消费者行为。

transcript_json.text: Those weather conditions trigger consumers to mentally visualize using products associated with the respective weather.
transcript_json.translation: 这些天气状况会促使消费者在脑海中想象自己使用与该天气相关产品的情景。

transcript_json.text: This leads to consumers placing a higher value on those products.
transcript_json.translation: 这使消费者对这些产品的估值更高。

transcript_json.text: That is, they're willing to pay more money for them.
transcript_json.translation: 也就是说，他们愿意花更多钱购买。

transcript_json.text: But the correlation is only found with products related to being outside.
transcript_json.translation: 但这种相关性只在跟户外活动有关的产品上才有。

transcript_json.text: How does this work?
transcript_json.translation: 这是怎么回事呢？

transcript_json.text: Researchers give the example of a beach towel.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员举了沙滩巾的例子。

transcript_json.text: On a sunny day, consumers who see that product are not just looking at the towel itself, they are likely imagining themselves lying on the towel in the sun.
transcript_json.translation: 在晴天，看到这个产品的消费者不只是盯着毛巾本身，他们很可能在想象自己躺在阳光下那条毛巾上的样子。

transcript_json.text: This mental picture of using the towel increases the value of the product in the consumers' mind.
transcript_json.translation: 这种使用毛巾的想象画面，提高了产品在消费者心中的价值。

transcript_json.text: Researchers put forward the following hypothesis to explain their findings.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员提出以下假设来解释他们的发现。

transcript_json.text: They think the mental picture works in sunshine and snow because these weather conditions have a positive association with outside activities.
transcript_json.translation: 他们认为这种想象画面在阳光和雪天之所以奏效，是因为这些天气与户外活动有着积极的联系。

transcript_json.text: The effect is not seen with rainy weather.
transcript_json.translation: 下雨天就没有这种效果。

transcript_json.text: Researchers assert this is because there aren't many activities that are enabled by rain.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员断言，这是因为下雨能带来的活动不多。

transcript_json.text: Most products associated with rain, like umbrellas, are only used for protection from the weather, and not for any activities.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数和雨有关的产品，比如雨伞，只是用来遮风挡雨，而不是用来开展什么活动的。

transcript_json.text: Researchers believe that companies that sell a wide array of products online can benefit most from the insights this study provides.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员认为，在网上销售多种多样产品的公司最能从这项研究提供的洞见中获益。

transcript_json.text: Online sellers often use complex mathematical formulas to determine what products to feature and how to price these products.
transcript_json.translation: 网上卖家常常用复杂的数学公式来决定重点推荐哪些产品以及如何定价。

transcript_json.text: Incorporating more data about weather would allow them to make better decisions.
transcript_json.translation: 纳入更多天气数据能让他们做出更好的决策。

transcript_json.text: This could bolster sales.
transcript_json.translation: 这可能会提振销售。

transcript_json.text: Setting the office air-conditioning at about 22℃ has become standard practice across the world.
transcript_json.translation: 把办公室空调设在22℃左右已成为全世界的通行做法。

transcript_json.text: Numerous guidebooks across the world on heating, ventilation and air-conditioning claim office performance peaks at 22 degrees.
transcript_json.translation: 世界各地众多关于供暖、通风与空调的指南都声称，办公效率在22度时达到峰值。

transcript_json.text: Many people indeed find relief from soaring summer temperatures in air-conditioned offices.
transcript_json.translation: 在装了空调的办公室里，很多人确实能躲避盛夏飙升的高温。

transcript_json.text: But recent studies have challenged the accepted wisdom that a cool office is more productive.
transcript_json.translation: 但最近的一些研究挑战了"凉爽的办公室效率更高"这一公认看法。

transcript_json.text: The reality is more complex.
transcript_json.translation: 实际情况要更复杂。

transcript_json.text: Researchers conducted a review of all studies relating to air-conditioning and productivity.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员对空调与效率相关的所有研究做了一次综述。

transcript_json.text: They found that 22 degrees was probably a little chilly, even at the height of summer.
transcript_json.translation: 他们发现，即使是在盛夏，22度可能也有点偏凉。

transcript_json.text: For a person dressed in typical summer clothing, an optimal range would be between 23 and 26 degrees.
transcript_json.translation: 对穿着典型夏装的人来说，最佳范围应该在23到26度之间。

transcript_json.text: And people can even tolerate temperatures beyond this comfort zone as long as they can adjust their clothing and expectations.
transcript_json.translation: 而且只要能调整衣着和预期，人们甚至可以忍受超出这个舒适区的温度。

transcript_json.text: In fact, even on very hot days, it makes sense to turn the air-conditioning up.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，即使在酷热的日子，把空调温度调高一点也是合理的。

transcript_json.text: People often chase just one optimum temperature, and this is understandable when people feel hot.
transcript_json.translation: 人们常常只追求一个最佳温度，这在天热的时候可以理解。

transcript_json.text: But there is a range of at least three to four degrees which does not have any adverse impact.
transcript_json.translation: 但至少有三到四度的范围不会产生任何不利影响。

transcript_json.text: Another issue related to this is that people can become psychologically dependent on air conditioning.
transcript_json.translation: 与此相关的另一个问题是，人们可能在心理上依赖空调。

transcript_json.text: If they're used to the environment which is air-conditioned, they tend to prefer lower temperatures.
transcript_json.translation: 如果习惯了有空调的环境，他们往往偏好更低的温度。

transcript_json.text: But the studies found that almost all humans became accustomed to the new temperature.
transcript_json.translation: 但研究发现，几乎所有人都会适应新的温度。

transcript_json.text: It was only at the extreme ends of the temperature range where people's productivity suffered.
transcript_json.translation: 只有在温度范围的两个极端，人的效率才会受到影响。

transcript_json.text: This range was above 26 degrees and below 19 degrees.
transcript_json.translation: 这个范围是高于26度和低于19度。

Psychology research has tended to portray solitude as a negative experience.
transcript_json.translation: 心理学研究往往把独处描绘成一种消极的体验。

transcript_json.text: Studies conducted in the 1970s and 1990s suggested that people felt less happy when alone as compared to being with others.
transcript_json.translation: 20世纪70年代和90年代的研究表明，与跟别人相处相比，人们独处时幸福感更低。

transcript_json.text: However, a new paper shows an alternative view of solitude, one in which solitude can be positive.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，一篇新论文展示了对独处的另一种看法：独处也可以是积极的。

transcript_json.text: Let's start by looking at the earlier research.
transcript_json.translation: 我们先来看看早期的研究。

transcript_json.text: It had a couple of shortcomings.
transcript_json.translation: 它有几个缺点。

transcript_json.text: First, it measured emotion on a scale from positive to negative, overlooking the possibility that our positive and negative emotions can fluctuate independently.
transcript_json.translation: 首先，它用一个从正面到负面的量表来测量情绪，忽视了正面情绪和负面情绪可能各自独立波动的情况。

transcript_json.text: Also, it categorized emotions as simply positive or negative.
transcript_json.translation: 此外，它只是简单地把情绪分为正面或负面。

transcript_json.text: It didn't consider that emotions arouse us to different degrees, and that both positive and negative emotions can arouse us a lot or a little.
transcript_json.translation: 它没有考虑到情绪对我们的唤醒程度不同，正面和负面情绪都可能强烈或轻微地唤醒我们。

transcript_json.text: That is, whether positive or negative, emotions can be either high-arousal or low-arousal.
transcript_json.translation: 也就是说，无论是正面还是负面情绪，都可以是高唤醒的或低唤醒的。

transcript_json.text: High-arousal emotions include excitement on the positive side or anger on the negative side, while low-arousal ones include feeling calm on the positive side or lonely on the negative.
transcript_json.translation: 高唤醒情绪包括正面一端的兴奋和负面一端的愤怒，而低唤醒情绪包括正面一端的平静和负面一端的孤独。

transcript_json.text: This new research attempted to overcome these shortcomings.
transcript_json.translation: 这项新研究试图克服这些缺点。

transcript_json.text: Researchers began with a simple study.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员从一个简单的实验做起。

transcript_json.text: They asked participants to spend 15 minutes sitting alone without engaging in any activity, and measured how this solitude influences their emotional state.
transcript_json.translation: 他们让参与者独自静坐15分钟、不做任何活动，并测量这种独处对情绪状态的影响。

transcript_json.text: This experiment specifically aimed to determine the effect of solitude on high-arousal emotions.
transcript_json.translation: 这个实验专门想确定独处对高唤醒情绪的影响。

transcript_json.text: It looked at positive emotions such as being excited or interested and negative emotions including being scared or distressed.
transcript_json.translation: 它考察了兴奋、感兴趣等正面情绪，以及害怕、痛苦等负面情绪。

transcript_json.text: The results were clear.
transcript_json.translation: 结果很明确。

transcript_json.text: After 15 minutes of solitude, the participants showed reductions in both types of emotion.
transcript_json.translation: 独处15分钟后，参与者这两类情绪都有所减弱。

transcript_json.text: A second study measured the effects of solitude on low-arousal emotions.
transcript_json.translation: 第二项研究测量了独处对低唤醒情绪的影响。

transcript_json.text: These included both positive and negative emotions, such as feeling calm, relaxed, sad or lonely.
transcript_json.translation: 这些情绪既有正面的也有负面的，比如平静、放松、悲伤或孤独。

transcript_json.text: That experiment found that all of these emotions were increased by time alone.
transcript_json.translation: 那项实验发现，独处时这些情绪全都增强了。

transcript_json.text: Thus it seems past depictions of solitude were wrong.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，过去对独处的描述似乎是错的。

transcript_json.text: It doesn't have a simple emotional effect that can be characterized as good or bad.
transcript_json.translation: 独处并不会产生可以简单归为好或坏的情绪效果。

transcript_json.text: Rather, it changes the intensity of our inner experience.
transcript_json.translation: 相反，它改变的是我们内在体验的强度。

transcript_json.text: It amplifies quieter emotions, but it diminishes the intensity of stronger feelings.
transcript_json.translation: 它放大较微弱的情绪，但会削弱较强烈感受的强度。

transcript_json.text: It's worth clarifying that these findings relate to relatively brief periods of solitude.
transcript_json.translation: 值得说明的是，这些发现针对的是相对较短的独处时间。

transcript_json.text: This is distinct from prolonged loneliness.
transcript_json.translation: 这与长期的孤独感不同。

transcript_json.text: Research has demonstrated that the latter is correlated with an assortment of negative physical and psychological effects.
transcript_json.translation: 研究已经证明，后者与种种负面的生理和心理影响相关。

transcript_json.text: How can people benefit from being alone?
transcript_json.translation: 人们如何从独处中受益呢？

transcript_json.text: The findings here suggest that people can use solitude to regulate their emotions.
transcript_json.translation: 这些发现表明，人们可以利用独处来调节情绪。

transcript_json.text: Solitude can help us become quiet after excitement, calm after an angry episode, or simply feel at peace.
transcript_json.translation: 独处能帮我们在兴奋后归于安静，在发怒后恢复平静，或者只是感到内心安宁。

transcript_json.text: In 1984, the World Chess Championship was called off abruptly, due to the withered frame of a player who was competing for the title.
transcript_json.translation: 1984年，世界国际象棋锦标赛突然中止，原因是一位争夺冠军头衔的棋手身体垮掉了。

transcript_json.text: He wasn't alone in experiencing the extreme physical effects of the game.
transcript_json.translation: 因这项运动产生极端身体反应的并非只有他一人。

transcript_json.text: Elite players can reportedly burn up to an absurd 6,000 calories in one day.
transcript_json.translation: 据报道，顶尖棋手一天消耗的热量可高达惊人的6000卡。

transcript_json.text: Does that mean that thinking harder is a simple route to losing weight?
transcript_json.translation: 这是不是意味着，更费脑子地思考是减肥的一条捷径呢？

transcript_json.text: Well, when the body is at rest, we know that the brain uses up a startling 20% to 25% of the body's overall energy.
transcript_json.translation: 嗯，我们知道，身体在静息状态时，大脑消耗的能量高达全身总能量的20%到25%，令人吃惊。

transcript_json.text: This level of utilization actually makes the brain the most energy-expensive organ in the body, and yet it makes up only 2% of the body's weight overall.
transcript_json.translation: 这样的消耗水平实际上使大脑成为身体中最耗能的器官，而它只占总体重的2%。

transcript_json.text: So the more we put this organ to work, the more calories we'll burn?
transcript_json.translation: 那么，这个器官用得越多，我们燃烧的热量就越多吗？

transcript_json.text: Technically, the answer is yes, for cognitively difficult tasks.
transcript_json.translation: 严格来说，对于认知上有难度的任务，答案是肯定的。

transcript_json.text: What counts as a "difficult" mental task varies between individuals.
transcript_json.translation: 什么才算"困难"的脑力任务因人而异。

transcript_json.text: But generally, it could be described as something that the brain cannot solve easily using previously learned routines, or tasks that change the conditions continuously.
transcript_json.translation: 但一般可以描述为大脑无法用已学会的老套路轻易解决的问题，或者条件不断变化的任务。

transcript_json.text: However, deep thinking will not burn off the calories gained from eating a sugary snack.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，深度思考并不能燃烧掉吃甜食摄入的热量。

transcript_json.text: Because in relation to the brain's huge overall energy usage, which is devoted to a multitude of tasks, the energy required just to think harder is actually comparatively tiny.
transcript_json.translation: 因为相对于大脑为大量任务所消耗的巨大总能量而言，仅仅是更用力思考所需的能量其实微不足道。

transcript_json.text: We are unconscious of most of what uses up the brain's energy.
transcript_json.translation: 大脑能量的消耗，大部分我们是没有意识的。

transcript_json.text: A lot of that activity is unrelated to conscious activities like learning how to sing or play the guitar.
transcript_json.translation: 其中很多活动与学唱歌或弹吉他这类有意识的活动无关。

transcript_json.text: The brain is able to allocate blood (and thus energy) to particular regions that are being active at that point.
transcript_json.translation: 大脑能够把血液（也就是能量）分配给当时活跃的特定区域。

transcript_json.text: But the overall energy availability in the brain is thought to be constant.
transcript_json.translation: 但人们认为大脑可用的总能量是恒定的。

transcript_json.text: So, while there might be significant increases in energy use at localized regions of the brain when we perform difficult cognitive tasks, when it comes to the whole brain's energy budget overall, these activities don't significantly alter it.
transcript_json.translation: 所以，虽然我们在执行困难的认知任务时，大脑局部区域的能量消耗可能显著增加，但就整个大脑的能量预算而言，这些活动并不会明显改变它。

transcript_json.text: So why did the chess champion grow too skinny to compete in his chess competition?
transcript_json.translation: 那么，为什么那位象棋冠军瘦得没法参加比赛了呢？

transcript_json.text: The general consensus is that it mostly comes down to stress and reduced food consumption, not mental exhaustion.
transcript_json.translation: 普遍的共识是，这主要归因于压力和进食减少，而不是脑力耗竭。

transcript_json.text: Keeping your body pumped up for action for long periods of time is very energy demanding.
transcript_json.translation: 长时间让身体保持随时行动的紧绷状态是非常耗能的。

transcript_json.text: If you can't eat as often or as much as you can or would normally-then you might lose weight.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你不能像往常那样想吃就吃、想吃多少就吃多少——那你可能就会瘦下来。

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 3
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: "Tell me about yourself" may seem like an easy job interview question, but the open-ended nature of this question often leaves job seekers at a loss where to start.
transcript_json.translation: "介绍一下你自己"这个求职面试问题看似简单，但它开放式的特点常常让求职者不知从何说起。

transcript_json.text: This common question is actually a critical test of a job candidate's communication skills.
transcript_json.translation: 这个常见问题实际上是对应聘者沟通能力的一次关键考验。

transcript_json.text: So it's important not to give an unprepared response or mess it up.
transcript_json.translation: 所以，千万别毫无准备地回答，也别把它搞砸，这一点很重要。

transcript_json.text: "Tell me about yourself" is often the first question professional career coaches prepare people for when they give interview guidance.
transcript_json.translation: "介绍一下你自己"往往是职业教练做面试辅导时第一个帮人准备的问题。

transcript_json.text: It's the opportunity for the candidate to take control of the narrative and tell their story in a way that really matters to their audience.
transcript_json.translation: 这是应聘者掌握话语权的机会，可以用真正打动听众的方式讲好自己的故事。

transcript_json.text: It takes hard work and extensive preparation to answer this question well.
transcript_json.translation: 要想答好这个问题，需要下功夫并做充分的准备。

transcript_json.text: When a person goes to a job interview, their interviewer has presumably read their résumé, so they don't need to repeat the information.
transcript_json.translation: 一个人去参加工作面试时，面试官想必已经读过他的简历，所以不需要重复那些信息。

transcript_json.text: But that's what most people will do, as it's their instinct to recite things that are already on their résumé.
transcript_json.translation: 但大多数人偏会那么做，因为背诵简历上已有的内容是他们的本能反应。

transcript_json.text: It's important for job seekers to do their homework on two crucial aspects.
transcript_json.translation: 求职者要在两个关键方面做好功课，这很重要。

transcript_json.text: First, they are not just telling someone a fact about themselves.
transcript_json.translation: 首先，他们不只是在告诉别人关于自己的一个事实。

transcript_json.text: They're telling a story.
transcript_json.translation: 他们是在讲一个故事。

transcript_json.text: And stories take work to create.
transcript_json.translation: 而故事是需要花功夫打磨的。

transcript_json.text: Coming up with a good story means getting reflective about what made their career accomplishments-something they're proud of, and what strengths those accomplishments highlight.
transcript_json.translation: 想出一个好故事，意味着要认真反思：是什么造就了他们职业生涯中的成就——那些令他们自豪的事，以及这些成就凸显了他们哪些长处。

transcript_json.text: Candidates shouldn't pick a broad general strength to elaborate on, such as "I'm smart.
transcript_json.translation: 应聘者不应选一个宽泛笼统的优点来展开，比如"我很聪明。

transcript_json.text: I work hard and I get things done." To come up with multiple career accomplishments or examples for different interview questions, job seekers should talk with others, especially people who know them, partners, friends or co-workers who will bring up different stories than the ones they remember.
transcript_json.translation: 我工作努力，也能把事情办好。"为了给不同的面试问题准备多个职业成就或事例，求职者应该和别人聊聊，尤其是了解他们的人——伴侣、朋友或同事，这些人会讲出一些他们自己都没想到的故事。

transcript_json.text: Secondly, candidates should know what's at stake for the company with this job opening.
transcript_json.translation: 其次，应聘者应该知道这个职位空缺对公司来说事关什么。

transcript_json.text: What they really are asking you is "tell me why you are going to help me." If the person is a prepared candidate, they should have already figured out those things.
transcript_json.translation: 面试官真正想问的是"告诉我你打算怎么帮我"。如果应聘者准备充分，这些事他应该早就弄清楚了。

transcript_json.text: They've read the job description and researched the company on the Internet.
transcript_json.translation: 他们读过职位描述，也在网上调查过这家公司。

transcript_json.text: What job applicants ought to be looking for is what the company is up to, what they are trying to accomplish and what is preventing them from accomplishing those things.
transcript_json.translation: 求职者应该弄清楚的是：这家公司在做什么、想达成什么目标，以及是什么在阻碍他们实现目标。

transcript_json.text: How long should it take to answer? Around a minute.
transcript_json.translation: 回答需要多长时间？大约一分钟。

transcript_json.text: That's about right for most people's attention spans.
transcript_json.translation: 这对大多数人的注意力持续时间来说刚刚好。

transcript_json.text: Under a minute could seem rushed, while over two minutes will start to feel more like a speech.
transcript_json.translation: 不到一分钟会显得仓促，超过两分钟就开始像演讲了。

transcript_json.text: But the length of the answer is not an exact science, and candidates need to keep their career story focused and tailored to their audience.
transcript_json.translation: 不过回答多长并没有精确的科学标准，应聘者需要让自己的职业故事重点突出，并因听众而调整。

transcript_json.text: M: It's my last day at work tomorrow.
transcript_json.translation: M: 明天是我工作的最后一天了。

transcript_json.text: I'll start my new job in 2 weeks.
transcript_json.translation: 两周后我就开始新工作了。

transcript_json.text: My human resources manager wants to conduct an interview with me before I leave.
transcript_json.translation: 人力资源经理想在我离开前对我做一次面谈。

transcript_json.text: W: Ah, an exit interview.
transcript_json.translation: W: 啊，离职面谈。

transcript_json.text: Are you looking forward to it?
transcript_json.translation: 你期待吗？

transcript_json.text: M: I'm not sure how I feel about it.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我说不清自己是什么感受。

transcript_json.text: I resigned because I've been unhappy at that company for a long time, but I'm not sure if I should tell them how I really feel.
transcript_json.translation: 我辞职是因为我在那家公司早就待得不开心了，但我不知道该不该告诉他们我的真实感受。

transcript_json.text: W: To my way of thinking, there are two main potential benefits that come from unleashing an agitated stream of truth during an exit interview.
transcript_json.translation: W: 依我看，在离职面谈中把憋着的真话一股脑倒出来，主要有两个潜在好处。

transcript_json.text: The first is release.
transcript_json.translation: 第一个是释放。

transcript_json.text: Unburdening yourself of frustration, and perhaps even anger to someone who isn't a friend or close colleague can be wonderfully free. M: Let me guess.
transcript_json.translation: 把沮丧甚至愤怒向一个既不是朋友也不是亲密同事的人一吐为快，会让人感到无比畅快。M: 让我猜猜。

transcript_json.text: The second is that the criticism will, theoretically, help the organization I'm leaving to improve, making sure employees of the future are less likely to encounter what I did?
transcript_json.translation: 第二个是，这些批评在理论上能帮助我要离开的组织改进，让以后的员工不太可能遭遇我遇到的事？

transcript_json.text: W: That's right.
transcript_json.translation: W: 没错。

transcript_json.text: But the problem with the company improvement part is that very often it doesn't happen.
transcript_json.translation: 但公司改进这一部分的问题在于，很多时候根本不会发生。

transcript_json.text: An exit interview is supposed to be private, but often isn't.
transcript_json.translation: 离职面谈本应是保密的，但常常并非如此。

transcript_json.text: In my company, the information gained from these interviews is often not confidential.
transcript_json.translation: 在我所在的公司，从这些面谈中获得的信息往往不是保密的。

transcript_json.text: The information is used as dirt against another manager, or can be traded among senior managers.
transcript_json.translation: 这些信息会被当作攻击别的经理的黑料，或者在高管之间拿来交易。

transcript_json.text: M: Now you've got me rethinking what I'll disclose in the interview.
transcript_json.translation: M: 现在你让我重新思考该在面谈里透露什么了。

transcript_json.text: There is always a chance that it could affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry.
transcript_json.translation: 这始终有可能影响我的名声和我在这个行业积累人脉的能力。

transcript_json.text: It is a pretty small industry after all.
transcript_json.translation: 毕竟这是个挺小的行业。

transcript_json.text: W: Anything you initially gained from the instant satisfaction of telling it like it is, you might lose down the track by injuring your future career prospects.
transcript_json.translation: W: 你从"有话直说"的即时痛快中得到的任何东西，日后都可能因为损害自己未来的职业前景而统统失去。

transcript_json.text: M: Right.
transcript_json.translation: M: 对。

transcript_json.text: Perhaps I would be better getting things off my chest by going to one of those rate-your-employer websites. W: You could.
transcript_json.translation: 也许我该去那些给雇主打分的网站上把心里话倒出来，这样会更好受些。W: 你可以这么做。

transcript_json.text: And don't do the interview at all.
transcript_json.translation: 或者干脆别去面谈。

transcript_json.text: Exit interviews are not mandatory.
transcript_json.translation: 离职面谈并不是强制的。
