transcript_json.text: M: Today, I'm talking to the renowned botanist, Jane Foster.
transcript_json.translation: M: 今天，我要与著名植物学家简·福斯特对谈。

transcript_json.text: W: Thank you for inviting me to join you on the show, Henry.
transcript_json.translation: W: 亨利，谢谢你邀请我参加节目。

transcript_json.text: M: Recently, Jane, you've become quite a celebrity, since the release of your latest documentary.
transcript_json.translation: M: 简，自从你的最新纪录片发布以来，你最近成了不小的人物。

transcript_json.text: Can you tell us a little about it?
transcript_json.translation: 能跟我们简单介绍一下吗？

transcript_json.text: W: Well, it follows my expedition to study the vegetation indigenous to the rain forest in equatorial areas of southeast Asia.
transcript_json.translation: W: 好的，这部片子记录了我去研究东南亚赤道地区雨林原生植被的考察之旅。

transcript_json.text: M: You certainly get to travel to some very exotic locations.
transcript_json.translation: M: 你确实跑了不少非常有异域风情的地方。

transcript_json.text: W: It was far from glamorous, to be honest.
transcript_json.translation: W: 说实话，一点也不光鲜。

transcript_json.text: The area we visited was accessible only by canoe and the living conditions in the hut were primitive to say the least.
transcript_json.translation: 我们要去的地区只有独木舟才能到达，小屋里的生活条件怎么说都够原始的。

transcript_json.text: There was no electricity.
transcript_json.translation: 没有电。

transcript_json.text: Our water supply was a nearby stream.
transcript_json.translation: 我们的水源是附近的一条小溪。

transcript_json.text: M: How were the weather conditions while you were there?
transcript_json.translation: M: 你们在那里的时候天气条件怎么样？

transcript_json.text: W: The weather was not conducive to work at all, since the humidity was almost unbearable.
transcript_json.translation: W: 天气根本不适合工作，湿度几乎让人难以忍受。

transcript_json.text: At midday, we stayed in the hut and did nothing.
transcript_json.translation: 中午，我们只能待在小屋里什么都不干。

transcript_json.text: It was too humid to either work or sleep.
transcript_json.translation: 又闷又湿，工作睡觉都不行。

transcript_json.text: M: How long did your team spend in the jungle?
transcript_json.translation: M: 你们团队在丛林里待了多久？

transcript_json.text: W: Originally, we planned to be there for a month.
transcript_json.translation: W: 最初我们计划待一个月。

transcript_json.text: But in the end, we stayed for only 2 weeks.
transcript_json.translation: 但最后只待了两个星期。

transcript_json.text: M: Why did you cut the expedition short?
transcript_json.translation: M: 你们为什么提前结束了考察？

transcript_json.text: W: Halfway through the trip, we received news that a hurricane was approaching.
transcript_json.translation: W: 行程过半时，我们收到消息说飓风正在逼近。

transcript_json.text: We had to evacuate on very short notice.
transcript_json.translation: 我们不得不在非常仓促的通知下撤离。

transcript_json.text: M: That sounds like a fascinating anecdote.
transcript_json.translation: M: 听起来是一段引人入胜的插曲。

transcript_json.text: W: It was frightening.
transcript_json.translation: W: 其实挺吓人的。

transcript_json.text: The fastest evacuation route was river rapids.
transcript_json.translation: 最快的撤离路线要经过湍急的河流。

transcript_json.text: We had to navigate them carrying all of our equipment.
transcript_json.translation: 我们得背着全部装备闯过急流。

transcript_json.text: M: So overall was the journey unsuccessful?
transcript_json.translation: M: 那么总的来说，这次旅程是不成功的吗？

transcript_json.text: W: Absolutely not.
transcript_json.translation: W: 完全不是。

transcript_json.text: We gathered a massive amount of data about the local plant life.
transcript_json.translation: 我们收集了大量关于当地植物的数据。

transcript_json.text: M: Why do you put up with such adverse conditions?
transcript_json.translation: M: 你为什么要忍受这么恶劣的条件呢？

transcript_json.text: W: Botany is an obsession for me.
transcript_json.translation: W: 植物学是我痴迷的事业。

transcript_json.text: Many of the destinations I visit have stunning scenery.
transcript_json.translation: 我去过的许多地方都有绝美的风景。

transcript_json.text: I get to meet a variety of people from all over the world.
transcript_json.translation: 我还能结识来自世界各地的形形色色的人。

transcript_json.text: M: So where will your next destination be?
transcript_json.translation: M: 那你的下一个目的地是哪里？

transcript_json.text: W: I haven't decided yet.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我还没决定。

transcript_json.text: M: Then we can leave it for another vacation.
transcript_json.translation: M: 那我们就留到下次节目再聊吧。

transcript_json.text: Thanks.
transcript_json.translation: 谢谢。

transcript_json.text: Scientists often use specialized jargon terms while communicating with laymen.
transcript_json.translation: 科学家在与外行交流时常使用专业术语。

transcript_json.text: Most of them don't realize the harmful effects of this practice.
transcript_json.translation: 他们中的大多数人并没有意识到这种做法的危害。

transcript_json.text: In a new study, people exposed to jargon when reading about subjects like autonomous vehicles and surgical robots later said they were less interested in science than others who read about the same topics, but without the use of specialized terms.
transcript_json.translation: 在一项新研究中，阅读自动驾驶汽车、手术机器人等主题时接触到专业术语的人，事后表示自己对科学的兴趣低于阅读同样主题但没有使用专业术语的人。

transcript_json.text: They also felt less informed about science and less qualified to discuss science topics. It's noteworthy that it made no difference if the jargon terms were defined in the text.
transcript_json.translation: 他们还觉得自己对科学了解得少、没资格讨论科学话题。值得注意的是，即使术语在文中给出了解释，情况也没有任何改变。

transcript_json.text: Even when the terms were defined, readers still felt the same lack of engagement as readers who read jargon that wasn't explained.
transcript_json.translation: 即使术语有释义，读者仍与读到未加解释术语的读者一样缺乏投入感。

transcript_json.text: The problem is that the mere presence of jargon sends a discouraging message to readers.
transcript_json.translation: 问题在于，仅仅出现术语就会给读者传递一种令人气馁的信号。

transcript_json.text: Hillary Schulman, the author of the study, asserts that specialized words are a signal.
transcript_json.translation: 该研究的作者希拉里·舒尔曼断言，专业词语是一种信号。

transcript_json.text: Jargon tells people that the message isn't for them.
transcript_json.translation: 术语告诉人们：这些内容不是写给你的。

transcript_json.text: There's an even darker side to how people react to jargon.
transcript_json.translation: 人们对术语的反应还有更黑暗的一面。

transcript_json.text: In another study, researchers found that reading scientific articles containing jargon led people to doubt the actual science.
transcript_json.translation: 在另一项研究中，研究人员发现，阅读含有术语的科学文章会让人怀疑科学本身。

transcript_json.text: They found the opposite, when a text is easier to read, then people are more persuaded.
transcript_json.translation: 他们还发现了相反的情形：文章越易读，人们越容易被说服。

transcript_json.text: Thus, it's important to communicate clearly when talking about complex science subjects.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，谈论复杂的科学话题时，清晰地表达很重要。

transcript_json.text: This is especially true with issues related to public health, like the safety of new medications and the benefits of vaccines.
transcript_json.translation: 对于涉及公共卫生的问题尤其如此，比如新药的安全性和疫苗的益处。

transcript_json.text: Schulman concedes that the use of jargon is appropriate with scientific audiences.
transcript_json.translation: 舒尔曼承认，面向科学受众时使用术语是合适的。

transcript_json.text: But scientists who want to communicate with the general public need to modify their language.
transcript_json.translation: 但想与普通公众交流的科学家需要调整自己的语言。

transcript_json.text: They need to eliminate jargon.
transcript_json.translation: 他们需要摒弃术语。

transcript_json.text: At the beginning of the twentieth century, on the Gulf Coast in the US state of Texas, there was a hill where gas leakage was so noticeable that schoolboys would sometimes set the hill on fire.
transcript_json.translation: 20 世纪初，在美国得克萨斯州墨西哥湾沿岸有一座小山，那里的天然气泄漏非常明显，学童们有时会干脆把山点着。

transcript_json.text: Patio Higgins, a disreputable local businessman, became convinced that there was oil below the gassy hill.
transcript_json.translation: 当地一位名声不佳的商人佩肖·希金斯确信，这座冒气的小山下面有石油。

transcript_json.text: Oil wells weren't drilled back then; they were essentially dug.
transcript_json.translation: 那时候的油井不是钻出来的，而基本上是挖出来的。

transcript_json.text: The sand under the hill defeated several attempts by Higgins' workers to make a proper hole.
transcript_json.translation: 山下的沙层让希金斯的工人们好几次都打不出一个像样的井孔。

transcript_json.text: Higgins had forecast oil at 1,000 feet, a totally made-up figure.
transcript_json.translation: 希金斯曾预测石油在 1000 英尺深处，这个数字完全是瞎编的。

transcript_json.text: Higgins subsequently hired a mining engineer, Captain Anthony Lucas.
transcript_json.translation: 希金斯随后雇了一名采矿工程师——安东尼·卢卡斯上尉。

transcript_json.text: After encountering several setbacks, Captain Lucas decided to use a drill, and his innovations created the modern oil drilling industry.
transcript_json.translation: 在遭遇几次挫折之后，卢卡斯上尉决定使用钻机，他的创新开创了现代石油钻井工业。

transcript_json.text: In January 1901, at 1,020 feet, almost precisely the depth predicted by Higgins' wild guess, the well roared and suddenly ejected mud and six tons of drilling pipe out of the ground, terrifying those present.
transcript_json.translation: 1901 年 1 月，在 1020 英尺深处——几乎正好是希金斯瞎猜的深度——油井轰然作响，猛地把泥浆和六吨钻杆喷出地面，吓坏了在场的人。

transcript_json.text: For the next nine days, until the well was capped, the well poured out more oil than all the wells in America combined.
transcript_json.translation: 接下来九天，直到油井被封上，它涌出的石油比全美国所有油井加起来还多。

transcript_json.text: In those days, Texas was almost entirely rural, with no large cities and practically no industry.
transcript_json.translation: 那个年代的得克萨斯几乎全是乡村，没有大城市，也几乎没有任何工业。

transcript_json.text: Cotton and beef were the foundation of the economy.
transcript_json.translation: 棉花和牛肉是经济的支柱。

transcript_json.text: Higgins' well changed that.
transcript_json.translation: 希金斯的油井改变了这一切。

transcript_json.text: The boom made some prospectors millionaires, but the sudden surplus of petroleum was not entirely a blessing for Texas.
transcript_json.translation: 这场热潮让一些勘探者成了百万富翁，但石油的突然过剩对得克萨斯来说并不完全是福音。

transcript_json.text: In the 1930s, prices crashed to the point that in some parts of the country, oil was cheaper than water.
transcript_json.translation: 20 世纪 30 年代，油价暴跌，以致在全国一些地方，石油比水还便宜。

transcript_json.text: That would become a familiar pattern of the boom or bust Texas economy.
transcript_json.translation: 这将成为得州经济"大起大落"的熟悉套路。

transcript_json.translation: Q12. 得州商人佩肖·希金斯相信什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q13. 什么使希金斯的工人挖不出一个能采油的像样井孔？

transcript_json.translation: Q14. 关于卢卡斯上尉的钻井方法，短文说了什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q15. 关于得州石油工业的繁荣，我们了解到什么？

Most people dislike their jobs.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数人不喜欢自己的工作。

transcript_json.text: It's an astonishing but statistical fact.
transcript_json.translation: 这是一个令人吃惊但却是统计上的事实。

transcript_json.text: A primary cause of employee dissatisfaction, according to fresh research, is that many believe they have terrible managers.
transcript_json.translation: 根据最新研究，员工不满意的一个主要原因是：许多人认为自己遇上了糟糕的经理。

transcript_json.text: Few describe their managers as malicious or manipulative, though, while those types certainly exist, they are a minority.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，很少有人把自己的经理描述成恶毒或爱操控人的——那种人当然存在，但只是少数。

transcript_json.text: The majority of managers seemingly just don't know any better.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数经理似乎只是不懂更好的管理方式。

transcript_json.text: They're often emulating bad managers they've had in the past.
transcript_json.translation: 他们常常是在模仿自己过去遇到过的差劲经理。

transcript_json.text: It's likely they've never read a management book or attended a management course.
transcript_json.translation: 他们很可能从未读过管理学书籍，也没上过管理课程。

transcript_json.text: They might not have even reflected on what good management looks like and how it would influence their own management style.
transcript_json.translation: 他们甚至可能从未思考过好的管理是什么样子，以及它会怎样影响自己的管理风格。

transcript_json.text: The researchers interviewed employees about their managers, beginning with a question about the worst manager they had ever had.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员就经理问题访谈了员工，第一个问题是你遇到过的最糟糕的经理。

transcript_json.text: From this, the researchers came up with four main causes of why some managers are perceived as being simply awful at their jobs.
transcript_json.translation: 由此，研究人员归纳出某些经理被认为完全不胜任的四个主要原因。

transcript_json.text: The first cause was company culture, which was seen by employees as enabling poor management practices.
transcript_json.translation: 第一个原因是公司文化，员工们认为它纵容了糟糕的管理行为。

transcript_json.text: It was specifically stressful work environments, minimal training, and a lack of accountability that were found to be the most blameworthy.
transcript_json.translation: 具体而言，研究发现最该指责的是高压的工作环境、极少的培训，以及问责缺失。

transcript_json.text: Often a manager's superiors can effectively encourage a manager's distasteful behavior when they fail to discipline the person's wrongdoings.
transcript_json.translation: 经理的上级若不对其不当行为进行惩戒，实际上就是在纵容经理的恶劣做派。

transcript_json.text: Such workplaces are sometimes described as toxic.
transcript_json.translation: 这样的职场有时被称为"有毒"。

transcript_json.text: The second cause was attributed to the managers' characteristics: those deemed to be most destructive were odd people, those without drive, those who allow personal problems into the workplace, and those with an unpleasant temperament or personality in general.
transcript_json.translation: 第二个原因归于经理本人的特质：被认为最具破坏性的是那些怪异的人、缺乏干劲的人、把私人问题带进职场的人，以及总体上脾气或性格讨人厌的人。

transcript_json.text: The third cause of poor management was associated with their deficiency of qualifications.
transcript_json.translation: 管理不善的第三个原因与他们的资历不足有关。

transcript_json.text: Not so much the formal variety one obtains from a university, but the informal variety that comes from credible work experience and professional accomplishments.
transcript_json.translation: 不是从大学获得的那种正规资历，而是来自可信的工作经验和职业成就的非正规资历。

transcript_json.text: The fourth cause concerned managers who've been promoted for reasons other than potential.
transcript_json.translation: 第四个原因涉及那些因潜力以外的理由获得晋升的经理。

transcript_json.text: One reason in particular why these people had been promoted was that they had been around the longest.
transcript_json.translation: 这些人获得晋升的一个特别原因，是他们资历最老、待得最久。

transcript_json.text: It wasn't their skillset or other merits that got them the job, it was their tenure.
transcript_json.translation: 让他们坐上这个位置的不是技能或其他优点，而是他们的年头。

transcript_json.text: A point worth making is that the study was based only on the perspective of employees.
transcript_json.translation: 值得指出的一点是，这项研究只基于员工的视角。

transcript_json.text: The researchers didn't ask senior leaders what they thought of their front-line managers.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员没有询问高层领导对一线经理的看法。

transcript_json.text: It's quite possible they're content with how the individuals they promoted are now performing, merrily ignorant of the damage they're actually causing, which might explain why, as the researchers conclude, those same middle managers are usually unaware that they are a bad manager.
transcript_json.translation: 很有可能，这些高层对自己提拔的人如今的表现颇为满意，浑然不觉他们实际造成的损害——这或许可以解释，正如研究人员所总结的，这些中层经理自己通常意识不到自己是个差劲的经理。

transcript_json.text: With the use of driverless vehicles seemingly inevitable, mining companies in the vast Australian desert state of Western Australia are definitely taking the lead.
transcript_json.translation: 无人驾驶车辆的使用似乎已是大势所趋，而位于广袤的澳大利亚沙漠之州西澳大利亚的矿业公司无疑正走在最前面。

transcript_json.text: Iron ore is a key ingredient in steel-making.
transcript_json.translation: 铁矿石是炼钢的关键原料。

transcript_json.text: The mining companies here produce almost 300 million tons of iron ore a year.
transcript_json.translation: 这里的矿业公司每年生产近 3 亿吨铁矿石。

transcript_json.text: The 240 giant autonomous trucks in use, in the Western Australian mines, can weigh 400 tons, fully loaded, and travel at speeds of up to 60 kilometers per hour.
transcript_json.translation: 西澳矿区投入使用的 240 辆巨型无人卡车，满载可达 400 吨，行驶时速最高 60 公里。

transcript_json.text: They are a technological leap, transporting iron ore along routes which run for hundreds of kilometers from mines to their destinations.
transcript_json.translation: 它们是一次技术飞跃，沿着从矿山通往目的地的数百公里长的路线运输铁矿石。

transcript_json.text: Here, when the truck arrives at its destination, staff in the operation center direct it precisely where to unload.
transcript_json.translation: 在这里，卡车到达目的地后，运营中心的工作人员精确指挥它到指定位置卸货。

transcript_json.text: Vast quantities of iron ore are then transported by autonomous trains to ocean ports.
transcript_json.translation: 然后，大量铁矿石由无人驾驶火车运往海港。

transcript_json.text: Advocates argue these automated vehicles will change mining forever.
transcript_json.translation: 支持者认为，这些自动化车辆将永远改变采矿业。

transcript_json.text: It may only be five years before the use of automation technology leads to a fully robotic mine.
transcript_json.translation: 也许只需五年，自动化技术的应用就会带来完全机器人化的矿山。

transcript_json.text: A range of factors has pushed Western Australia's desert region to the lead of this automation revolution.
transcript_json.translation: 一系列因素把西澳沙漠地区推到了这场自动化革命的前列。

transcript_json.text: These include the huge size of the mines, the scale of equipment, and the repetitive nature of some of the work.
transcript_json.translation: 这些因素包括矿山规模巨大、设备体量庞大，以及部分工作的重复性质。

transcript_json.text: Then there's the area's remoteness, at 502,000 square kilometers, it can sometimes make recruiting staff a challenge.
transcript_json.translation: 还有该地区的偏远——面积达 50.2 万平方公里——有时让招聘员工成为难题。

transcript_json.text: Another consideration is the risks when humans interact with large machinery.
transcript_json.translation: 另一个考量是人机互动大型机械时的风险。

transcript_json.text: There are also the financial imperatives.
transcript_json.translation: 此外还有财务上的迫切需求。

transcript_json.text: The ongoing push by the mining corporations to be more productive and more efficient is another powerful driver in embracing automation technology.
transcript_json.translation: 矿业公司持续追求更高产能和更高效率，是拥抱自动化技术的另一个强大驱动力。

transcript_json.text: The concept of a fully autonomous mine is a bit of a misleading term, however.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，"完全无人化矿山"这个概念有点名不副实。

transcript_json.text: This is because the more technology is put into the field, the more people are needed to deploy, maintain and improve it.
transcript_json.translation: 这是因为投入现场的技术越多，就越需要更多的人来部署、维护和改进它。

transcript_json.text: The automation and digitization of the industry is creating a need for different jobs.
transcript_json.translation: 行业的自动化和数字化正在催生对新型岗位的需求。

transcript_json.text: These include data scientists and engineers in automation and artificial intelligence.
transcript_json.translation: 这包括数据科学家，以及自动化和人工智能领域的工程师。

transcript_json.text: The mining companies claim automation and robotics present opportunities to make mining more sustainable and safer.
transcript_json.translation: 矿业公司宣称，自动化和机器人技术提供了让采矿更可持续、更安全的机会。

transcript_json.text: Employees will be offered a career that is even more fulfilling and more rewarding.
transcript_json.translation: 员工将获得一份更有成就感、回报更丰厚的职业。

transcript_json.text: Workers' unions have accepted the inevitability of the introduction of new technology, but they still have reservations about the rise of automation technology.
transcript_json.translation: 工会已经接受了引进新技术的必然性，但对自动化技术的崛起仍持保留态度。

transcript_json.text: Their main concern is the potential impact on remote communities.
transcript_json.translation: 他们主要的担忧是它对偏远社区的潜在影响。

transcript_json.text: As automation spreads further, the question is how these remote communities will survive when the old jobs are eliminated.
transcript_json.translation: 随着自动化进一步普及，问题在于：当旧岗位被淘汰后，这些偏远社区将如何生存。

transcript_json.text: And this may well prove to be the most significant impact of robotic technology in many places around the world.
transcript_json.translation: 而这很可能被证明是机器人技术在世界上许多地方最重要的影响。

transcript_json.text: According to official statistics, Thailand's annual road death rate is almost double the global average.
transcript_json.translation: 根据官方统计，泰国每年的道路交通死亡率几乎是全球平均水平的两倍。

transcript_json.text: Thai people know that their roads are dangerous, but they don't know this could easily be changed.
transcript_json.translation: 泰国人知道自己的道路危险，却不知道这种情况其实很容易改变。

transcript_json.text: Globally, road accidents kill more people every year than any infectious disease.
transcript_json.translation: 在全球范围，道路交通事故每年致死的人数超过任何一种传染病。

transcript_json.text: Researchers at the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in America put the death toll in 2017 at 1. 24 million.
transcript_json.translation: 美国健康指标与评估研究所的研究人员估计，2017 年的死亡人数为 124 万。

transcript_json.text: According to the institute, the overall number of deaths has been more or less static since the turn of the century.
transcript_json.translation: 据该研究所称，自世纪之交以来，死亡总人数基本保持稳定。

transcript_json.text: But that disguises a lot of changes in individual countries.
transcript_json.translation: 但这掩盖了各个国家的许多变化。

transcript_json.text: In many poor countries, road accidents are killing more people than ever before.
transcript_json.translation: 在许多贫穷国家，道路事故致死的人数比以往任何时候都多。

transcript_json.text: Those countries have swelling, young populations, a fast-growing fleet of cars and motorbikes, and a limited supply of surgeons.
transcript_json.translation: 这些国家人口年轻且不断膨胀，汽车和摩托车数量快速增长，外科医生却供不应求。

transcript_json.text: It is impossible to know for sure, because official statistics are so inadequate.
transcript_json.translation: 由于官方统计极不完善，无法确切知道。

transcript_json.text: But deaths are thought to have risen by 40% since 1990 in many low income countries.
transcript_json.translation: 但据认为，自 1990 年以来，许多低收入国家的死亡人数上升了 40%。

transcript_json.text: In many rich countries, by contrast, roads are becoming even safer.
transcript_json.translation: 相比之下，在许多富裕国家，道路正变得越来越安全。

transcript_json.text: In Estonia and Ireland, for example, the number of deaths has fallen by about two thirds since the late 1990s.
transcript_json.translation: 例如在爱沙尼亚和爱尔兰，自 20 世纪 90 年代末以来，死亡人数下降了约三分之二。

transcript_json.text: But the most important and intriguing changes are taking place in middle income countries, which contain most of the world's people and have some of the most dangerous roads.
transcript_json.translation: 但最重要、也最耐人寻味的变化正发生在中等收入国家，那里有世界上大多数人口，也有一些最危险的道路。

transcript_json.text: According to researchers in China and South Africa, traffic deaths have been falling since 2000, and in India since 2012, and the Philippines reached its peak four years ago.
transcript_json.translation: 据中国和南非的研究人员称，交通死亡人数自 2000 年以来一直在下降，印度自 2012 年起下降，菲律宾则在四年前达到峰值后开始下降。

transcript_json.text: The question is whether Thailand can soon follow suit.
transcript_json.translation: 问题是泰国能否很快效仿。

transcript_json.text: Rob McKinney, head of the International Road Assessment Program, says that all countries tend to go through three phases.
transcript_json.translation: 国际道路评估项目负责人罗布·麦金尼说，所有国家往往都要经历三个阶段。

transcript_json.text: They begin with poor, slow roads.
transcript_json.translation: 第一阶段是路况差、车速慢。

transcript_json.text: In the second phase, as they grow wealthier, they pave the roads, allowing traffic to move faster and pushing up the death rate.
transcript_json.translation: 第二阶段，随着国家变富，他们铺设道路，让车流更快，死亡率也随之上升。

transcript_json.text: Lastly, in the third phase, countries act to make their roads safer.
transcript_json.translation: 最后，在第三阶段，各国采取行动让道路更安全。

transcript_json.text: The trick, then, is to reach the third stage sooner by focusing earlier and more closely on fatal accidents.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，诀窍在于更早、更紧密地关注致死事故，从而更早进入第三阶段。

transcript_json.text: How to do that?
transcript_json.translation: 怎么做呢？

transcript_json.text: The solution lies not just in better infrastructure, but in better social incentives.
transcript_json.translation: 解决办法不仅在于更好的基础设施，还在于更好的社会激励机制。

transcript_json.text: Safe driving habits are practices which people know they should follow but often don't.
transcript_json.translation: 安全驾驶习惯是人人都知道该遵守却常常不遵守的行为。

transcript_json.text: Dangerous driving is not a fixed cultural trait as some imagine.
transcript_json.translation: 危险驾驶并不像有些人想象的那样是一种固定的文化特质。

transcript_json.text: People respond to incentives such as traffic laws that are actually enforced.
transcript_json.translation: 人们会对激励作出反应，比如真正得到执行的交通法规。

transcript_json.text: M: How are you enjoying your new job?
transcript_json.translation: M: 新工作感觉怎么样？

transcript_json.text: W: So far, so good.
transcript_json.translation: W: 目前为止还不错。

transcript_json.text: I don't miss having managers who deliver blunt, harsh feedback in the name of efficiency.
transcript_json.translation: 我一点也不怀念那些打着效率旗号、说话又直又刻薄给你反馈的经理们。

transcript_json.text: M: From the way you described your last company, no wonder they had a problem with high staff turnover.
transcript_json.translation: M: 听你这样描述上一家公司，难怪他们员工流失率居高不下。

transcript_json.text: W: Yeah.
transcript_json.translation: W: 是啊。

transcript_json.text: I couldn't wait to get out of there once my contract expired.
transcript_json.translation: 合同一到期我就迫不及待地离开了。

transcript_json.text: The problem with a company culture that prizes directness above all else is that it creates a toxic culture of brilliant jerks that drives people out and erodes itself from within.
transcript_json.translation: 把直来直去捧得高于一切的公司文化，问题在于它会催生一种“聪明混蛋”的有毒文化，把人逼走，还从内部侵蚀公司。

transcript_json.text: M: My company's managers tend to be accommodating and kind, overlooking mistakes or issues so as not to hurt feelings.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我们公司的经理们往往迁就和气，为了不伤感情而对错误和问题睁一只眼闭一只眼。

transcript_json.text: Issues often get ignored there until they build up and reach a crisis point.
transcript_json.translation: 在那里，问题常常被忽视，直到积攒起来到了危机爆发的地步。

transcript_json.text: W: That's not surprising.
transcript_json.translation: W: 这不奇怪。

transcript_json.text: My new company seems to employ a feedback policy that combines compassion and directness.
transcript_json.translation: 我的新公司似乎实行一套把体恤和直接结合起来的反馈制度。

transcript_json.text: Employees have the power to speak up, give feedback, disagree and discuss problems in real time.
transcript_json.translation: 员工可以大胆发声、给出反馈、提出异议并实时讨论问题。

transcript_json.text: It seems to help us to course correct, improve and meet challenges while also building teams that collaborate and care for one another.
transcript_json.translation: 这似乎帮助我们纠偏、改进、迎接挑战，同时也打造出协作互助、彼此关心的团队。

transcript_json.text: M: But that would be based on an atmosphere of mutual trust, wouldn't it?
transcript_json.translation: M: 但这得建立在相互信任的氛围之上，不是吗？

transcript_json.text: Otherwise, people might interpret feedback as some kind of personal attack. W: True.
transcript_json.translation: 否则，人们可能把反馈理解成某种人身攻击。W: 的确。

transcript_json.text: Without an atmosphere of trust, feedback can create stress and self-doubt.
transcript_json.translation: 没有信任的氛围，反馈会带来压力和自我怀疑。

transcript_json.text: But I think when we get feedback from someone we trust, we understand that the feedback isn't some kind of personal attack.
transcript_json.translation: 但我想，当我们从信任的人那里得到反馈时，我们会明白反馈并不是什么人身攻击。

transcript_json.text: It's actually a kind of support because it's offered in the spirit of helping us improve.
transcript_json.translation: 它其实是一种支持，因为它是在帮助我们进步的善意之下给出的。

transcript_json.text: I think sometimes people need to shift their mindsets around how they receive feedback. M: Yes.
transcript_json.translation: 我觉得有时候，人们需要转变自己接受反馈时的心态。M: 是。

transcript_json.text: Constructive feedback, after all, is how we learn and grow.
transcript_json.translation: 毕竟，建设性的反馈正是我们学习和成长的方式。

transcript_json.text: It's the basis for healthy parenting, lasting friendships, career development, and so much more.
transcript_json.translation: 它是健康育儿、长久友谊、职业发展等等许多事情的基础。

transcript_json.text: If we shelter our children, friends and colleagues from information that might enrich and enhance their lives, we are not being caring.
transcript_json.translation: 如果我们把孩子、朋友和同事屏蔽在可能让生活更充实、更美好的信息之外，那并不是关爱。

transcript_json.text: We're actually doing harm to them.
transcript_json.translation: 我们实际上是在伤害他们。

transcript_json.text: W: That's exactly right.
transcript_json.translation: W: 说得太对了。

transcript_json.text: W: How was your holiday?
transcript_json.translation: W: 假期过得怎么样？

transcript_json.text: Not too many other tourists around, were there?
transcript_json.translation: 周围没有太多别的游客吧？

transcript_json.text: M: No, very few, relatively.
transcript_json.translation: M: 是的，相对来说很少。

transcript_json.text: But I found myself moving from one accommodation to another, trying to find the perfect place.
transcript_json.translation: 但我发现自己从一家住处换到另一家，总想找到完美的落脚点。

transcript_json.text: It made me realize that indecision is a big problem for me.
transcript_json.translation: 这让我意识到犹豫不决是我的大毛病。

transcript_json.text: Instead of relaxing, I was looking for the best spot.
transcript_json.translation: 我没在放松，而是在寻找最佳住处。

transcript_json.text: W: It seems you suffer from "Fear of Better Options. " I've read about it.
transcript_json.translation: W: 看来你得了“更优选择恐惧症”。我读到过这个说法。

transcript_json.text: It describes this loop of indecision as part of our programming.
transcript_json.translation: 它把这种犹豫不决的循环描述成我们天生的程序设定。

transcript_json.text: Essentially, we have this tendency to keep stretching out the decision-making process.
transcript_json.translation: 从根本上说，我们有一种不断拖长决策过程的倾向。

transcript_json.text: Because as human beings, we are hard-wired to optimize.
transcript_json.translation: 因为作为人类，追求最优是我们的天性。

transcript_json.text: We have always looked to get the best things we can as a sort of survival of the fittest.
transcript_json.translation: 我们总是想方设法拿到能得到的最好的东西，这算是一种适者生存。

transcript_json.text: Optimizing isn't the problem, but rather the process that we go through.
transcript_json.translation: 追求最优本身不是问题，问题在于我们经历的那个过程。

transcript_json.text: M: Well, that makes me feel better.
transcript_json.translation: M: 嗯，这让我好受些了。

transcript_json.text: But I think thanks to technology, we can make comparisons more easily and have more access to choice and customization.
transcript_json.translation: 但我想，多亏了技术，我们更容易货比三家，也拥有更多选择和定制的空间。

transcript_json.text: We can now see what we could have, how we might get it and what others have that we might want.
transcript_json.translation: 我们现在能看到自己能拥有什么、可能怎么得到它，以及别人有什么是我们可能想要的。

transcript_json.text: We keep looking over and return to the same options again and again. W: Yes.
transcript_json.translation: 我们不停地反复审视，一次又一次回到同样的选项上。W: 是。

transcript_json.text: Fear of better options offers little benefit.
transcript_json.translation: 更优选择恐惧症几乎没什么好处。

transcript_json.text: It's an ailment of abundance.
transcript_json.translation: 这是一种“富足病”。

transcript_json.text: You must have choices to have that fear of missing out on better options.
transcript_json.translation: 你得先有选择，才会害怕错过更好的选项。

transcript_json.text: M: Yes, I need to note when I'm worrying about inconsequential things, I guess.
transcript_json.translation: M: 是的，我想我得留意自己什么时候在为无关紧要的事情操心。

transcript_json.text: If I'm spending too much time worrying over what to have for lunch, I'm robbing myself of the energy to focus on the things that matter. W: Exactly.
transcript_json.translation: 如果我花太多时间纠结午饭吃什么，我就是在剥夺自己专注于要事的精力。W: 完全正确。

transcript_json.text: But for more important matters, I think gut instinct might be overrated.
transcript_json.translation: 但对于更重要的事，我觉得跟着直觉走可能被高估了。

transcript_json.text: When you have 30 odd options, trusting your gut is not practical.
transcript_json.translation: 当你面对三十来个选项时，相信直觉并不现实。

transcript_json.text: What you need to do is research, have a process, invest time exploring your options, and eliminate as many things as you can.
transcript_json.translation: 你需要做的是做研究、有一套流程、投入时间探索各个选项，并尽可能多地排除。

transcript_json.text: The most toxic part of decision making is going over the same options time and time again.
transcript_json.translation: 决策中最有害的部分，就是把同样的选项翻来覆去地看。

transcript_json.text: The role of homework in classrooms is not a new debate.
transcript_json.translation: 家庭作业在课堂中的作用并不是一个新话题。

transcript_json.text: Many parents and teachers are ardent supporters of homework.
transcript_json.translation: 许多家长和老师是家庭作业的坚定支持者。

transcript_json.text: But do all students benefit from homework?
transcript_json.translation: 但所有学生都能从作业中受益吗？

transcript_json.text: A 2006 research paper suggested some correlation between the amount of homework done by a student and future academic achievement for middle and high school students—but not so much for younger kids.
transcript_json.translation: 2006 年的一篇研究论文指出，对初高中学生来说，学生作业量与未来学业成绩存在一定相关性——但对年龄更小的孩子却不然。

transcript_json.text: A Stanford study in 2014 suggested the same was true for students in California's affluent communities.
transcript_json.translation: 斯坦福大学 2014 年的一项研究表明，加州富裕社区的学生也是如此。

transcript_json.text: The findings challenged the idea that homework was "inherently good."
transcript_json.translation: 这些发现挑战了"家庭作业天生有益"的观念。

transcript_json.text: " The researchers concluded that there was an upper limit to the correlation between homework and achievement, suggesting that high school students shouldn't be doing more than two hours of homework a night.
transcript_json.translation: ”研究人员得出结论，作业与成绩之间的相关性存在上限，也就是说，高中生每晚的作业不应超过两个小时。

transcript_json.text: And the most valuable kind of homework for elementary level children was simply assigned free reading.
transcript_json.translation: 而对小学阶段的孩子来说，最有价值的作业就是布置自由阅读。

transcript_json.text: The topic gets more complicated when we talk about the divide between rural and urban communities.
transcript_json.translation: 当我们谈到城乡社区之间的差距时，这个话题就更复杂了。

transcript_json.text: Studies found that in remote areas the poor quality or lack of Internet access can put students at a disadvantage, because 70% of teachers in these areas assign homework that requires Internet access.
transcript_json.translation: 研究发现，在偏远地区，网络接入质量差或缺失会让学生处于劣势，因为这些地区 70% 的老师布置的作业需要联网。

transcript_json.text: But one in three households doesn't have Internet.
transcript_json.translation: 但每三户家庭中就有一户没有网络。

transcript_json.text: Experts assert homework requiring the Internet isn't fair.
transcript_json.translation: 专家断言，需要联网的作业不公平。

transcript_json.text: While the debate continues about the effect of homework on academic achievements, there are studies focusing on other benefits of homework.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然关于作业对学业成绩影响的争论仍在继续，也有一些研究关注作业的其他好处。

transcript_json.text: A study in Germany found that homework could have an effect on students' personalities, suggesting that doing homework might help kids to become more conscientious and independent learners.
transcript_json.translation: 德国的一项研究发现，作业可能对学生的性格产生影响，这表明做作业或许有助于孩子成为更认真尽责、更独立的学习者。

transcript_json.text: Robert Goddard, an American born in 1882, is widely regarded as the world's first rocket scientist.
transcript_json.translation: 罗伯特·戈达德，1882 年出生的美国人，被普遍认为是世界上第一位火箭科学家。

transcript_json.text: At age 27, Goddard published his first book, in which he hypothesized that a rocket launched from Earth could reach the moon.
transcript_json.translation: 27 岁时，戈达德出版了他的第一本书，在书中他提出假说：从地球发射的火箭可以到达月球。

transcript_json.text: Like many visionaries, the young scientist encountered numerous skeptics.
transcript_json.translation: 像许多有远见的人一样，这位年轻科学家遇到了无数质疑者。

transcript_json.text: In January 1920, the New York Times ridiculed Goddard's theory that rockets could be utilized for space exploration.
transcript_json.translation: 1920 年 1 月，《纽约时报》嘲讽了戈达德关于火箭可用于太空探索的理论。

transcript_json.text: 49 years later, Apollo 11 reached the moon, and the famed newspaper published an apology to Goddard. Goddard launched his first rocket from an aunt's farm in his native Massachusetts in March 1926.
transcript_json.translation: 49 年后，阿波罗 11 号登上月球，这家著名报纸向戈达德刊发了道歉。1926 年 3 月，戈达德在他家乡马萨诸塞州姨妈的农场发射了他的第一枚火箭。

transcript_json.text: His maiden rocket voyage lasted a mere three seconds.
transcript_json.translation: 这枚火箭的处女航只持续了短短三秒。

transcript_json.text: It scaled an altitude of only 12 meters.
transcript_json.translation: 它只爬升到 12 米的高度。

transcript_json.text: Nonetheless, it was a milestone in rocket science.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管如此，它仍是火箭科学的一座里程碑。

transcript_json.text: Goddard later consulted with a weather expert and determined that the climate of New Mexico was ideal for year-round rocket launches.
transcript_json.translation: 戈达德后来咨询了一位气象专家，认定新墨西哥州的气候是全年发射火箭的理想之选。

transcript_json.text: In 1930, Goddard and his family relocated there to a remote valley in the southwest of the country.
transcript_json.translation: 1930 年，戈达德和家人搬到了那里——该州西南部一个偏远的山谷。

transcript_json.text: There he established a laboratory and test range.
transcript_json.translation: 他在那里建立了实验室和试验场。

transcript_json.text: However, the ambitious scientist received negligible support from the government.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，这位雄心勃勃的科学家几乎得不到政府的支持。

transcript_json.text: For four years, wealthy businessman Daniel Guggenheim provided Goddard with an annual $25,000 grant to pursue his dreams.
transcript_json.translation: 四年里，富商丹尼尔·古根海姆每年向戈达德提供 25000 美元资助，支持他追逐梦想。

transcript_json.text: Other rocket enthusiasts also raised funds for him.
transcript_json.translation: 其他火箭爱好者也为他筹款。

transcript_json.text: Over time, Goddard's rockets grew more sophisticated and included the installation of instruments.
transcript_json.translation: 随着时间的推移，戈达德的火箭越来越精密，还装上了仪器设备。

transcript_json.text: In spite of his many successes, Goddard was never able to interest the US military in rocket-propelled weapons.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管屡获成功，戈达德始终无法让美国军方对火箭推进武器产生兴趣。

transcript_json.text: He was granted over 200 patents and continued to pioneer rocket technology until his death in 1945.
transcript_json.translation: 他获得了 200 多项专利，并继续开拓火箭技术，直到 1945 年去世。

transcript_json.text: Working for a new venture comes with a lot of risks-that is, instability, unclear responsibilities and the need to be a master of all trades.
transcript_json.translation: 在初创公司工作伴随着许多风险——也就是说，不稳定、职责不清，还得样样都懂。

transcript_json.text: But the primary benefit is usually the passion and excitement associated with a role in a promising new company.
transcript_json.translation: 但最主要的回报，通常是与在一家有前景的新公司任职相伴的热情与兴奋。

transcript_json.text: The person to thank for that passion and excitement is almost always the entrepreneur.
transcript_json.translation: 这份热情和兴奋几乎总该归功于创业者本人。

transcript_json.text: There's something about the founder's energy and enthusiasm that infects the rest of the team.
transcript_json.translation: 创始人的干劲和热忱有一种感染团队其他成员的魔力。

transcript_json.text: The willingness to take risks may inspire others to be more courageous.
transcript_json.translation: 敢于冒险的意愿可能激励他人更有勇气。

transcript_json.text: The optimism and positivity may motivate people to focus less on trivial and unimportant matters.
transcript_json.translation: 乐观和积极可能促使人们少把注意力放在琐碎无关紧要的事情上。

transcript_json.text: The celebration of milestones may prompt staff to be more grateful about their own accomplishments and privileges.
transcript_json.translation: 庆祝里程碑可能促使员工更感恩自己的成就和所拥有的条件。

transcript_json.text: What becomes set in the firm's culture is a contagious collection of affirmative and positive emotions which are usually shared among the team.
transcript_json.translation: 融入公司文化的，是一组具有感染力的积极正面情绪，它们通常在团队中共享。

transcript_json.text: Science has already done a good job of proving the results that follow.
transcript_json.translation: 科学已经很好地证明了随之而来的效果。

transcript_json.text: These include better processes, greater team cohesion, reduced conflict and sharper alertness.
transcript_json.translation: 这包括更顺畅的流程、更强的团队凝聚力、更少的冲突和更敏锐的警觉。

transcript_json.text: But what is yet to be demonstrated is whether the founder's passion leads to increased team performance.
transcript_json.translation: 但尚未得到证明的是：创始人的热情是否带来团队绩效的提升。

transcript_json.text: This was recently tested in research, which analyzed the teams of 73 new companies across a range of industries such as IT, medicine and energy.
transcript_json.translation: 最近有一项研究检验了这一点，它分析了 IT、医药、能源等多个行业 73 家新公司的团队。

transcript_json.text: The CEOs were consulted once again years after the initial analysis, and most shared their firm's performance reports, so that their success could be more objectively measured.
transcript_json.translation: 在初次分析数年后，研究人员再次走访了这些首席执行官，大多数人提供了公司的绩效报告，以便更客观地衡量他们的成功。

transcript_json.text: Entrepreneurial teams generally progress through three phases.
transcript_json.translation: 创业团队一般要经历三个阶段。

transcript_json.text: The first is inventing a product or service, the second is founding the venture to sell that product or service, and the third is developing the firm so it continues to grow.
transcript_json.translation: 第一阶段是发明一种产品或服务，第二阶段是创办公司来销售该产品或服务，第三阶段是发展公司使其持续成长。

transcript_json.text: The researchers discovered that when the team is passionate about the third phase-developing a firm-there's a clear link to performance.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员发现，当团队对第三阶段——发展公司——满怀热情时，它与绩效之间存在明显关联。

transcript_json.text: But the first phase-a passion for invention-is not a reliable indicator that the firm will still be open for business a few years later.
transcript_json.translation: 但第一阶段——对发明的热情——并不能可靠地预示公司几年后还在正常经营。

transcript_json.text: Likewise, the second-a passion for founding the venture-doesn't necessarily translate into great success.
transcript_json.translation: 同样，第二阶段——创办公司的热情——也未必转化为巨大的成功。

transcript_json.text: The solution to great team performance stems from a willingness to recruit others who could direct their passion towards the third phase of entrepreneurialism: developing the business.
transcript_json.translation: 打造卓越团队绩效的解决之道，在于愿意招募那些能把热情投向创业第三阶段——发展业务——的人才。

transcript_json.text: Employing more staff can, in itself, be a risk for an entrepreneur, as is paying them big dollars to attract them.
transcript_json.translation: 对创业者而言，多雇员工本身就是一种风险，花大价钱吸引人才同样如此。

transcript_json.text: On many occasions, the entrepreneurs reported not paying themselves a wage at all initially in order to cover salaries and expenses.
transcript_json.translation: 很多情况下，创业者说他们起初压根不给自己发工资，就是为了支付员工的薪水和各项开支。

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 2
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 2

transcript_json.text: Ageing is a curious thing, and people's desire to beat it and death has become an industry worth hundreds of billions of dollars.
transcript_json.translation: 衰老是一件奇妙的事，人们想要战胜衰老和死亡的愿望，已经催生出一个价值数千亿美元的产业。

transcript_json.text: Despite the huge investment into research, ageing remains somewhat obscure, although there are certain things researchers do understand.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管研究投入巨大，衰老依然有些神秘，不过有些事情研究人员确实已经弄清。

transcript_json.text: They know that women tend to have longer life spans, living on average six years longer than men.
transcript_json.translation: 他们知道女性往往更长寿，平均比男性多活六年。

transcript_json.text: No one is really certain of the reason for this, although the speculation centers around the idea that women are more capable of surviving or handling disease than men. For virtually every disease, the effects are greater on men than they are on women.
transcript_json.translation: 没有人确切知道其中的原因，不过推测主要集中在这样一种观点上：女性比男性更能在疾病中存活或应对疾病。几乎在所有疾病上，男性受到的影响都大于女性。

transcript_json.text: Some suggest that women's immune systems benefit from their tendency to prioritize and nurture social connections.
transcript_json.translation: 有人认为，女性的免疫系统得益于她们重视并经营社会联结的倾向。

transcript_json.text: But for me, this explanation is hardly convincing.
transcript_json.translation: 但在我看来，这个解释很难令人信服。

transcript_json.text: Researchers also know to an extent what causes ageing.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员在某种程度上也知道是什么导致衰老。

transcript_json.text: For 60 years, it was believed that cells would continue to divide forever.
transcript_json.translation: 60 年来，人们一直以为细胞会永远分裂下去。

transcript_json.text: It was only uncovered in relatively recent times that older people's cells divide a smaller number of times than younger people's. Only cancer cells, in fact, are capable of dividing forever.
transcript_json.translation: 直到较近的时候人们才发现，老年人细胞的分裂次数比年轻人少。事实上，只有癌细胞能够无限分裂。

transcript_json.text: Human cells have a limited reproductive ability.
transcript_json.translation: 人体细胞的繁殖能力是有限的。

transcript_json.text: To an extent, we can postpone the eventual stop of cells' dividing through nutrition, exercise, good sleep and even relaxation techniques, but we cannot stop the ageing process.
transcript_json.translation: 在某种程度上，我们可以通过营养、锻炼、良好睡眠甚至放松技巧来推迟细胞分裂最终停止，但我们无法阻止衰老进程。

transcript_json.text: And researchers are yet to answer the ultimate question of ageing: why does the body ultimately fall to pieces?
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员还有待回答关于衰老的终极问题：为什么身体最终会分崩离析？

transcript_json.text: In the opinion of some of the world's best scientific minds on the subject, part of the reason we don't yet have any answer is because many researchers are looking in the wrong direction.
transcript_json.translation: 在这一课题上一些全球顶尖的科学头脑看来，我们至今没有答案的部分原因，在于许多研究者找错了方向。

transcript_json.text: Many public health policymakers believe that the resolution of age-associated disease will tell us something fundamental about the ageing process, but, say some top scientists, "that's completely erroneous.
transcript_json.translation: 许多公共卫生政策制定者相信，攻克与年龄相关的疾病将让我们对衰老过程获得根本性的认识，但一些顶尖科学家说，“这完全错了。

transcript_json.text: " They point to when the diseases of childhood were eliminated, but this did not provide any insight into childhood development.
transcript_json.translation: ”他们以儿童疾病被消灭为例——但这并没有为理解儿童发育提供任何洞见。

transcript_json.text: In the same way, the idea that the resolution of age-associated diseases like heart disease and stroke will inform us about ageing is not based on sound science or logic.
transcript_json.translation: 同理，认为攻克心脏病、中风这类与年龄相关的疾病就能让我们了解衰老的想法，并没有健全的科学或逻辑依据。

transcript_json.text: At best, if the major causes of death in developed countries were eliminated, this would only add a decade to average life expectancy.
transcript_json.translation: 充其量，即便消灭了发达国家的主要死因，也只会让人均预期寿命延长十年。

transcript_json.text: But while there is money available to be spent on it, the search to understand the secrets of ageing will be ongoing.
transcript_json.translation: 但只要还有经费可花，探索衰老奥秘的研究就会继续下去。

transcript_json.translation: 问题 19：关于女性往往更长寿的可能原因，我们了解到什么？

transcript_json.translation: 问题 20：关于人体细胞，最近有什么发现？

transcript_json.text: Q21. What do many public health policymakers believe?
transcript_json.translation: 问题 21：许多公共卫生政策制定者相信什么？

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 3
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: Good afternoon.
transcript_json.translation: 下午好。

transcript_json.text: In today's talk, we'll discuss how managers can get their staff to do what they are asked.
transcript_json.translation: 在今天的讲座中，我们将讨论管理者如何让员工按要求行事。

transcript_json.text: Much to their frustration, managers often struggle to get their staff to comply with even simple instructions. Often, they blame their employees: "They don't read emails, they don't listen, they don't care"-that kind of thing.
transcript_json.translation: 令管理者沮丧的是，他们常常很难让员工遵守哪怕最简单的指令。他们往往怪罪员工：“他们不看邮件、不听话、不上心”——诸如此类。

transcript_json.text: But according to recent research conducted in Australia, it looks like it's not the employees' fault, but the managers'.
transcript_json.translation: 但根据澳大利亚最近开展的一项研究，看来这不是员工的错，而是管理者的错。

transcript_json.text: It's easy to understand why people sometimes disobey procedures intentionally.
transcript_json.translation: 人们有时故意不按规程办事，这不难理解。

transcript_json.text: Occasionally, it's because they're pressured to finish in a short time.
transcript_json.translation: 有时是因为他们被要求在短时间内完成，压力很大。

transcript_json.text: At other times, they may disagree with the spirit of the procedure-the effort demanded, the time consumed, the lack of potential effectiveness.
transcript_json.translation: 另一些时候，他们可能不认同规程的实质——要求投入的力气、耗费的时间、效果上的不尽如人意。

transcript_json.text: And every now and then, they just don't want to, maybe deliberately or out of stubbornness.
transcript_json.translation: 还有时候，他们纯粹不想照办，也许是故意的，也许是出于固执。

transcript_json.text: So apart from that, what else gets in the way of procedural compliance?
transcript_json.translation: 那么除此之外，还有什么妨碍员工遵守规程呢？

transcript_json.text: The research scholars surveyed 152 blue-collar workers from two separate sites in the mining industry.
transcript_json.translation: 研究学者调查了采矿业两个不同场址的 152 名蓝领工人。

transcript_json.text: They asked the workers a range of procedure-related questions, such as whether they found the procedures useful, how confident they felt in their job, how comfortable they were to speak up in the workplace, and how closely they followed any new procedures set by their managers.
transcript_json.translation: 他们向工人们提出了一系列与规程相关的问题，比如他们是否觉得规程有用、对工作有多大信心、在工作场合畅所欲言有多自在，以及他们多严格地遵守管理者定下的新规程。

transcript_json.text: They were also asked to rate the extent to which they perceived their supervisors to be helpful.
transcript_json.translation: 他们还被要求评价自己觉得主管乐于助人的程度。

transcript_json.text: That last statement was the most instructive because, as the researchers found, there was a remarkably strong correlation between how helpful supervisors were perceived to be and how likely their employees were to follow their directives. Supervisors' helping behavior was found to be motivational in nature.
transcript_json.translation: 最后那句话最有启发意义，因为研究人员发现，主管被认为有多乐于助人，与员工遵从其指示的可能性之间存在极强的相关性。研究发现，主管的帮助行为本质上具有激励作用。

transcript_json.text: It increased employees' perception of the likelihood of success in the attainment of job goals, and therefore fostered a willingness to dedicate their effort and ability to their work.
transcript_json.translation: 它提升了员工对达成工作目标成功几率的感知，从而培养出愿意把努力和能力投入工作的意愿。

transcript_json.text: In short, managers should be ongoing role models for the change.
transcript_json.translation: 简言之，管理者应当持续做推动变革的榜样。

transcript_json.text: As the saying goes: Do as I do, not as I say.
transcript_json.translation: 正如俗话所说：照我做的做，别照我说的做。

transcript_json.text: To affect behavioral change, what's most required is interaction and involvement-the human touch-and, naturally, processes that add value.
transcript_json.translation: 要促成行为改变，最需要的是互动和参与——人情味——当然，还要有能创造价值的流程。

transcript_json.text: Although procedures are designed to guide and support employees' work, employees, it seems, can't always be expected to comply with procedures that are not seen as useful.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管规程的初衷是指导和支持员工的工作，但似乎不能总指望员工去遵守那些被认为没用的规程。

transcript_json.text: And of course, managers shouldn't keep resending emails.
transcript_json.translation: 当然，管理者也不该一遍遍重发邮件。

transcript_json.text: They are an effective tool for the sharing of data reports, but they are a hopeless tool if what a manager's desiring is a change in behavior.
transcript_json.translation: 邮件是分享数据报告的有效工具，但如果管理者想要的是行为的改变，它就无能为力了。

transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 1

transcript_json.text: W: Hi, David.
transcript_json.translation: W: 你好，大卫。

transcript_json.text: I haven't seen you in class for almost two weeks.
transcript_json.translation: 快两个星期没在课堂上见到你了。

transcript_json.text: We thought you had disappeared on holiday early or something.
transcript_json.translation: 我们还以为你提前去度假消失了呢。

transcript_json.text: M: Hi, Sarah.
transcript_json.translation: M: 你好，萨拉。

transcript_json.text: Well, it's a bit of a long story I'm afraid.
transcript_json.translation: 唉，说来话长。

transcript_json.text: I got a throat infection last week and had to go to the hospital to get some antibiotics as I really wasn't getting any better.
transcript_json.translation: 我上星期喉咙发炎，因为一直不见好转，只好去医院开了些抗生素。

transcript_json.text: W: Oh yeah.
transcript_json.translation: W: 哦，是啊。

transcript_json.text: There have been so many viruses going around this winter.
transcript_json.translation: 今年冬天到处都在流行各种病毒。

transcript_json.text: The weather has been so awful for the last few weeks.
transcript_json.translation: 这几个星期的天气实在太糟糕了。

transcript_json.text: M: And, on the way back from the hospital, I slipped on some ice and fell and then had to go to the hospital to get an X-ray because I basically thought I broke my wrist, although, thankfully, it's not broken.
transcript_json.translation: M: 而且，从医院回来的路上，我在冰上滑了一跤，又得回医院拍X光，因为我基本以为自己手腕骨折了，不过幸好没断。

transcript_json.text: But I need to be careful with it for the next few weeks.
transcript_json.translation: 但接下来的几个星期我得小心呵护它。

transcript_json.text: W: Oh, that's too bad!
transcript_json.translation: W: 哦，那真是太糟糕了！

transcript_json.text: How unfortunate!
transcript_json.translation: 真是不走运！

transcript_json.text: M: To make things worse, I managed to fall right in front of four girls from the ninth grade.
transcript_json.translation: M: 更糟的是，我偏偏摔在了九年级四个女生面前。

transcript_json.text: So I was utterly humiliated.
transcript_json.translation: 我当时简直无地自容。

transcript_json.text: Plus, the laptop in my bag was broken too.
transcript_json.translation: 而且，我包里的笔记本电脑也摔坏了。

transcript_json.text: W: No, what a complete catastrophe!
transcript_json.translation: W: 不会吧，真是祸不单行！

transcript_json.text: Is the laptop still under warranty?
transcript_json.translation: 电脑还在保修期内吗？

transcript_json.text: If it is, then you can easily send it back to the manufacturer, and they'll send you a brand-new one for free surely.
transcript_json.translation: 如果在的话，你可以轻松地把它寄回厂家，他们肯定会免费给你寄一台全新的。

transcript_json.text: M: The warranty ran out three days before I broke it.
transcript_json.translation: M: 保修期在我摔坏它的三天前刚过期。

transcript_json.text: And all my essays are in there, and I need to hand them in before we break for the Christmas holidays.
transcript_json.translation: 我所有的论文都在里面，圣诞节放假前就得交。

transcript_json.text: W: Listen, I have the number of a really good, affordable computer repair shop at home.
transcript_json.translation: W: 听我说，我家有一家又好又实惠的电脑维修店的电话。

transcript_json.text: My dad has used this guy before and he can work miracles.
transcript_json.translation: 我爸以前找过这个人，他简直能创造奇迹。

transcript_json.text: Let's go back to my house and we can call the repair shop, and you can have some tea and cookies too.
transcript_json.translation: 我们回我家吧，可以打电话给维修店，你还能喝点茶、吃点饼干。

transcript_json.text: M: Wow, thanks, Sara! That would be great!
transcript_json.translation: M: 哇，谢了，萨拉！那太好了！

transcript_json.text: Let me just call my mom and let her know I'll be home a little bit later.
transcript_json.translation: 我先给我妈打个电话，告诉她我会晚一点回家。

transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 2

transcript_json.text: M: Welcome to this week's episode of Book Talk.
transcript_json.translation: M: 欢迎收听本周的《读书漫谈》节目。

transcript_json.text: With me today is Heidi Brown, a historian who has written five critically acclaimed books about military history.
transcript_json.translation: 今天的嘉宾是海蒂·布朗，一位历史学家，她写过五本广受好评的军事史著作。

transcript_json.text: W: Thanks for having me, John.
transcript_json.translation: W: 谢谢你邀请我，约翰。

transcript_json.text: I'm so excited to talk about my latest book, which was published last month.
transcript_json.translation: 我很高兴能聊聊我上个月出版的新书。

transcript_json.text: M: So this book is a novel, your first attempt at that genre.
transcript_json.translation: M: 这本书是一本小说，是你首次尝试这种体裁。

transcript_json.text: I thought it was a bit of a departure for you.
transcript_json.translation: 我觉得这对你来说算是有点转型了。

transcript_json.text: W: I'd say it's a major departure as it's not just a work of fiction.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我觉得这是个大转型，因为它不只是虚构作品。

transcript_json.text: It's set 200 years in the future.
transcript_json.translation: 它的故事设定在200年后的未来。

transcript_json.text: M: Right.
transcript_json.translation: M: 是的。

transcript_json.text: So how did that happen?
transcript_json.translation: 这是怎么发生的呢？

transcript_json.text: You spent three decades writing about the past and focusing on the 18th and 19th centuries.
transcript_json.translation: 你花了三十年写过去，专注于18和19世纪。

transcript_json.text: And now you're speculating about the future.
transcript_json.translation: 而现在你在畅想未来。

transcript_json.text: W: Well, after years of researching soldiers and chronicling their lives during battle, I just started wondering about other facets of their lives, especially their personal lives.
transcript_json.translation: W: 嗯，在研究士兵、记录他们战时生活多年之后，我开始好奇他们生活的其他方面，尤其是他们的个人生活。

transcript_json.text: M: I can see that.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我看出来了。

transcript_json.text: Your novel is about soldiers and it focuses on their relationships,especially the bond between sons and mothers and men and their wives.
transcript_json.translation: 你的小说以士兵为主题，着重描写他们的人际关系，尤其是母子之间以及夫妻之间的情感纽带。

transcript_json.text: W: Yes.
transcript_json.translation: W: 是的。

transcript_json.text: That focus came about when I still intended to write another book of history.
transcript_json.translation: 这个着眼点是在我还打算再写一本历史书的时候形成的。

transcript_json.text: I started by researching soldiers' actual personal lives, studying their letters home.
transcript_json.translation: 我从研究士兵真实的个人生活入手，研读他们寄回家的信件。

transcript_json.text: M: So how did that history book become a novel?
transcript_json.translation: M: 那这本历史书是怎么变成小说的呢？

transcript_json.text: W: Well, I realized that the historical record was incomplete.
transcript_json.translation: W: 嗯，我意识到历史记录并不完整。

transcript_json.text: So I'd either have to leave a lot of gaps or make a lot more assumptions than a historian should.
transcript_json.translation: 所以我要么留下大量空白，要么做出远超历史学家本分的假设。

transcript_json.text: M: But why write a novel set in the future when your credentials are perfect for a historical novel?
transcript_json.translation: M: 可是你的资历写历史小说再合适不过，为什么要写一部以未来为背景的小说呢？

transcript_json.text: As a historian, any historical novel you write would have a lot of credibility.
transcript_json.translation: 作为历史学家，你写的任何历史小说都会很有可信度。

transcript_json.text: W: I felt too constrained working with the past, like what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction, but writing about the future gave me more freedom to imagine, to invent.
transcript_json.translation: W: 写过去让我觉得太受束缚，好像我写的东西必须是史实而不是虚构，而写未来给了我更多想象和创作的自由。

transcript_json.text: M: Well, having read your book, I'm glad you made that choice to move into fiction.
transcript_json.translation: M: 嗯，读了你的书之后，我很高兴你做出了转写虚构作品的选择。

transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 1

transcript_json.text: Whether it's in the hands of animated polar bears or Santa Claus, there's one thing you'll find in nearly all ads for Coca-Cola: the characteristic glass bottle.
transcript_json.translation: 无论是在动画北极熊手里还是圣诞老人手里，几乎在可口可乐所有的广告里你都能看到一样东西：那个标志性的玻璃瓶。

transcript_json.text: Most Americans don't drink soda out of the glass bottles seen in Coke's ads anymore.
transcript_json.translation: 如今大多数美国人已经不再用可口可乐广告里的那种玻璃瓶喝汽水了。

transcript_json.text: But this week, the company is celebrating a century of the bottle that's been sold in more than 200 countries.
transcript_json.translation: 但本周，这家公司正在庆祝这款已在200多个国家销售的瓶子问世一百周年。

transcript_json.text: Flash back to 1915, when a bottle of Coca-Cola cost just a nickel.
transcript_json.translation: 让我们回到1915年，那时一瓶可口可乐只要5美分。

transcript_json.text: As the soft drink gained in popularity, it faced a growing number of competitors-counterfeits even trying to copy Coke's logo.
transcript_json.translation: 随着这款软饮料越来越受欢迎，它面对的竞争者也越来越多——甚至有假冒产品试图抄袭可口可乐的商标。

transcript_json.text: So, according to Coca-Cola historian Ted Ryan, the company decided to come up with packaging that couldn't be duplicated.
transcript_json.translation: 据可口可乐公司的历史学家泰德·瑞安说，公司于是决定设计出无法被仿制的包装。

transcript_json.text: A product request was sent to eight different glass makers.
transcript_json.translation: 他们向八家不同的玻璃制造厂发出了产品需求。

transcript_json.text: Workers at the Root Glass Company got the request and began flipping through the encyclopedia at the local library, landing on cocoa seed.
transcript_json.translation: 鲁特玻璃公司的员工接到需求后，开始翻阅当地图书馆的百科全书，最终翻到了可可豆那一页。

transcript_json.text: Though cocoa seed is not an ingredient of the soda, they designed their bottle based on the seed's shape and large middle.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然可可豆并不是这种汽水的原料，他们还是根据可可豆的外形和鼓起的中部设计了瓶子。

transcript_json.text: It won over Coke executives in Atlanta and would go on to receive its own trademark, spur collections and earn Coca-Cola an iconic image that made it part of American culture for a century.
transcript_json.translation: 它赢得了亚特兰大可口可乐高管的青睐，随后还注册了专属商标，掀起了收藏热潮，并为可口可乐赢得了一个标志性形象，使其在一个世纪里成为美国文化的一部分。

transcript_json.text: It was 100 years ago this week that the bottle earned a patent.
transcript_json.translation: 就在100年前的本周，这款瓶子获得了专利。

transcript_json.text: By World War II, Coke bottle sales had ballooned into billions.
transcript_json.translation: 到第二次世界大战时，可乐瓶的销量已经膨胀到数十亿。

transcript_json.text: Americans mostly consume Coke out of aluminum or plastic today, but the glass bottle remains a symbol of America that's readily recognized around the world.
transcript_json.translation: 如今美国人喝可乐大多用铝罐或塑料瓶，但玻璃瓶依然是美国的一个象征，在全世界都一眼可辨。

transcript_json.text: PASSAGE 2
transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 2

transcript_json.text: Research shows that a few moments of conversation with a stranger creates a measurable improvement in mood.
transcript_json.translation: 研究表明，与陌生人聊上几句，就能让心情得到可测量的改善。

transcript_json.text: But most of us are reluctant to start these conversations because we presume the opposite.
transcript_json.translation: 但我们大多数人都不愿开启这样的对话，因为我们以为结果恰恰相反。

transcript_json.text: In an experiment, commuters who talked to nearby strangers found their commute more enjoyable than those who didn't.
transcript_json.translation: 在一项实验中，与身旁陌生人交谈的通勤者，觉得通勤比不交谈的人更愉快。

transcript_json.text: They were asked to predict whether they'd enjoy the commute more if they conversed with other people.
transcript_json.translation: 他们被要求预测：如果与其他人交谈，通勤是否会更愉快。

transcript_json.text: Intriguingly, most expected the more solitary experience to be more pleasurable. Why is this?
transcript_json.translation: 有趣的是，大多数人原本以为更独处的体验会更愉快。这是为什么呢？

transcript_json.text: Social anxiety appears to be the problem.
transcript_json.translation: 社交焦虑似乎就是问题所在。

transcript_json.text: People's reluctance to start conversations with nearby strangers comes partly from "underestimating others' interest in connecting".
transcript_json.translation: 人们不愿与身旁的陌生人交谈，部分源于"低估了别人与人交流的意愿"。

transcript_json.text: The sad thing is that people presume that a nearby stranger doesn't want to converse and don't start a conversation.
transcript_json.translation: 令人遗憾的是，人们想当然地认为身旁的陌生人不想聊天，于是就不开启对话。

transcript_json.text: Only those who forced themselves to chat because it was required by the experiment found out what a pleasant experience it could be.
transcript_json.translation: 只有那些因为实验要求而强迫自己聊天的人，才发现这原来可以是一段多么愉快的经历。

transcript_json.text: Human beings are social animals.
transcript_json.translation: 人是社会性动物。

transcript_json.text: Those who misunderstand the impact of social interactions may not, in some contexts, be social enough for their own well-being.
transcript_json.translation: 那些误解社交影响的人，在某些情况下，为了自身福祉，社交得还不够。

transcript_json.text: You should be chatting with the strangers you encounter.
transcript_json.translation: 你应该和遇到的陌生人聊聊天。

transcript_json.text: You may occasionally have a negative encounter that might stick in your memory.
transcript_json.translation: 你偶尔可能会遇到不愉快的经历，并留在记忆里。

transcript_json.text: This is because the human brain is biased to dwell on negative events.
transcript_json.translation: 这是因为人脑天生倾向于纠结负面事件。

transcript_json.text: But starting conversations with strangers is still well worth the risk of rejection.
transcript_json.translation: 但主动和陌生人交谈仍然非常值得冒被拒绝的风险。

transcript_json.text: It may surprise you that conversing with strangers will make them happier too.
transcript_json.translation: 和陌生人交谈也会让对方更快乐，这可能让你意外。

transcript_json.text: The pleasure of connection seems contagious.
transcript_json.translation: 交流的快乐似乎会传染。

transcript_json.text: People who are talked to have equally positive experiences as those who initiate a conversation.
transcript_json.translation: 被搭话的人和主动开启对话的人，体验同样积极。

transcript_json.translation: Q12. 关于陌生人之间的交谈，研究显示了什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q13. 什么阻碍了人们与陌生人开启对话？

transcript_json.translation: Q14. 与陌生人的不愉快经历为什么会留在记忆里？

transcript_json.translation: Q15. 短文说交流的快乐似乎是什么？

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 1
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 1

transcript_json.text: The Caribbean islands are divided into two worlds, a rich one and a poor one.
transcript_json.translation: 加勒比群岛分为两个世界：一个富裕，一个贫穷。

transcript_json.text: This tropical region's economy is based mainly on farming.
transcript_json.translation: 这个热带地区的经济主要以农业为基础。

transcript_json.text: Farmers are of two types.
transcript_json.translation: 农民分为两种。

transcript_json.text: One is the plantation owner who may have hundreds of thousands of acres.
transcript_json.translation: 一种是种植园主，可能拥有几十万亩土地。

transcript_json.text: In contrast, the small cultivator is working only a few acres of land.
transcript_json.translation: 相比之下，小耕农只种几英亩地。

transcript_json.text: Most visitors to the Caribbean are rich, like the plantation owner.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数去加勒比的游客都很富有，就像种植园主一样。

transcript_json.text: They do not realize or do not want to realize that many farm families barely managed to get by on what they grow.
transcript_json.translation: 他们没有意识到，或者不愿意识到，许多农户光靠自己种的东西勉强糊口。

transcript_json.text: The Caribbean produces many things.
transcript_json.translation: 加勒比地区出产很多东西。

transcript_json.text: Sugar is the main product.
transcript_json.translation: 糖是主要产品。

transcript_json.text: Other export crops are tobacco, coffee, bananas, spices and citrus fruits, such as orange, lemon or grapefruit.
transcript_json.translation: 其他出口作物有烟草、咖啡、香蕉、香料和柑橘类水果，比如橙子、柠檬或葡萄柚。

transcript_json.text: From the West Indies also come oil, mineral pitch and many forest products.
transcript_json.translation: 石油、矿脂和许多林产品也产自西印度群岛。

transcript_json.text: Jamaica's aluminum ore supplies are the world's largest.
transcript_json.translation: 牙买加的铝土矿储量居世界之首。

transcript_json.text: Oil comes from Trinidad, Aruba and Curacao.
transcript_json.translation: 石油产自特立尼达、阿鲁巴和库拉索。

transcript_json.text: But for many of the smaller islands, sugar is the only export.
transcript_json.translation: 但对许多较小的岛屿来说，糖是唯一的出口品。

transcript_json.text: Rum, a strong alcoholic drink, which is distilled from sugar cane, is also an export.
transcript_json.translation: 朗姆酒，一种用甘蔗蒸馏出来的烈性酒，也是出口品。

transcript_json.text: The world's best rum comes from this area.
transcript_json.translation: 世界上最好的朗姆酒就产自这个地区。

transcript_json.text: Local kinds vary from the light rums of Puerto Rico to the heavier darker rums of Barbados and Jamaica.
transcript_json.translation: 当地的朗姆酒多种多样，从波多黎各的清淡朗姆酒，到巴巴多斯和牙买加更浓更黑的朗姆酒。

transcript_json.text: American tourists enjoy stocking up on inexpensive high quality Caribbean rum while they're on vacation.
transcript_json.translation: 美国游客度假时喜欢囤购物美价廉的加勒比朗姆酒。

transcript_json.text: In Curacao, the well-known liquor of that name is made from the thick outer skin of a native orange.
transcript_json.translation: 在库拉索，著名的同名利口酒是用当地一种橙子厚厚的外皮制成的。

transcript_json.text: Ever since America's colonial days, the Caribbean islands have been favorite places to visit.
transcript_json.translation: 从美国殖民地时期起，加勒比群岛就一直是人们喜爱的旅游胜地。

transcript_json.text: Since World War II, tourism has increased rapidly.
transcript_json.translation: 第二次世界大战以来，旅游业迅速增长。

transcript_json.text: Because great numbers of people go there, the islanders have built elaborate resorts, developed harbors and airfields, improved the beaches and have expanded sea and air routes.
transcript_json.translation: 由于大量游客前往，岛上居民修建了精致的度假村，开发了港口和机场，改善了海滩，并拓展了海路和航线。

transcript_json.text: Everything is at the resort-hotel, beach, shopping and recreation.
transcript_json.translation: 度假村里应有尽有——旅馆、海滩、购物和娱乐。

transcript_json.text: The vacationer never has any reason to explore the island.
transcript_json.translation: 度假者根本没有理由去探索这座岛。

transcript_json.text: As in most places, those who have money live well indeed.
transcript_json.translation: 和大多数地方一样，有钱人在这里确实过得很好。

transcript_json.text: Those who don't have money live at various levels of poverty.
transcript_json.translation: 没钱的人则过着不同程度的贫困生活。

transcript_json.text: But here the poor greatly outnumber the wealthy.
transcript_json.translation: 而在这里，穷人大大超过富人。

transcript_json.text: A visitor will find rich people living in apartments or Spanish houses at the seaside or in the countryside.
transcript_json.translation: 游客会发现，富人住在海边或乡下的公寓或西班牙式宅邸里。

transcript_json.text: Their servants might include a cook, a maid, and a nurse for their children.
transcript_json.translation: 他们的仆人可能包括厨师、女佣和照看孩子的保姆。

transcript_json.text: Most of the people live well below the poverty level.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数人生活在远低于贫困线的水平。

transcript_json.text: In towns, they live crowded together in tiny houses.
transcript_json.translation: 在城镇里，他们拥挤地住在狭小的房子里。

transcript_json.text: Islanders make the best they can of what they have.
transcript_json.translation: 岛上居民尽量把手头的东西物尽其用。

transcript_json.text: Their homes are quite shabby.
transcript_json.translation: 他们的家十分破旧。

transcript_json.text: Sadly, most tourists never see the side of the Caribbean.
transcript_json.translation: 遗憾的是，大多数游客从来看不到加勒比的这一面。

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 2
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 2

transcript_json.text: Talk to anyone who's a generation not too older and they would most likely comment that children are more spoiled these days.
transcript_json.translation: 随便找一个辈分稍高一点的人聊聊，他们多半会说如今的孩子更被宠坏了。

transcript_json.text: No one wants to have or be around demanding, selfish and spoiled children, those who get bad-tempered or silently-brute when they are not given everything they want immediately.
transcript_json.translation: 没有人想养育或身边有索取成性、自私又娇惯的孩子——那种要求不被立刻满足就发脾气或闷声使性子的孩子。

transcript_json.text: Paradoxically, the parents of such children encourage this demanding behavior in the mistaken belief that by giving their children everything they can their children will be happy.
transcript_json.translation: 矛盾的是，这类孩子的父母反而助长了这种索求行为，他们误以为尽力给孩子一切，孩子就会快乐。

transcript_json.text: In the short term, perhaps they are right.
transcript_json.translation: 短期来看，也许他们是对的。

transcript_json.text: But in the longer term, such children end up lonely, dependent, chronically dissatisfied and resentful of the parents who tried so hard to please them.
transcript_json.translation: 但从长远看，这样的孩子最终会孤独、依赖成性、长期不满足，并且怨恨那些极力想讨好他们的父母。

transcript_json.text: Undoubtedly parents want to raise happy children who are confident, capable and likable rather than spoiled and miserable.
transcript_json.translation: 毫无疑问，父母都想培养出自信、能干、讨人喜欢、快乐的孩子，而不是被宠坏又痛苦的孩子。

transcript_json.text: One factor hindering this is that parents can't or don't spend enough quality time with their kids, and substitute this deficit with toys, games, gadgets and the like.
transcript_json.translation: 阻碍这一点的一个因素是，父母没法或没有和孩子共度足够的高质量时光，而是用玩具、游戏、电子产品之类来弥补。

transcript_json.text: Rather than getting material things, children need parents' devoted attention.
transcript_json.translation: 孩子需要的不是物质东西，而是父母全心的关注。

transcript_json.text: The quantity of time spent together is less important than the content of that time.
transcript_json.translation: 共处时间的多少，没有这段时间的内容重要。

transcript_json.text: Instead of instantly satisfying their wishes, parents should help them work out a plan to earn things they'd like to have.
transcript_json.translation: 父母不应立刻满足孩子的愿望，而应帮他们制定一个计划，去挣得自己想要的东西。

transcript_json.text: This teaches them to value the effort as well as what it achieves.
transcript_json.translation: 这教会他们既珍视努力本身，也珍视努力取得的成果。

transcript_json.text: Allow them to enjoy anticipation.
transcript_json.translation: 让他们学会享受期待。

transcript_json.text: Numerous psychological studies have demonstrated that children who learn to wait for things they desire are more likely to succeed in a number of ways later in life.
transcript_json.translation: 大量心理学研究表明，学会等待自己想要的东西的孩子，日后在多个方面更容易成功。

transcript_json.text: One famous experiment in the 1960s involved 3- to 6-year-old children.
transcript_json.translation: 20世纪60年代有一个著名实验，对象是3至6岁的孩子。

transcript_json.text: They were given a choice between receiving a small reward, such as a cookie, immediately, or if they waited 15 minutes, they could have two.
transcript_json.translation: 他们可以选择立刻拿一份小奖励，比如一块饼干，或者等15分钟拿两份。

transcript_json.text: Follow up studies have found that those who chose to delay satisfaction are now more academically successful, have greater selfworth, and even tend to be healthier.
transcript_json.translation: 后续研究发现，选择延迟满足的人如今学业更成功，自尊心更强，甚至往往更健康。

transcript_json.text: If they fail, children should be encouraged to keep trying rather than to give up if they really want the desired result.
transcript_json.translation: 如果失败了，只要孩子真心想要那个结果，就应鼓励他们继续尝试而不是放弃。

transcript_json.text: This teaches them how to handle and recover from disappointment, which is associated with greater success and satisfaction academically, financially and in personal relationships.
transcript_json.translation: 这教会他们如何应对失望并从中恢复，而这与学业、财务和个人关系上更大的成功与满足相关。

transcript_json.text: And lastly, parents should encourage their children to look at life from other points of view, as well as their own.
transcript_json.translation: 最后，父母应鼓励孩子除了从自己的角度看生活，也从别人的角度看生活。

transcript_json.text: This teaches them to be understanding of and sympathetic towards others-qualities sure to take them a long way in life.
transcript_json.translation: 这教会他们体谅他人、富有同情心——这些品质必将在人生路上让他们走得更远。

transcript_json.translation: Q19. 如果孩子总是立刻得到满足，会怎么样？

transcript_json.text: Q20. What may prevent parents from raising confident and capable children?
transcript_json.translation: Q20. 什么可能妨碍父母培养出自信能干的孩子？

transcript_json.text: Q21. Why should children be encouraged to keep trying when they fail?
transcript_json.translation: Q21. 孩子失败时为什么应鼓励他们继续尝试？

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 3
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: It is not hard to mess up an interview.
transcript_json.translation: 搞砸一场面试并不难。

transcript_json.text: Most people feel nervous sitting across from a hiring manager, answering questions that effectively open themselves up for judgment.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数人坐在招聘经理对面，回答那些实际上是让自己接受评判的问题时，都会紧张。

transcript_json.text: And your chances of being more carefully considered for the job can quickly go downhill just by saying the wrong thing at the wrong time.
transcript_json.translation: 只要在错误的时机说了错话，你获得这份工作认真考虑的机会就会急转直下。

transcript_json.text: The most obvious thing not to do is complain.
transcript_json.translation: 最显而易见的禁忌就是抱怨。

transcript_json.text: Employers want to hire positive people.
transcript_json.translation: 雇主想雇用积极向上的人。

transcript_json.text: Talking about a previous job negatively raises concerns that you might be difficult to manage, or you might be someone that blames management for your own poor performance.
transcript_json.translation: 负面评价前一份工作会让人担心你难以管理，或者你会把自己表现差归咎于管理层。

transcript_json.text: Don't say that you've moved around in jobs because you haven't found the right fit or feel that you were not challenged enough.
transcript_json.translation: 不要说你频繁换工作是因为没找到合适的，或觉得自己没受到足够的挑战。

transcript_json.text: Statements like these will make you sound aimless and lost.
transcript_json.translation: 这类话会让你显得没有方向、很迷茫。

transcript_json.text: An interviewer may well think, why would this role be any different for you?
transcript_json.translation: 面试官很可能会想：这个职位对你来说又会有什么不同呢？

transcript_json.text: You will probably leave here in six months.
transcript_json.translation: 你很可能半年后就离开这里了。

transcript_json.text: It also bags the question of what type of relationship you had with your manager.
transcript_json.translation: 这也让人不禁要问：你之前和经理是什么关系。

transcript_json.text: It doesn't sound like you had open communication with him or her.
transcript_json.translation: 听起来你和经理之间似乎没有开诚布公的沟通。

transcript_json.text: Managers usually love people who can self-sustain and enable growth through taking initiative, who are strong at following through their work, and who bring ideas and solutions to the table.
transcript_json.translation: 经理通常喜欢这样的人：能自我驱动、通过主动进取带来成长、做事有始有终，并且能提出想法和解决方案。

transcript_json.text: If you were in a management or leadership position, when discussing your current role, never take all the credit for accomplishments or achievements.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你担任过管理或领导职务，在谈论现任职务时，千万不要把所有成绩和成就的功劳都揽到自己身上。

transcript_json.text: Emphasize your team and how through their talents, your vision was realized.
transcript_json.translation: 要强调你的团队，强调正是凭借他们的才华，你的愿景才得以实现。

transcript_json.text: Most successful leaders know that they are only as good as their team.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数成功的领导人都知道，自己有多好取决于团队有多好。

transcript_json.text: And acknowledging this in an interview will go a long way towards suggesting that you might be the right person for the position you are applying for.
transcript_json.translation: 在面试中承认这一点，会大大有助于表明你可能正是所应聘职位的合适人选。

transcript_json.text: Lastly, have a good idea of what your role will be and try and convey the idea that you're flexible.
transcript_json.translation: 最后，要清楚自己的职责会是什么，同时尽量传达出你很灵活的信息。

transcript_json.text: Asking what your role will be suggests you will limit yourself purely to what is expected of you.
transcript_json.translation: 询问自己的职责是什么，会让人觉得你只愿局限于别人对你的要求。

transcript_json.text: In reality, your role is whatever you make of it.
transcript_json.translation: 实际上，你的角色是由你自己塑造的。

transcript_json.text: This is especially true in small companies, where the ability to adapt and take on new responsibilities is highly valued.
transcript_json.translation: 在小公司尤其如此，适应能力和承担新职责的能力在那里备受重视。

transcript_json.text: And this is equally important if you're just starting out.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你刚刚入行，这一点同样重要。

transcript_json.text: Entry level interviewees would do well to demonstrate a broad set of skills in most interviews.
transcript_json.translation: 初级岗位的面试者在大多数面试中最好展示广泛的技能。

transcript_json.text: It's important to have a wide skill set as many startups and small companies are moving really fast.
transcript_json.translation: 掌握多种技能很重要，因为许多初创公司和小公司发展非常快。

transcript_json.text: Employers are looking for candidates that are intelligent and can quickly adapt and excel in a growing company.
transcript_json.translation: 雇主在寻找聪明、能在成长型公司里快速适应并脱颖而出的候选人。
