transcript_json.text: M: Good morning and welcome to "People in the News".
transcript_json.translation: M: 早上好，欢迎收看《新闻人物》。

transcript_json.text: With me today is Megan Brown, an environmental activist whose controversial new book Beyond Recycling is making headlines.
transcript_json.translation: 今天的嘉宾是梅根·布朗，一位环保活动家，她那本颇具争议的新书《超越回收》正在成为头条新闻。

transcript_json.text: W: Hi Brian, thanks for having me today.
transcript_json.translation: W: 你好，布莱恩，谢谢你今天邀请我来。

transcript_json.text: I'm excited to explain to the audience what my book is really about.
transcript_json.translation: 我很乐意向观众解释一下我的书到底讲了什么。

transcript_json.text: M: Critics of your book assert that you're trying to force radical changes on the entire country.
transcript_json.translation: M: 你这本书的批评者断言，你是在试图把激进的变革强加给整个国家。

transcript_json.text: Some claim that you want to force everyone to eat a vegetarian diet and make private transport illegal.
transcript_json.translation: 有人声称你想强迫所有人吃素，并让私人交通变成违法行为。

transcript_json.text: W: I'm aware of those claims but they simply aren't true.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我知道这些说法，但它们完全不是真的。

transcript_json.text: People who haven't read the book are making assumptions about my arguments.
transcript_json.translation: 那些没读过这本书的人在凭空猜测我的观点。

transcript_json.text: They know I'm a vegetarian, that I don't wear leather or fur and that I always use public transportation, so they're depicting me as a radical animal rights activist and environmentalist, determined to force my beliefs on others.
transcript_json.translation: 他们知道我吃素、不穿皮革和皮草、总是乘坐公共交通，于是把我描绘成一个激进的动物权利活动家和环保主义者，一心要把自己的信念强加给别人。

transcript_json.text: M: But don't you want others to adopt your practices?
transcript_json.translation: M: 但你难道不希望别人也照你的方式生活吗？

transcript_json.text: You've campaigned for animal rights and the environment for decades.
transcript_json.translation: 你为动物权利和环保奔走了几十年。

transcript_json.text: W: I'd love it if people chose to live as I do, but my life choices are based on my personal convictions, they aren't my recommendations for others who don't share those convictions.
transcript_json.translation: W: 如果人们选择像我这样生活，我当然高兴，但我的生活选择是基于我个人的信念，对那些不认同这些信念的人，这并不是我的建议。

transcript_json.text: M: Well, in this excerpt from your book, you argue that meat consumption and private transport are devastating the environment and that the best choices for the planet are vegetarian diets and public transport.
transcript_json.translation: M: 嗯，在你这本书的这段节选里，你提出肉食消费和私人交通正在毁坏环境，对这个星球来说最好的选择是素食和公共交通。

transcript_json.text: W: I did write that, but those are examples of what I call best practices not what I'm actually suggesting.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我确实那样写了，但那些只是我所说的最佳实践的例子，并不是我真正的建议。

transcript_json.text: In my guidelines for saving the environment, I suggest modest changes, like eating vegetarian meals two days a week.
transcript_json.translation: 在我的环保指南中，我建议的是温和的改变，比如每周有两天吃素。

transcript_json.text: M: You also endorse high taxes on meat and other animal products and increase taxes on gasoline.
transcript_json.translation: M: 你还支持对肉类和其他动物产品征收重税，并提高汽油税。

transcript_json.text: Those taxes could force poor people to adopt your life choices.
transcript_json.translation: 这些税收可能会迫使穷人接受你的生活选择。

transcript_json.text: W: But the taxes I suggest aren't that high, less than 3% only.
transcript_json.translation: W: 但我建议的税没那么高，只有不到3%。

transcript_json.text: Plus the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection which benefits everyone.
transcript_json.translation: 而且产生的这笔钱会用于环境保护，这对每个人都有好处。

transcript_json.text: M: With me in the studio today is Miss Jane Logan, author of the new book Secrets to Success.
transcript_json.translation: M: 今天和我一起在演播室的是简·洛根小姐，新书《成功的秘诀》的作者。

transcript_json.text: She claims to have uncovered how people achieve success.
transcript_json.translation: 她声称已经揭示了人们是如何取得成功的。

transcript_json.text: So Miss Logan, in your book you claim that successful people have many things in common.
transcript_json.translation: 那么洛根小姐，你在书中说成功人士有许多共同点。

transcript_json.text: For instance, they know their strengths when pursuing a goal.
transcript_json.translation: 比如，他们在追求目标时清楚自己的优势。

transcript_json.text: W: That's right.
transcript_json.translation: W: 没错。

transcript_json.text: They also tend to be motivated by a negative or positive life event.
transcript_json.translation: 他们往往还会受到生活中某个负面或正面事件的激励。

transcript_json.text: They credit their success to having someone in their life who believes in them.
transcript_json.translation: 他们把成功归功于生命中有人相信他们。

transcript_json.text: M: You also write that there are a number of different factors related to success.
transcript_json.translation: M: 你还写道，与成功相关的因素有很多。

transcript_json.text: And while successful people are driven to achieve their goals, the ultra successful have even greater ambition.
transcript_json.translation: 成功人士有实现目标的驱动力，而超级成功人士的雄心更大。

transcript_json.text: W: Yes, greater ambition as well as a burning desire to be the best of the best is also a common characteristic.
transcript_json.translation: W: 是的，更大的雄心以及成为人中翘楚的强烈渴望，也是一个共同特征。

transcript_json.text: M: Right, so those who are determined don't see obstacles as something that prevents success, but mere inconveniences that need to be overcome.
transcript_json.translation: M: 对，所以那些意志坚定的人不会把障碍看成阻止成功的东西，而只当成需要克服的小小不便。

transcript_json.text: W: Absolutely.
transcript_json.translation: W: 完全正确。

transcript_json.text: Successful people are also optimistic as it is important to stay positive while being aware of obstacles that can deter us from achieving our goals.
transcript_json.translation: 成功人士还很乐观，因为在意识到可能阻碍我们实现目标的障碍的同时，保持积极心态很重要。

transcript_json.text: M: That's a good point.
transcript_json.translation: M: 说得好。

transcript_json.text: All too often people give up at the first hurdle.
transcript_json.translation: 人们常常在第一个坎儿就放弃了。

transcript_json.text: Would you say then that most successful people make it all by themselves?
transcript_json.translation: 那么你认为大多数成功人士都是完全靠自己成功的吗？

transcript_json.text: W: Not exactly.
transcript_json.translation: W: 不完全是。

transcript_json.text: They are usually good at cooperating with people and understanding the needs of others.
transcript_json.translation: 他们通常善于与人合作，也善于理解别人的需求。

transcript_json.text: M: So people will be willing to help them, I guess.
transcript_json.translation: M: 所以我猜人们会愿意帮助他们。

transcript_json.text: W: That's correct and this often leads to a great deal of mutual respect whether it's with a colleague, an assistant or even a receptionist.
transcript_json.translation: W: 正是如此，而且这往往会带来大量的相互尊重，无论对方是同事、助理，甚至是一位前台接待。

transcript_json.text: M: Most successful people I know are very passionate about their work.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我认识的大多数成功人士都对工作充满热情。

transcript_json.text: Would you say that passion is the single biggest key to success?
transcript_json.translation: 你会说热情是成功最大的唯一关键吗？

transcript_json.text: W: Not entirely.
transcript_json.translation: W: 不完全是。

transcript_json.text: There's a prerequisite that is you have to work in an environment that nurtures passion.
transcript_json.translation: 有一个前提条件，那就是你必须在能滋养热情的环境中工作。

transcript_json.text: If that exists, success will follow.
transcript_json.translation: 如果具备了这一点，成功就会随之而来。

transcript_json.translation: 问题5至8基于你刚刚听到的对话。

transcript_json.text: That saying "blind as a bat" simply isn't correct.
transcript_json.translation: "瞎得像蝙蝠"这句俗话根本不对。

transcript_json.text: The truth is that all 1,100 bat species can see and often their vision is pretty good, although not as excellent as other night hunting animals.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，全部1100种蝙蝠都能看见东西，而且它们的视力往往相当好，只是不如其他夜间捕猎的动物出色。

transcript_json.text: There are two main groups of bats which are believed to have evolved independently of each other but both from a common ancestor.
transcript_json.translation: 蝙蝠有两大类群，据认为它们是彼此独立进化而来的，但都源自同一个共同祖先。

transcript_json.text: The first group known as mega bats are mostly medium sized or large bats who eat fruits, flowers and sometimes small animals or fish.
transcript_json.translation: 第一类被称为大蝙蝠，多为中型或大型蝙蝠，吃水果、花朵，有时也吃小动物或鱼。

transcript_json.text: These species have distinctive visual centers and big eyes.
transcript_json.translation: 这些物种有发达的视觉中枢和大眼睛。

transcript_json.text: They use senses of vision and smell to capture their prey.
transcript_json.translation: 它们靠视觉和嗅觉来捕捉猎物。

transcript_json.text: For example, flying foxes not only see well during daylight but can also distinguish colors.
transcript_json.translation: 例如，狐蝠不仅白天视力很好，还能分辨颜色。

transcript_json.text: They actually rely on their daylight vision and cannot fly during the night with no moonlight.
transcript_json.translation: 它们实际上依赖白天的视力，在没有月光的夜里无法飞行。

transcript_json.text: The second group called micro bats are smaller in size and mostly eat insects.
transcript_json.translation: 第二类叫小蝙蝠，体型更小，主要吃昆虫。

transcript_json.text: These species use echolocation to find their way and identify food.
transcript_json.translation: 这些物种用回声定位来认路和辨别食物。

transcript_json.text: Scientists have proven that despite their poorly developed small eyes, these bats still can see during the day.
transcript_json.translation: 科学家已经证明，尽管这些蝙蝠的小眼睛发育不良，它们白天仍然看得见。

transcript_json.text: When we consider the nightly lifestyle of these bats, we will see they have to be sensitive to the changing light levels.
transcript_json.translation: 想一想这些蝙蝠的夜间生活方式就会发现，它们必须对光线水平的变化保持敏感。

transcript_json.text: Because this is how they sense when to start hunting.
transcript_json.translation: 因为它们正是以此来感知何时开始捕猎。

transcript_json.text: Moreover, vision is used by micro bats to travel over long distances beyond the range of echolocation, so the truth is there are no bats which are naturally blind.
transcript_json.translation: 此外，小蝙蝠会利用视力在超出回声定位范围的长距离上飞行，所以事实是，天生失明的蝙蝠是不存在的。

transcript_json.text: Some species use their sense of hearing more than their eyes as a matter of adaptation to a particular lifestyle, but their eyes are still functional.
transcript_json.translation: 有些物种更多用听觉而不是眼睛，这是对特定生活方式的一种适应，但它们的眼睛仍然有用。

transcript_json.text: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
transcript_json.translation: 问题9至11基于你刚刚听到的短文。

transcript_json.text: Q9. What do we learn about mega bats?

transcript_json.text: Q10. How do micro bats find their way and identify food?

transcript_json.text: A study has found that educational TV shows come with an added lesson that influences the child's behavior.
transcript_json.translation: 一项研究发现，教育类电视节目还附带着另一堂课，会影响孩子的行为。

transcript_json.text: Children spending more time watching educational programs increase their emotional aggression toward other children.
transcript_json.translation: 花更多时间看教育节目的孩子，会增加对其他孩子的情绪攻击性。

transcript_json.text: This shows that children can learn the educational lesson that was intended.
transcript_json.translation: 这表明孩子们能够学到节目想要传达的教育内容。

transcript_json.text: However, they're also learning other things along the way.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，他们在这个过程中也学到了别的东西。

transcript_json.text: This unintended impact has to do with the portrayal of conflict in media and how preschool age children comprehend that conflict.
transcript_json.translation: 这种意外的影响与媒体对冲突的呈现方式，以及学龄前儿童如何理解这种冲突有关。

transcript_json.text: TV and movie producers often incorporate an element of bad behavior.
transcript_json.translation: 电视和电影制作人常常加入一些不良行为的元素。

transcript_json.text: This is to teach children a lesson at the end of the program.
transcript_json.translation: 这是为了在节目结尾给孩子们一个教训。

transcript_json.text: Educational shows have pro-education and pro-social goals.
transcript_json.translation: 教育类节目有着促进教育和亲社会的目标。

transcript_json.text: However, conflict between characters is often depicted with characters being unkind to each other.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，角色之间的冲突常常表现为角色彼此不友善。

transcript_json.text: Or they may use emotionally aggressive tactics with each other.
transcript_json.translation: 或者他们可能对彼此使用情绪攻击的手段。

transcript_json.text: Preschool children really don't get the moral of the story.
transcript_json.translation: 学龄前儿童真的领会不了故事的寓意。

transcript_json.text: That's because it requires that they understand how all the parts of the show fit together.
transcript_json.translation: 因为这需要他们理解节目的各个部分是如何组合在一起的。

transcript_json.text: You need pretty complicated cognitive skills and memory skills to be able to do that.
transcript_json.translation: 要做到这一点，需要相当复杂的认知能力和记忆能力。

transcript_json.text: These are still developing in young children.
transcript_json.translation: 而这些能力在小孩子身上还在发展之中。

transcript_json.text: However, parents shouldn't completely constrain children's viewing.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，父母不应完全限制孩子看电视。

transcript_json.text: Parents should instead watch with their kids and help them to understand the plot.
transcript_json.translation: 父母反而应该陪孩子一起看，帮他们理解情节。

transcript_json.text: Parents can comment along the way and then explain the message at the end.
transcript_json.translation: 父母可以在观看过程中随时点评，最后再解释节目传达的信息。

transcript_json.text: They should explain how certain types of behavior were not appropriate.
transcript_json.translation: 他们应该解释某些行为为什么是不恰当的。

transcript_json.text: This will help children interpret and get the message and help them learn to watch the show for those messages.
transcript_json.translation: 这会帮助孩子理解并领会这些信息，也帮他们学会带着领会信息的目的去看节目。

transcript_json.text: While it has long been a practice in Asian countries, many people in Western countries have yet to embrace the no shoes in the house rule.
transcript_json.translation: 在亚洲国家，进屋脱鞋早已是习惯，但西方国家还有很多人没有接受进屋不穿鞋的规矩。

transcript_json.text: For many in those countries, wiping their shoes before going inside is regarded as sufficient.
transcript_json.translation: 在那些国家，很多人认为进门前蹭一蹭鞋就够了。

transcript_json.text: After all, they may think a little dirt doesn't hurt anyone, but I can give you several good reasons why people should remove their shoes before going inside their homes.
transcript_json.translation: 毕竟，他们可能觉得有点脏也碍不了谁，但我可以给你几个好理由，说明人们进家门之前为什么应该脱鞋。

transcript_json.text: Bacteria are everywhere.
transcript_json.translation: 细菌无处不在。

transcript_json.text: They collect on your shoes when you walk along sidewalks, public toilet floors and even office carpets.
transcript_json.translation: 当你走过人行道、公共厕所的地面甚至办公室的地毯时，细菌就会附着在你的鞋上。

transcript_json.text: In one study conducted at an American university, researchers collected microscopic germs from footwear.
transcript_json.translation: 在美国一所大学进行的一项研究中，研究人员从鞋子上采集了肉眼看不见的细菌。

transcript_json.text: They found that up to 421,000 units of bacteria can collect on the outside of a single shoe.
transcript_json.translation: 他们发现，一只鞋的外部能附着多达42.1万个单位的细菌。

transcript_json.text: And it only takes a little bit of dirt to damage your timber floors.
transcript_json.translation: 而且只要一点点灰尘就会损伤你的木地板。

transcript_json.text: The more dirt you track in, the more it scratches and the more often you have to clean.
transcript_json.translation: 你带进屋的灰尘越多，刮伤就越多，需要打扫的次数也越频繁。

transcript_json.text: The extra scrubbing will harm your floors over time.
transcript_json.translation: 额外的擦洗时间久了会伤地板。

transcript_json.text: Shoes can also leave marks and scratches on floors, especially high heels or shoes with pointy or hard parts.
transcript_json.translation: 鞋子也会在地板上留下印痕和划痕，尤其是高跟鞋或带尖硬部件的鞋。

transcript_json.text: These can dent and scratch your floor.
transcript_json.translation: 这些鞋会压凹和刮伤地板。

transcript_json.text: And if you live in an apartment building, removing your noisy shoes is the polite thing to do out of consideration for your downstairs neighbors.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你住在公寓楼里，脱掉那双吵人的鞋是礼貌的做法，这也是为楼下的邻居着想。

transcript_json.text: Walking around with bare feet is actually better for your feet.
transcript_json.translation: 光着脚走动其实对脚更好。

transcript_json.text: It strengthens the muscles in your feet though many people are accustomed to wearing shoes during all their waking hours.
transcript_json.translation: 它能锻炼你脚部的肌肉，尽管很多人习惯在醒着的所有时间都穿着鞋。

transcript_json.text: The more time you spend wearing shoes, the more likely you are to incur foot injuries as a result.
transcript_json.translation: 你穿鞋的时间越长，越可能因此造成脚部损伤。

transcript_json.text: And if people aren't yet convinced by my arguments, I can give one final reason.
transcript_json.translation: 如果这些论据还没能说服大家，我还可以给出最后一个理由。

transcript_json.text: The dust and toxic chemicals you bring into your house via your shoes can deteriorate the air quality in your home.
transcript_json.translation: 你用鞋子带进家里的灰尘和有毒化学物质，会使家里的空气质量变差。

transcript_json.text: Toxic chemicals are everywhere in our lives: insect killing chemicals used on public grass areas, cleaning chemicals on the floors of public areas.
transcript_json.translation: 有毒化学物质在我们的生活中无处不在：公共草坪上喷洒的杀虫剂，公共场所地面上的清洁剂。

transcript_json.text: By kicking off your shoes before you enter the home, you are denying entry to these harmful chemicals.
transcript_json.translation: 进家前脱掉鞋子，就是把这些有害化学物质拒之门外。

transcript_json.text: Given the amount of time we spend in classrooms and the number of shoes that pass through them every day, you may well understand me if I were to propose a no shoes in the classroom rule.
transcript_json.translation: 考虑到我们在教室里度过的时间，以及每天有多少双鞋进出教室，如果我提议在教室里也实行不穿鞋的规定，你们很可能会理解我。

transcript_json.text: Emotions are an essential and inseparable part of our consciousness.
transcript_json.translation: 情绪是我们意识中不可缺少、不可分割的一部分。

transcript_json.text: They are part of a built-in mechanism which allows us to cope with the ups and downs of our lives both physically and mentally.
transcript_json.translation: 它们是一种内置机制的组成部分，让我们能够在身心两方面应对人生的起起落落。

transcript_json.text: When we hide our emotions and our true feelings, we stop being genuine, spontaneous and authentic in our relationships.
transcript_json.translation: 当我们隐藏自己的情绪和真实感受时，我们在人际关系中就不再真诚、自然、真实。

transcript_json.text: When we put on cultivated and polished faces in the company of others, we stop being true to ourselves.
transcript_json.translation: 当我们在别人面前摆出端庄得体的面孔时，我们就不再忠于自己。

transcript_json.text: Socially, it may be a good tactic to hide our true emotions but morally it is also a breach of faith and trust.
transcript_json.translation: 从社交角度看，隐藏真实情绪也许是好策略，但从道德上看，这也是对诚信和信任的违背。

transcript_json.text: Although humans are more advanced and intelligent, animals are more genuine and authentic in their behavior and responses than human beings.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然人类更高级、更聪明，但动物在行为和反应上比人类更真实、更本色。

transcript_json.text: The more educated we are, the less transparent and reliable we become.
transcript_json.translation: 我们受的教育越多，就变得越不透明、越不可靠。

transcript_json.text: We are drawn to our pets because pets do not lie.
transcript_json.translation: 我们被宠物吸引，是因为宠物不说谎。

transcript_json.text: One of the first steps in dealing with emotions such as anger or fear is to acknowledge them as normal and human.
transcript_json.translation: 处理愤怒或恐惧等情绪的第一步，就是承认它们是正常的、人之常情的。

transcript_json.text: There is nothing sinful or immoral about being emotional unless your emotions make you inhuman, insensitive and cruel to others.
transcript_json.translation: 情绪化并没有什么罪恶或不道德的，除非你的情绪让你丧失人性、冷漠麻木、对他人残酷。

transcript_json.text: Feelings of guilt associated with emotions are more devastating and damaging than the experience of emotion itself.
transcript_json.translation: 与情绪相伴的负罪感，比情绪体验本身更具毁灭性和伤害性。

transcript_json.text: So when you deal with the problem of emotions, you should learn not only how to control them but also how to accept them and manage the guilt and anguish arising from them.
transcript_json.translation: 所以当你处理情绪问题时，不仅要学会如何控制它们，还要学会如何接受它们，并处理好由它们产生的负罪感和痛苦。

transcript_json.text: Our brains are made up of a primitive inner core and a more evolved and rational outer core.
transcript_json.translation: 我们的大脑由一个原始的内核和一个更进化、更理性的外核组成。

transcript_json.text: Most of the time, the rational part of the mind controls the information coming from the primitive core and makes its own decisions as to what to do and how to respond.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数时候，大脑中理性的部分控制着来自原始内核的信息，并自行决定做什么、如何回应。

transcript_json.text: However, during critical situations, especially when a threat is perceived, the outer core loses control and fails to regulate the impulses and instinctive responses coming from the primitive brain.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，在危急情况下，尤其是察觉到威胁时，外核会失去控制，无法调节来自原始大脑的冲动和本能反应。

transcript_json.text: As a result, we let disturbing thoughts and emotions arise in our consciousness and surrender to our primitive behavior.
transcript_json.translation: 结果，我们任由烦乱的念头和情绪在意识中升起，屈从于原始的行为。

transcript_json.text: In times of emotional turmoil, remember that emotions arise because your sensors are wired to the primitive part of your mind which is self-regulated, autonomous and spontaneous.
transcript_json.translation: 在情绪纷乱的时候，记住：情绪之所以出现，是因为你的感知器连接着大脑中自我调节、自主而自发的那一部分。

transcript_json.text: Your rational mind does not always deal with the messages coming from it effectively.
transcript_json.translation: 你的理性思维并不总能有效处理来自它的信息。

transcript_json.text: These messages are part of your survival mechanism and should not be stifled simply because emotions are unhealthy and betray your weaknesses.
transcript_json.translation: 这些信息是你生存机制的一部分，不应仅仅因为情绪显得不健康、暴露了你的弱点就被扼杀。

transcript_json.text: When emotions arise, instead of stifling them, pay attention to them and try to understand the messages they are trying to deliver.
transcript_json.translation: 当情绪升起时，不要压制它们，而要关注它们，并试着理解它们想要传递的信息。

transcript_json.text: This way you make use of your emotions without losing your balance and inner stability.
transcript_json.translation: 这样你就能利用自己的情绪，同时不失平衡和内心的稳定。

transcript_json.text: Good morning, class.
transcript_json.translation: 同学们，早上好。

transcript_json.text: My topic today is how to feed a hungry world.
transcript_json.translation: 我今天的主题是如何喂饱这个饥饿的世界。

transcript_json.text: The world's population is expected to grow from 6.8 billion today to 9.1 billion by 2050.
transcript_json.translation: 预计世界人口将从今天的68亿增长到2050年的91亿。

transcript_json.text: Meanwhile, the world's population more than doubled from 3 billion between 1961 and 2007.
transcript_json.translation: 与此同时，1961年至2007年间，世界人口从30亿增加了一倍多。

transcript_json.text: Simultaneously, food production has been constrained by a lack of scientific research.
transcript_json.translation: 与此同时，粮食生产一直受到科学研究不足的制约。

transcript_json.text: Still, the task of feeding the world's population in 2050 seems "easily possible".
transcript_json.translation: 尽管如此，养活2050年世界人口的任务看起来还是"完全可行的"。

transcript_json.text: What is needed is a second green revolution.
transcript_json.translation: 我们需要的是第二次绿色革命。

transcript_json.text: This is an approach that is described as the sustainable growth of global agriculture.
transcript_json.translation: 这被称为全球农业可持续增长的一种路径。

transcript_json.text: Such a revolution will require a wholesale shift of priorities in agricultural research.
transcript_json.translation: 这样一场革命将需要农业研究重点的全面转移。

transcript_json.text: There is an urgent need for new crop varieties.
transcript_json.translation: 对新的作物品种有着迫切需求。

transcript_json.text: They must offer higher yields, but use less water, nitrogen-rich fertilizers or other inputs.
transcript_json.translation: 这些品种必须产量更高，但用水更少，所需的高氮化肥或其他投入也更少。

transcript_json.text: These new crops must also be more resistant to drought, heat and pests.
transcript_json.translation: 这些新作物还必须更能抗旱、抗热、抗虫害。

transcript_json.text: Equally crucial is lower-tech research into basics such as crop rotation and mixed farming of animals and plants on small farms.
transcript_json.translation: 同样关键的是对基础项目的低技术研究，比如小农场的轮作和动植物混养。

transcript_json.text: Developing nations could score substantial gains in productivity by making better use of modern technologies and practices.
transcript_json.translation: 发展中国家可以通过更好地利用现代技术和做法，在生产力上取得可观收获。

transcript_json.text: But that requires money.
transcript_json.translation: 但这需要钱。

transcript_json.text: It is estimated that to meet the 2050 challenge, investment must double to $83 billion US dollars a year.
transcript_json.translation: 据估计，要应对2050年的挑战，投资必须翻倍，达到每年830亿美元。

transcript_json.text: Most of that money needs to go towards improving agricultural infrastructure.
transcript_json.translation: 这些钱的大部分需要用于改善农业基础设施。

transcript_json.text: Everything from production to storage and processing must improve.
transcript_json.translation: 从生产到储存和加工的每一个环节都必须改进。

transcript_json.text: However, research agendas need to be focused on the needs of the poorest and most resource-limited countries.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，研究议程需要聚焦在最贫穷、资源最有限的国家的需求上。

transcript_json.text: It is there that most of the world's population lives, and it is there that population growth over the next decades will be the greatest.
transcript_json.translation: 世界上大部分人口生活在那里，未来几十年人口增长最多的也将是那里。

transcript_json.text: To their credit, the world's agricultural scientists are embracing such a broad view.
transcript_json.translation: 值得称赞的是，全世界的农业科学家正在接受这样一种宽广的视野。

transcript_json.text: In March, for example, they came together at the first Global Conference on Agricultural Research to begin working out how to change research agendas to help meet the needs of farmers in poorer nations.
transcript_json.translation: 例如，今年3月，他们齐聚首届全球农业研究大会，开始研究如何调整研究议程，以帮助满足较贫困国家农民的需求。

transcript_json.text: But these plans will not bear fruit unless they get considerably more support from policy-makers.
transcript_json.translation: 但除非能得到决策者多得多的支持，否则这些计划不会结出果实。

transcript_json.text: The growth in public agricultural-research spending peaked in the 1970s and has been shrinking ever since.
transcript_json.translation: 公共农业研究支出的增长在20世纪70年代达到顶峰，此后一直在萎缩。

transcript_json.text: The big exception is China, where spending has far surpassed other countries over the past decade.
transcript_json.translation: 最大的例外是中国，过去十年中国的支出远超其他国家。

transcript_json.text: China seems set to transition to become the key supplier of relevant science and technology to poorer countries.
transcript_json.translation: 中国似乎注定要转型成为向较贫困国家提供相关科技的主要供应方。

transcript_json.text: But developed countries have a humanitarian responsibility, too.
transcript_json.translation: 但发达国家也负有人道主义责任。

transcript_json.text: Calls by scientists for large increases in the appropriation of funds for public spending on agricultural research are more than justified.
transcript_json.translation: 科学家呼吁大幅增加农业研究公共支出的拨款，这是完全正当的。

transcript_json.text: CONVERSATION 1
transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 1

transcript_json.text: W: Mr. David Jackson, a staff writer at the New Yorker, is known for his non-fiction books of adventure.
transcript_json.translation: W: 大卫·杰克逊先生是《纽约客》的撰稿人，以非虚构冒险类书籍闻名。

transcript_json.text: Today, we go on a different kind of adventure: Jackson's life of parenting his offspring.
transcript_json.translation: 今天，我们要经历另一种冒险：杰克逊养育儿女的生活。

transcript_json.text: David, as a parent of an 11-and a 14-year-old, what is the most interesting issue you are dealing with right now?
transcript_json.translation: 大卫，作为一个11岁和一个14岁孩子的家长，你现在正在处理的最有趣的问题是什么？

transcript_json.text: M: It's easy to focus on the challenges, but so far,I find these ages to be kind of wonderful.
transcript_json.translation: M: 人们容易只盯着挑战，但到目前为止，我觉得这两个年龄段相当美好。

transcript_json.text: They are independent, and they have their own curiosities and obsessions.
transcript_json.translation: 他们很独立，有自己的好奇心和痴迷的东西。

transcript_json.text: You can talk to them about fairly sophisticated subject matter such as politics.
transcript_json.translation: 你可以和他们谈论相当深入的话题，比如政治。

transcript_json.text: W: Yes, that does sound refreshing compared with talking to younger children.
transcript_json.translation: W: 是啊，和跟小孩子说话相比，这听起来确实让人耳目一新。

transcript_json.text: Do they ask you to proofread their essays?
transcript_json.translation: 他们会请你帮他们校对作文吗？

transcript_json.text: M: Certainly, with writing they do.
transcript_json.translation: M: 当然，写作方面会。

transcript_json.text: I really just try to be encouraging.
transcript_json.translation: 我真的只是尽量多鼓励。

transcript_json.text: I think at this age, editorial guidance is less important than encouragement.
transcript_json.translation: 我觉得在这个年纪，修改指导远不如鼓励重要。

transcript_json.text: W: Are there books that you think are important that your children read, and that all children read?
transcript_json.translation: W: 有没有你觉得自己的孩子、以及所有孩子都应该读的重要书籍？

transcript_json.text: M: My general thought is to read widely and to incorporate a love for reading.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我的总体想法是广泛阅读，并培养对阅读的热爱。

transcript_json.text: Learning to love to read, I think, is the optimal thing, because it gives you a skill you can take anywhere.
transcript_json.translation: 我觉得，学会爱上阅读是最理想的事，因为它给你一种走到哪里都带得走的能力。

transcript_json.text: W: So you're not too concerned like some parents with the content they're reading?
transcript_json.translation: W: 所以你不像有些家长那样，太在意他们读的内容？

transcript_json.text: I know I have some worries about that.
transcript_json.translation: 我知道我自己对此就有些担心。

transcript_json.text: M: Yeah, read what you like.
transcript_json.translation: M: 嗯，喜欢读什么就读什么。

transcript_json.text: If a child loves graphic novels or comic books, whatever it is, that is turning them on to read and turning on their imagination.
transcript_json.translation: 如果一个孩子喜欢图像小说或漫画书，不管是什么，只要能让他们爱上阅读、激发他们的想象力就行。

transcript_json.text: W: I feel that children's tastes in books change as they reach adolescence.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我觉得孩子到了青春期，对书的口味会发生变化。

transcript_json.text: I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager. What do you think?
transcript_json.translation: 我知道我十几岁的时候肯定是这样。你怎么看？

transcript_json.text: M: I think it's especially important as they get older to read subject matter that'll open their eyes to the world and people.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我认为随着年龄增长，尤其要读那些能让他们睁开眼睛看世界、看人心的内容。

transcript_json.text: So I think both fiction and non-fiction are really important because they give you the power to begin to perceive the world through the lives of others.
transcript_json.translation: 所以我认为虚构和非虚构作品都很重要，因为它们给你一种能力，让你开始透过别人的人生来认识世界。

transcript_json.text: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
transcript_json.translation: 问题1至4基于你刚刚听到的对话。

transcript_json.translation: Q1. 从对话中我们了解到关于大卫·杰克逊的什么情况？

transcript_json.text: Q2. What does the man think of young teenagers?
transcript_json.translation: Q2. 男士怎么看十几岁的少年？

transcript_json.translation: Q3. 男士是怎么帮助孩子修改作文的？

transcript_json.text: CONVERSATION 2
transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 2

transcript_json.text: M: In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders,a university student and a successful young entrepreneur.
transcript_json.translation: M: 在本期《金钱漫谈》节目中，我们的嘉宾是莫莉·桑德斯，一位大学生，也是一位成功的年轻创业者。

transcript_json.text: Molly, tell us about your business.
transcript_json.translation: 莫莉，跟我们讲讲你的生意吧。

transcript_json.text: W: Well, I sell specialty clothes through a website, mainly for women who have trouble finding suitable clothes in main street shops because of their height or weight.
transcript_json.translation: W: 嗯，我通过一个网站销售特体服装，主要是面向那些因为身高或体重而很难在商业街普通店铺里找到合适衣服的女性。

transcript_json.text: But I do some men's clothes too.
transcript_json.translation: 不过我也卖一些男装。

transcript_json.text: M: How did you get started in this business at such a young age?
transcript_json.translation: M: 你这么年轻是怎么入这一行的？

transcript_json.text: Are you studying fashion design?
transcript_json.translation: 你学的是服装设计吗？

transcript_json.text: W: Actually, I'm majoring in finance, but I've always loved clothes.
transcript_json.translation: W: 其实我学的是金融，但我一直喜欢服装。

transcript_json.text: And I started making my own at 14.
transcript_json.translation: 我14岁就开始自己做衣服了。

transcript_json.text: M: Did you have any sort of training in design or sewing?
transcript_json.translation: M: 你受过设计或缝纫方面的训练吗？

transcript_json.text: Or was it a natural ability?
transcript_json.translation: 还是天生的本事？

transcript_json.text: W: I'd have to say no to both.
transcript_json.translation: W: 两个都得说没有。

transcript_json.text: No one taught me to make clothes and most of the things I made at first were disasters.
transcript_json.translation: 没有人教我做衣服，我最开始做的衣服大多一塌糊涂。

transcript_json.text: M: Why did you persevere?
transcript_json.translation: M: 你为什么能坚持下去？

transcript_json.text: I think most people would give up if they kept failing, especially at that age.
transcript_json.translation: 我觉得要是不断失败，大多数人都会放弃，尤其是在那个年纪。

transcript_json.text: W: I kept on out of necessity.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我是因为现实需要才坚持下来的。

transcript_json.text: As you can see, I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops.
transcript_json.translation: 如你所见，我个子很高，在普通商店里根本找不到合身的衣服。

transcript_json.text: So I kept trying and developed my skills over time.
transcript_json.translation: 所以我不断尝试，慢慢地练出了手艺。

transcript_json.text: M: Well, my notes say you earned $50,000 in profits last year, an extraordinary amount for a 20-year-old student.
transcript_json.translation: M: 嗯，我的记录显示你去年盈利5万美元，对一个20岁的学生来说，这是个惊人的数字。

transcript_json.text: How did that happen?
transcript_json.translation: 这是怎么做到的？

transcript_json.text: Did you see a gap in the market and decide to fill it?
transcript_json.translation: 是你发现了市场空白并决定填补它吗？

transcript_json.text: W: No.
transcript_json.translation: W: 不是。

transcript_json.text: When I started university, some classmates complimented my clothes.
transcript_json.translation: 我刚上大学时，一些同学称赞我的衣服。

transcript_json.text: And when I said I made them myself, other tall women started asking if I would make theirs.
transcript_json.translation: 当我说这是我自己做的，其他高个子女生就开始问我能不能帮她们做。

transcript_json.text: And I did.
transcript_json.translation: 我就做了。

transcript_json.text: And before I knew it, I was an entrepreneur.
transcript_json.translation: 不知不觉，我就成了创业者。

transcript_json.text: M: So what are your plans for the future?
transcript_json.translation: M: 那你未来的计划是什么？

transcript_json.text: Do you intend to open a physical store?
transcript_json.translation: 你打算开实体店吗？

transcript_json.text: W: No.
transcript_json.translation: W: 不是。

transcript_json.text: I'll keep things online to keep costs down.
transcript_json.translation: 我会继续只做线上，以控制成本。

transcript_json.text: But I will add more clothes for children, both girls and boys, and possibly even for infants.
transcript_json.translation: 但我会增加更多儿童服装，女孩和男孩的都有，甚至可能加婴儿服装。

transcript_json.text: And I hope to add to my range of designs for men.
transcript_json.translation: 我还希望扩充我的男装设计系列。

transcript_json.text: PASSAGE 1
transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 1

transcript_json.text: Researchers have identified a potent new antibiotic compound using artificial intelligence.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员利用人工智能发现了一种强效的新型抗生素化合物。

transcript_json.text: The antibiotic can kill very dangerous bacteria.
transcript_json.translation: 这种抗生素能杀死非常危险的细菌。

transcript_json.text: According to a study published in the journal Cell, the compound successfully removed deadly strains of bacteria in mice which are resistant to all known antibiotics.
transcript_json.translation: 根据发表在《细胞》杂志上的一项研究，这种化合物成功清除了小鼠体内对所有已知抗生素都具有耐药性的致命菌株。

transcript_json.text: The researchers say this is the first time that artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员说，这是首次利用人工智能找到强效的新型抗生素分子。

transcript_json.text: Why does this matter?
transcript_json.translation: 这为什么重要呢？

transcript_json.text: The answer is antibiotic resistance.
transcript_json.translation: 答案在于抗生素耐药性。

transcript_json.text: This happens when bacteria develop the ability to survive the medications designed to kill them.
transcript_json.translation: 当细菌发展出在原本要杀死它们的药物中存活下来的能力时，就会出现这种情况。

transcript_json.text: Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat to health and the problem is growing.
transcript_json.translation: 抗生素耐药性是对健康的严重威胁，而且这个问题还在加剧。

transcript_json.text: This makes finding new antibiotics very important.
transcript_json.translation: 这使得寻找新的抗生素非常重要。

transcript_json.text: However, in recent decades, very few have been developed, and those that have tend to be very similar to drugs already available.
transcript_json.translation: 然而近几十年来，新开发的抗生素寥寥无几，而开发出来的那些也往往与现有药物非常相似。

transcript_json.text: The searches also tend to only focus on a narrow spectrum of chemical compounds, but this is where artificial intelligence comes in.
transcript_json.translation: 而且搜索往往只聚焦于一小部分化合物，而这正是人工智能的用武之地。

transcript_json.text: Why?
transcript_json.translation: 为什么呢？

transcript_json.text: To find new drugs, scientists screen molecules to predict how effective they might be.
transcript_json.translation: 为了找到新药，科学家会筛选分子，预测它们可能有多好的效果。

transcript_json.text: Typically, such screening is done by humans in the lab, which is both costly and slow.
transcript_json.translation: 通常，这种筛选由人在实验室完成，既昂贵又缓慢。

transcript_json.text: Artificial intelligence is different.
transcript_json.translation: 人工智能则不同。

transcript_json.text: It's fast, and it can process a high volume.
transcript_json.translation: 它速度快，而且能处理海量数据。

transcript_json.text: It can screen hundreds of millions of compounds to identify a few interesting candidates that require experimental testing.
transcript_json.translation: 它能筛选数亿个化合物，找出少数几个值得进行实验测试的有潜力的候选者。

transcript_json.text: Artificial intelligence is also able to predict if compounds are likely to be toxic.
transcript_json.translation: 人工智能还能预测化合物是否可能有毒性。

transcript_json.text: Some experts assert that this work signifies a paradigm shift in antibiotic discovery.
transcript_json.translation: 一些专家断言，这项工作标志着抗生素发现领域的范式转变。

transcript_json.text: It could change drug discovery more generally.
transcript_json.translation: 它还可能在更广泛的意义上改变药物研发。

transcript_json.translation: 问题9至11基于你刚刚听到的短文。

transcript_json.text: Q9. What have researchers done for the first time in history?
transcript_json.translation: Q9. 研究人员历史上首次做成了什么事？

transcript_json.text: Q10. What makes it important to find new antibiotic drugs?
transcript_json.translation: Q10. 什么使得寻找新的抗生素药物变得重要？

transcript_json.text: Q11. What does the passage say artificial intelligence is able to do in antibiotic research?
transcript_json.translation: Q11. 短文说人工智能在抗生素研究中能做什么？

transcript_json.text: PASSAGE 2
transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 2

transcript_json.text: A recent study overturned what we think we know about lying.
transcript_json.translation: 最近的一项研究颠覆了我们自以为了解的说谎认知。

transcript_json.text: Most of us have a theory about how to tell if someone is telling a lie.
transcript_json.translation: 我们大多数人都有自己的一套判断别人是否说谎的理论。

transcript_json.text: We may develop that theory from observations of those people we know well and see regularly, but we tend to generalize what we gather from that unscientific daily research and make it a universal theory.
transcript_json.translation: 这套理论可能来自我们对熟人和常打交道的人的观察，但我们往往把从这种不科学的日常观察中收集到的东西加以推广，变成一个放之四海而皆准的理论。

transcript_json.text: So we might imagine that liars have evasive eyes, or the opposite-they simply stare at you.
transcript_json.translation: 所以我们可能会想，说谎的人眼神躲闪，或者恰恰相反——他们会直勾勾地盯着你。

transcript_json.text: Or perhaps it is more generally nervous behavior we associate with lies.
transcript_json.translation: 或者，我们更容易把说谎与总体上的紧张行为联系起来。

transcript_json.text: Whatever the particular theory, it's usually based on close observation of people we know.
transcript_json.translation: 无论具体是哪一种理论，它通常都建立在对熟人的细致观察之上。

transcript_json.text: And we get lots of practice.
transcript_json.translation: 而且我们有很多练习机会。

transcript_json.text: On average, we're lied to some 200 times per day.
transcript_json.translation: 平均下来，我们每天被骗大约200次。

transcript_json.text: These are mostly harmless lies, but lies nonetheless.
transcript_json.translation: 这些大多是无伤大雅的谎，但毕竟也是谎。

transcript_json.text: But there's a problem with our theories, even though they're based on all these observations.
transcript_json.translation: 但尽管我们的理论基于这么多观察，它们还是有个问题。

transcript_json.text: The average person you and me tested rigorously on how well we detect lies fails to do better than chance.
transcript_json.translation: 普通人——你和我——经过严格测试后发现，识别谎言的水平并不比瞎猜强。

transcript_json.text: That's well established over many studies and lots of attempts by researchers to work out reliable ways to detect lies.
transcript_json.translation: 这一点已经经过大量研究以及研究人员找出可靠测谎方法的许多尝试所证实。

transcript_json.text: It's even relatively easy to fool lie detectors, the gold standard of lie detection, by training yourself in breathing techniques and symptom suppression.
transcript_json.translation: 甚至连测谎仪这个测谎的黄金标准，也相对容易骗过——只要训练自己控制呼吸和抑制症状就行。

transcript_json.text: Is there any way to get better at detecting lies?
transcript_json.translation: 有没有办法提高识谎能力呢？

transcript_json.text: The new research offers some surprising advice.
transcript_json.translation: 这项新研究给出了一些出人意料的建议。

transcript_json.text: Stop looking and listen instead.
transcript_json.translation: 别再盯着看，改用耳朵听。

transcript_json.text: It turns out that if we're unable to see the face, but rather focus on the voice of the person in question, our accuracy rate improves considerably.
transcript_json.translation: 事实证明，如果我们看不到对方的面孔，而是专注于当事人的声音，我们的准确率会显著提高。

transcript_json.translation: Q13. 关于大多数谎言，短文说了什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q14. 关于普通人的识谎能力，许多研究揭示了什么？

transcript_json.text: Q15. What advice does the new research offer regarding lie detection?
transcript_json.translation: Q15. 关于识别谎言，新研究给出了什么建议？

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 1
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 1

transcript_json.text: Appear to be submissive, humble, grateful and undemanding; show great pleasure when a doctor comes into your room, even if the visit is brief and useless.
transcript_json.translation: 要显得顺从、谦卑、感恩、无所要求；医生走进你的病房时要表现得非常高兴，哪怕这次查房既短暂又没用。

transcript_json.text: Don't challenge anyone with authority unless you are famous or very rich.
transcript_json.translation: 不要挑战任何有权威的人，除非你很有名或非常有钱。

transcript_json.text: Those are a few strategies for dealing with today's American medical establishment.
transcript_json.translation: 这些是应对当今美国医疗体制的几条策略。

transcript_json.text: What patients want is to be treated with respect and consideration.
transcript_json.translation: 病人想要的是得到尊重和体贴的对待。

transcript_json.text: But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that.
transcript_json.translation: 但据我的经验，愿意这么做的医院和医生太少了。

transcript_json.text: In his book, A Whole New Life, novelist Reynolds Price recalls that his doctors chose a crowded hallway as the place to tell him he might have a tumor on his spinal cord.
transcript_json.translation: 小说家雷诺兹·普赖斯在《全新的人生》一书中回忆说，他的医生们选了一条拥挤的走廊，来告诉他他的脊髓上可能长了肿瘤。

transcript_json.text: It did not occur to the two physicians that a hallway was not the most appropriate place for that particular piece of news.
transcript_json.translation: 这两位医生根本没想过，走廊并不是告知这样一个消息最合适的地方。

transcript_json.text: My surgeon, who is in his mid-thirties, looks tired.
transcript_json.translation: 我的外科医生三十五六岁，看上去很疲惫。

transcript_json.text: He has been overwhelmed with patients who have fallen on the winter ice.
transcript_json.translation: 在冬季冰面上滑倒的病人让他应接不暇。

transcript_json.text: He is a witty man, but sometimes his wit is unwelcome.
transcript_json.translation: 他是个风趣的人，但有时他的俏皮话并不受欢迎。

transcript_json.text: "The health insurance company Blue Cross wants me to put you out in the snow tomorrow afternoon," he tells me after I have been in the hospital for more than a week.
transcript_json.translation: "蓝十字保险公司想让我明天下午把你扔到雪地里去，"在我住院一个多星期后，他这样对我说。

transcript_json.text: I'm terrified because I have no idea where to go.
transcript_json.translation: 我吓坏了，因为我不知道该去哪里。

transcript_json.text: I cannot walk or even lift my leg a few inches.
transcript_json.translation: 我不能走路，甚至连腿都抬不起几英寸。

transcript_json.text: The hospital social worker strikes me as an idiot.
transcript_json.translation: 医院的社工在我看来就是个白痴。

transcript_json.text: But my complaints about her only annoy my surgeon.
transcript_json.translation: 但我对她的抱怨只会惹恼我的外科医生。

transcript_json.text: "I have to work with these people," he tells my friend, Dr. Karen Brudlney, when she mercifully intervenes on my behalf and arranges for me to be transferred to another hospital.
transcript_json.translation: "我还得和这些人共事呢，"他对我的朋友凯伦·布鲁德尼医生说。当时她好心替我出面，安排把我转到另一家医院。

transcript_json.text: "If you say one negative thing, they get defensive," she tells me later.
transcript_json.translation: "你只要说一句负面的话，他们就会起戒心，"她后来告诉我。

transcript_json.text: "They have this kind of institutional loyalty.
transcript_json.translation: "他们有一种机构忠诚感。

transcript_json.text: Always bring an advocate, that is, any other person with you to the hospital, and write down every single question and the answer, the name of every doctor and nurse.
transcript_json.translation: 去看病时务必带一个帮手，也就是说，带另一个人陪你上医院，并把每一个问题和答案、每一位医生和护士的名字都记下来。

transcript_json.text: When people know you have their names, they behave better.
transcript_json.translation: 当人们知道你掌握了他们的名字，表现就会好一些。

transcript_json.text: And," Brudney adds, "if you, as a patient, suggest that you might like to control even part of the situation or be consulted or informed, then you are considered difficult.
transcript_json.translation: 而且，"布鲁德尼补充说，"如果你作为病人，表示哪怕只想掌控一点局面，或者希望被征求意见、被告知情况，你就会被当成难缠的病人。

transcript_json.text: They want you to be totally passive.
transcript_json.translation: 他们希望你完全被动。

transcript_json.text: The entire health care system, particularly hospitals and nursing homes, exists for reasons that have nothing to do with taking care of patients.
transcript_json.translation: 整个医疗体系，尤其是医院和养老院，其存在的理由与照顾病人毫无关系。

transcript_json.text: Patients are incidental."
transcript_json.translation: "病人只是附带品。"

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 2
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 2

transcript_json.text: There are probably teams you've worked with but you never want to work with again.
transcript_json.translation: 可能有些团队你共事过，但再也不想与他们合作了。

transcript_json.text: But there must have also been other teams that you would prize reuniting with professionally.
transcript_json.translation: 但也一定有另一些团队，你会很珍视能再次与他们在职业上重聚。

transcript_json.text: In other words, your team had vitality.
transcript_json.translation: 换句话说，你的团队有生命力。

transcript_json.text: Vitality comes about when the ties people form with their fellow team members are such that they stay connected even after the team breaks up.
transcript_json.translation: 当人们与团队成员建立的纽带牢固到即使团队解散后仍保持联系时，这种生命力就产生了。

transcript_json.text: What characteristics of a team make its members more likely to stay in contact despite no longer working together?
transcript_json.translation: 团队的什么特征会让成员在不再共事之后仍更有可能保持联系？

transcript_json.text: This question has been answered recently in a study publisbed in a business journal.
transcript_json.translation: 最近发表在一本商业期刊上的一项研究回答了这个问题。

transcript_json.text: One of the two key factors the research team discovered is sameness.
transcript_json.translation: 研究团队发现的两个关键因素之一是同质性。

transcript_json.text: Specifically, sharing the same gender or ethnic origin.
transcript_json.translation: 具体来说，就是拥有相同的性别或族裔。

transcript_json.text: The more members of a team share similar demographics, the more inclined they will be to remain associates long after the team has served its purpose.
transcript_json.translation: 团队成员的人口特征越相似，在团队完成使命后很久，他们就越倾向于继续保持联系。

transcript_json.text: After ties are established, similarity strengthens them.
transcript_json.translation: 纽带建立之后，相似性会让它们更加牢固。

transcript_json.text: As a result, they regard these individuals with greater trust and mutual understanding, which motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，他们对这些人怀有更多的信任和相互理解，这促使他们寻求更多合作机会。

transcript_json.text: In effect, people tend to create stronger and longer-lasting connections with similar others.
transcript_json.translation: 实际上，人们往往与和自己相似的人建立更强、更持久的联系。

transcript_json.text: Someone who looks and sounds different from us may have the resources we need to be more successful.
transcript_json.translation: 长相和口音与我们不同的人，可能拥有让我们更成功所需的资源。

transcript_json.text: Yet, we find then to be significantly less credible simply because they are different.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，我们仅仅因为他们与自己不同，就觉得他们明显更不可信。

transcript_json.text: If you are a fierce advocate of workplace diversity, you'll no doubt be horrified by such a revelation.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你是职场多元化的坚定拥护者，这样的发现无疑会让你震惊。

transcript_json.text: The second factor identified by the researchers is the quality of the relationships among the team members.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员发现的第二个因素是团队成员之间关系的质量。

transcript_json.text: The more they trust one another, share the same goals and depend on each other for the achievement of those goals, the stronger their chances of maintaining their connections, despite no longer working as one team.
transcript_json.translation: 他们越信任彼此、目标一致、并在实现目标的过程中相互依赖，即使不再作为一个团队工作，他们保持联系的可能性就越大。

transcript_json.text: Teams with quality relationships have a shared belief that it's safe to take risks with each ether, and their members are obliged to share the workload and help out.
transcript_json.translation: 关系良好的团队有一个共同信念：在彼此面前冒险是安全的，成员们也有义务分担工作、互相帮衬。

transcript_json.text: From personal experience, I can see both the truth and the inconsistency of such studies.
transcript_json.translation: 从个人经验来看，我既看到这类研究的真实性，也看到了其中的不一致。

transcript_json.text: The truth is some of my closest friendships were formed as a result of having worked together on teams, and I actively seek opportunities to work with them again.
transcript_json.translation: 真实之处在于，我一些最亲密的友谊正是在团队共事中形成的，我也主动寻找与他们再次合作的机会。

transcript_json.text: The inconsistency, though, is that I've never worked for a team more successful and cohesive than the one of which I am a member right now.
transcript_json.translation: 而不一致之处在于，我工作过的团队里，没有哪个比我现在的团队更成功、更有凝聚力。

transcript_json.text: And yet, the four of us have very little in common and are completely different demographically.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，我们四个人几乎没有共同点，人口特征上也完全不同。

transcript_json.text: So I am unlikely to question the value of a diverse workforce.
transcript_json.translation: 所以我不太可能去质疑多元化员工队伍的价值。

transcript_json.translation: 问题19至21基于你刚刚听到的录音。

transcript_json.translation: Q19. 关于有生命力的团队，说话人说了什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q20. 关于团队成员，研究人员发现了什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q21. 关于说话人现在所在的团队，我们了解到什么？

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 3
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: An American researcher who studied 600 millionaires found how rich you can get comes down to six wealth factors.
transcript_json.translation: 一位研究过600名百万富翁的美国研究者发现，你能变得多富有取决于六个财富因素。

transcript_json.text: She found that six behaviors are related to net worth potential, regardless of age or income.
transcript_json.translation: 她发现，无论年龄或收入如何，有六种行为都与净资产潜力相关。

transcript_json.text: These were thriftiness, confidence, responsibility, planning, focus and social indifference.
transcript_json.translation: 这就是节俭、自信、责任、规划、专注和对外界眼光的淡然。

transcript_json.text: Being thrifty comes as no great surprise.
transcript_json.translation: 节俭并不让人意外。

transcript_json.text: Spending above your means, spending instead of saving for retirement,spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy,makes you a slave to the paycheck.
transcript_json.translation: 入不敷出地花，把本该存作退休金的钱花掉，幻想着自己即将暴富而提前花钱——这些都会让你沦为工资的奴隶。

transcript_json.text: "Even with an astronomical level of income," she wrote, "to properly build wealth, experts recommend saving 20% of your income and living off the remaining 80%."
transcript_json.translation: "即使收入高得惊人，"她写道，"要合理地积累财富，专家建议把收入的20%存起来，靠剩下的80%生活。"

transcript_json.text: Having confidence is another key characteristic, as it helps people to be thrifty.
transcript_json.translation: 自信是另一个关键特质，因为它有助于人们做到节俭。

transcript_json.text: It takes confidence to live within your means.
transcript_json.translation: 量入为出需要自信。

transcript_json.text: It also takes confidence to invest properly.
transcript_json.translation: 合理投资同样需要自信。

transcript_json.text: Instead of making investing decisions with your emotions, financial planners advise that you should leave your investrnents alone and focus on a long term investment plan.
transcript_json.translation: 理财规划师建议，不要凭情绪做投资决定，而应放着你的投资不去折腾，专注于长期投资计划。

transcript_json.text: But people can't invest or manage their own money without accepting responsibility for the outcomes.
transcript_json.translation: 但人们若不接受对结果的责任，就无法投资或管理自己的钱。

transcript_json.text: Many millionaires take on personal responsibility, and most also happen to be self-made, meaning they didn't acquire their wealth through luck.
transcript_json.translation: 许多百万富翁勇于承担个人责任，而且大多数恰好都是白手起家，也就是说他们的财富不是靠运气得来的。

transcript_json.text: Millionaires don't count on anyone else to make them rich, and they don't blame anyone else if they fall short.
transcript_json.translation: 百万富翁不指望别人让自己发财，如果没达到目标，他们也不怪别人。

transcript_json.text: They focus on things they can control and align their daily habits to the goals they have set for themselves.
transcript_json.translation: 他们专注于自己能控制的事情，并让日常习惯与为自己设定的目标保持一致。

transcript_json.text: They tend to be goal-oriented and hard workers, which enables them to plan financially and focus on seeing those plans through. 92% of the milionaires surveyed developed a longterm plan for their money and 97% almost always achieved the goals they set for themselves.
transcript_json.translation: 他们往往目标明确、勤奋肯干，这使他们能够做好理财规划，并专注于把计划贯彻到底。受访的百万富翁中有92%为自己的钱制定了长期计划，97%的人几乎总能达成自己设定的目标。

transcript_json.text: And it is these behaviors that make it easy for them to be socially indifferent.
transcript_json.translation: 正是这些行为让他们能够轻松做到不在意外界的眼光。

transcript_json.text: They resist lifestyle creep, the tendency to spend more whenever one earns more.
transcript_json.translation: 他们抵制生活方式膨胀，也就是一挣得多就花得多的倾向。

transcript_json.text: Essentially, they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others or what they have acquired.
transcript_json.translation: 从根本上说，他们不屈服于购买最新潮东西的压力，也不为了追赶别人或别人已有的东西而花钱。

transcript_json.text: Instead of being focused on what might make them happy today, they're focused on their long-term wealth-building plan.
transcript_json.translation: 他们关注的不是今天什么能让自己开心，而是自己的长期财富积累计划。

transcript_json.translation: 问题22至25基于你刚刚听到的录音。

transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 1

transcript_json.text: M: Welcome to Money Matters, a weekly program that helps you manage your money.
transcript_json.translation: M: 欢迎收听《理财有道》，一档帮助你管理钱财的每周节目。

transcript_json.text: Tonight, I'll be talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting.
transcript_json.translation: 今晚，我将和玛丽·约翰逊聊聊做预算的问题。

transcript_json.text: W: Hello everyone.
transcript_json.translation: W: 大家好。

transcript_json.text: M: There's a magic about money.
transcript_json.translation: M: 金钱这东西很神奇。

transcript_json.text: When it's not planned for, tracked, and kept a record of, it literally disappears.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你不做规划、不追踪、不记账，钱真的会不知不觉就没了。

transcript_json.text: What are some of the steps we can take to prevent this from happening?
transcript_json.translation: 我们可以采取哪些措施来防止这种情况发生？

transcript_json.text: W: It's all about keeping track of your money.
transcript_json.translation: W: 关键就在于记好自己的账。

transcript_json.text: If you don't do that, you'll never be able to set any goals for your budget or have the discipline to stick to them.
transcript_json.translation: 如果不这样做，你就永远无法为预算设定目标，也谈不上有纪律去坚持执行。

transcript_json.text: M: That's easier said than done.
transcript_json.translation: M: 说起来容易做起来难。

transcript_json.text: I read recently that only 41% of Americans adhere to a budget.
transcript_json.translation: 我最近读到，只有 41% 的美国人坚持做预算。

transcript_json.text: W: Yes, but knowing what you earn and what you spend can give you reassurance that you won't get into debt in the first place.
transcript_json.translation: W: 没错，但清楚自己的收入和支出，能让你放心自己从一开始就不会负债。

transcript_json.text: You can do this by adding up all of your sources of income you have and writing them all down on a piece of paper.
transcript_json.translation: 你可以把所有收入来源加总，一条条写在纸上。

transcript_json.text: On the same page, write down all of your monthly expenses.
transcript_json.translation: 在同一张纸上，写下你所有的每月开支。

transcript_json.text: M: I'm always amazed at how much my expenses add up, but designating each item as an income or an expense really helps me have a much better sense of all my spending.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我的开支加起来总是多得惊人，不过把每一项标注为收入或支出，确实让我对自己的花销有了清楚得多的认识。

transcript_json.text: W: Right.
transcript_json.translation: W: 对。

transcript_json.text: Most people have no idea how much they spend each day, let alone each week or month, no matter how careful they are.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数人根本不知道自己每天花了多少钱，更别说每周或每月了，无论他们多小心。

transcript_json.text: Next, subtract your monthly expenses from income.
transcript_json.translation: 接着，用收入减去每月开支。

transcript_json.text: If the result is positive, you are living within your means.
transcript_json.translation: 如果结果是正数，说明你做到了量入为出。

transcript_json.text: If the result is a negative number, you're going to have to cut back on your spending.
transcript_json.translation: 如果是负数，你就得削减开支了。

transcript_json.text: M: I'm usually a negative number.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我通常是负数。

transcript_json.text: I just can't resist the lure of all those prestigious goods.
transcript_json.translation: 我就是抵挡不住那些名牌商品的诱惑。

transcript_json.text: W: Well, it's not a catastrophe.
transcript_json.translation: W: 嗯，这还不算灾难。

transcript_json.text: But you do have to make some changes.
transcript_json.translation: 但你的确得做些改变。

transcript_json.text: Try cutting back on those non-essential items, sell some stuff in your attic or shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations like chocolate.
transcript_json.translation: 试着少买那些非必需品，把阁楼里的东西卖点掉，或者改在网上购物，避开巧克力之类不必要的诱惑。

transcript_json.text: Failing that you can always find yourself a part-time job.
transcript_json.translation: 实在不行，你总可以给自己找份兼职。

transcript_json.text: I think it's a winner for us.

transcript_json.text: All the appliances are brand new.

transcript_json.text: There's a washing machine and a tumble dryer in the utility room next to the kitchen.
transcript_json.translation: 厨房旁边的杂物间里有洗衣机和烘干机。

transcript_json.text: M: Lots of closet space, too, which is fabulous.

transcript_json.text: It's perfect if tranquility is what you are looking for.

transcript_json.text: As we only have one car, and my wife has to use it as she works nights at the hospital.

transcript_json.text: Thank you so much.

transcript_json.text: A new study has found a positive correlation between how much television children watch and their parents' stress levels.
transcript_json.translation: 一项新研究发现，孩子看电视时间的长短与父母的压力水平呈正相关。为什么会这样？

transcript_json.text: Why?
transcript_json.translation: 一项新研究发现，孩子看电视时间的长短与父母的压力水平呈正相关。为什么会这样？

transcript_json.text: Because the more television kids watch, the more they're exposed to advertising.
transcript_json.translation: 因为孩子看电视越多，接触到的广告就越多。

transcript_json.text: The more advertising they see, the more likely they are to insist on purchasing items when they go with their parents to the store.
transcript_json.translation: 他们看到的广告越多，跟父母去商店时就越可能坚持要买东西。

transcript_json.text: This could generate conflict if the parents refuse.
transcript_json.translation: 如果父母拒绝，就可能引发冲突。

transcript_json.text: All that, researchers say, can contribute to parents' overall stress levels.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员说，这些都会加重父母的整体压力。

transcript_json.text: What's the solution?
transcript_json.translation: 解决办法是什么？

transcript_json.text: Perhaps the most obvious is curtailing screen time.
transcript_json.translation: 也许最显而易见的办法是减少屏幕时间。

transcript_json.text: Commercial content is there for a reason: to elicit purchasing behavior.
transcript_json.translation: 商业内容的存在是有目的的：诱使人们购买。

transcript_json.text: So, parents might want to shut off the TV.
transcript_json.translation: 所以，家长或许应该关掉电视。

transcript_json.text: Researchers concede that this is easier said than done, so they suggest another option.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员承认这说起来容易做起来难，于是他们提出了另一个办法。

transcript_json.text: Parents can change how they talk to their kids about purchases.
transcript_json.translation: 家长可以改变与孩子谈论购物的方式。

transcript_json.text: The researchers suggest that parents seek input from their children on family purchasing decisions.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员建议，家长在家庭购买决策上征求孩子的意见。

transcript_json.text: They shouldn't try to control all purchases.
transcript_json.translation: 他们不该试图控制所有购买行为。

transcript_json.text: Instead, parents might tell their children things like, "I will listen to your advice on certain products or brands."
transcript_json.translation: 相反，父母可以对孩子这样说：“在某些产品或品牌上，我会听你的建议。

transcript_json.text: This type of communication, the researchers assert, can lead to children making fewer purchasing demands.
transcript_json.translation: ”研究人员断言，这种沟通方式能让孩子提出更

transcript_json.text: That means less parents' stress.
transcript_json.translation: 少的购买要求，也就意味着父母的压力更小。

transcript_json.text: However, the protective effect of this kind of communication diminishes with greater exposure to television.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，这种沟通的保护作用会随着看电视时间的增多而减弱。

transcript_json.text: This is because advertising aimed at children is especially persuasive.
transcript_json.translation: 这是因为针对儿童的广告尤其有说服力。

transcript_json.text: Advertisers use an assortment of tactics, such as bright colors, happy music, and celebrity endorsements to appeal to children.
transcript_json.translation: 广告商使用各种手段吸引儿童，比如鲜艳的色彩、欢快的音乐和名人代言。

transcript_json.text: Plus, children don't have the cognitive ability to fully understand advertising's intent, which makes them particularly vulnerable to advertisements.
transcript_json.translation: 此外，儿童不具备完全理解广告意图的认知能力，这使他们特别容易受广告影响。

transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 2

transcript_json.text: Everyone is supposed to cheer for good guys.
transcript_json.translation: 人人都应该为好人喝彩。

transcript_json.text: We should only punish the bad guys.
transcript_json.translation: 我们应该只惩罚坏人。

transcript_json.text: That's not what we always do.
transcript_json.translation: 但我们的所作所为并非总是如此。

transcript_json.text: Most of the time, we do indeed reward good people.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数时候，我们确实会奖励好人。

transcript_json.text: We also often punish people who harm others, or who aren't good team players.
transcript_json.translation: 我们也常常惩罚伤害他人或不善合作的人。

transcript_json.text: But sometimes the good guys also get punished or criticized, specifically because they are so good.
transcript_json.translation: 但有时好人也会受到惩罚或批评，恰恰就是因为他们太好了。

transcript_json.text: This seems baffling because it's detrimental to group cooperation.
transcript_json.translation: 这看起来令人费解，因为它有损群体合作。

transcript_json.text: However, the phenomenon has been discovered in multiple fields.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，这一现象已在多个领域被发现。

transcript_json.text: It has been found in every society.
transcript_json.translation: 在每一个社会中都发现过它。

transcript_json.text: Why does this happen?
transcript_json.translation: 为什么会这样？

transcript_json.text: Research suggests a simple reason.
transcript_json.translation: 研究给出了一个简单的解释。

transcript_json.text: When one person looks really good, others look bad by comparison.
transcript_json.translation: 当一个人显得特别优秀时，其他人相形之下就显得差了。

transcript_json.text: Those others then have an incentive in stopping that person from looking good, especially if they can't or won't compete.
transcript_json.translation: 于是这些人就有了阻止那个人继续出彩的动机，尤其是在他们无法或不愿与之竞争的情况下。

transcript_json.text: After all, we're all judged in comparison with others.
transcript_json.translation: 毕竟，我们都是在与他人的比较中被评价的。

transcript_json.text: When faced with someone better, what can a normal person do?
transcript_json.translation: 面对比自己强的人，普通人能怎么做？

transcript_json.text: One option is to actively compete.
transcript_json.translation: 一个选择是积极竞争。

transcript_json.text: A second option is to bring that person down.
transcript_json.translation: 另一个选择是把那个人拉下来。

transcript_json.text: That is to suppress their cooperation or work ethic, infer selfish motives for their actions, or imply real or imagined hypocrisy.
transcript_json.translation: 也就是压制对方的合作精神或敬业精神，揣测其行为出于私心，或暗指其有真真假假的虚伪。

transcript_json.text: Other tactics include attacking them on unrelated dimensions or punishing them outright.
transcript_json.translation: 其他手段还包括在无关的方面攻击他们，或者直接惩罚他们。

transcript_json.text: Why does this matter?
transcript_json.translation: 为什么这一点很重要？

transcript_json.text: Critics often attack the motives of people who protect the environment, donate money, or work too hard.
transcript_json.translation: 批评者常常攻击那些保护环境、捐款捐物或过度拼命工作的人，质疑其动机。

transcript_json.text: Such good deeds are dismissed as naive or hypocritical by those who do not perform those deeds.
transcript_json.translation: 不做这些善事的人会把这类善举斥为幼稚或虚伪。

transcript_json.text: This criticism may ultimately discourage people from doing good deeds.
transcript_json.translation: 这种批评最终可能打消人们行善的积极性。

transcript_json.text: So it's important to recognize these attacks for what they are.
transcript_json.translation: 所以，认清这些攻击的实质很重要。

transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 1

transcript_json.text: In America, most researchers concede that boys and girls are brought up in different ways, taught different skills and rewarded for different acts.
transcript_json.translation: 在美国，大多数研究人员承认，男孩和女孩的养育方式不同，被教授不同的技能，也因不同的行为受到奖励。

transcript_json.text: Women, it is agreed, excel at certain tasks, men at others.
transcript_json.translation: 人们公认，女性擅长某些任务，男性擅长另一些任务。

transcript_json.text: There is little argument that some personality traits appear more dominant in one sex than in the other.
transcript_json.translation: 对于某些性格特征在一种性别中比在另一种性别中更突出这一点，几乎没有人有异议。

transcript_json.text: All of this notwithstanding, gender differences are very much in the media these days.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管如此，如今性别差异仍是媒体热议的话题。

transcript_json.text: Since the rise of the women's movement, gender role behavior has come under closer scrutiny.
transcript_json.translation: 自女权运动兴起以来，性别角色行为受到了更严格的审视。

transcript_json.text: How has this affected friendship?
transcript_json.translation: 这如何影响了友谊？

transcript_json.text: How do the sexes differ in their friendship relations?
transcript_json.translation: 两性在友谊关系上有何差异？

transcript_json.text: Most pre-teen children have a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex and similar age.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数青春期前的孩子都有一个最好的朋友，通常是同性别、年龄相仿的人。

transcript_json.text: Both sexes share an essentially positive recollection of these childhood friendships.
transcript_json.translation: 两性对这类童年友谊的回忆在本质上都是积极的，这一点是共通的。

transcript_json.text: They do not differ in this respect.
transcript_json.translation: 在这方面他们没有差异。

transcript_json.text: However, the type of play engaged in during these early friendships is telling of the difference to come.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，在这些早期友谊中参与的游戏类型，预示了日后将要显现的差异。

transcript_json.text: Boys tend to form play groups that are competitive in nature.
transcript_json.translation: 男孩往往结成本质上带竞争性的玩伴群体。

transcript_json.text: Girls' groups more frequently revolve around cooperative enterprises.
transcript_json.translation: 女孩的群体则更多围绕合作性活动展开。

transcript_json.text: Thus at an early age, boys become concerned with trying hard and winning, while girls, by contrast, play house and school, engaging in roles that require complementary support.
transcript_json.translation: 于是，男孩小小年纪就开始在意努力和输赢，而女孩则相反，她们玩过家家、扮老师上课，扮演的是需要相互配合的角色。

transcript_json.text: Men recall being highly responsive to and aware of the gender role opinions of other boys.
transcript_json.translation: 男性回忆说，他们当年对其他男孩关于性别角色的看法非常敏感、十分在意。

transcript_json.text: Girls in pre-teen years appear to be less susceptible to gender role pressure.
transcript_json.translation: 青春期前的女孩似乎较不易受性别角色压力的影响。

transcript_json.text: It is not until the dating years that women report being concerned with feminine behavior.
transcript_json.translation: 女性要等到开始约会的年纪，才表示在意女性化的举止。

transcript_json.text: Males, for the most part, are responsive to the suggestion that their behavior is unmanly at almost any age.
transcript_json.translation: 而男性在几乎任何年龄段，都会因别人说他们举止不够男子气而有所反应。

transcript_json.text: These early attitudes reinforced by social conditioning continue to play an active part in the friendships of both sexes during adolescence.
transcript_json.translation: 这些早期态度经社会熏陶而强化，在青春期继续活跃地影响着两性的友谊。

transcript_json.text: This is a period when the majority of males, once again, report a close alliance with same-sex friends.
transcript_json.translation: 这一时期，大多数男性再次表示与同性朋友结成了亲密的同盟。

transcript_json.text: Now, however, with heightened intensity, considerable energy is devoted to competing for position, and a definite undercurrent of competition permeates the relationship.
transcript_json.translation: 然而此时，竞争的烈度加剧，大量精力被投入到争夺地位上，一股明显的竞争暗流弥漫在这段关系之中。

transcript_json.text: Although in dissimilar fashion, females share equally fragile relationships at this age.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然形式不同，女性在这个年龄段的友谊同样脆弱。

transcript_json.text: For them, the bond of loyalty extends only to the line of romantic involvement.
transcript_json.translation: 对她们来说，忠诚的纽带只延续到恋爱关系这条线为止。

transcript_json.text: This is most apt to be the case in late adolescence, when dating and relationships with boys take sharp precedence over sisterhood.
transcript_json.translation: 这种情况最常出现在青春期晚期，此时与男孩约会、恋爱远比姐妹情谊重要。

transcript_json.text: Actually, dating dilutes the intensity of same-sex friendships for men also.
transcript_json.translation: 实际上，约会同样会淡化男性的同性友谊。

transcript_json.text: For the majority of us, the moment we begin to date seriously, there's a competition between romance and friendship.
transcript_json.translation: 对我们大多数人来说，一旦开始认真恋爱，爱情和友谊之间就存在一场较量。

transcript_json.text: Good afternoon.
transcript_json.translation: 下午好。

transcript_json.text: Today's lecture, we'll be talking about how and when to disclose a disability when applying for a job.
transcript_json.translation: 今天的讲座，我们要谈谈求职时如何以及何时披露残疾情况。

transcript_json.text: On average, about 20% of the population has some form of disability.
transcript_json.translation: 平均而言，大约 20% 的人有某种形式的残疾。

transcript_json.text: Most countries these days have equal opportunity and nondiscrimination laws.
transcript_json.translation: 如今大多数国家都有机会平等和反歧视方面的法律。

transcript_json.text: Yet, disabled people often find it hard to decide when, how, and if at all, to raise their disability problem with a potential employer.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，残疾人往往难以决定何时、如何、甚至要不要向潜在雇主提起自己的残疾问题。

transcript_json.text: There is uncertainty about how a recruiter will perceive their disability.
transcript_json.translation: 招聘者会如何看待他们的残疾，这一点存在不确定性。

transcript_json.text: As such, many candidates fear they wouldn't be considered for a position as a result of disclosing this personal information.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，许多求职者担心，披露这一个人信息会导致自己得不到那个职位。

transcript_json.text: And research has validated this as a genuine concern for many job applicants.
transcript_json.translation: 研究证实，这确实是许多求职者真实的顾虑。

transcript_json.text: It's a natural reaction, but it shouldn't be a reason to stay quiet.
transcript_json.translation: 这是很自然的反应，但不应该成为保持沉默的理由。

transcript_json.text: People need to remember that they are applying for a position they have the skills and experience to excel in.
transcript_json.translation: 人们要记住，自己申请的是一个凭自身技能和经验完全能胜任的职位。

transcript_json.text: Discussing a disability with a potential employer may help them make reasonable workplace adjustments in their favor.
transcript_json.translation: 与潜在雇主讨论残疾情况，也许有助于他们做出对求职者有利的合理职场调整。

transcript_json.text: It's most appropriate to discuss a disability when they reply to confirm an interview.
transcript_json.translation: 在回复确认面试时提及残疾情况最为合适。

transcript_json.text: This information needn't be put up front in their cover letter or resume, because it's probably not relevant to the position itself.
transcript_json.translation: 这一信息不必放在求职信或简历的开头，因为它很可能与职位本身无关。

transcript_json.text: Candidates with disabilities should feel they have the power to make their own decisions around sharing this information free from prejudice.
transcript_json.translation: 残疾求职者应当感到，自己有权在不受偏见的情况下自主决定是否分享这一信息。

transcript_json.text: If they find an organization that doesn't celebrate diversity and inclusion, it could say a lot about the company's culture.
transcript_json.translation: 如果发现某个组织并不推崇多元与包容，这很能说明这家公司的文化。

transcript_json.text: Perhaps the organization isn't the right fit.
transcript_json.translation: 也许这个组织并不适合你。

transcript_json.text: It's important for them to remember that they are seeking a manager and employer that's going to be supportive and continue to give them a great employment experience.
transcript_json.translation: 重要的是要记住，他们寻找的是一位愿意支持他们、并持续带给他们良好工作体验的主管和雇主。

transcript_json.text: Companies sometimes offer candidates the chance to disclose disabilities on their application form, but people shouldn't feel restricted by this method or timing.
transcript_json.translation: 公司有时会让求职者在申请表上披露残疾情况，但人们不应受这种途径或时机的束缚。

transcript_json.text: People should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition.
transcript_json.translation: 人们应避免透露自己残疾或病症的名称。

transcript_json.text: There is always the risk that the recruiter will research information that is inaccurate or irrelevant.
transcript_json.translation: 招聘者查到的信息总有可能是错误或无关的。

transcript_json.text: If people don't think their disability will impact their ability to perform in the advertised position, then it's entirely their entitlement to choose when and whether to share this information.
transcript_json.translation: 如果人们认为自己的残疾不会影响其在所聘职位上的表现，那么何时披露、是否披露这一信息，完全是他们的权利。

transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: Smartphones distract attention and reduce learning because of their potential to offer activities more inviting than study.
transcript_json.translation: 智能手机会分散注意力、妨碍学习，因为它可能提供比学习更诱人的活动。

transcript_json.text: But what about background sound alone?
transcript_json.translation: 但仅仅是背景声音又如何呢？

transcript_json.text: A group of American researchers compared students' comprehension of verbal material when reading in the presence of background speech, instrumental music or general noise.
transcript_json.translation: 一组美国研究人员比较了学生在背景说话声、器乐或一般噪音中进行阅读时对文字材料的理解情况。

transcript_json.text: General noise is neutral, such as that from the sound of an air conditioner or fan.
transcript_json.translation: 一般噪音是中性的，比如空调或风扇发出的声音。

transcript_json.text: Students' scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech.
transcript_json.translation: 有背景说话声时，学生的分数下降最多。

transcript_json.text: Comprehension was slightly better with the presence of music than with speech.
transcript_json.translation: 有音乐时理解力比有说话声时稍好一些。

transcript_json.text: However, when they were asked to identify melodies rather than understand text, background music interfered more.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，当要求他们辨识旋律而不是理解文字时，背景音乐的干扰更大。

transcript_json.text: When the background speech was in a language unfamiliar to participants, there was little if any hindrance of reading comprehension.
transcript_json.translation: 当背景说话声是参与者不熟悉的语言时，对阅读理解几乎没有妨碍。

transcript_json.text: British researchers compared the effects of background speech, vocal music, instrumental music, general background noise, and silence on short-term memory.
transcript_json.translation: 英国研究人员比较了背景说话声、声乐、器乐、一般背景噪音和安静环境对短期记忆的影响。

transcript_json.text: Background speech had the biggest negative effect.
transcript_json.translation: 背景说话声的负面影响最大。

transcript_json.text: Vocal music was slightly more disruptive than instrumental.
transcript_json.translation: 声乐比器乐的干扰稍大。

transcript_json.text: In general, background noise and silence were least disruptive.
transcript_json.translation: 总体而言，一般背景噪音和安静环境的干扰最小。

transcript_json.text: It seems the degree of interference from background noise depends on the overlap between the processing required on the task and the processing required to screen out the background noise.
transcript_json.translation: 看来背景噪音干扰的程度，取决于完成该任务所需的加工与排除背景噪音所需的加工之间的重叠程度。

transcript_json.text: The studies suggest that when people read and when they try to remember any verbal material, background speech will inhibit their ability.
transcript_json.translation: 这些研究表明，人们在阅读或试图记忆任何文字材料时，背景说话声都会削弱其能力。

transcript_json.text: Instrumental music will have, at worst, a slight effect.
transcript_json.translation: 器乐至多只有轻微的影响。

transcript_json.text: When students write essays, however, other research has found it is best to reduce all background noise as much as possible.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，其他研究发现，学生写文章时最好尽可能减少一切背景噪音。

transcript_json.text: Not everyone reacts in the same way to distractions.
transcript_json.translation: 并不是每个人对干扰的反应都一样。

transcript_json.text: Other studies suggest some aspects of personality may make a difference.
transcript_json.translation: 其他研究表明，性格的某些方面可能造成差异。

transcript_json.text: The researchers subjected shy, quiet people and confident, outgoing ones to high arousal or low arousal background music, general noise or silence while asking them to remember words.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员让害羞安静的人和自信外向的人分别在激昂或舒缓的背景音乐、一般噪声或安静环境中记单词。

transcript_json.text: Everyone performed best in the silent condition, but less sociable people were more negatively affected by each of the distractions.
transcript_json.translation: 所有人在安静条件下表现最好，但每一种干扰对不善社交的人的负面影响都更大。

transcript_json.text: So when children are reading and trying to incorporate new material, parents could consider allowing some background music, particularly if it is instrumental and their child is the outgoing type.
transcript_json.translation: 所以，当孩子阅读并试图吸收新内容时，家长可以考虑允许放一些背景音乐，尤其是器乐，而且孩子要属于外向型。

transcript_json.text: M: How's your dissertation going?

transcript_json.text: I'm proofreading my first draft and will submit it to my professor tomorrow.

transcript_json.translation: M: 你的意思是连开头都还没写？

transcript_json.text: The final draft is due in five months.
