transcript_json.text: Hello, I am co-founder of the popular female travel community, We Are Travel Girls.
transcript_json.translation: 大家好，我是颇受欢迎的女性旅行社区 We Are Travel Girls 的联合创始人。

transcript_json.text: We collect and publish stories from women traveling all over the world.
transcript_json.translation: 我们收集并发表世界各地旅行女性的故事。

transcript_json.text: We promote women's blogs, we host meetings and events, and are getting ready to launch our "Travel With Us" trips in Bali, Japan, and Malawi.
transcript_json.translation: 我们推广女性博主的博客，举办各类会议和活动，还准备推出我们的'与我们一起旅行'行程，目的地包括巴厘岛、日本和马拉维。

transcript_json.text: Before I started We Are Travel Girls, I had a successful 10-year career in finance in London where I advised private clients on their investments.
transcript_json.translation: 在创办 We Are Travel Girls 之前，我在伦敦金融行业有过成功的 10 年职业生涯，为私人客户提供投资建议。

transcript_json.text: Having always had a huge love for travel, I finally took the leap and left finance to pursue my dream of starting a travel company.
transcript_json.translation: 因为一直酷爱旅行，我最终放手一搏，离开金融业，去追寻创办旅行公司的梦想。

transcript_json.text: For as long as I can remember, I wanted to be a travel writer.
transcript_json.translation: 从记事起，我就想成为一名旅行作家。

transcript_json.text: Before blogs existed, and everything we read was online, I would go to travel writing seminars by writers who were published in travel magazines.
transcript_json.translation: 在博客出现、我们读的东西都在网上之前，我会去参加旅行写作研讨班，主讲人都是在旅行杂志上发表过作品的作家。

transcript_json.text: I was desperate to write for one of those magazines but didn't know how to break into that industry.
transcript_json.translation: 我迫切想为其中一家杂志撰稿，却不知道如何打入那个行业。

transcript_json.text: After university, I ended up working in finance, but always had a desire to travel and write about it.
transcript_json.translation: 大学毕业后我进了金融业，但始终怀有去旅行并写作的愿望。

transcript_json.text: In 2015, I was looking at ways to leave finance, and my friend Vanessa, who grew up on a ranch on the central coast of California, suggested starting a blog.
transcript_json.translation: 2015 年，我正在寻找离开金融业的途径，我朋友瓦妮莎——她在加利福尼亚中部海岸的一个牧场长大——建议我开博客。

transcript_json.text: But when we started creating it, we realized that was the same thing every girl was doing.
transcript_json.translation: 但当我们开始动手做时，发现每个女孩都在做同样的事。

transcript_json.text: So we turned our attention to creating a community among these women.
transcript_json.translation: 于是我们把注意力转向在这些女性中建立一个社区。

transcript_json.text: This led us to start We Are Travel Girls, which has now grown into a community of over 200,000 followers.
transcript_json.translation: 这促使我们创办了 We Are Travel Girls，如今它已发展成一个拥有 20 多万关注者的社区。

transcript_json.text: To anyone thinking about becoming a travel writer, I would suggest they first try and look for a unique way to enter the industry.
transcript_json.translation: 对任何想成为旅行作家的人，我建议首先设法找到一条独特的入行之路。

transcript_json.text: There are a lot of travel writers now and it can be hard to stand out from the crowd.
transcript_json.translation: 如今旅行作家很多，想脱颖而出并不容易。

transcript_json.text: My advice would be to find a niche and focus on that. For example, if you love adventure travel, focus on that. If you love food, focus on food travel.
transcript_json.translation: 比如，如果你热爱探险旅行，就专注于探险；如果你热爱美食，就专注于美食之旅。

transcript_json.text: The more specific you are, the easier it will be to build an audience.
transcript_json.translation: 定位越具体，就越容易积累读者。

transcript_json.text: Another thing I would suggest is to avoid too much advertising early on.
transcript_json.translation: 另外我建议，前期不要投放太多广告。

transcript_json.text: When you first start out, your audience is there for your content, not to be sold to.
transcript_json.translation: 刚起步时，读者是冲着你的内容来的，不是来被推销的。

transcript_json.text: If you start bombarding them with ads too early, they will lose interest.
transcript_json.translation: 如果太早开始用广告轰炸他们，他们会失去兴趣。

transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 1

transcript_json.text: M: Hi Lily, how's the new apartment?
transcript_json.translation: M: 你好，莉莉，新公寓怎么样？

transcript_json.text: W: It's okay.
transcript_json.translation: W: 还行吧。

transcript_json.text: M: What?
transcript_json.translation: M: 什么？

transcript_json.text: How can it be just okay when last week you were thrilled about the place and kept posting photos of it online?
transcript_json.translation: 上周你还对那个地方兴奋不已，不停在网上晒照片，怎么会只是还行？

transcript_json.text: W: Well, last week when I moved in, the apartment seemed cozy, just the right size for one person.
transcript_json.translation: W: 唉，上周刚搬进来的时候，公寓显得温馨舒适，对一个人来说大小正合适。

transcript_json.text: But now it just seems tiny, shabby and solitary.
transcript_json.translation: 但现在它看起来又小又破又冷清。

transcript_json.text: M: Ah that's the problem.
transcript_json.translation: M: 啊，问题就在这儿。

transcript_json.text: You miss your roommates from university, don't you?
transcript_json.translation: 你想念大学时的室友了，是不是？

transcript_json.text: W: I'm going to sound like an idiot because I used to complain to you all the time about how crowded our dormitory room was, and about all the things they did to irritate me, like watching movies late at night without headphones, or talking loudly early in the morning.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我这么说会显得很傻，因为我以前老是向你抱怨宿舍房间多么拥挤，抱怨她们怎么招我烦，比如深夜不带耳机看电影，或者一大早大声说话。

transcript_json.text: But now I miss them terribly.
transcript_json.translation: 可现在我特别想念她们。

transcript_json.text: M: Of course you do. That's perfectly normal.
transcript_json.translation: M: 你当然会想家，这完全正常。

transcript_json.text: When I got my first place, I remember thinking I couldn't wait to live by myself and get away from my juvenile roommates and all their annoying habits.
transcript_json.translation: 我有了第一个住处时，还记得自己心想，终于可以迫不及待地独自生活，摆脱那些幼稚的室友和他们所有恼人的习惯了。

transcript_json.text: But then I began missing them and feeling lonely and thinking that our dormitory was like paradise.
transcript_json.translation: 可后来我开始想念他们，觉得孤独，甚至觉得我们的宿舍简直就是天堂。

transcript_json.text: Even though there were six of us guys in one small room.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管我们六个男生挤在一间小屋里。

transcript_json.text: W: I thought it was just me who felt like that.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我还以为只有我有这种感觉呢。

transcript_json.text: M: Look, you lived at home with us.
transcript_json.translation: M: 你看，你以前和我们住在一起。

transcript_json.text: And then you had three roommates.
transcript_json.translation: 后来你有三个室友。

transcript_json.text: And this is your first time living alone. So it's hard.
transcript_json.translation: 而且这是你第一次独自生活，所以不容易。

transcript_json.text: But your first apartment is a milestone in your life.
transcript_json.translation: 但你的第一套公寓是你人生的一个里程碑。

transcript_json.text: And you should celebrate it.
transcript_json.translation: 你应该庆祝一下。

transcript_json.text: Tell me about the apartment.
transcript_json.translation: 跟我说说那套公寓吧。

transcript_json.text: W: Actually, it's not bad.
transcript_json.translation: W: 其实还不错。

transcript_json.text: In fact, it's pretty adorable.
transcript_json.translation: 说真的，还挺可爱的。

transcript_json.text: Now that I have decorated it and it has everything I need.
transcript_json.translation: 现在我把它布置好了，需要的东西都齐了。

transcript_json.text: I have a kitchen to cook in, the bathroom all to myself.
transcript_json.translation: 我有厨房可以做饭，浴室归我一个人用。

transcript_json.text: And then another room with my bed at one end and the sofa, a small table and chairs at the other end.
transcript_json.translation: 还有一个房间，一头放着我的床，另一头是沙发、一张小桌子和几把椅子。

transcript_json.text: M: That does sound adorable, and I can't wait to see it. And neither can mom and dad.
transcript_json.translation: M: 那听起来真可爱，我都等不及想看看了。爸妈也等不及了。

transcript_json.text: CONVERSATION 2
transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 2

transcript_json.text: W: Welcome to our program book talk.
transcript_json.translation: W: 欢迎收听我们的节目《读书漫谈》。

transcript_json.text: Our guest today is Frank Jones, a critic of our education system and the author of new book, How to reform our universities.
transcript_json.translation: 今天的嘉宾是弗兰克·琼斯，一位教育体制批评者，也是新书《如何改革我们的大学》的作者。

transcript_json.text: M: Hello, Susan.
transcript_json.translation: M: 你好，苏珊。

transcript_json.text: W: Frank, you support radically changing universities in America.
transcript_json.translation: W: 弗兰克，你支持对美国大学进行彻底变革。

transcript_json.text: Yes.
transcript_json.translation: 是的。

transcript_json.text: M: I believe that the purpose of higher education is to prepare young people to enter the workforce and that our current system fails to do this.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我认为高等教育的目的是让年轻人做好进入职场的准备，而我们当前的体制没有做到这一点。

transcript_json.text: We're allocating too many resources to disciplines that don't match the needs of employers.
transcript_json.translation: 我们把太多资源分配给了与雇主需求不匹配的学科。

transcript_json.text: W: I think your attitude to education is a bit cynical Frank.
transcript_json.translation: W: 弗兰克，我觉得你对教育的态度有点愤世嫉俗。

transcript_json.text: Surely the purpose of university is to prepare young people to participate fully in civic life rather than just to find well paid jobs.
transcript_json.translation: 大学的目的一定是让年轻人做好准备充分参与公民生活，而不仅仅是找到高薪工作。

transcript_json.text: M: Susan, many young graduates struggle to find any job let alone a good one.
transcript_json.translation: M: 苏珊，许多刚毕业的年轻人连份工作都难找，更别说好工作了。

transcript_json.text: The job market is grim.
transcript_json.translation: 就业市场很严峻。

transcript_json.text: Particularly for students who study the arts.
transcript_json.translation: 对学文科的学生来说尤其如此。

transcript_json.text: W: I agree that it isn't easy for young people to find work, but you propose closing down all departments that aren't directly related to science and technology.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我同意年轻人找工作不容易，可你提议关闭所有与科学技术没有直接关系的院系。

transcript_json.text: Is that really the solution?
transcript_json.translation: 那真的是解决办法吗？

transcript_json.text: M: You're overstating my point.
transcript_json.translation: M: 你把我的观点说过头了。

transcript_json.text: My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering.
transcript_json.translation: 我的主张是，我们需要把更多预算用在科学和工程这类领域上。

transcript_json.text: To do that, we need to take money from subjects like literature and music.
transcript_json.translation: 要做到这一点，我们就得从文学、音乐这类学科那里挪钱。

transcript_json.text: W: But the arts have value.
transcript_json.translation: W: 但人文学科是有价值的。

transcript_json.text: They're an important part of our culture.
transcript_json.translation: 它们是我们文化的重要组成部分。

transcript_json.text: Studying literature or music or sculpture might not result in a job in that area.
transcript_json.translation: 学习文学、音乐或雕塑，未必能带来那一行的工作。

transcript_json.text: But it helps young people to think about the world in a deeper way, which makes them better citizens and makes for a better society.
transcript_json.translation: 但它有助于年轻人更深地思考世界，这使他们成为更好的公民，也让社会变得更好。

transcript_json.text: M: I agree that the arts are valuable to society, but it's naive to think that not only the most talented, but all students should study them at university level.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我承认人文学科对社会有价值，但认为不仅是最有天分的、而是所有学生都应该在大学阶段学习这些学科，那就太天真了。

transcript_json.text: The odds are very competitive, and most graduates will end up with a great deal of debt, obtaining a degree that has little value on the job market.
transcript_json.translation: 竞争非常激烈，大多数毕业生最终会背上一大笔债，拿到的学位在就业市场上却没什么价值。

transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 1

transcript_json.text: Do you ever have the annoying feeling that you don't have time to really think anymore?
transcript_json.translation: 你有没有过那种烦人的感觉：自己再也没有时间真正地思考了？

transcript_json.text: You're not alone.
transcript_json.translation: 有这种感受的不止你一个。

transcript_json.text: A variety of factors have conspired to rob us of time for reflection on ourselves and our lives.
transcript_json.translation: 种种因素合起伙来，夺走了我们审视自己和生活的反思时间。

transcript_json.text: Preoccupied minds are rarely silent.
transcript_json.translation: 被杂事占满的头脑很少安静。

transcript_json.text: The average person receives hundreds of texts and voice messages a day.
transcript_json.translation: 普通人每天会收到数百条文字和语音消息。

transcript_json.text: And holidays for many of us are action-packed weeks more likely full of family activities than opportunities for tranquility and contemplation.
transcript_json.translation: 对我们许多人来说，假期是行程满满的一周，更可能是被家庭活动填满，而不是宁静与沉思的机会。

transcript_json.text: Regular reflection, however, underlies all great professionals.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，经常性的反思是一切杰出专业人士的根基。

transcript_json.text: It's a prerequisite for you to recharge your mental batteries, see things in a new light and tap into your creativity.
transcript_json.translation: 它是你给精神充电、以新视角看待事物、激发创造力的前提。

transcript_json.text: Almost all of the great advisors that I have studied have found ways to get away from it all and contemplate their life and work.
transcript_json.translation: 我研究过的几乎所有杰出顾问，都找到了抽身出局、沉思自己生活与工作的办法。

transcript_json.text: Some researchers in the field of creativity, in fact, believe that insight occurs during the reflection and relaxation that follows a period of intense activity.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，创造力领域的一些研究者认为，顿悟发生在一段高强度活动之后的反思与放松之中。

transcript_json.text: Schedule your time for reflection about your work or a particular project you're engaged in.
transcript_json.translation: 为你自己的工作或正在参与的某个特定项目安排反思时间。

transcript_json.text: I usually block out half an hour.
transcript_json.translation: 我通常会留出半小时。

transcript_json.text: Don't answer the phone.
transcript_json.translation: 不要接电话。

transcript_json.text: Push your papers to the side.
transcript_json.translation: 把文件推到一边。

transcript_json.text: Sketch, make lists, draw mind maps of ideas that come to you.
transcript_json.translation: 画草图、列清单，把脑海里冒出的想法画成思维导图。

transcript_json.text: At the end, write down any emerging ideas.
transcript_json.translation: 最后，把浮现出来的任何想法写下来。

transcript_json.text: When you're alone, stop worrying and think.
transcript_json.translation: 独处时，别再忧心，去思考。

transcript_json.text: A lot of our downtime is spent worrying about troubles or things in our lives or fantasizing about how we'd like our lives to be.
transcript_json.translation: 我们的许多闲暇时间都花在为生活中的麻烦事担忧，或者幻想自己希望的生活是什么样。

transcript_json.text: Revisit things during moments of relaxation after a period of intense work.
transcript_json.translation: 在一段高强度工作之后的放松时刻，重新回想那些事。

transcript_json.text: This is when we are the most creative.
transcript_json.translation: 这正是我们最有创造力的时候。

transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 2

transcript_json.text: Before Colorado became a state, it already had post offices.
transcript_json.translation: 在科罗拉多建州之前，它就已经有邮局了。

transcript_json.text: The first opened in 1859 in a settlement founded by migrants searching for gold.
transcript_json.translation: 第一家于1859年开设在一个由淘金移民建立的定居点。

transcript_json.text: Life could be unpredictable out west.
transcript_json.translation: 在西部，生活难以预料。

transcript_json.text: Gold failed to appear.
transcript_json.translation: 金子没有出现。

transcript_json.text: Drought ruined farmers, and settlers clashed with Native Americans.
transcript_json.translation: 旱灾毁了农民，定居者与印第安人发生冲突。

transcript_json.text: On the settlement's location now stands a sprawling University campus.
transcript_json.translation: 如今，那个定居点的位置上矗立着一座占地广阔的大学校园。

transcript_json.text: Amid all the changes, one feature remained constant: the postal service.
transcript_json.translation: 在所有这些变迁中，有一点始终不变：邮政服务。

transcript_json.text: The maps tracing America's westward expansion are telling.
transcript_json.translation: 描绘美国西进扩张的地图很能说明问题。

transcript_json.text: In 1864 there were few postal branches on land controlled by Native Americans, which still accounted for most of the West.
transcript_json.translation: 1864年，在印第安人控制的土地上几乎没有邮政分支，而那些土地当时仍占西部的大部分。

transcript_json.text: Over the next 25 years, post offices grew quickly.
transcript_json.translation: 在接下来的25年里，邮局迅速增多。

transcript_json.text: Colonization of the West could be regarded as a result of big government rather than pioneers.
transcript_json.translation: 对西部的开拓可以看作是大政府的功劳，而不是拓荒者的功劳。

transcript_json.text: As federal subsidies and land grants tempted people into the deserts and plains, the post kept them connected.
transcript_json.translation: 联邦补贴和赠地吸引人们进入沙漠和平原，邮政则让他们保持联系。

transcript_json.text: In the mid-19th century, the Post Office Department was far from a centralized bureaucracy.
transcript_json.translation: 在19世纪中叶，邮政部门远不是一个集权化的官僚机构。

transcript_json.text: To keep up with migration patterns, postal services were added to existing businesses.
transcript_json.translation: 为了跟上移民的流动趋势，邮政服务被附加到现有的商户上。

transcript_json.text: The federal government commissioned private wagons to carry the mail.
transcript_json.translation: 联邦政府委托私人马车运送邮件。

transcript_json.text: Short term contracts were granted to local businessmen to act as postmasters.
transcript_json.translation: 当地商人通过短期合同受聘担任邮政局长。

transcript_json.text: These partnerships enabled the mail to quickly follow migrants, helping knit together remote parts of the country.

transcript_json.text: In last week's lecture, we discussed reasons why people forget things.
transcript_json.translation: 在上周的课上，我们讨论了人们遗忘的原因。

transcript_json.text: This week we will discuss a surprising reason why we might remember some things: anxiety.
transcript_json.translation: 本周我们将讨论一个让人记住某些事情的惊人原因：焦虑。

transcript_json.text: Think about something as simple as buying a coffee.
transcript_json.translation: 想想买杯咖啡这么简单的事。

transcript_json.text: That may not seem like an experience that would make a deep impression on your memory.
transcript_json.translation: 这看起来不像会给你留下深刻记忆的经历。

transcript_json.text: But anxiety could change that.
transcript_json.translation: 但焦虑可能会改变这一点。

transcript_json.text: In fact, a new study suggests that people with higher anxiety levels might remember certain information better than people with lower anxiety levels.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，一项新研究表明，焦虑水平较高的人对某些信息的记忆可能比焦虑水平较低的人更好。

transcript_json.text: That's because higher levels of anxiety may make people more susceptible to negative feelings, putting them in a more negative state of mind.
transcript_json.translation: 这是因为较高的焦虑水平可能使人更容易受负面情绪影响，让他们处于更消极的心理状态。

transcript_json.text: That in turn, may make them able to better remember some events.
transcript_json.translation: 这反过来又可能使他们能更好地记住某些事件。

transcript_json.text: Let's take a closer look at that new study now.
transcript_json.translation: 现在我们来仔细看看那项新研究。

transcript_json.text: In this study, the researchers started by giving 80 undergraduate students an anxiety test.
transcript_json.translation: 在这项研究中，研究人员首先对80名本科生进行了焦虑测试。

transcript_json.text: The test measured the participants' anxiety levels over the proceeding two weeks.
transcript_json.translation: 该测试测量了参与者在之前两周内的焦虑水平。

transcript_json.text: Then, to test memory, the participants were shown a series of neutral words one at a time.
transcript_json.translation: 然后，为了测试记忆，参与者被逐个展示一系列中性词汇。

transcript_json.text: Some of the words were printed onto photos of negative scenes, meaning images that could affect their emotions negatively, such as a photo of a car accident, or a cemetery.
transcript_json.translation: 其中一些词印在负面场景的照片上，也就是可能对情绪产生负面影响的照片，比如车祸或墓地的照片。

transcript_json.text: The rest of the words were printed onto photos of neutral scenes, such as a photo of a lake or trees.
transcript_json.translation: 其余的词则印在中性场景的照片上，比如湖泊或树林的照片。

transcript_json.text: Neutral words included words like table or desk that don't elicit emotion.
transcript_json.translation: 中性词包括"桌子"这类不会引发情绪的词。

transcript_json.text: Later, the participants were asked to think back to the words they were shown earlier, which caused them to reenter either a negative or neutral mindset.
transcript_json.translation: 随后，参与者被要求回想之前看到的词，这让他们重新进入负面或中性的心态。

transcript_json.text: The participants were then presented with another set of neutral words, and their memory of these new words was tested.
transcript_json.translation: 接着，向参与者展示另一组中性词，并测试他们对这些新词的记忆。

transcript_json.text: The researchers found that the new words presented to people in a negative mindset were better remembered by people with higher levels of anxiety than those with lower levels of anxiety.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员发现，对于在负面心态下展示的新词，焦虑水平较高的人比焦虑水平较低的人记得更牢。

transcript_json.text: In other words, when highly anxious individuals took in otherwise emotionally neutral information that was presented to them, it became colored by their negative mindset, making them remember the information better.
transcript_json.translation: 换句话说，当高度焦虑的人接收那些本无情绪色彩的中性信息时，这些信息被他们的消极心态染上了色，使他们把信息记得更牢。

transcript_json.text: But these same effects were not seen in people with low levels of anxiety.
transcript_json.translation: 但同样的效应没有出现在焦虑水平低的人身上。

transcript_json.text: Previous studies have found that extreme levels of anxiety such as those experienced by people diagnosed with an anxiety disorder can be quite detrimental to memory and cognitive performance.
transcript_json.translation: 此前的研究发现，极端的焦虑水平——比如被诊断为焦虑症的人所经历的——对记忆和认知表现可能相当有害。

transcript_json.text: But the highly anxious people in this study represent individuals who are managing their anxiety and for whom anxiety is not a serious problem.
transcript_json.translation: 但这项研究中高度焦虑的人，指的是那些能够管理自己焦虑、焦虑对他们来说并不是严重问题的人。

transcript_json.text: Over the past 20 years, the internet has gradually become a dominant feature of our lives.
transcript_json.translation: 过去20年里，互联网已逐渐成为我们生活中的主导性特征。

transcript_json.text: It has changed how we communicate with each other.
transcript_json.translation: 它改变了我们相互交流的方式。

transcript_json.text: And it has definitely transformed the way we do business with each other.
transcript_json.translation: 它也确确实实改变了我们彼此做生意的方式。

transcript_json.text: Marketing has also changed in a number of ways.
transcript_json.translation: 营销也在多个方面发生了变化。

transcript_json.text: For instance, in the past, consumers had to call a phone number and patiently wait on hold in order to get the information they wanted.
transcript_json.translation: 比如，过去消费者得打电话，然后耐心等待接通，才能获得想要的信息。

transcript_json.text: Today, they want the information immediately.
transcript_json.translation: 如今，他们想要立刻获得信息。

transcript_json.text: They'll go to the company's social media pages and post comments and questions expecting to receive an immediate response.
transcript_json.translation: 他们会去公司的社交媒体页面发表评论和提问，期待马上得到回复。

transcript_json.text: If they don't get their questions answered soon, they'll move on to another company that will answer them quickly.
transcript_json.translation: 如果问题没有得到及时解答，他们就会转向另一家能快速回应的公司。

transcript_json.text: Marketing departments today need to follow technological development.
transcript_json.translation: 如今的营销部门需要跟上技术发展。

transcript_json.text: For example, this year's smartphone is smarter than last year's.
transcript_json.translation: 比如，今年的智能手机比去年的更智能。

transcript_json.text: Self-driving cars are now on the road.
transcript_json.translation: 自动驾驶汽车已经上路了。

transcript_json.text: Marketers have to do research on which technologies are coming into being, otherwise, they risk being left behind in the virtual dust.
transcript_json.translation: 营销人员必须研究哪些技术正在兴起，否则就有在虚拟世界的尘埃中被甩在后面的风险。

transcript_json.text: Marketing has also changed due to the importance of video.
transcript_json.translation: 由于视频的重要性，营销也发生了变化。

transcript_json.text: People don't just want to read text.
transcript_json.translation: 人们不再只想读文字。

transcript_json.text: They want to watch things happening.
transcript_json.translation: 他们想看到事情在发生。

transcript_json.text: Companies now have to explore how they can use video on a consistent basis to share information about their businesses.
transcript_json.translation: 公司现在必须探索如何持续利用视频来分享自己业务的信息。

transcript_json.text: Fortunately, it's extremely easy to shoot something these days.
transcript_json.translation: 幸运的是，如今拍点东西极其容易。

transcript_json.text: All you need is a smartphone.
transcript_json.translation: 你只需要一部智能手机。

transcript_json.text: But what's the result of all this?
transcript_json.translation: 但这一切的结果是什么呢？

transcript_json.text: Shorter attention spans?
transcript_json.translation: 注意力持续时间更短了？

transcript_json.text: We aren't the same people that we were 20 years ago.
transcript_json.translation: 我们已经不是20年前的我们了。

transcript_json.text: Not only have we grown accustomed to getting the information we want instantaneously, our attention spans are much shorter.
transcript_json.translation: 我们不仅习惯了即时获得想要的信息，注意力持续的时间也短得多了。

transcript_json.text: If something doesn't capture our attention within a few seconds, we're on to the next piece of content.
transcript_json.translation: 如果一件事几秒钟内抓不住我们的注意力，我们就去看下一条内容了。

transcript_json.text: Marketers need to figure out ways to speak directly to the customer's emotions and they need to figure out how to do that as quickly as possible.
transcript_json.translation: 营销人员需要想出直击顾客情感的方法，而且要尽快想出来。

transcript_json.text: Once people are emotionally engaged, they'll stick with you.
transcript_json.translation: 一旦人们在情感上被调动起来，他们就会一直跟着你。

transcript_json.text: If marketing has changed this much in the past 20 years, imagine what the next 20 years will bring.
transcript_json.translation: 如果过去20年营销发生了这么大的变化，想象一下未来20年会带来什么。

transcript_json.text: In a recent survey, only 9% of marketers could say with confidence that their marketing efforts were actually working.
transcript_json.translation: 在最近的一项调查中，只有9%的营销人员能够自信地说他们的营销努力确实有效。

transcript_json.text: Their confidence is being shaken because the rules of the game change every year.
transcript_json.translation: 他们的信心正在动摇，因为游戏规则每年都在变。

transcript_json.text: That's why it's important for marketers to pay attention to the latest technological developments and consider collaborating with technological innovators.
transcript_json.translation: 这就是为什么营销人员要关注最新的技术发展，并考虑与技术革新者合作。

transcript_json.text: That way, they'll be moving at the same pace as the tech industry.
transcript_json.translation: 这样，他们就能与科技行业保持同步前进。

transcript_json.text: You might be surprised to learn that the benefits of friendships extend beyond people's social life and into their work, which is interesting when you consider the extent to which people sacrifice friendships, or at least the time they spend with friends because of the extra hours they're devoting to work.
transcript_json.translation: 你可能会惊讶地发现，友谊的好处不仅延伸到人们的社交生活，还延伸到工作中。想到人们为了工作多投入的那些时间，在多大程度上牺牲了友谊、或至少牺牲了与朋友相处的时光，这一点就格外有意思。

transcript_json.text: Just last week, I was remarking to a colleague that I'm content with only one social engagement per week.
transcript_json.translation: 就在上周，我还跟一位同事说，我每周只有一次社交活动就很满足了。

transcript_json.text: But according to recent research, that's evidently not enough.
transcript_json.translation: 但根据最近的研究，这显然还不够。

transcript_json.text: In an initial study of more than 700 respondents, scholars from an American university analyzed the impact that friends, as opposed to family, have on self-esteem and well-being.
transcript_json.translation: 在一项对700多名受访者的初步研究中，一所美国大学的学者分析了朋友（相对于家人）对自尊和幸福感的影响。

transcript_json.text: Friends came out substantially on top.
transcript_json.translation: 朋友的影响明显更胜一筹。

transcript_json.text: That's because to be someone's mate is a voluntary act.
transcript_json.translation: 这是因为做一个人的朋友是一种自愿行为。

transcript_json.text: Unlike family who people rarely get to choose.
transcript_json.translation: 而家人则很少能由人自己选择。

transcript_json.text: The researchers found that when people choose to cultivate and maintain supportive friendships with an individual, it means that the person is valued and worthy of their limited time.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员发现，当人们选择与某个人培养并维持相互支持的友谊时，这意味着这个人受到重视、值得他们付出有限的时间。

transcript_json.text: Such sentiments of value and worthiness boost our self-esteem.
transcript_json.translation: 这种被重视、被认可的感觉会提升我们的自尊。

transcript_json.text: The second study comprised more than 300 participants.
transcript_json.translation: 第二项研究有300多名参与者。

transcript_json.text: It proved that the better we feel about ourselves, the more likely we will perform our job confidently and competently.
transcript_json.translation: 研究证明，我们对自己的感觉越好，就越有可能自信而胜任地完成工作。

transcript_json.text: This follow-up study found that non-work friends even improved people's job satisfaction.
transcript_json.translation: 这项后续研究发现，工作之外的朋友甚至能提高人们的工作满意度。

transcript_json.text: They have as much of an impact on how much they love their jobs, as do the friends they have at work, despite not actually being at our place of work.
transcript_json.translation: 他们虽然并不出现在我们的工作场所，但对人们热爱自己工作程度的影响，和职场朋友一样大。

transcript_json.text: These types of friends tend to be our preferred outlet for complaining about work-related matters.
transcript_json.translation: 这类朋友往往是我们抱怨工作相关事情时的首选倾诉对象。

transcript_json.text: This is an avenue that may not be available at the office.
transcript_json.translation: 这种渠道在办公室里可能并不存在。

transcript_json.text: So even though friendships can be easy to neglect when confronted by pressures at work, or even pressures at home, neglecting our friends can turn out to be harmful and counterproductive.
transcript_json.translation: 所以，尽管面对工作压力甚至家庭压力时友谊容易被忽视，忽视朋友最终可能有害无益、适得其反。

transcript_json.text: That's why when determining how to create a better work-life balance, we need to consider not only how to balance work and family demands, but also how to cultivate and sustain supportive friendships.
transcript_json.translation: 这就是为什么在决定如何更好地平衡工作与生活时，我们不仅要考虑如何平衡工作与家庭需求，还要考虑如何培养和维系相互支持的友谊。

transcript_json.text: It's for employees for flexible work arrangements.
transcript_json.translation: 这对申请弹性工作安排的员工来说也是如此。

transcript_json.text: It's irrelevant whether their need for a desired schedule is due to say, parenting responsibilities, or a craving to hang out with their best mate.
transcript_json.translation: 他们想要某种日程安排，是出于抚养孩子的责任，还是想跟最好的朋友聚一聚，这并不重要。

transcript_json.text: What matters is the opportunity to engage in a nourishing activity outside of work.
transcript_json.translation: 重要的是有机会在工作之外从事一种滋养身心的活动。

transcript_json.text: That will definitely have a follow-on effect at work.
transcript_json.translation: 这肯定会在工作中产生后续的积极影响。

transcript_json.text: Adventure sports are undeniably attractive to many energetic and thrill-seeking kids.
transcript_json.translation: 不可否认，探险运动对许多精力充沛、追求刺激的孩子很有吸引力。

transcript_json.text: Sports like rock climbing, surfing, skiing, and mountain biking, thus have lots of appeal.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，攀岩、冲浪、滑雪和山地自行车这类运动非常有吸引力。

transcript_json.text: They don't have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports, but they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity.
transcript_json.translation: 它们没有传统团队运动那么多的规则和压力，却保留了户外体育活动的种种好处。

transcript_json.text: When properly supervised, extreme sports can be a part of a healthy, balanced life.
transcript_json.translation: 在有适当监护的情况下，极限运动可以成为健康平衡生活的一部分。

transcript_json.text: Some adventure sports may be associated with higher risks of injury, so it's important for kids to figure out when to take risks, and when not to.
transcript_json.translation: 有些探险运动可能伴随较高的受伤风险，所以孩子要学会分辨什么时候该冒险、什么时候不该，这一点很重要。

transcript_json.text: Risk-free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears.
transcript_json.translation: 毫无风险的活动会剥夺孩子考验自己、克服恐惧的机会。

transcript_json.text: But, to some, these very risks are what makes these sports a bad choice.
transcript_json.translation: 但对有些人来说，恰恰是这些风险让这类运动成为糟糕的选择。

transcript_json.text: They say that extreme sports can often lead to devastating injuries, especially as young thrill seekers may attempt feats that are too advanced for them.
transcript_json.translation: 他们说，极限运动常常导致严重的伤害，尤其是年轻的刺激追求者可能会尝试对他们来说过于高难的动作。

transcript_json.text: But let's be real.
transcript_json.translation: 但我们要面对现实。

transcript_json.text: Most kids do all kinds of dangerous stuff whether you want them to or not.
transcript_json.translation: 不管你愿不愿意，大多数孩子都会做各种危险的事。

transcript_json.text: Adventure sports have many of the same risks and dangers.
transcript_json.translation: 探险运动也有许多同样的风险和危险。

transcript_json.text: But, they have an additional sense of adventure, courage and autonomy that is important to foster in young children.
transcript_json.translation: 但它们还多了一种冒险、勇气和自主的意识，而这种意识对培养小孩子很重要。

transcript_json.text: As always, it's up to parents to decide what's best for their kids.
transcript_json.translation: 一如既往，什么对孩子最好要由父母来决定。

transcript_json.text: But, if you do decide that adventure sports are a bit too much, do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives.
transcript_json.translation: 但如果你确实觉得探险运动有点过头，那也请把其他形式的户外探险引入孩子的生活。

transcript_json.text: Camping under the stars, fishing, stargazing, or even just playing in the woods can help a lot in building the same sense of self-confidence and risk-taking as in adventure sports.
transcript_json.translation: 在星空下露营、钓鱼、观星，甚至只是在树林里玩耍，都有助于培养与探险运动相同的自信感和冒险精神。

transcript_json.text: The shiny gadgets of today will be waste tomorrow.
transcript_json.translation: 今天闪亮的电子产品，明天就会变成垃圾。

transcript_json.text: Manufacturers don't talk much about this when they announce the big new thing that will replace your mostly just as good old thing.
transcript_json.translation: 厂商宣布用全新的大热门取代你那件其实还一样好用的旧设备时，很少谈到这一点。

transcript_json.text: In fact, technology firms often purposely design devices that will not last long and cannot be repaired so that consumers will have to spend their money on a new one.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，科技公司常常故意把设备设计得不耐用、修不了，好让消费者不得不花钱买新的。

transcript_json.text: This year, the French government began requiring tech manufacturers to list a repairability score.
transcript_json.translation: 今年，法国政府开始要求科技厂商标注可维修性评分。

transcript_json.text: If a device can be repaired, then its life can be extended, saving consumers money and the planet the burden of so many trashed gadgets.
transcript_json.translation: 如果设备能修，寿命就能延长，既为消费者省钱，也减轻地球承受大量废弃电子产品的负担。

transcript_json.text: Equipped with this knowledge, consumers can make better choices about which products to buy.
transcript_json.translation: 有了这个信息，消费者就能更好地选择该买什么产品。

transcript_json.text: Some 59 million tons of old TVs, computers, screens, smartphones, washers and other electronics are discarded every year.
transcript_json.translation: 每年大约有 5900 万吨旧电视、电脑、屏幕、智能手机、洗衣机和其他电子产品被丢弃。

transcript_json.text: This waste is dangerous.
transcript_json.translation: 这些垃圾很危险。

transcript_json.text: Batteries explode in recycling facilities.
transcript_json.translation: 电池会在回收设施里爆炸。

transcript_json.text: Toxic substances like mercury leak into soil and groundwater and disperse in the air.
transcript_json.translation: 汞等有毒物质会渗入土壤和地下水，并扩散到空气中。

transcript_json.text: Manufacturing flat screens adds greenhouse gases to the atmosphere.
transcript_json.translation: 制造平板屏幕会向大气排放温室气体。

transcript_json.text: We need tech companies to take the lead to solve this problem.
transcript_json.translation: 我们需要科技公司带头解决这个问题。

transcript_json.text: If they won't, governments must make them do so.
transcript_json.translation: 如果它们不愿意，政府就必须强制它们这么做。

transcript_json.text: Although tech companies will often speak of environmental sustainability, many lobby against repair legislation, fearful it will eat into their profits.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管科技公司常常把环境可持续挂在嘴边，许多公司却游说反对维修立法，生怕它侵蚀自己的利润。

transcript_json.text: Sustainability matters, but marketable design appears to matter more to these companies.
transcript_json.translation: 可持续固然重要，但对这些公司来说，好卖的设计似乎更重要。

transcript_json.text: Consumers should support right-to-repair legislation.
transcript_json.translation: 消费者应当支持维修权立法。

transcript_json.text: In this world, damage is a certainty.
transcript_json.translation: 在这个世界上，损坏在所难免。

transcript_json.text: But we cannot leave things broken: A problem of our creation is a problem that can be fixed.
transcript_json.translation: 但我们不能放任东西坏下去：由我们造成的问题，是可以修复的。

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 1
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 1

transcript_json.text: On average, U.S. workers spend about 10% of their workday surfing the internet, emailing friends or shopping online.
transcript_json.translation: 平均而言，美国上班族每天约有 10% 的工作时间在上网冲浪、给朋友发邮件或网上购物。

transcript_json.text: This behavior, called cyberloafing, is believed to cost employers up to $85 billion a year in lost productivity.
transcript_json.translation: 这种行为被称为"网络摸鱼"，据信每年让雇主因生产力损失而付出高达 850 亿美元的代价。

transcript_json.text: The majority of cyberloafing research focuses on ways to prevent employees from engaging in this behavior through interventions such as internet monitoring and computer use policies.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数关于网络摸鱼的研究，都集中在通过网络监控、计算机使用规定等干预手段防止员工实施这种行为上。

transcript_json.text: But it turns out, such behaviors may not be a sign that a worker is lazy or just wasting time.
transcript_json.translation: 但事实证明，这类行为未必说明员工懒惰或纯粹在浪费时间。

transcript_json.text: Social media use at work has been linked to higher levels of employee engagement and job satisfaction.
transcript_json.translation: 工作时段使用社交媒体，被发现与更高的员工投入度和工作满意度相关。

transcript_json.text: New research suggests cyberloafing can help workers cope with an exceptionally stressful work environment.
transcript_json.translation: 新研究表明，网络摸鱼可以帮助员工应对压力极大的工作环境。

transcript_json.text: But is cyberloafing actually effective at reducing employee stress levels?
transcript_json.translation: 但网络摸鱼真的能有效降低员工的压力水平吗？

transcript_json.text: That's the question my research team wanted to answer in our new study.
transcript_json.translation: 这正是我的研究团队想在新研究中回答的问题。

transcript_json.text: Our hypothesis was that cyberloafing may serve as a mini-break, giving employees an opportunity to recover from stressful work situations.
transcript_json.translation: 我们的假设是：网络摸鱼可以充当一次小憩，让员工有机会从紧张的工作状态中恢复过来。

transcript_json.text: To test this, we asked workers to complete an online survey and rank how much time they spent cyberloafing, checking non-work emails and shopping.
transcript_json.translation: 为验证这一点，我们请上班族填写一份在线调查，评估他们花在网络摸鱼、查看非工作邮件和购物上的时间有多少。

transcript_json.text: We also asked them to rank job satisfaction, their desire to quit, and how often they've experienced mistreatment at work, such as being bullied, threatened or yelled at.
transcript_json.translation: 我们还请他们评估工作满意度、辞职意愿，以及在工作中遭受苛待的频率，比如被欺负、被威胁或被吼。

transcript_json.text: As you might expect, we found that overall, more mistreatment at work was correlated with lower levels of job satisfaction and a greater desire to quit.
transcript_json.translation: 和你预期的一样，我们发现总体而言，职场中遭受的苛待越多，工作满意度越低，离职的意愿越强。

transcript_json.text: More interestingly, we found that cyberloafing effectively buffered this connection.
transcript_json.translation: 更有意思的是，我们发现“网络摸鱼”能有效缓冲这一关联。

transcript_json.text: That is, mistreated workers who spent more time surfing the web and checking emails reported higher job satisfaction and were less likely to want to quit than similar participants who didn't cyberloaf as much.
transcript_json.translation: 也就是说，与上网、查邮件时间较少的类似受试者相比，遭受苛待但花更多时间上网查邮件的员工报告的工作满意度更高，也不太想辞职。

transcript_json.text: This suggests that cyberloafing acts as a sort of relief valve for workers, helping them recover from stressful experiences.
transcript_json.translation: 这表明，网络摸鱼对员工来说就像一个减压阀，帮助他们从紧张的经历中恢复。

transcript_json.text: While we did not directly assess how cyberloafing affects worker performance, we believe by relieving stress it may not only reduce worker turnover, but also ultimately bolster productivity.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然我们没有直接评估网络摸鱼如何影响员工绩效，但我们相信，通过缓解压力，它不仅能减少员工流失，最终还可能提升生产力。

transcript_json.text: This fits with other recent research that suggests taking short breaks is associated with higher levels of daily job performance.
transcript_json.translation: 这与近期其他研究相符，那些研究表明短暂休息与更高的日常工作绩效相关。

transcript_json.text: That isn't to say cyberloafing is always good.
transcript_json.translation: 这并不是说网络摸鱼总是好事。

transcript_json.text: Too much time spent on non-work activities likely causes performance to suffer.
transcript_json.translation: 花太多时间在非工作活动上，很可能会拖累绩效。

transcript_json.text: All in all, managers should be more lenient with employees.
transcript_json.translation: 总而言之，管理者对员工应该更宽容一些。

transcript_json.text: We believe a bit of online shopping or surfing the internet at work could make workers more productive in the long run.
transcript_json.translation: 我们相信，工作时上一点网、买点东西，从长远看反而能让员工更有生产力。

transcript_json.text: When Julius Morton moved to Nebraska City in 1854, he faced a problem shared by many settlers in the territory: It was a treeless plain.
transcript_json.translation: 1854 年，朱利叶斯·莫顿搬到内布拉斯

transcript_json.text: That meant no trees for building materials, or for fuel.
transcript_json.translation: 加州城时，他面临着一个当地许多定居者共有

transcript_json.text: But Morton was one of the world's first conservationists, stating, "For prosperity, we ought to plant as many forests as we have exhausted and consumed".
transcript_json.translation: 的难题：那是一片寸树不生的平原。这意味着

transcript_json.text: So he started planting trees, beginning with his own land.
transcript_json.translation: 既没有树用作建筑材料，也没有树可当燃料。

transcript_json.text: By 1860 Morton possessed a forest of more than 300 trees.
transcript_json.translation: 到 1860 年，莫顿已拥有一片 300 多棵树的林子。

transcript_json.text: A few years later, he had more than 1,000.
transcript_json.translation: 几年后，他的树超过了 1000 棵。

transcript_json.text: As the forest grew, so did Morton's influence in Nebraska.
transcript_json.translation: 随着这片林子长大，莫顿在内布拉斯加州的影响力也越来越大。

transcript_json.text: This was largely because Morton founded the Nebraska City News, the state's first newspaper, in which he frequently wrote editorials about the practical and aesthetic benefits of tree planting.
transcript_json.translation: 这在很大程度上是因为莫顿创办了该州第一份报纸《内布拉斯加城新闻》，并经常在上面发表社论，论述种树在实用和美观上的好处。

transcript_json.text: He also organized the Nebraska State Gardening Society and served on the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture.
transcript_json.translation: 这在很大程度上是因为莫顿创办了该州第一份报纸《内布拉斯加州城新闻报》，并经常在上面发表社论，宣扬植树在实用和美观上的好

transcript_json.text: While serving on the Board, Morton came up with an idea to spread his belief in tree planting statewide.
transcript_json.translation: 处。他还组建了内布拉斯加州园艺协会，并在州农业委员会任职。在委员会任职期间，莫顿想出了一个把植树理念推广到全州的点子。

transcript_json.text: On January 4, 1872, Morton drafted a resolution that April 10 be designated a day for the planting of trees in the State of Nebraska and urged people to go out and plant trees themselves.
transcript_json.translation: 1872 年 1 月 4 日，莫顿起草了一项决议，提议将 4 月 10 日定为内布拉斯加州的植树日，并敦促人们亲自出门种树。

transcript_json.text: Morton called the special event Arbor Day as "arbor" is Latin for "tree".
transcript_json.translation: 莫顿把这个特别的日子称为"植树节"（Arbor Day），因为 arbor 在拉丁语中意为"树"。

transcript_json.text: The state government agreed.
transcript_json.translation: 州政府同意了。

transcript_json.text: And on April 10, 1872, the first unofficial Arbor Day was celebrated throughout Nebraska.
transcript_json.translation: 1872 年 4 月 10 日，首个非官方植树节在整个内布拉斯加州举行。

transcript_json.text: Prizes were awarded to counties, cities, and individuals who planted the largest number of trees.
transcript_json.translation: 种树最多的县、城市和个人获得了奖励。

transcript_json.text: That day, an astounding one million trees were planted in Nebraska—an average of more than six for every man, woman and child in the state.
transcript_json.translation: 那一天，内布拉斯加州种下了惊人的 100 万棵树——平均全州男女老少每人超过 6 棵。

transcript_json.text: Since 1885, Nebraska has planted more than 700,000 acres of trees, earning it the nickname "the Tree Planters State".
transcript_json.translation: 自 1885 年以来，内布拉斯加州已种植了 70 多万英亩的树木，因此赢得了"植树者之州"的绰号。

transcript_json.text: Arbor Day became a legal, civic holiday in the state in 1885.
transcript_json.translation: 自 1885 年以来，内布拉斯加州已植树 70 多万英亩，赢得了“植树者之州”的绰号。

transcript_json.text: It was held on April 22—Julius Morton's birthday.
transcript_json.translation: 1885 年，植树节成为该州的法定公民节日，定在 4 月 22 日——朱利叶斯·莫顿的生日。

transcript_json.text: In addition to a parade in Nebraska City, Morton introduced what has since become a long-standing Arbor Day tradition: Schoolchildren went outside and planted trees together.
transcript_json.translation: 除了在内布拉斯加城举行游行，莫顿还开创了一项延续至今的植树节传统：学生们到户外一起种树。

transcript_json.text: In 1970, nearly a century after Arbor Day was first celebrated, President Richard Nixon declared the last Friday of every April to be observed as National Arbor Day.
transcript_json.translation: 1970 年，在首个植树节过后近一个世纪，理查德·尼克松总统宣布将每年 4 月的最后一个星期五定为全国植树节。

transcript_json.text: All 50 states recognize the April observance, although many hold an additional state Arbor Day in a month more suited to local tree planting.
transcript_json.translation: 全部 50 个州都认可 4 月的植树节，不过许多州还会在更适合当地植树的月份再过一次州植树节。

transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: Modern humans arose in Africa about 200,000 years ago.
transcript_json.translation: 现代人大约 20 万年前起源

transcript_json.text: They then spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago.
transcript_json.translation: 于非洲，随后在 6 万年前

transcript_json.text: This is the "Out of Africa" model, as it's commonly known.
transcript_json.translation: 的某个时候扩散到欧洲和亚洲。

transcript_json.text: In the 1990s, the hypothesis found widespread acceptance.
transcript_json.translation: 20 世纪 90 年代，这一假说得到了广泛接受。

transcript_json.text: But this popular idea is in need of revision, particularly given the number of important findings across Asia over the past few decades.
transcript_json.translation: 但这一流行的观点需要修正，尤其是考虑到过去几十年亚洲各地的众多重要发现。

transcript_json.text: For instance, many new human fossils found, particularly in China, are now dated as older than 60,000 years.
transcript_json.translation: 例如，新发现的许多人骨化石——尤以中国为多——现在测定的年代都超过 6 万年。

transcript_json.text: This calls into question the idea that modern humans migrated out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.
transcript_json.translation: 这让"现代人类仅在 6 万年前才迁出非洲"的观点受到质疑。

transcript_json.text: Take the recent discovery of two modern human teeth found in the Luna cave in China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
transcript_json.translation: 就拿最近在中国广西壮族自治区的 Luna 洞里发现的两颗现代人牙齿来说。

transcript_json.text: When my research team and I dated these teeth, we found they were more than 70,000 years old—a situation clearly impossible if modern humans moved out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.
transcript_json.translation: 我和研究团队对这些牙齿测年后发现，它们有 7 万多年的历史——如果现代人只是在 6 万年前才走出非洲，这种情况显然不可能。

transcript_json.text: So with such findings, what happened exactly?
transcript_json.translation: 那么，面对这些发现，实际情况究竟是怎样的？

transcript_json.text: Where does the most current data suggest we came from?
transcript_json.translation: 最新的数据表明我们来自哪里？

transcript_json.text: The first question we should ask is why did modern humans leave Africa to begin with?
transcript_json.translation: 我们该问的第一个问题是：现代人类当初为什么要离开非洲？

transcript_json.text: If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment and has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move or change.
transcript_json.translation: 如果一个族群已经完全适应了特定环境，又有丰富的资源可用，那其实没有理由迁徙或改变。

transcript_json.text: For instance, some monkeys in Africa have a set of teeth that has hardly changed over the course of millions of years, indicating that they found a place that has worked for them.
transcript_json.translation: 例如，非洲的某些猴子，其牙齿在数百万年间几乎没有变化，说明它们找到了一个适合自己的地方。

transcript_json.text: So what happened with humans?
transcript_json.translation: 那人类是怎么一回事？

transcript_json.text: Some researchers have suggested that population density increased to the point where smaller human groups were forced to explore new lands.
transcript_json.translation: 一些研究人员认为，人口密度增长到了一定程度，迫使较小的人类群体去探索新的土地。

transcript_json.text: Other researchers have suggested that due to major environmental events in East Africa, humans were prompted to find greener pastures.
transcript_json.translation: 另一些研究人员认为，由于东非发生了重大环境变故，人类被迫去寻找更宜居的地方。

transcript_json.text: Yet another explanation could simply be that early modern human hunters were following the large animals that they relied on, and so they moved out of Africa without realizing that they were actually moving from one continent to another.
transcript_json.translation: 还有一种解释可能很简单：早期现代人类猎手是在追踪他们赖以生存的大型动物，因此走出了非洲，却没意识到自己实际上是从一个大陆迁移到了另一个大陆。

transcript_json.text: Humans need daily access to reliable fresh water, which appears to be absent from many coastal areas.
transcript_json.translation: 人类每天都需要可靠的淡水来源，而许多沿海地区似乎并不具备。

transcript_json.text: This brings us to another question: by which route did modern humans move out of Africa?
transcript_json.translation: 这就引出了另一个问题：现代人类是通过哪条路线走出非洲的？

transcript_json.text: No clear routes across the Mediterranean from North Africa appear to be present, so the earlier dispersals out of Africa and into Europe and Asia might have been across the Arabian Peninsula.
transcript_json.translation: 从北非横渡地中海似乎并无清晰的路线，因此早期走出非洲、进入欧洲和亚洲的扩散，可能是经阿拉伯半岛完成的。

transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 1

transcript_json.text: M: Hello, Doctor.
transcript_json.translation: M: 你好，医生。

transcript_json.text: W: Hello, please take a seat.
transcript_json.translation: W: 你好，请坐。

transcript_json.text: I have your test results here, and it's good news.
transcript_json.translation: 你的检查结

transcript_json.text: The blood test came back clear.
transcript_json.translation: 果在这儿，是

transcript_json.text: There is no indication of any digestive issues.
transcript_json.translation: 个好消息。

transcript_json.text: M: So then, why do I feel so poorly all the time?
transcript_json.translation: M: 那为什么我一直觉得这么难受？

transcript_json.text: W: It's probably due to overwork and stress.
transcript_json.translation: W: 可能是过度劳累和压力造成的。

transcript_json.text: M: No, it can't be.
transcript_json.translation: M: 不，不可能。

transcript_json.text: I've always been working hard, but I've never felt stress.
transcript_json.translation: 我一直工作很拼命，但从没感觉到压力。

transcript_json.text: Other people suffer and complain about that, but I don't.
transcript_json.translation: 别人会为此痛苦、抱怨，但我不会。

transcript_json.text: It must be something else.
transcript_json.translation: 肯定是别的原因。

transcript_json.text: W: What you have just described is a common sentiment.
transcript_json.translation: W: 你刚才说的这种想法很常见。

transcript_json.text: Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognize it.
transcript_json.translation: 许多承受着压力的人自己却意识不到。

transcript_json.text: You told me you often work long into the night, right?
transcript_json.translation: 你跟我说过你经常工作到深夜，对吧？

transcript_json.text: M: Yes, most days in fact.
transcript_json.translation: M: 是的，实际上大多数日子都如此。

transcript_json.text: But I've been doing that for about 20 years now.
transcript_json.translation: 可这种事我已经做了差不多 20 年了。

transcript_json.text: W: That doesn't matter.
transcript_json.translation: W: 那不要紧。

transcript_json.text: You could have been suffering from stress for 20 years without knowing it.
transcript_json.translation: 你可能 20 年来一直承受着压力而不自知。

transcript_json.text: And now it's catching up to you.
transcript_json.translation: 现在它开始找上门了。

transcript_json.text: M: But what about my feeling tired all the time, and not being able to sleep well at night?
transcript_json.translation: M: 那我总感觉疲倦、晚上睡不好又是怎么回事？

transcript_json.text: W: Those are common consequences of stress.
transcript_json.translation: W: 这些都是压力的常见后果。

transcript_json.text: And if you don't sleep well, then of course you will feel fatigued.
transcript_json.translation: 而且睡不好，你当然会感到疲乏。

transcript_json.text: I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you.
transcript_json.translation: 我给你开一些特别的安眠药。

transcript_json.text: They have a soft, gentle effect, and are made from natural ingredients.
transcript_json.translation: 它们药性温和，由天然成分制成。

transcript_json.text: So your stomach should tolerate them fine, and there shouldn't be any negative side effects.
transcript_json.translation: 所以你的胃应该能承受，也不该有什么不良副作用。

transcript_json.text: Take one with your dinner, and come see me after a month.
transcript_json.translation: 晚饭时吃一片，一个月后再来复诊。

transcript_json.text: If there is no improvement, I'll give you something stronger.
transcript_json.translation: 如果没有好转，我再给你开药效强一些的。

transcript_json.text: M: Thank you, Doctor.
transcript_json.translation: M: 谢谢您，医生。

transcript_json.text: W: That's not all.
transcript_json.translation: W: 还不止这些。

transcript_json.text: You should try and work less.
transcript_json.translation: 你应该尽量少工作一点。

transcript_json.text: Is there any way you can decrease your workload?
transcript_json.translation: 有没有办法减少你的工作量？

transcript_json.text: M: Um, I'd have to think about it.
transcript_json.translation: M: 呃，我得想想。

transcript_json.text: I'm a restaurant manager, and this industry is very competitive.
transcript_json.translation: 我是一名餐厅经理，这个行业竞争非常激烈。

transcript_json.text: There are many things to keep track of and stay on top of.
transcript_json.translation: 有许多事情要跟进、要打理妥当。

transcript_json.text: W: I recommend you think about delegating some responsibilities to someone else.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我建议你考虑把一些职责分给别人。

transcript_json.text: I'm not asking you to retire, just to slow down a bit.
transcript_json.translation: 我不是让你退休，只是让你慢下来一点。

transcript_json.text: It's for your own health.
transcript_json.translation: 这是为了你自己的健康。

transcript_json.text: CONVERSATION 2
transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 2

transcript_json.text: W: Today on People in the News, our guest is John Williams.
transcript_json.translation: W: 今天的《新闻人物》节目，我们的嘉宾是约翰·威廉姆斯。

transcript_json.text: The name may not sound familiar to you, but John was once an acclaimed basketball player.
transcript_json.translation: 这个名字你听着可能不耳熟，但约翰曾是一位广受好评的篮球运动员。

transcript_json.text: John, you stunned fans by leaving the sport at just 25.
transcript_json.translation: 约翰，你在年仅 25 岁时离开赛场，让球迷震惊不已。

transcript_json.text: Why did you retire so early?
transcript_json.translation: 你为什么这么早退役？

transcript_json.text: M: Meg, I loved being an athlete, but I didn't love being a celebrity.
transcript_json.translation: M: 梅格，我喜欢当运动员，但不喜欢当名人。

transcript_json.text: I was in the limelight when I was still a high school student, and went professional right after high school graduation, which was a mistake.
transcript_json.translation: 我还是高中生时就已身处聚光灯下，高中一毕业就转入职业，这是个错误。

transcript_json.text: I was a shy kid, and I wasn't ready for all the media attention.
transcript_json.translation: 我是个害羞的孩子，还没准备好面对铺天盖地的媒体关注。

transcript_json.text: W: But walking away from millions of dollars at the height of your career?
transcript_json.translation: W: 可你在职业生涯的巅峰期放弃了数百万美元？

transcript_json.text: Most people wouldn't be able to resist the lure of such a high salary.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数人无法抗拒这么高薪水的诱惑。

transcript_json.text: When you left the sport, there was speculation that you were having issues with your teammates, or even an injury.
transcript_json.translation: 你退役的时候，外界纷纷猜测是你和队友有矛盾，甚至说是受伤了。

transcript_json.text: M: Not at all.
transcript_json.translation: M: 完全不是。

transcript_json.text: It was hard to quit.
transcript_json.translation: 只是退出很难。

transcript_json.text: I was tempted to stay in the game, because I loved basketball, and I loved my team.
transcript_json.translation: 我也很想继续打下去，因为我热爱篮球，也热爱我的球队。

transcript_json.text: As for money, I turned professional at 18, so I'd actually earned a lot and saved most of it, because I had great financial advisors.
transcript_json.translation: 至于钱，我 18 岁就转入职业，所以其实已经挣了很多，而且存下了大部分，因为我有很棒的理财顾问。

transcript_json.text: I knew basketball wasn't a career with a lot of longevity for most players.
transcript_json.translation: 我知道对大多数球员来说，篮球并不是能干很久的职业。

transcript_json.text: So I wanted to change careers while I was still young.
transcript_json.translation: 所以我想趁还年轻就转行。

transcript_json.text: W: Okay, that was 20 years ago, and you're back in the news.
transcript_json.translation: W: 好的，那是 20 年前的事了，而你又回到了新闻里。

transcript_json.text: You've created a foundation that works to get more kids playing team sports.
transcript_json.translation: 你创立了一个基金会，致力于让更多孩子参加团队运动。为什么呢？

transcript_json.text: Why?
transcript_json.translation: 你创立了一个基金会，致力于让更多孩子参加团队运动。为什么呢？

transcript_json.text: M: I went to university, and I studied public health and learned about the seriousness of the obesity epidemic, particularly among kids and adolescents in poor communities.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我上了大学，学的是公共卫生，了解到肥胖问题的严重性，尤其是在贫困社区的儿童和青少年当中。

transcript_json.text: I've spent the last two decades trying to alleviate the problem.
transcript_json.translation: 过去 20 年我一直在努力缓解这个问题。

transcript_json.text: The Foundation is just the latest attempt.
transcript_json.translation: 这个基金会只是最新的尝试。

transcript_json.text: W: The Foundation uses private donations to support basketball teams for girls and boys in primary school, right?
transcript_json.translation: W: 基金会用私人捐款来支持小学男生和女生的篮球队，对吧？

transcript_json.text: M: Actually, we support teams for secondary school students, too.
transcript_json.translation: M: 其实，我们也资助中学生的

transcript_json.text: And also have some public funding.
transcript_json.translation: 运动队，另外还有一些公共拨款。

transcript_json.text: Kate Atkinson was born in York, England in 1951.
transcript_json.translation: 凯特·阿特金森 1951 年出生于英国约克。

transcript_json.text: She worked hard to gain her credentials as an author.
transcript_json.translation: 她为获得作家的资历付出了艰苦努力。

transcript_json.text: She studied English literature at University in Scotland.
transcript_json.translation: 她在苏格兰的大学学习英国文学。

transcript_json.text: After graduating in 1974, she researched a doctorate on American literature.
transcript_json.translation: 1974 年毕业后，她从事美国文学方向的博士研究。

transcript_json.text: Later, she taught at the university she graduated from, and began writing short stories in 1981.
transcript_json.translation: 后来，她在自己毕业的大学任教，并于 1981 年开始写短篇小说。

transcript_json.text: She began writing for women's magazines after winning the 1986 Women's Own Short Story Competition.
transcript_json.translation: 在赢得 1986 年《女性天地》短篇小说比赛后，她开始为女性杂志撰稿。

transcript_json.text: Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award.
transcript_json.translation: 她的首部小说《博物馆幕后》获得了 1995 年英国年度图书奖。

transcript_json.text: The book is set in Yorkshire and has been adapted for radio, theatre, and TV.
transcript_json.translation: 这本书以约克郡为背景，已被改编成广播剧、话剧和电视剧。

transcript_json.text: She has written two plays for a theatre in Edinburgh.
transcript_json.translation: 她为爱丁堡的一家剧院写过两部剧本。

transcript_json.text: The first was called Abandonment and the second, Nice, performed as part of the Edinburgh Festival in August 2000.
transcript_json.translation: 第一部叫《遗弃》，第二部《美好》于 2000 年 8 月作为爱丁堡艺术节的一部分上演。

transcript_json.text: Whatever genre Atkinson writes in, her books touch on the themes of love and loss and how to carry on.
transcript_json.translation: 无论阿特金森写哪种体裁，她的书都触及爱与失去以及如何继续前行这些主题。

transcript_json.text: They are always presented with ingenuity and a wicked sense of humor.
transcript_json.translation: 这些主题总是以匠心独运的方式呈现，还带着一种狡黠的幽默感。

transcript_json.text: Her books tend to be populated by odd, sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentrics who become credible by virtue of being so fully realized.
transcript_json.translation: 她的书里往往满是古怪、有时带点罪过、总体上不完美的人物，这些人因为刻画得极其饱满而显得真实可信。

transcript_json.text: Her books have frequently been described as comedies of manners.
transcript_json.translation: 她的书常被描述为世态喜剧。

transcript_json.text: That is to say, comedies that represent the complex and sophisticated code of behavior current in fashionable circles of society, where appearances count more than true moral character.
transcript_json.translation: 也就是说，这类喜剧表现的是上流时髦圈子里复杂精微的行为准则，在那里，表面形象比真正的道德品质更重要。

transcript_json.text: A comedy of manners tends to reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds.
transcript_json.translation: 世态喜剧往往让机智而狡诈的角色得到好处，而不是惩罚他们的恶行。

transcript_json.text: The humor of a comedy of manners relies on verbal wit and playful teasing.
transcript_json.translation: 世态喜剧的幽默依靠的是语言上的机锋和俏皮的调侃。

transcript_json.text: Why is adaptability an important skill to exercise in the workplace?
transcript_json.translation: 为什么适应力是职场中需要锻炼的一项重要技能？

transcript_json.text: Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for.
transcript_json.translation: 简单来说，适应力是雇主越来越看重的一项技能。

transcript_json.text: When you spend time learning a new task rather than resisting it, your productivity goes up.
transcript_json.translation: 当你肯花时间学习一项新任务而不是抗拒它时，你的效率就会提高。

transcript_json.text: You can also serve as an example to your coworkers who may be having trouble adapting, and can help lead your team forward.
transcript_json.translation: 你还可以为那些适应困难的同事树立榜样，并帮助带领团队前进。

transcript_json.text: Strategy consultant, Dorie Clark, explains it to us this way: "I'd say that adaptability is an important skill in the workplace because, frankly, circumstances change—competitors introduce new products, the economy might enter a recession, customer preferences differ over time, and more.
transcript_json.translation: 战略顾问多莉·克拉克是这样向我们解释的："我认为适应力是职场中的一项重要技能，因为坦率地说，环境会变——竞争对手会推出新产品，经济可能陷入衰退，顾客偏好会随时间改变，等等。

transcript_json.text: If you shake your fist at the sky and say, 'why can't it stay the same?!', that's not going to do very much good.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你对着天空挥拳大喊：“为什么不能一切照旧？！”，那不会有什么用。

transcript_json.text: Instead, you need to recognize when circumstances have changed so you can take appropriate action based on what is, rather than how you wish the world would be.
transcript_json.translation: 相反，你需要认清环境何时发生了变化，这样才能基于现实而非自己期望中的世界，采取恰当的行动。

transcript_json.text: That enables you to make more accurate, informed, and effective choices."
transcript_json.translation: 这能让你做出更准确、更有依据、更有效的选择。”

transcript_json.text: Also, the workplace itself has been evolving.
transcript_json.translation: 此外，职场本身也在不断演变。

transcript_json.text: Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork, rather than a rigid hierarchy.
transcript_json.translation: 如今的工作文化和管理风格往往建立在团队合作之上，而不是僵化的等级制度。

transcript_json.text: Brainstorming, which requires creativity, flexibility, and emotional intelligence, is a typical problem-solving technique.
transcript_json.translation: 头脑风暴是一种典型的问题解决技巧，它需要创造力、灵活性和情商。

transcript_json.text: Employees who are unable or unwilling to participate will not easily move forward in the company.
transcript_json.translation: 无法参与或不愿参与的员工，在公司里不容易获得晋升。

transcript_json.text: Employees who are flexible demonstrate other skills too.
transcript_json.translation: 灵活变通的员工还会展现出其他技能。

transcript_json.text: They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur and suggest additional modifications when something is not working.
transcript_json.translation: 变化发生时，他们能迅速调整轻重缓急；事情行不通时，他们能提出进一步的修改建议。

transcript_json.text: They can also regroup quickly when a setback occurs, adapting to the new situation confidently and without overreacting.
transcript_json.translation: 遭遇挫折时，他们也能迅速重整旗鼓，自信地适应新情况，而不反应过度。

transcript_json.text: What makes humans different from other species?
transcript_json.translation: 然后在答题卡1上把对应字母用一条横线

transcript_json.text: Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development.
transcript_json.translation: 一些哲学家认为答案是道德或伦理，而一些科学家则断言是我们更发达的认知能力。

transcript_json.text: But I argue that the main difference is our desire to combat routine.
transcript_json.translation: 但我认为，主要的区别在于我们对抗千篇一律的欲望。

transcript_json.text: This makes being creative a biological mandate, as what we seek in art and technology is surprise, not simply a fulfillment of expectations.
transcript_json.translation: 这使创造力成为一种生物学上的必然，因为我们在艺术和技术中寻求的是惊喜，而不只是预期的满足。

transcript_json.text: As a result, a wild imagination has characterized the history of our species: we build intricate habitats, devise complex recipes for our food, wear clothes that reflect constant changes in fashion, communicate with elaborate signs, symbols and sounds, and travel between habitats on wings and wheels of our own design.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，天马行空的想象力贯穿了我们这个物种的历史：我们建造复杂的居所，为食物设计繁复的配方，穿着反映时尚不断变化的衣服，用精致的符号、标志和声音交流，乘坐自己设计的带翅膀和轮子的交通工具在居所之间往来。

transcript_json.text: To satisfy our appetite for novelty, innovation is key.
transcript_json.translation: 要满足我们对新奇的渴望，创新是关键。

transcript_json.text: But who innovates?
transcript_json.translation: 但谁来创新呢？

transcript_json.text: Now, many people, both laymen and experts, believe that only geniuses innovate.
transcript_json.translation: 如今，许多人——无论外行还是专家——都认为只有天才才会创新。

transcript_json.text: But I believe that innovation is not something that only a few people do.
transcript_json.translation: 但我认为，创新并不是只有少数人才做的事。

transcript_json.text: The innovative drive lives in every human brain, and the resulting war against the repetitive is what powers the massive changes that distinguish one generation from the next.
transcript_json.translation: 创新的驱动力存在于每个人的大脑中，由此产生的对千篇一律的战争，正是推动代际巨变的动力。

transcript_json.text: The drive to create the new is a trait of being human.
transcript_json.translation: 创造新事物的驱动力是人类的一种特质。

transcript_json.text: We build cultures by the hundreds and tell new stories by the millions.
transcript_json.translation: 我们建造数以百计的文化，讲述数以百万计的新故事。

transcript_json.text: We create and surround ourselves with things that have never existed before, while animals do not.
transcript_json.translation: 我们创造出前所未有的东西并用它们环绕自身，而动物不会。

transcript_json.text: But where do our new ideas come from?
transcript_json.translation: 但我们的新想法从何而来？

transcript_json.text: According to many, new ideas come from seemingly nowhere, to great minds.
transcript_json.translation: 在很多人看来，新想法仿佛凭空出现在伟大人物的头脑中。

transcript_json.text: From this perspective, new ideas are almost like magic.
transcript_json.translation: 从这个角度看，新点子几乎像魔法一样，

transcript_json.text: They come in a flash of inspiration to a select few.
transcript_json.translation: 会在灵光一现间降临到极少数人身上。

transcript_json.text: However, the reality is that, across the spectrum of human activities, prior work propels the creative process.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，现实是，在人类活动的各个领域，先前的成果推动着创造过程。

transcript_json.text: We may think of innovation as being the result of inspiration or genius, but it's really the result of developing the ideas of others further.
transcript_json.translation: 我们也许把创新看作灵感或天才的产物，但它实际上是把他人的想法进一步发展而来的结果。

transcript_json.text: This happens in technology where one invention enables or inspires further inventions.
transcript_json.translation: 技术在往如此：一项发明促成或启发更多的发明。

transcript_json.text: And it happens in the arts, as writers, composers, and painters use the work of previous artists in their own work.
transcript_json.translation: 艺术领域也是如此，作家、作曲家和画家都在自己的创作中借用前人的作品。

transcript_json.text: The human brain works from precedent.
transcript_json.translation: 人脑依照先例运转。

transcript_json.text: We take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape.
transcript_json.translation: 我们把继承来的想法组合成某种新的形态。

transcript_json.text: What is a true creator?
transcript_json.translation: 什么才是真正的创造者？

transcript_json.text: Is a creator a genius who makes something out of nothing?
transcript_json.translation: 创造者是凭空造物的天才吗？不是。

transcript_json.text: No.
transcript_json.translation: 创造者是凭空造物的天才吗？不是。

transcript_json.text: Creators are simply humans who use what they inherit who absorb the past and manipulate it to create possible futures.
transcript_json.translation: 创造者不过是普通人：他们利用自己继承的东西，吸收过去并加以改造，从而创造出可能的未来。

transcript_json.text: Thus, humans are creators as a rule rather than as an exception.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，人类作为创造者是常态，而非例外。

transcript_json.text: Many dog owners will tell you that their dog somehow knows when they're ill or upset, and, according to researchers who study dog cognition, those pet owners are right.
transcript_json.translation: 许多养狗的人会告诉你，他们的狗不知怎的知道他们什么时候生病或难过，而研究犬类认知的研究人员认为，这些宠物主人说得对。

transcript_json.text: Dogs do know when their human companions are having a rough time.
transcript_json.translation: 狗确实知道它们的人类伙伴什么时候不好过。

transcript_json.text: Not only can your dog sense when you have a cold, but domestic dogs have shown an aptitude for detecting both much smaller mood fluctuations and far more serious physical conditions.
transcript_json.translation: 你的狗不仅能察觉你感冒了，家犬还表现出能侦测更细微的情绪波动和严重得多的身体状况的能力。

transcript_json.text: This is because dogs are extremely sensitive to changes in the people they're familiar with, and illness causes change.
transcript_json.translation: 这是因为狗对熟悉的人身上的变化极其敏感，而疾病会造成变化。

transcript_json.text: If a person is infected with a virus or bacteria, for example, their odour will be abnormal, and dogs are able to smell that change even if a human can't, because dogs have a much more powerful sense of smell than humans.
transcript_json.translation: 例如，一个人如果感染了病毒或细菌，他的气味就会异常，即使人闻不出来，狗也能嗅出这种变化，因为狗的嗅觉比人类强大得多。

transcript_json.text: Researchers have also found that a person's mood, which can be an indicator of a larger illness, triggers a dog's sense of smell.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员还发现，人的情绪——它可能是更严重疾病的一个征兆——会触发狗的嗅觉。

transcript_json.text: Human emotions manifest physically in chemical signals that are emitted by the body, and dogs are able to smell those as well.
transcript_json.translation: 人的情绪会以身体释放的化学信号的形式在生理上表现出来，狗同样能闻到这些信号。

transcript_json.text: Beyond smell, dogs gather information from a person's voice in order to sense changes.
transcript_json.translation: 除了嗅觉，狗还会从人的声音中收集信息来察觉变化。

transcript_json.text: In 2014, researchers discovered that dogs have an area of the brain, similar to one in humans, that allows them to understand emotional cues in the tone of a speaker's voice, beyond what they'd be able to pick up from familiar words alone.
transcript_json.translation: 2014 年，研究人员发现，狗的大脑中有一个与人类类似的区域，使它们能听懂说话者语气中的情绪线索，而不只是听懂熟悉的词语。

transcript_json.text: A person's voice can also carry indicators of illness.
transcript_json.translation: 人的声音也可能携带疾病的征兆。

transcript_json.text: What's not understood quite so well is what dogs understand about these changes.
transcript_json.translation: 还不太清楚的是

transcript_json.text: Humans send out lots of cues, but whether dogs know some of these cues mean "illness" isn't clear.
transcript_json.translation: ，狗对这些变化理

transcript_json.text: What we perceive as concern on a dog's part might be more like increased curiosity or suspicion that something is wrong with us, and sticking close by is a great way to gather more information about the situation.
transcript_json.translation: 解到什么程度。

transcript_json.text: Some researchers assert dogs will one day help doctors diagnose diseases, as some dogs have already demonstrated the ability to detect an assortment of ailments, including diabetes and certain types of cancer.
transcript_json.translation: 一些研究人员断言，狗有朝一日将帮助医生诊断疾病，因为有些狗已经表现出侦测多种疾病的能力，包括糖尿病和某些类型的癌症。

transcript_json.text: But those researchers concede that's probably in the distant future.
transcript_json.translation: 但这些研究人员也承认，那可能是遥远未来的事。

transcript_json.text: For now, research suggests dog ownership can have an array of benefits in and of itself.
transcript_json.translation: 就目前而言，研究表明，养狗本身就能带来一系列好处。

transcript_json.text: Keeping a pet dog has been shown to bolster health and boost mood.
transcript_json.translation: 养宠物狗已被证明能增进健康、改善情绪。

transcript_json.text: Dogs also help people relax, and they can be a particular comfort to those with chronic diseases.
transcript_json.translation: 狗还能帮助人放松，对慢性病患者来说，它们能带来特别的慰藉。

transcript_json.text: Earlier this month, the think-tank called Onward published a report, "A Question of Degree", which argues that degrees in the creative arts are not good value for money.
transcript_json.translation: 本月早些时候，一个名为"前进"（Onward）的智库发布了一份题为《学位问题》的报告，认为创意艺术类的学位性价比不高。

transcript_json.text: Ministers, according to Onward, should "crack down on courses that offer extremely limited value for money to students ten years after graduation", restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students, if the average graduate earns below the student loans payment threshold.
transcript_json.translation: 在"前进"智库看来，如果毕业生平均收入低于学生贷款还款门槛，部长们就应当"严查那些毕业十年后给学生的回报极为有限的专业"，限制这类专业招收新生的能力。

transcript_json.text: Courses like science, technology, engineering, and math, and economics, where the average graduate earns a lot, should be favored.
transcript_json.translation: 而理科、技术、工程、数学和经济学这类毕业生平均收入高的专业，则应受到优待。

transcript_json.text: The report provides insight into a government review which looks at how to reform technical education and how to ensure students get good value for money.
transcript_json.translation: 这份报告让我们得以窥见政府的一项评估，该评估研究如何改革技术教育、如何确保学生花的钱物有所值。

transcript_json.text: At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point.
transcript_json.translation: 乍一看，"前进"智库的说法似乎还真有几分道理。

transcript_json.text: According to their data, the majority of creative arts students earn less than £25,000 a year, ten years after graduation.
transcript_json.translation: 根据他们的数据，大多数创意艺术专业的学生毕业十年后年收入不足 2.5 万英镑。

transcript_json.text: The average male creative arts students, indeed, apparently earn much less than they would, had they simply never gone to university.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，创意艺术专业的男性学生平均收入显然远低于他们当初干脆不上大学的情形。

transcript_json.text: This isn't really good for anyone—and it's certainly no good for graduates, who are forced to endure a lifestyle where they can never save up, never buy a house, never hope to retire.
transcript_json.translation: 这对谁都没什么好处——对毕业生来说更是如此，他们被迫忍受一种永远攒不下钱、买不起房、不敢指望退休的生活方式。

transcript_json.text: Onward have identified a real problem.
transcript_json.translation: "前进"智库指出的确实是一个真实存在的问题。

transcript_json.text: Creative arts graduates from top universities like Oxford, with a high proportion of privately-educated students, have fairly good work prospects, while 40 percent of all graduates—regardless of their degree—are on less than £25,000 a year, five years after graduation.
transcript_json.translation: 牛津这类私立学校学生比例很高的顶尖大学的创意艺术毕业生，就业前景相当不错；而所有毕业生中——无论什么学位——有 40% 在毕业五年后年薪不足 2.5 万英镑。

transcript_json.text: This suggests that the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole.
transcript_json.translation: 这说明，问题其实并不在于特定的学生读特定的专业，而在于整个经济大盘。

transcript_json.text: Regardless of what they've studied, young people find it hard to get ahead, unless they're lucky enough to be born with successful parents.
transcript_json.translation: 不管学的是什么专业，年轻人都很难出人头地，除非他们运气好，生在了成功的父母家里。

transcript_json.text: If ministers want to make education pay for young people, they need to look beyond the higher education sector, towards the wider world.
transcript_json.translation: 如果部长们想让教育对年轻人有所回报，就需要把目光投向高等教育领域之外、投向更广阔的世界。

transcript_json.text: The rewards that education gives us are not measurable—they are not always instantly obvious, and certainly not always direct.
transcript_json.translation: 教育给我们的回报是无法量化的——它们并不总是立竿见影，当然也不总是直接的。

transcript_json.text: An education makes you a different person from the one you would have been if you hadn't received it.
transcript_json.translation: 教育让你成为一个与未曾受教育时不同的自己。

transcript_json.text: We need to look at the value of education not in the context of a bank balance, but of a life.
transcript_json.translation: 我们需要在人生的语境中、而不是在银行存款的语境中看待教育的价值。

transcript_json.text: If we continue to allow ourselves to be distracted with talk of "value for money", we will all be made poorer as a result.
transcript_json.translation: 如果我们继续让"物有所值"的论调分散注意力，最终人人都将因此变得更穷。

transcript_json.text: There are many factors that impact our health.
transcript_json.translation: 影响我们健康的因素有很多。

transcript_json.text: These include our finances, our emotions and the way we work.
transcript_json.translation: 包括我们的财务状况、情绪和工作方式。

transcript_json.text: Education is one such factor.
transcript_json.translation: 教育就是其中之一。

transcript_json.text: Research suggests that higher levels of education can lead to better health and even greater longevity.
transcript_json.translation: 研究表明，受教育程度越高，健康状况越好，甚至更长寿。

transcript_json.text: But what about the education of your partner?
transcript_json.translation: 那你伴侣的受教育程度呢？

transcript_json.text: New research seeks to answer this question.
transcript_json.translation: 一项新研究试图回答这个问题。

transcript_json.text: Researchers use data from a longitudinal study.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员使用了一项纵向研究的数据。

transcript_json.text: The data came from surveys first administered to high school seniors in 1957.
transcript_json.translation: 数据来自 1957 年首次对高中毕业班学生开展的调查。

transcript_json.text: The surveys ended in 2011.
transcript_json.translation: 调查于 2011 年结束。

transcript_json.text: The team found that a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health.
transcript_json.translation: 团队发现，配偶受教育程度较高的人往往自报健康状况更好。

transcript_json.text: This remained the case when adjusting for other factors, such as participants' own education, social background and health status before and after marriage.
transcript_json.translation: 在调整了其他因素——比如参与者自身的受教育程度、社会背景以及婚前婚后的健康状况——之后，这一结果依然成立。

transcript_json.text: The authors suggest that high levels of education provide shared social, intellectual, emotional and financial resources.
transcript_json.translation: 作者认为，高学历能提供共享的社会、智力、情感和经济资源。

transcript_json.text: These include things like higher levels of emotional intelligence, particular skills or knowledge, or more money.
transcript_json.translation: 比如更高的情商、特定的技能或知识，或者更多的钱。

transcript_json.text: The researchers concede that an individual's own level of education is clearly important for their health, but they assert that individuals also can reap the benefits of their partner's education.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员承认，个人自身的受教育程度显然对其健康很重要，但他们断言，个人也能从伴侣的教育中获益。

transcript_json.text: It is noteworthy that the effects vary by gender.
transcript_json.translation: 值得注意的是，这种效应因性别而异。

transcript_json.text: For women, health was more closely correlated to their spouse's education than for men.
transcript_json.translation: 对女性而言，其健康状况与配偶教育程度的关联比对男性更紧密。

transcript_json.text: The team suggests this may be related to the time period of the study.
transcript_json.translation: 团队认为，这可能与研究所处的时代有关。

transcript_json.text: Women in this sample had lower levels of education and lower occupational achievements than the men.
transcript_json.translation: 该样本中女性的受教育程度和职业成就都低于男性。

transcript_json.text: The researchers' hypothesis is that this made the husband's resources more likely to have a shared impact.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员的推测是，这使得丈夫的资源更有可能产生共享效应。
