transcript_json.text: Climate scientists predict that many parts of the world will be increasingly prone to floods.
transcript_json.translation: 这对人的生命和财产构成严重威胁。因

transcript_json.text: This is a serious risk to human lives and property.
transcript_json.translation: 此，理解并准确预测洪水风险，是全

transcript_json.text: So understanding and accurately forecasting flood risks is a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe.
transcript_json.translation: 球各易受灾城市面临的一项关键挑战。

transcript_json.text: In 2017, Derek Loftis of the Virginia Institute of Marine Science started a project called Catch the King.
transcript_json.translation: 2017 年，弗吉尼亚海洋科学研究所的德里克·洛夫蒂斯启动了一个名为“擒王潮”的项目。

transcript_json.text: It uses a smartphone app to collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides.
transcript_json.translation: 该项目用一款手机应用收集普通市民在大潮期间的数据。

transcript_json.text: He'll use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model, called TideWatch.
transcript_json.translation: 他将用这些数据来验证并改进他的数学洪水模型“观潮”。

transcript_json.text: Loftis's mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there.
transcript_json.translation: 洛夫蒂斯的使命是在洪水到来之前预知水会流向哪里。

transcript_json.text: But collecting necessary data and then processing that information quickly enough to make usable forecasts is anything but easy.
transcript_json.translation: 但收集必要数据，再把信息处理得足够快、做出可用的预报，绝非易事。

transcript_json.text: Accurate flood forecasts require an understanding of the situation on the ground.
transcript_json.translation: 准确的洪水预报需要对地面实况的了解。

transcript_json.text: By the early 2000s, supercomputing had advanced enough that scientists could integrate weather forecasting models with such measurements.
transcript_json.translation: 到 21 世纪初，超级计算已足够先进，科学家能够把天气预报模型与这类测量数据结合起来。

transcript_json.text: But they still didn't have the critically important ability to forecast fast-moving floods in real time.
transcript_json.translation: 但他们仍然缺乏实时预报快速推进的洪水这一至关重要的能力。

transcript_json.text: So, in 2017, Loftis and colleagues set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors throughout the flood risk community of Norfolk, Virginia.
transcript_json.translation: 于是，2017 年，洛夫蒂斯和同事在弗吉尼亚州诺福克这个易涝社区布设了 28 个联网水位传感器。

transcript_json.text: The new sensors relayed rough measurements about water height and movement to a computer at the Virginia Institute.
transcript_json.translation: 这些新传感器把关于水位和水流的大致测量数据传回弗吉尼亚研究所的计算机。

transcript_json.text: Along with those sensors, hundreds of local citizens take photos of rising tides and transmit them in real time to the institute.
transcript_json.translation: 除这些传感器外，数百名当地市民拍摄涨潮照片并实时传给研究所。

transcript_json.text: Scientists hope that the data collected by these citizens can help sharpen the ability to forecast exactly when and where damaging floods will occur.
transcript_json.translation: 科学家希望，这些市民收集的数据能帮助提高预报能力，精确预测破坏性洪灾将在何时何地发生。

transcript_json.text: Now, it's become something of a ritual to debate the value of a college degree, but as Current Population Survey data show, there has been a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees compared with those who have them.
transcript_json.translation: 如今，争论大学文凭的价值已经差不多成了例行话题，但正如当前人口调查数据所示，与有大学文凭的男性相比，没有大学文凭的男性就业率急剧下降。

transcript_json.text: This decline began in the 1960s and has become more serious over time.
transcript_json.translation: 这种下降始于 20 世纪 60 年代，并随着时间推移愈发严重。

transcript_json.text: What has actually caused this decline?
transcript_json.translation: 究竟是什么导致了这种下降？

transcript_json.text: Well, economists have been working to ascertain the roots of the decline for decades and have come up with several theories.
transcript_json.translation: 嗯，几十年来经济学家一直在努力查明这一下降的根源，并提出了几种理论。

transcript_json.text: One popular theory is that it's a case of too low wages for jobs that don't require a degree.
transcript_json.translation: 一个流行的理论是：不需要文凭的工作工资太低。

transcript_json.text: An alternate theory is that there were more jobs not requiring a college degree in the past than now.
transcript_json.translation: 另一种理论是：过去不需要大学文凭的工作比现在多。

transcript_json.text: A recent working paper from the National Bureau of Economic Research reviewed those theories and put forward additional hypotheses about the causes of the problem.
transcript_json.translation: 美国国家经济研究局最近的一份工作论文回顾了这些理论，并就问题成因提出了额外的假设。

transcript_json.text: Let's look at that paper now.
transcript_json.translation: 我们现在就来看看这篇论文。

transcript_json.text: First, the researchers considered the issue of wages.
transcript_json.translation: 首先，研究人员考虑了工资问题。

transcript_json.text: As the wage gap has grown between those with college degrees and those without, economists have suggested that men aren't as interested in taking some of the less lucrative jobs.
transcript_json.translation: 随着有无大学文凭者之间工资差距的扩大，经济学家认为男性对从事一些收入较低的工作不那么感兴趣了。

transcript_json.text: While the authors of the paper found truth in this explanation, they assert that low wages can't be the only factor, as wages for men without college degrees, adjusting for inflation, haven't changed much since the 1960s, making it hard to see why fewer men seem willing to accept those wages.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然论文作者认为这一解释有道理，但他们断言，低工资不可能是唯一因素，因为经通胀调整后，没有大学文凭的男性工资自 20 世纪 60 年代以来变化不大，这就很难解释为什么愿意接受这种工资的男性似乎变少了。

transcript_json.text: This leads to the second theory, that more jobs require a college degree today than in the past.
transcript_json.translation: 这就引出第二种理论：如今比过去有更多工作要求大学文凭。

transcript_json.text: Indeed, that theory seems valid, because in America today, 2/3 of jobs are filled by workers with at least some college education.
transcript_json.translation: 的确，这个理论似乎站得住脚，因为如今的美国，三分之二的工作由至少受过部分大学教育的劳动者担任。

transcript_json.text: However, the authors of the paper argue that there are other factors amplifying the problem.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，论文作者认为还有其他因素在放大这一问题。

transcript_json.text: They identified two new potential explanations: the first being the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees since the 1960s; and the second, being the increase in women participating in the workforce that was concurrent with the decline in marriage.
transcript_json.translation: 他们找出了两个新的潜在解释：一是自 20 世纪 60 年代以来没有大学文凭的男性结婚率大幅下降；二是与结婚率下降同步出现的女性劳动参与率上升。

transcript_json.text: These two changes mean that men might not have families to support, or if they do, their wives might be doing more of the providing, both of which might remove the financial incentive to work.
transcript_json.translation: 这两个变化意味着，男性可能没有家庭要养，即便有，养家的担子也可能更多落在妻子身上，这两种情况都可能削弱工作的经济动力。

transcript_json.text: The authors of the paper concede that research on the subject isn't complete, but they argue that their work supports the value of a college education.
transcript_json.translation: 论文作者承认这方面的研究还不完备，但他们认为自己的工作支持了大学教育的价值。

transcript_json.text: While an increasing number of people are trying to eat less meat, a market research team has found in its latest fashion and sustainability report that the trend is now spreading from kitchen to closet.
transcript_json.translation: 就在越来越多的人努力少吃肉的同时，一个市场调研团队在其最新的时尚与可持续报告中发现，这股潮流正在从厨房蔓延到衣橱。

transcript_json.text: It found animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes, with 42% saying it was important to them.
transcript_json.translation: 报告发现，在人们买衣服前考虑的问题清单中，动物福利位居榜首，42% 的人说这对他们很重要。

transcript_json.text: The researchers of the team predicted that the next year would see a boom in animal-free shoe collections, since they heard shoppers of all ages say they would buy footwear designated as "vegan", meaning the goods were produced without using any animal or animal part.
transcript_json.translation: 该团队的研究人员预测，来年无动物成分鞋履系列将迎来大热，因为他们听到各年龄层的购物者都说，愿意购买标注“纯素”的鞋类，即商品在生产过程中不使用任何动物或动物部位。

transcript_json.text: As well as being on trend, and with a much better ring to it than synthetic leather, the vegan label does convey an important extra distinction.
transcript_json.translation: “纯素”标签不仅顺应潮流、听起来也比“人造革”体面得多，它还传达了一项重要的额外区别。

transcript_json.text: If you label something as vegan, then the whole product needs to be animal free.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你把某件产品标注为纯素，那么整个产品都必须不含动物成分。

transcript_json.text: That means checking things like the glue that holds the shoe together, for example, and the chemicals used for finishing them.
transcript_json.translation: 这意味着要检查诸如粘鞋的胶水、以及用于成品整饰的化学品之类的东西。

transcript_json.text: At the top end, some of the world-renowned fashion designers have avoided leather and fur for some time.
transcript_json.translation: 在高端领域，一些世界知名时装设计师已有一段时间不用皮革和毛皮了。

transcript_json.text: In fact, The Animal Free Product Society says they've seen a boom in products registered with the vegan trademark.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，“无动物制品协会”表示，注册纯素商标的产品出现了激增。

transcript_json.text: In 2018, there were 119.
So far this year, one of the first reputable store chains to use the vegan trademark, prices ballet shoes at £7.99 and a vegan laptop handbag at £29.99, comparable with its other products.
transcript_json.translation: 今年到目前为止，作为最早使用纯素商标的知名连锁商店之一，该店把芭蕾舞鞋定价为 7. 99 英镑，纯素笔记本电脑手提包定价为 29. 99 英镑，与店里其他商品的价格相当。

transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: By the end of 2016, anyone who had been paying even passing attention to the news headlines was highly likely to conclude that everything was terrible, and that the world was going to hell.
transcript_json.translation: 到 2016 年年底，凡是稍微留意过新闻标题的人，多半都会得出这样的结论：一切都糟透了，世界正在走向毁灭。

transcript_json.text: It was easy to feel depressed by the wars in different parts of the world, the spread of deadly viruses or terror attacks.
transcript_json.translation: 世界各地的战乱、致命病毒的蔓延或是恐怖袭击，都很容易让人感到沮丧。

transcript_json.text: Yet, 2016 was the best year in the history of humanity.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，2016 年却是人类历史上最好的一年。

transcript_json.text: Child mortality was roughly half what it was as recently as 1990.
transcript_json.translation: 儿童死亡率大约只是 1990 年时的一半。

transcript_json.text: And 300,000 more people gained access to electricity each day.
transcript_json.translation: 而且，每天还有 30 万人新用上了电。

transcript_json.text: Every single measure of material and environmental welfare in America, Europe, Asia, Africa and the world as a whole has improved rather than deteriorated.
transcript_json.translation: 美洲、欧洲、亚洲、非洲乃至全世界在物质与环境福利上的每一项指标都在改善，而非恶化。

transcript_json.text: We are living in history's most peaceful era, with violence of all kinds in steep decline.
transcript_json.translation: 我们正生活在历史上最和平的时代，各类暴力事件都在急剧减少。

transcript_json.text: Those are the facts.
transcript_json.translation: 这些都是事实。

transcript_json.text: So why aren't we all optimists?
transcript_json.translation: 那么，为什么我们并不都是乐观主义者呢？

transcript_json.text: In a 2015 survey for YouGov, 65% of British people and 81% of the French said they thought the world was getting worse.
transcript_json.translation: 在 2015 年民调机构 YouGov 的一项调查中，65% 的英国人和 81% 的法国人表示，他们认为世界正在变得更糟。

transcript_json.text: However, according to numerous sensible statistics, these people are simply wrong.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，大量可靠的统计数据表明，这些人的看法完全错了。

transcript_json.text: Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century.
transcript_json.translation: 任何头脑清醒的人，都不该希望自己生活在上一个世纪。

transcript_json.text: Yet people do.
transcript_json.translation: 但偏偏有人这么想。

transcript_json.text: Why?
transcript_json.translation: 为什么？

transcript_json.text: Our prevailing mood of despair is irrational.
transcript_json.translation: 我们这种普遍的绝望情绪其实是不理性的。

transcript_json.text: It says more about us than it does about how things really are.
transcript_json.translation: 它更多地反映了我们自身的问题，而不是事情的真实面貌。

transcript_json.text: It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors— but now, in a media-saturated era, constantly mislead us.
transcript_json.translation: 对此最好的解释是：种种心理偏误在进化历程中曾对祖先们有用，但在媒体无处不在的今天，它们却在不断误导我们。

transcript_json.text: Once upon a time, it was of great survival value to be worried about everything that could go wrong. This is what makes bad news especially compelling.
transcript_json.translation: 在很久以前，为一切可能出问题的事情担忧具有重大的生存价值。这正是坏消息格外吸引人的原因。

transcript_json.text: In our evolutionary past, it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival.
transcript_json.translation: 在人类演化的过去，注意力容易被负面信息攫取是一件大好事，因为它很可能预示着危及自身生存的风险。

transcript_json.text: The caveman, who always assumed there was a lion behind the next rock, would usually be wrong, but he'd be much more likely to survive and reproduce than one who always assumed the opposite.
transcript_json.translation: 那个总以为下一块岩石后面有狮子的穴居人通常会猜错，但他比总往好处想的同类更可能活下来并繁衍后代。

transcript_json.text: But that was all before newspapers, television, and the Internet. In today's hyper-connected times, our addiction to bad news just leads us to vacuum up depressing stories from around the globe.
transcript_json.translation: 但那都是在报纸、电视和互联网出现之前的事了。在如今这个高度互联的时代，对坏消息的'瘾'只会让我们把全球各地的丧气故事一股脑吸进来。

transcript_json.text: Whether these news stories threaten us or not, we conclude that things are much worse than they actually are. Really good news, on the other hand, can be a lot harder to spot in a newspaper because predictable daily events, by definition, aren't news.
transcript_json.translation: 无论这些新闻报道的威胁是否与我们相关，我们都会得出'世道比实际糟得多'的结论。另一方面，真正的好消息在报纸上却难觅踪影，因为按定义来说，可预见的日常事件根本算不上新闻。

transcript_json.text: CONVERSATION 1
transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 1

transcript_json.text: W: Thank you for meeting with me, Stephen, at such short notice.
transcript_json.translation: W: 史蒂芬，谢谢你这么仓促还赶来见我。

transcript_json.text: M: Not a problem, Margaret.
transcript_json.translation: M: 没问题，玛格丽特。

transcript_json.text: Now, please give me some good news.
transcript_json.translation: 那么，请给我带点好消息吧。

transcript_json.text: Have you agreed to my last proposal?
transcript_json.translation: 你答应我上次提的方案了吗？

transcript_json.text: W: I have, indeed.
transcript_json.translation: W: 确实答应了。

transcript_json.text: And I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change to be made to the contract.
transcript_json.translation: 我想签这份协议，只待合同再做一处小小的修改。

transcript_json.text: M: Margaret, we have been through this for almost a year now, back and forth, making alterations.
transcript_json.translation: M: 玛格丽特，这件事我们前前后后反复修改快一年了。

transcript_json.text: Are you sure you want to make a sponsorship deal for your clients, or not?
transcript_json.translation: 你到底想不想为你的客户达成这笔赞助交易？

transcript_json.text: I ask this, because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience. But as I'm sure you understand, we hold our clients' best interests to be of the utmost concern.
transcript_json.translation: 我这么问，是因为坦白讲，我们这边有些人已经快没耐心了。但我相信您能理解，客户的最大利益是我们最关心的事。

transcript_json.text: W: I understand your concerns.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我理解你的顾虑。

transcript_json.text: We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts.
transcript_json.translation: 因此我们会仔细梳理所有合同的细节条款。

transcript_json.text: We therefore come through the fine details of all contracts, rest assured, we all appreciate your firm's patience.
transcript_json.translation: 所以我们要把每份合同的细节都过一遍。请放心，我们都很感激贵公司的耐心。

transcript_json.text: M: OK, fine.
transcript_json.translation: M: 好吧，行。

transcript_json.text: So what changes do you wish to make?
transcript_json.translation: 那么你们想改哪里？

transcript_json.text: W: Essentially, we would like the new deal to exclude the Middle East. That's all.
transcript_json.translation: W: 基本上，我们希望新协议把中东排除在外。就这一点。

transcript_json.text: M: The Middle East. Why?
transcript_json.translation: M: 中东？为什么？

transcript_json.text: W: My client has a couple of other prospective marketing deals from companies in the Middle East.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我的客户在中东还有几笔潜在的营销合作在谈。

transcript_json.text: Those offers, should they materialize, would exclusively employ my client's image in the Middle East only.
transcript_json.translation: 那些合作如果落地，将只在中东范围内独家使用我客户的形象。

transcript_json.text: Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，为了避免任何冲突，我们必须确保这两个营销活动在地域上不重叠。

transcript_json.text: M: What business sector in the Middle East are we talking about here?
transcript_json.translation: M: 这里说的是中东哪个行业？

transcript_json.text: W: Real estate.
transcript_json.translation: W: 房地产。

transcript_json.text: M: Well, that should be okay then.
transcript_json.translation: M: 嗯，那应该没问题。

transcript_json.text: So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market, there should be no conflict of interest.
transcript_json.translation: 只要产品与我们的食品饮料市场差别很大，就不存在利益冲突。

transcript_json.text: Nevertheless, I will have to run this through my people.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，我还是得让手下的人过一遍。

transcript_json.text: I don't foresee any problem, though.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然我预计不会有什么问题。

transcript_json.text: The Middle East is a negligible market for us, but I still need to check this with a couple of departments.
transcript_json.translation: 中东市场对我们来说微不足道，但我还是得跟几个部门核实一下。

transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 2

transcript_json.text: M: Next, we have a special science-related news story.
transcript_json.translation: M: 接下来是一条特别的科技新闻。

transcript_json.text: Paula Hancock is at the Denver Observatory.
transcript_json.translation: 葆拉·汉考克正在丹佛天文台。

transcript_json.text: Paula, what is the big story over there?
transcript_json.translation: 葆拉，那边有什么大新闻？

transcript_json.text: W: Hi, John.
transcript_json.translation: W: 你好，约翰。

transcript_json.text: Yes, all the astronomers on site here are very excited.
transcript_json.translation: 是的，这里在场的所有天文学家都非常兴奋。

transcript_json.text: In fact, space enthusiasts all across North America and the rest of the Northern Hemisphere will be congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night sky.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，今晚北美乃至整个北半球的太空爱好者都将聚集在山顶观赏夜空。

transcript_json.text: M: Why? What's the big event?
transcript_json.translation: M: 为什么？有什么大事？

transcript_json.text: Is there an eclipse happening soon?
transcript_json.translation: 是马上要发生日食或月食吗？

transcript_json.text: W: Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet.
transcript_json.translation: W: 今晚，地球将与奥本海默彗星近距离接近。

transcript_json.text: It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years.
transcript_json.translation: 这是 100 多年来我们的行星与这类天体最接近的一次。

transcript_json.text: For this reason, it is expected that thousands of people will gaze up at the sky tonight in order to see this formidable object.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，预计今晚会有成千上万的人仰望天空，一睹这个壮观天体的风采。

transcript_json.text: M: How far away is this comet?
transcript_json.translation: M: 这颗彗星离我们有多远？

transcript_json.text: Will people be able to see it with the naked eye?
transcript_json.translation: 人们能用肉眼看到它吗？

transcript_json.text: W: The Oppenheimer comet will still be millions of miles away, on the edge of our galaxy, but nevertheless, this is a relatively close distance, close enough for people to observe in good detail through a telescope.
transcript_json.translation: W: 奥本海默彗星仍将在数百万英里之外，位于我们银河系的边缘，不过这已经是相对较近的距离了，足够人们通过望远镜观察到清晰的细节。

transcript_json.text: People will only see a blur without one.
transcript_json.translation: 没有望远镜的话，人们只能看到一团模糊的光斑。

transcript_json.text: However, that does not mean one needs professional equipment.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，这并不意味着必须用专业设备。

transcript_json.text: Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object.
transcript_json.translation: 哪怕是最普通的望远镜，也足以让人们观测并惊叹这个飞行天体。

transcript_json.text: M: Many of our viewers will be wondering how they too can take part in this once-in-a-lifetime event.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我们的许多观众都想知道自己该如何参与这场千载难逢的活动。

transcript_json.text: Where will this comet be in the sky? How can people find it?
transcript_json.translation: 这颗彗星会出现在天空的什么位置？人们怎样才能找到它？

transcript_json.text: W: The comet will be almost exactly due north, at 60 degrees above the equator.
transcript_json.translation: W: 彗星几乎就在正北方，赤纬 60 度的位置。

transcript_json.text: However, finding the comet is indeed very tricky, and scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，找到这颗彗星确实很难，这里的科学家告诉我，有很多手机应用可以助你一臂之力。

transcript_json.text: M: How fantastic.
transcript_json.translation: M: 太棒了。

transcript_json.text: Thank you, Paula, for the information.
transcript_json.translation: 谢谢你带来的消息，葆拉。

transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 1

transcript_json.text: Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition advice and regulations around the world.
transcript_json.translation: 膳食指南是世界各地营养建议和法规的基础。

transcript_json.text: While there is strong scientific consensus around most existing guidelines, one question has recently stirred debate: Should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods?
transcript_json.translation: 尽管现有的大多数指南都有很强的科学共识，但最近有一个问题引发了争论：是否应该警告消费者避免食用超加工食品？

transcript_json.text: Two papers published today in The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition outline the case for and against using the concept of ultra-processed foods to help inform dietary guidelines beyond conventional food classification systems.
transcript_json.translation: 今天发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上的两篇论文，分别阐述了支持与反对把超加工食品这一概念引入膳食指南、以超越传统食品分类体系的理由。

transcript_json.text: The authors, Carlos Monteiro of the University of São Paulo and Arne Astrup of Novo Nordisk Foundation will discuss the issue in a live virtual debate August 14, during NUTRITION 2024 LIVE ONLINE. The debate centers around a system developed by Montiero and colleagues that classifies the debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra-processed.
transcript_json.translation: 圣保罗大学的卡洛斯·蒙特罗和诺和诺德基金会的阿尔内·阿斯特鲁普将在 8 月 14 日'2024 营养学线上大会'期间的一场线上直播辩论中讨论这一问题。辩论围绕蒙特罗及其同事开发的一套分类体系展开，该体系将辩论围绕蒙泰罗及其同事开发的一套体系展开，该体系按工业化加工程度对食品分类，从未加工到超加工不等。

transcript_json.text: The system defines ultra-processed foods as those made using sequences of processes that extract substances from foods and alter them with chemicals in order to formulate the final product.
transcript_json.translation: 该体系将超加工食品定义为：通过一系列工序从食物中提取物质并用化学品加以改变，从而配制出最终产品的食品。

transcript_json.text: Ultra-processed foods are characteristically designed to be cheap, tasty and convenient; examples include soft drinks and candy, packaged snacks and pastries, ready-to-heat products, and reconstituted meat products.
transcript_json.translation: 超加工食品的典型特点是便宜、美味、方便，例如软饮料和糖果、包装零食和糕点、即热食品以及重组肉制品。

transcript_json.text: Studies have linked consumption of ultra-processed foods - which are often high in salt, sugar and fat - with weight gain and an increased risk of chronic diseases, even after adjusting for the amount of salt, sugar and fat in the diet.
transcript_json.translation: 研究表明，食用超加工食品——通常高盐、高糖、高脂肪——与体重增加和慢性病风险上升相关，即使对饮食中盐、糖、脂肪的含量进行调整后依然如此。

transcript_json.text: While the mechanisms behind these associations are not fully understood, Monteiro argues that the existing evidence is sufficient to justify discouraging consumption of ultra-processed foods in dietary recommendations and government policies.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管这些关联背后的机制尚未完全弄清，蒙泰罗认为现有证据已足以支持在膳食建议和政府政策中劝阻人们食用超加工食品。

transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 2

transcript_json.text: Believe it or not, human creativity benefits from constraints.
transcript_json.translation: 信不信由你，人类的创造力反而受益于限制。

transcript_json.text: According to psychologists, when you have less to work with, you actually begin to see the world differently.
transcript_json.translation: 心理学家认为，当你手头的资源更少时，你反而会开始用不同的眼光看世界。

transcript_json.text: With constraints, you dedicate your mental energy to acting more resourcefully.
transcript_json.translation: 有了限制，你会把精神能量集中在更机智地行动上。

transcript_json.text: When challenged, you figure out new ways to be better.
transcript_json.translation: 面对挑战时，你会想出新的办法做得更好。

transcript_json.text: The most successful creative people know that constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher.
transcript_json.translation: 最成功的创意人都懂得，限制能给思维以跃升的动力。

transcript_json.text: People who invent new products are not limited by what they don't have or can't do.
transcript_json.translation: 发明新产品的人不会被自己缺什么、不能做什么束缚。

transcript_json.text: They leverage their limitations to push themselves even further.
transcript_json.translation: 他们把自己的局限转化为动力，推动自己走得更远。

transcript_json.text: Many products and services are created because the founders saw a limitation in what they use.
transcript_json.translation: 许多产品和服务的诞生，都是因为创始人看到了自己所用之物的局限。

transcript_json.text: They created innovation based on what was not working for them at the moment.
transcript_json.translation: 他们根据当下不好用的东西创造出了革新。

transcript_json.text: Innovation is a creative person's response to limitation.
transcript_json.translation: 创新就是有创造力的人对局限的回应。

transcript_json.text: In a 2015 study, which examined how thinking about scarcity or abundance influences how creatively people use their resources, Ravi Mehta at the University of Illinois and Meng Zhu at Johns Hopkins University found that people simply have no incentive to use what's available to them in novel ways.
transcript_json.translation: 在 2015 年一项考察稀缺思维或充裕思维如何影响人们创造性使用资源的研究中，伊利诺伊大学的拉维·梅塔和约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的朱萌发现，人们根本没有动力以新颖的方式利用手头的资源。

transcript_json.text: When people face scarcity, they give themselves the freedom to use resources in less conventional ways because they have to.
transcript_json.translation: 当人们面对稀缺时，他们会给自己松绑，用不那么常规的方式使用资源，因为别无选择。

transcript_json.text: Obstacles can broaden your perception and open up your thinking processes.
transcript_json.translation: 障碍能拓宽你的感知，打开你的思维过程。

transcript_json.text: Consistent constraints help you improve at connecting unrelated ideas and concepts.
transcript_json.translation: 持续的限制能帮你提高关联看似无关的想法和概念的能力。

transcript_json.text: Marissa Mayer, former vice-president for search products and user experience at Google, once wrote in a publication on Bloomberg.
transcript_json.translation: 谷歌前搜索产品与用户体验副总裁玛丽莎·梅耶尔曾在彭博社的一篇文章中写道：

transcript_json.text: "Constraints shape and focus problems and provide clear challenges to overcome.
transcript_json.translation: “限制能塑造问题、聚焦问题，并提供明确的挑战去克服。

transcript_json.text: Creativity thrives best when constrained. "
transcript_json.translation: 在受约束时，创造力反而最旺盛。”

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 1
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 1

transcript_json.text: Different people use different strategies for managing conflicts.
transcript_json.translation: 不同的人用不同的策略来处理冲突。

transcript_json.text: These strategies are learned in childhood.
transcript_json.translation: 这些策略是在童年时期习得的。

transcript_json.text: Usually, we are not aware of how we act in conflict situations.
transcript_json.translation: 通常，我们意识不到自己在冲突情境下是如何行事的。

transcript_json.text: We just do whatever seems to come naturally.
transcript_json.translation: 我们只是凭本能行事。

transcript_json.text: But we do have a personal strategy; and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts.
transcript_json.translation: 但我们确实有一套个人策略；正因为它是学来的，我们随时可以通过学习新的、更有效的冲突处理方法来改变它。

transcript_json.text: When you get involved in a conflict, there are two major concerns you have to take into account: achieving your personal goals and keeping a good relationship with the other person.
transcript_json.translation: 当你卷入一场冲突时，有两个重要因素必须考虑：实现个人目标，以及与对方保持良好关系。

transcript_json.text: How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act in a conflict.
transcript_json.translation: 你的个人目标有多重要、这段关系对你有多重要，会影响你在冲突中的行事方式。

transcript_json.text: Given these two concerns, five styles of managing conflicts can be identified:
transcript_json.translation: 基于这两个考量，可以识别出五种处理冲突的风格：

transcript_json.text: 1. The turtle.
transcript_json.translation: 1. 海龟型。

transcript_json.text: Turtles withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts.
transcript_json.translation: 海龟型的人缩回壳里躲避冲突。

transcript_json.text: They give up their personal goals and relationships.
transcript_json.translation: 他们放弃个人目标，也放弃关系。

transcript_json.text: They believe it is easier to withdraw from a conflict than to face it.
transcript_json.translation: 他们认为退出冲突比直面冲突更容易。

transcript_json.text: 2. The shark.
transcript_json.translation: 2. 鲨鱼。

transcript_json.text: Sharks try to overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution to the conflict.
transcript_json.translation: 鲨鱼型的人试图压倒对手，强迫对方接受自己解决冲突的方案。

transcript_json.text: They seek to achieve their goals at all costs.
transcript_json.translation: 他们不惜一切代价也要达成目标。

transcript_json.text: Sharks assume that conflicts are settled by one person winning and one person losing.
transcript_json.translation: 鲨鱼型的人认为冲突的解决就是你赢我输。

transcript_json.text: Winning gives sharks a sense of pride and achievement.
transcript_json.translation: 获胜让鲨鱼型的人感到自豪和有成就感。

transcript_json.text: Losing gives them a sense of weakness, inadequacy and failure.
transcript_json.translation: 失败则让他们感到软弱、无能和挫败。

transcript_json.text: 3. The Teddy bear.
transcript_json.translation: 3. 泰迪熊。

transcript_json.text: Teddy bears want to be accepted and liked by other people.
transcript_json.translation: 泰迪熊型的人渴望被他人接纳和喜爱。

transcript_json.text: They think that conflicts should be avoided in favor of harmony, and believe that conflicts cannot be discussed without damaging relationships.
transcript_json.translation: 他们认为为了和谐应当避免冲突，并相信一旦讨论冲突就必然会伤害关系。

transcript_json.text: They give up their goals to preserve the relationship.
transcript_json.translation: 他们为保全关系而放弃自己的目标。

transcript_json.text: 4. The fox.
transcript_json.translation: 4. 狐狸。

transcript_json.text: Foxes are moderately concerned with their own goals and about their relationships with other people.
transcript_json.translation: 狐狸型的人对自己的目标和与他人的关系都有适度的关注。

transcript_json.text: They give up part of their goals and persuade the other person in a conflict to give up part of his goals.
transcript_json.translation: 他们放弃一部分目标，并劝说冲突中的对方也放弃一部分目标。

transcript_json.text: They seek a solution to conflicts where both sides gain something.
transcript_json.translation: 他们寻求双方都有所得的冲突解决方案。

transcript_json.text: 5. The owl.
transcript_json.translation: 5. 猫头鹰型。

transcript_json.text: Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved.
transcript_json.translation: 猫头鹰型的人把冲突视为有待解决的问题。

transcript_json.text: They see conflicts as improving relationships by reducing tension between two people.
transcript_json.translation: 他们认为冲突可以通过减少两人之间的紧张关系来改善关系。

transcript_json.text: They try to begin a discussion that identifies the conflict as a problem.
transcript_json.translation: 他们试图开启讨论，把冲突明确为一个问题。

transcript_json.text: By seeking solutions that satisfy both themselves and the other person, owls maintain the relationship.
transcript_json.translation: 通过寻求让自己和对方都满意的解决方案，猫头鹰型的人维系了关系。

transcript_json.text: Owls are not satisfied until a solution is found that achieves their own goals and the other person's goals, and they are not satisfied until the tensions and negative feelings have been fully resolved.
transcript_json.translation: 除非找到能同时实现自己和对方目标的方案，猫头鹰型的人不会罢休；除非紧张关系和负面情绪被完全化解，他们也不会满意。

transcript_json.translation: 问题 16：讲话人为什么说处理冲突的策略总是可以改变的？

transcript_json.text: Q17. What is said to affect the way one acts in a conflict?

transcript_json.translation: 问题 18：在讲话人讨论的五种风格中，哪一种把冲突视为待解决的问题？

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 2
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 2

transcript_json.text: The genetic code of all 1.5 million known species of animals and plants living on earth will be mapped to help save species from extinction and boost human health.
transcript_json.translation: 对地球上已知的全部 150 万个动植物物种进行基因测序，将有助于拯救濒危物种并增进人类健康。

transcript_json.text: Scientists hope that cracking the genetic code of plants and animals could help uncover new treatments for infectious diseases, slow aging, improve crops in agriculture and create new bio-materials. new biomaterials.
transcript_json.translation: 科学家希望，破译动植物的遗传密码有助于发现治疗传染病的新疗法、延缓衰老、改良农作物并创造新型生物材料。

transcript_json.text: In Britain, organisations including the Natural History Museum, the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew and the Welcome Sanger Institute have joined forces to sequence Britain's 66,000 Dubbed the Darwin Tree of Life Project, it is expected to take 10 years and cost 100 million pounds.
transcript_json.translation: 在英国，包括自然历史博物馆、皇家植物园（邱园）和韦尔科姆桑格研究所在内的机构已联手这项名为“达尔文生命之树计划”的工程预计耗时 10 年，耗资 1 亿英镑。

transcript_json.text: Once completed, all the information will be publicly available to researchers.
transcript_json.translation: 一旦完成，所有信息都将向研究人员公开。

transcript_json.text: Many scientists believe that earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction, with humans creating a toxic mix of habitat loss, pollution and climate change, which has already led to the loss of at least 77 species of mammals and 140 types of birds since 1500.
transcript_json.translation: 许多科学家认为，地球已进入第六次大灭绝：人类造成了栖息地丧失、污染和气候变化的恶性叠加，自 1500 年以来已导致至少 77 种哺乳动物和 140 种鸟类消失。

transcript_json.text: It is the biggest loss of species since the dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago.

transcript_json.translation: 科学家说，给每个物种测序将彻底改变人们对生物学和进化的理解，并有力推动保护工作以及生物多样性的保护和恢复。

transcript_json.text: Tim Littlewood, head of Life Sciences Department at the Natural History Museum, said whether you are interested in food or disease, the history of how every organism on the planet has adapted to its environment is recorded in its genetic makeup.
transcript_json.translation: 自然历史博物馆生命科学部主任蒂姆·利特尔伍德博士说，无论你感兴趣的是食物还是疾病，地球上每个生物如何适应环境的历史都记录在它的基因构成之中。

transcript_json.text: How you then harness that is dependent on your ability to understand it.

transcript_json.text: We will be using modern methods to get a really good window on the present and the past.
transcript_json.translation: 我们将用现代方法打开一扇观察现在与过去的绝佳窗口。

transcript_json.text: And of course, a window on the past gives you a prospective model on the future.

transcript_json.text: Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, said, "Try as I might, I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project.

transcript_json.text: Since 1970, humanity has wiped out 60% of animal populations.

transcript_json.text: John Donne, the English poet, wrote in the 17th century: "No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main.
transcript_json.translation: 英国诗人约翰·多恩在 17 世纪写道：“没有人是一座孤岛，可以自全；每个人都是大陆的一片，整体的一部分。

transcript_json.text: " Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical and cultural level than people realise.
transcript_json.translation: ”而如今，一位英国学者声称，人的个体性其实只是一种幻觉，因为社会在精神、身体和文化层面的相互关联远远超出人们的认识。

transcript_json.text: In his new book, The Self-Dillusion, Professor Tom Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and
transcript_json.translation: 在新书《自我错觉》中，雷丁大学生态与进化研究小组的研究员汤姆·奥利弗教授提出

transcript_json.text: In his new book, The Self Delusion, Professor Tom Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and Evolution group at the University of Reading, argues there is no such thing as "self" and not even our bodies are truly "us".
transcript_json.translation: 雷丁大学生态与进化研究组的研究员汤姆·奥利弗教授在新书《自我错觉》中提出，“自我”根本不存在，甚至我们的身体也并非真正的“我们”。

transcript_json.text: Just as Copernicus realised the Earth is not the center of the universe, Professor Oliver said society urgently needs a Copernican-like revolution to understand people are not detached beings but rather part of one connected identity.
transcript_json.translation: 正如哥白尼认识到地球不是宇宙的中心，奥利弗教授说，社会迫切需要一场哥白尼式的革命，认识到人不是孤立的个体，而是一个相互连接的整体的一部分。

transcript_json.text: "A significant milestone in the cultural evolution of human minds was the acceptance that the Earth is not the center of the universe, the so-called Copernican Revolution," he writes.
transcript_json.translation: 他写道：“人类心智文化进化的一个重要里程碑，是接受了地球并非宇宙中心这一事实，即所谓的哥白尼革命。”

transcript_json.text: "However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the center of a subjective universe.
transcript_json.translation: “然而，我们还有一个更大的迷思要破除：以为我们是独立的自我，存在于主观宇宙的中心。

transcript_json.text: You may feel as if you are an independent individual, acting autonomously in the world; that you have unchanging inner self that persists throughout your lifetime, acting as a central anchor-point with the world changing around you.
transcript_json.translation: 你也许觉得自己是独立的个体，在世界中自主行动；觉得自己有一个终生不变的内在自我，是连接世界的中心锚点，而周围的世界在不断变化。

transcript_json.text: This is the illusion I seek to tackle. We are intimately connected to the world around us.
transcript_json.translation: 我们与周围的世界紧密相连。

transcript_json.text: " Professor Oliver argues there are around 37 trillion cells in the body but most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks, so the material "us" is constantly changing.
transcript_json.translation: “奥利弗教授认为，人体内约有 37 万亿个细胞，但大多数细胞的寿命只有几天或几周，所以物质层面的“我们”在不断变化。

transcript_json.text: In fact, there is no part of your body that has existed for more than 10 years.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，你身体的任何部分都不曾存在超过 10 年。

transcript_json.text: "Since our bodies are essentially made anew every few weeks, the material in them alone is clearly insufficient to explain the persistent thread of an identity.
transcript_json.translation: “既然我们的身体基本上每隔几周就会翻新一遍，单凭其中的物质，显然不足以解释身份认同何以延续不变。

transcript_json.text: " Professor Oliver claims that individualism is actually bad for society, and only by realising we are a part of a bigger entity can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems.
transcript_json.translation: ”奥利弗教授声称，个人主义实际上对社会有害，只有认识到我们是更大整体的一部分，才能解决紧迫的环境和社会问题。

transcript_json.text: Through selfish over-consumption we are destroying the natural world and using non-renewable resources at an accelerating rate.
transcript_json.translation: 通过自私的过度消费，我们正在摧毁自然界，并以越来越快的速度消耗不可再生资源。

transcript_json.text: "We are at a critical crossroads as a species where we must rapidly reform our mindsets and behavior to act in less selfish ways," he said.
transcript_json.translation: 他说：“作为一个物种，我们正处在一个关键的十字路口，必须迅速革新思维方式和行为，以不那么自私的方式行事。”

transcript_json.text: So let's open our eyes to the hidden connections all around us.
transcript_json.translation: 所以，让我们睁开眼睛，看见身边那些隐形的联系吧。

transcript_json.text: Researchers described it as the smallest-ever remote-controlled walking robot.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员称它是有史以来最小的遥控行走机器人。

transcript_json.text: The tiny robot can bend, twist, crawl, walk, turn and even jump, without the use of complex hardware or special power.
transcript_json.translation: 这台微型机器人能弯曲、扭转、爬行、行走、转弯，甚至跳跃，而且不需要复杂硬件或特殊电源。

transcript_json.text: The engineers said this is because the robot is powered by the elastic property of its body.
transcript_json.translation: 工程师们说，这是因为机器人靠其身体的弹性特性来驱动。

transcript_json.text: To construct the robot, the researchers used a shape-memory alloy material that transforms to its remembered shape when heated.
transcript_json.translation: 为制造这台机器人，研究人员使用了一种形状记忆合金材料，它受热时会变回被记忆的形状。

transcript_json.text: Using a laser, the team is able to heat the robot at specific parts of its body, causing it to change shape.
transcript_json.translation: 利用激光，该团队能对机器人身体的特定部位加热，使其改变形状。

transcript_json.text: As the robot deforms and goes back to its original shape, it creates movement from one place to another.
transcript_json.translation: 机器人变形再恢复原状的过程，就产生了从一处到另一处的移动。

transcript_json.text: “Because these structures are so tiny, the rate of cooling is very fast,” project lead Prof. John A. Rogers said.
transcript_json.translation: "由于这些结构极其微小，冷却速度非常快，"项目负责人约翰·A·罗杰斯教授说。

transcript_json.text: “In fact, reducing the sizes of these robots allows them to run faster.”
transcript_json.translation: “事实上，把这些机器人的尺寸做小，反而能让它们跑得更快。”

transcript_json.text: While the research is still in the exploratory phase, the team believes the technology could lead to micro-sized robots that can perform practical tasks in tightly confined spaces.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然这项研究还处于探索阶段，但团队相信，这项技术能催生微型机器人，在极其狭小的空间里执行实际任务。

transcript_json.text: “You might imagine micro-robots as agents to repair or assemble small structures or machines in industry or as surgical assistants to clear clogged arteries, to stop internal bleeding or to eliminate cancerous tumors — all in minimally invasive procedures,” Rogers said.
transcript_json.translation: "你可以把微型机器人想象成工业中修理或组装小型结构和机器的作业者，或者想象成外科手术助手，用于疏通堵塞的动脉、止住内出血或消除癌性肿瘤——而且都是微创操作，"罗杰斯说。

transcript_json.text: I don't want to boast or anything, but I've always considered myself something of an elite sleeper.
transcript_json.translation: 我无意自夸什么的，但我一直觉得自己算是个精英睡眠者。

transcript_json.text: Given the opportunity, I will sleep for marathon stretches and can doze through the most extreme situations.
transcript_json.translation: 只要有机会，我能一睡就是马拉松式的长觉，再极端的环境也能照样打盹。

transcript_json.text: On one very rough ferry crossing on the route to the Isles of Scilly, for example, my travelling companions spent the entire three-hour ride throwing up in the bathroom while I dozed happily on a plastic chair.
transcript_json.translation: 比如，有一回去锡利群岛的渡轮遇上大风浪，同行伙伴在洗手间里吐了整整三个小时，而我在塑料椅上睡得香甜。

transcript_json.text: Unfortunately, it has come to my attention that I am not an elite sleeper after all.
transcript_json.translation: 遗憾的是，我后来发现，自己根本算不上精英睡眠者。

transcript_json.text: It seems I am just lazy.
transcript_json.translation: 看来我只是懒。

transcript_json.text: Because elite sleepers are defined as the approximately 3% of the population who are biologically programmed to need less sleep than the rest of us.
transcript_json.translation: 因为精英睡眠者指的是人群中约 3% 的人，他们的生物机能决定了他们天生就比我们其他人睡得少。

transcript_json.text: According to a study that came out in March, elite sleepers have rare genetic changes, which means they can sleep fewer hours than mere mortals without any risk of cognitive decline.
transcript_json.translation: 根据 3 月发表的一项研究，精英睡眠者拥有罕见的基因变异，这意味着他们能比普通人睡得更少，而不会有任何认知衰退的风险。

transcript_json.text: It may not be possible to change your own genes, but can you train yourself to need less sleep?
transcript_json.translation: 改变自己的基因或许不可能，但能不能训练自己减少睡眠需求呢？

transcript_json.text: Is there a non-biological way to reach elite sleeper status?
transcript_json.translation: 有没有不靠生物机能就能达到精英睡眠者境界的办法？

transcript_json.text: I have spent the past year trying to answer that question.
transcript_json.translation: 过去一年我一直在努力回答这个问题。

transcript_json.text: Not for fun, I should add, but because having a baby has severely disrupted my sleep, for which I still have a great passion.
transcript_json.translation: 我得说明，这可不是为了好玩，而是因为有了孩子后我的睡眠被严重打乱，而我对睡觉仍然怀有极大的热情。

transcript_json.text: For a while, I assumed I'd be forced to become one of those people who jump out of bed at the crack of dawn.
transcript_json.translation: 有一阵子，我以为自己将不得不变成那些天一亮就跳下床的人。

transcript_json.text: After a year of tough scientific study, however, I have discovered being forced to get up early in the morning is very different from being an early bird.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，经过一年艰苦的科学研究，我发现被迫早起与真正的早鸟完全是两回事。

transcript_json.text: If you read an article about a controversial issue, do you think you'd realise if it had changed your beliefs?

transcript_json.text: No one knows your own mind like you do — it seems obvious that you would know if your beliefs had shifted.
transcript_json.translation: 没有谁比你更了解你自己的内心——你的信念是否动摇了自己似乎理应知道。

transcript_json.text: And yet a new paper in The Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggests that we actually have very poor “awareness” of our own belief change, meaning that we will tend to underestimate how much we've been swayed by a convincing article.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你读到一篇关于争议话题的文章，你觉得你能察觉它是否改变了你的看法吗？没有人比你更了解自己的想法——如果你的看法变了，你似乎理所当然会知道。然而，《实验心理学季刊》上的一篇新论文表明，我们对自

transcript_json.text: The researchers recruited over 200 undergraduates across two studies and focused on their beliefs about whether physical punishment of kids is an effective form of discipline.
transcript_json.translation: 己看法变化的“觉察力”其实非常差，也就是说，我们往往会低估自己被一篇有说服力的文章改变了多少。研究人员在两项研究中招募了 200 多名本科生，聚焦他们对“体罚孩子是否是有效的管教方式”的看法。

transcript_json.text: The students reported their initial beliefs about whether physical punishment is an effective way to discipline a child on a scale from 1 (completely disbelieve) to 9 (completely believe).
transcript_json.translation: 学生们以 1（完全不信）到 9（完全相信）的量表，报告了他们对"体罚是否是管教孩子的有效方式"的最初看法。

transcript_json.text: Several weeks later, they were given one of two research-based texts to read.
transcript_json.translation: 几周后，他们拿到两篇基于研究的文章中的一篇来阅读。

transcript_json.text: Each was several pages long, and either presented the arguments and data in favor of physical punishment or against it.
transcript_json.translation: 学生们以 1 分（完全不相信）到 9 分（完全相信）的量表，报告了自己对“体罚是否是管教孩子的有效方式”的最初看法。几周后，他们分别拿到两篇

transcript_json.text: After this, the students answered some questions to test their comprehension and memory of the text.
transcript_json.translation: 基于研究的文章之一来读。每篇文章都有好几页，分别陈述支持或反对体罚的论点和数据。读完之后，学生们回答一些问题，以测试他们对文章的理解和记忆。

transcript_json.text: Then, the students again scored their belief in whether physical punishment is effective or not.
transcript_json.translation: 随后，学生们再次就“体罚是否有效”给自己的看法打分。

transcript_json.text: Finally, the researchers asked them to recall what their belief had been at the start of the study.
transcript_json.translation: 最后，研究人员请他们回忆研究开始时自己的看法是什么。

transcript_json.text: The students' belief about physical punishment changed when they read a text that argued against their own initial position.
transcript_json.translation: 当学生们读到与自己最初立场相悖的文章时，他们对体罚的看法发生了改变。

transcript_json.text: Crucially, the memory of their initial belief was shifted in the direction of their new belief — in fact, their memory was closer to their current belief than their original belief.
transcript_json.translation: 关键在于，他们对最初看法的记忆朝着新看法的方向偏移了——事实上，他们的记忆更接近当前看法，而不是最初看法。

transcript_json.text: The more their belief had changed, the larger this memory bias tended to be, suggesting the students were relying on their current belief to deduce their initial belief.
transcript_json.translation: 信念改变越大，这种记忆偏差往往就越大，这说明学生们是依据当前信念来推断最初信念的。

transcript_json.text: The memory bias was unrelated to the measures of how well they'd understood or recalled the text, suggesting these factors didn't play a role in memory of initial belief or awareness of belief change.
transcript_json.translation: 这种记忆偏差与他们理解或回忆文章的程度无关，表明这些因素在最初信念的记忆或信念变化的觉察上并未起作用。

transcript_json.text: The researchers conceded that this research was about changes to mostly moderate beliefs.
transcript_json.translation: 这种记忆偏差与他们理解或回忆文章的好坏无关，说明这些因素对最初看法的记忆或对看法改变的觉察并没有影响。研究人

transcript_json.text: It's likely the findings would be different in the context of changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs.
transcript_json.translation: 员承认，这项研究针对的主要是温和看法的改变。在极端或根深蒂固的看法发生改变的情况下，研究结果可能会有所不同。

transcript_json.text: However, our beliefs on most topics are in the moderate range, and as we go about our daily lives reading informative material, these intriguing findings suggest we are mostly ignorant of how what we just read has updated and altered our own position.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，我们在大多数话题上的信念都处于温和区间，而在日常生活中阅读各类资讯时，这些耐人寻味的发现表明：我们大多意识不到刚读到的内容已经在多大程度上更新、改变了我们自己的立场。

transcript_json.text: As the American population grows, so does the number of American moms.
transcript_json.translation: 随着美国人口增长，美国妈妈的人数也在增加。

transcript_json.text: But, more than a century after Mother's Day became an official holiday, even as that number increases, the share of the American population who are mothers is at the lowest point in a quarter century.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，在母亲节成为法定节日一百多年后的今天，即便这个数字还在增长，身为母亲的美国人所占比例却降到了 25 年来的最低点。

transcript_json.text: It's frequently noted that fertility rates are falling sharply in richer countries, but the less observed consequence of this trend is that a decline in births can also mean a decline in motherhood in general.
transcript_json.translation: 人们经常提到，较富裕国家的生育率正在急剧下降，但这一趋势一个较少被注意到的后果是，出生人数的下降也意味着母亲身份整体的衰落。

transcript_json.text: According to my analysis of data from the Census Bureau, the decline of American motherhood is real, occurring very quickly, and may continue for some time yet.
transcript_json.translation: 根据我对人口普查局数据的分析，美国母职的衰退是真实存在的，来得非常快，而且可能还会持续一段时间。

transcript_json.text: Not only are moms making up less of the population, but their characteristics are changing too, and in a way that might be linked to their proportional decline.
transcript_json.translation: 不仅妈妈们在人口中的占比在下降，她们的特征也在变化，而且这种变化可能与她们占比下降有关。

transcript_json.text: Moms today tend to be older than in the past.
transcript_json.translation: 如今的妈妈往往比过去年龄更大。

transcript_json.text: Just looking at recent years, the change in age-specific birth rates has been drastic.
transcript_json.translation: 仅就近年来看，各年龄段生育率的变化非常剧烈。

transcript_json.text: In just the past few years, the peak childbearing age range for American women has advanced from that of 25-to-29 to that of 30-to-34.
transcript_json.translation: 就在短短几年间，美国女性生育高峰年龄段已从 25 至 29 岁推移到 30 至 34 岁。

transcript_json.text: Meanwhile, childbearing among women under 20 has fallen by half or more, while childbearing among women 35 and older is rising.
transcript_json.translation: 与此同时，20 岁以下女性的生育减少了一半甚至更多，而 35 岁及以上女性的生育却在上升。

transcript_json.text: One positive consequence of this age shift is that a larger proportion of new mothers are economically prepared to raise children.
transcript_json.translation: 这一年龄变化的一个积极后果是，更大比例的新妈妈在经济上做好了养育孩子的准备。

transcript_json.text: Less positively, however, many women find that, as they age, they can't have as many kids as they would like.
transcript_json.translation: 不过不太积极的一面是，许多女性发现，随着年龄增长，她们无法要自己想要的那么多孩子。

transcript_json.text: Plus, having children later in life can increase the risk of health complications.
transcript_json.translation: 此外，晚育会增加出现健康并发症的风险。

transcript_json.text: These finer points aside, one major consequence of the older-moms trend is that fewer years of a woman's life are spent as a mother.
transcript_json.translation: 抛开这些细节不谈，妈妈年龄增大这一趋势的一个重大后果是，女性一生中身为人母的年头变少了。

transcript_json.text: This means that at any given time, a larger share of women and thus of the whole population will report not having children in government surveys.
transcript_json.translation: 这意味着在任何时点，政府调查中报告没有孩子的女性比例、进而整个人口中的比例都会更大。

transcript_json.text: In other words, later motherhood means less motherhood.
transcript_json.translation: 换句话说，晚当妈等于少当妈。

transcript_json.text: Even as motherhood rates decline, Mother's Day, of course, will endure.
transcript_json.translation: 即使为人母的比例在下降，母亲节当然仍会延续下去。

transcript_json.text: In fact, despite the demographic shift, retail spending on the holiday appears to be rising.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，尽管人口结构在变化，这一节日的零售消费似乎仍在上升。

transcript_json.text: It is hard to say if Mother's Day spending is rising more than one would expect given that the American population keeps growing.
transcript_json.translation: 考虑到美国人口持续增长，很难说母亲节消费的涨幅是否超出预期。

transcript_json.text: But one factor might be that the proportion of women who are the mothers of adult children is rising, and those adult children may spend more generously when it comes to celebrating the moms they no longer live with.
transcript_json.translation: 但一个可能的因素是，身为成年子女之母的女性比例在上升，而这些成年子女在孝敬不再同住的母亲时，花钱可能更大方。

transcript_json.text: Since NASA published a paper in 1989 claiming that houseplants can soak up pollution and toxic chemicals, businesses and homeowners have increasingly invested in greenery to help clean their air.
transcript_json.translation: 自美国国家航空航天局（NASA）1989 年发表论文称室内植物能吸收污染和有毒化学物质以来，企业和房主们越来越多地投资绿植来净化空气。

transcript_json.text: But a new analysis suggests it could actually take more than 1,000 plants per square meter to gain a benefit any greater than simply opening a couple of windows.
transcript_json.translation: 但一项新分析表明，实际上可能需要每平方米超过 1000 株植物，带来的好处才能胜过仅仅打开几扇窗。

transcript_json.text: The problem lies in the fact that NASA conducted their test in sealed containers that do not simulate the conditions in most people's homes or offices.
transcript_json.translation: 问题在于，NASA 的测试是在密封容器中进行的，这并不能模拟大多数人家里或办公室的环境。

transcript_json.text: The space agency was primarily concerned about keeping the air fresh for astronauts' cut-off in biosphere or space stations and helping to combat sick building syndrome, which had become a problem due to the super-insulated and energy-efficient offices of the late 1970s.
transcript_json.translation: 该航天机构主要关心的是让在生物圈或空间站中与外界隔绝的宇航员保持空气新鲜，并帮助对抗病态建筑综合征——由于 20 世纪 70 年代末超高保温、高能效的办公室，这种综合征已成为一个问题。

transcript_json.text: By the early 1980s, workers regularly complained of skin rashes, sleepiness, headaches, and allergies as they breathed in toxic chemicals from paints and plastics.
transcript_json.translation: 到 20 世纪 80 年代初，工人们因吸入油漆和塑料中的有毒化学物质，经常抱怨出现皮疹、嗜睡、头痛和过敏。

transcript_json.text: NASA found that certain plants could remove chemicals from the air, and even today, garden centers recommend the plants for air-cleaning properties.
transcript_json.translation: NASA 发现某些植物能清除空气中的化学物质，时至今日，园艺中心仍在推荐这些植物的空气净化功效。

transcript_json.text: However, a new evaluation of dozens of studies spanning 30 years found that houseplants in a normal environment have little impact.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，一项对 30 年间数十项研究的新评估发现，在正常环境中，室内植物的影响微乎其微。

transcript_json.text: In fact, natural ventilation is far better at cleaning the air.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，自然通风净化空气的效果要好得多。

transcript_json.text: The researchers also calculated the clean air delivery rate for plants in the studies they analyzed and found that the rate at which plants dispersed the compounds was well below the usual rate of air exchange in a normal building caused by the movements of people coming and going, opening doors and windows.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员还计算了所分析研究中植物的洁净空气输送率，发现植物分解这些化合物的速率，远低于普通建筑中因人员进出、开关门窗而形成的正常空气交换速率。

transcript_json.text: Many of the studies did show a reduction in the concentration of volatile organic compounds over time, which is likely why people have seized on them to praise the air-purifying virtues of plants.
transcript_json.translation: 许多研究确实显示了挥发性有机化合物浓度随时间下降，这大概就是人们借此大加赞赏植物空气净化美德的原因。

transcript_json.text: But the research's calculation showed it would take 10 to 1,000 plants per square meter of floor space to compete with the air-cleaning capacity of a building's air-handling system or even just a couple of open windows in a house.
transcript_json.translation: 但该研究的计算表明，每平方米地面需要 10 到 1000 株植物，才能与建筑物空气处理系统的空气净化能力相匹敌，甚至只是与家里开着的几扇窗相当。

transcript_json.text: In contrast, NASA's sealed experiment recommended one potted plant per 100 square feet.
transcript_json.translation: 相比之下，NASA 的密封实验建议每 100 平方英尺放一盆植物。

transcript_json.text: This is certainly an example of how scientific findings can be misleading or misinterpreted over time.
transcript_json.translation: 这无疑是一个例子，说明科学发现随时间推移可能会产生误导或被误读。

transcript_json.text: But it's also a great example of how scientific research should continually reexamine and question findings to get closer to the ground truth of understanding what's actually happening.
transcript_json.translation: 但它也是一个绝佳的例子，说明科学研究应当不断重新审视和质疑既有发现，以便更接近于理解实际情况的真相。

transcript_json.text: All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded.
transcript_json.translation: 牛津大学得出结论：所有社会都靠七条普世道德规则维系，其中包括服从上级和尊重他人财产。

transcript_json.text: Although many cultures are moving towards more liberal, less hierarchical organizations, the new research suggests that traditional power structures and basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管许多文化正走向更自由、等级更弱的组织形式，这项新研究表明，传统的权力结构以及仁爱与友爱的基本价值观，才是成功社会的基石。

transcript_json.text: The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all communities operate under seven basic moral codes.
transcript_json.translation: 这项对全球 60 种不同文化的大规模研究发现，所有社群都在七条基本道德准则下运转。

transcript_json.text: Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favours, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly and respect the property of others.
transcript_json.translation: 这些普世规则是：帮助家人、帮助群体、知恩图报、勇

transcript_json.text: The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter-gatherers or advanced civilizations, helping to uphold civilized society and foster social cooperation, researchers found.
transcript_json.translation: 敢无畏、服从上级、公平分配资源、尊重他人财产。

transcript_json.text: "Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code," said Dr. Oliver Scott Curry, lead author and senior researcher at Oxford.
transcript_json.translation: “世界各地的每个人都共享一套共同的道德准则，”该研究第一作者、牛津大学高级研究员奥利弗·斯科特·柯里博士说道。

transcript_json.text: "These seven moral rules appear to be universal across cultures because people face the same social problems.
transcript_json.translation: “这七条道德规则在各文化中似乎是普世的，因为人们面对的是同样的社会问题。

transcript_json.text: Even if some of these traits look right-wing or conservative, for example, deferring to authority, left-wing people will still have a group loyalty and deference to someone or something."
transcript_json.translation: 即使其中有些特质看起来偏右翼或保守，比如服从权威，左翼

transcript_json.text: The study, published in Current Anthropology, is the largest and most comprehensive cross-cultural survey of morality ever conducted.
transcript_json.translation: 人士也仍然会对某个群体忠诚，并服从某人或某种事物。”

transcript_json.text: The team examined the ethnographic records of 60 societies from around the world.
transcript_json.translation: 研究团队检视了来自世界各地 60 个社会的民族志记录。

transcript_json.text: They found that the seven rules were considered morally good in all societies and were observed across all continents, religions, and politics.
transcript_json.translation: 他们发现，这七条规则在所有社会都被视为道德上正确，并在各大洲、各宗教和各政治体制中都被遵守。

transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 2

transcript_json.text: When it comes to food, color is money.
transcript_json.translation: 对食品而言，颜色就是金钱。

transcript_json.text: Food companies know that better color gives better prices, so they ensure that their products are attractive in color to bolster earnings.
transcript_json.translation: 食品公司深知颜色好就能卖个好价钱，所以他们确保产品颜色诱人，以提高收益。

transcript_json.text: Oranges, for example, have to meet specific color standards, and oranges are just the beginning.
transcript_json.translation: 比如，橙子必须达到特定的颜色标准，而橙子只是个开始。

transcript_json.text: There are color standards for foods including French fries, tomatoes, pumpkins, olives, honey, and cherries.
transcript_json.translation: 包括炸薯条、番茄、南瓜、橄榄、蜂蜜和樱桃在内的食品都有颜色标准。

transcript_json.text: The attention to color is for good reason.
transcript_json.translation: 对颜色的讲究是有充分理由的。

transcript_json.text: For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of our eating experience.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管人们总说味觉靠舌头，但我们吃饭时最重要的器官可能其实是眼睛。

transcript_json.text: A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision, while only a percent or two is given over to taste faculties, and the result is that color actually changes how we taste food.
transcript_json.translation: 大脑的很大一部分功能用于处理视觉，而只有百分之一二负责味觉，结果是颜色实际上改变了我们对食物的味觉体验。

transcript_json.text: Scientists have demonstrated many times the importance of color to taste.
transcript_json.translation: 科学家已多次证明颜色对味觉的重要性。

transcript_json.text: In a 1980s study, for example, test participants were asked to name the flavor of the beverage they were drinking without being able to see that beverage.
transcript_json.translation: 例如，在 20 世纪 80 年代的一项研究中，受试者被要求说出所喝饮料的味道，但不能看到饮料。

transcript_json.text: Only one in five was able to identify it as orange.
transcript_json.translation: 五个人中只有一人认出那是橙子味。

transcript_json.text: But when they were allowed to see what they were drinking which was orange in color, each of them identified the orange flavor.
transcript_json.translation: 但当允许他们看到自己喝的是橙色的饮料时，每个人都辨认出了橙子味。

transcript_json.text: And when a drink that was lime flavor was colored orange, nearly half of respondents identified the flavor of the beverage as orange.
transcript_json.translation: 而当酸橙味的饮料被调成橙色时，近一半受访者把饮料的味道说成了橙子味。

transcript_json.text: None made that mistake when the beverage was green in color.
transcript_json.translation: 当饮料是绿色时，没人犯这种错误。

transcript_json.text: What's happening when someone fails to identify the flavor of a beverage they can't see or that has an abnormal color?
transcript_json.translation: 当有人无法辨认看不到的饮料或颜色异常的饮料的味道时，到底发生了什么？

transcript_json.text: Is it that participants can't discern what the flavor is, and so rely on visual cues?
transcript_json.translation: 是参与者分辨不出味道，于是依赖视觉线索？

transcript_json.text: Or does color actually change the experience of taste?
transcript_json.translation: 还是颜色真的改变了味觉体验？

transcript_json.text: The key to these questions is the effect of color on expectation.
transcript_json.translation: 这些问题的关键在于颜色对预期的影响。

transcript_json.text: The brain makes predictions using color.
transcript_json.translation: 大脑利用颜色做预测。

transcript_json.text: These predictions rely on expectations that come from experience.
transcript_json.translation: 这些预测依赖于来自经验的预期。

transcript_json.text: Research shows that we're all born liking sweet things and desire to eat them, but we aren't born knowing what the sweet things we crave look like.
transcript_json.translation: 研究表明，我们天生就喜欢甜食、想吃甜食，但我们并非生来就知道自己渴望的甜食长什么样。

transcript_json.text: So we need to learn this over time.
transcript_json.translation: 所以我们需要花时间慢慢学习。

transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: Searching for meaning is something many of us experience throughout our lives.
transcript_json.translation: 追寻人生意义是我们许多人一生中都会经历的事。

transcript_json.text: For some, this meaning is religious, some political and some interpersonal.
transcript_json.translation: 对有些人来说，这种意义是宗教性的，有些是政治性的，有些则是人际层面的。

transcript_json.text: And having a sense of meaning can bring us happiness.
transcript_json.translation: 拥有意义感能给我们带来幸福。

transcript_json.text: A new study looks at the relationship between meaning and happiness in the context of financial resources.
transcript_json.translation: 一项新研究在经济资源的背景下

transcript_json.text: Rhia Catapano from the University of Toronto and colleagues find meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness for rich people than poorer people, suggesting economic resources can impact how we experience meaning.
transcript_json.translation: 考察意义与幸福之间的关系。

transcript_json.text: The team analysed data from over 500,000 people across 123 countries.
transcript_json.translation: 团队分析了来自 123 个国家 50 多万人的数据。

transcript_json.text: The first study used data from a daily poll of US residents collected between 2013 and 2015.
transcript_json.translation: 第一项研究使用了 2013 至 2015 年间收集的美国居民每日民调数据。

transcript_json.text: Well-being was tracked using measures of positive affect—whether, during the day before they were surveyed, participants had smiled or laughed a lot or experienced a lot of happiness.
transcript_json.translation: 幸福感通过积极情绪指标来追踪——即受访前一天，参与者是否经常微笑或大笑、是否体验到大量幸福感。

transcript_json.text: Meaning was measured through a daily "purpose index", which explored the extent to which participants felt that they like what they do every day and are motivated to achieve their goals.
transcript_json.translation: 意义则通过每日“目标指数”来衡量，考察参与者在多大程度上觉得自己喜欢每天做的事、并有动力去实现目标。

transcript_json.text: Finally, income levels were assessed.
transcript_json.translation: 最后再评估收入水平。

transcript_json.text: The results showed that the correlation between meaning and happiness was strongest among those in lower income brackets.
transcript_json.translation: 结果显示，意义与幸福之间的相关性在低收入人群中最强。

transcript_json.text: But as income levels increased, the correlation became weaker.
transcript_json.translation: 但随着收入水平提高，相关性变弱了。

transcript_json.text: The second study looked at worldwide data.
transcript_json.translation: 第二项研究考察的是全球数据。

transcript_json.text: Happiness was measured using the same questions as in the first study, while meaning was measured using the single question: "Do you feel your life has an important purpose or meaning?"
transcript_json.translation: 幸福感的测量沿用第一项研究中的同一套问题，而意义感则用一个问题来测量：“你觉得你的生活有重要的目的或意义吗

transcript_json.text: Again, the strength of the relationship between meaning and happiness depended on participants' income.
transcript_json.translation: ”同样，意义与幸福之间关联的强度取决于参与者的收入。

transcript_json.text: Meaning had a greater influence on happiness for those on lower incomes compared to those in higher brackets.
transcript_json.translation: 与高收入人群相比，意义对低收入人群幸福的影响更大。

transcript_json.text: In the final study, French participants indicated the extent to which they felt they led a purposeful and meaningful life and how much they considered themselves a happy person.
transcript_json.translation: 在最后一项研究中，法国参与者表明他们在多大程度上觉得自己过着有目标、有意义的生活，以及在多大程度上认为自己是快乐的人。

transcript_json.text: Finally, rather than using specific income brackets, they placed themselves on a social ladder, representing where they stood in terms of wealth, education and occupation.
transcript_json.translation: 最后，他们不按具体的收入区间划分，而是把自己放在一个社会阶梯上，代表他们在财富、教育和职业方面所处的位置。

transcript_json.text: The results from the study duplicated those of the first two.
transcript_json.translation: 这项研究的结果与前两项研究一致。

transcript_json.text: So overall, meaning and happiness had a stronger relationship for those with fewer resources than those with more.
transcript_json.translation: 总体而言，对资源较少的人来说，意义与幸福的关系比资源较多的人更紧密。

transcript_json.text: This might be the case because richer individuals have more access to other sources of happiness, many of which will be external, like lack of stress or community.
transcript_json.translation: 情况可能是这样：因为更富有的人有更多途径获得其他幸福来源，其中许多是外在的，比如没有压力或社区归属。

transcript_json.text: Thus, a focus on an internal sense of satisfaction, purpose or meaning is less important.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，专注于内在的满足感、目标感或意义就没那么重要了。

transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 1

transcript_json.text: W: Hi Alan, sorry for not calling you back sooner.
transcript_json.translation: W: 你好，艾伦，抱歉没能早点回你电话。

transcript_json.text: You said on the phone you had something you needed to discuss with me?
transcript_json.translation: 你电话里说有件事要跟我谈谈？

transcript_json.text: M: Well, to get right down to it, I'm having second thoughts about my major.
transcript_json.translation: M: 嗯，直说了吧，我对自己的专业动摇了。

transcript_json.text: With my family situation getting more complicated, and the end of my university education nearing, persisting with art history just doesn't seem the right choice.
transcript_json.translation: 家里情况越来越复杂，大学学业也快结束了，继续读艺术史似乎不是个正确的选择。

transcript_json.text: W: Alan, in the last three years, I have heard nothing but how passionate you are about the art history program.
transcript_json.translation: W: 艾伦，这三年里，我听到的全是你对艺术史项目有多热爱。

transcript_json.text: You often told fellow classmates how fabulous the instructors were, and that you finally felt accepted.
transcript_json.translation: 你常跟同学们说老师们多么出色，说你终于有了归属感。

transcript_json.text: What would cause you to abandon it?
transcript_json.translation: 是什么让你想放弃呢？

transcript_json.text: M: My father's current financial situation has helped me realize that a more financially viable employment opportunity is not necessarily a bad thing.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我父亲目前的财务状况让我意识到，一份经济上更有保障的工作机会未必是坏事。

transcript_json.text: Art history nourishes my soul, but does nothing to put food on my plate.
transcript_json.translation: 艺术史滋养我的灵魂，却填不饱我的肚子。

transcript_json.text: W: What about all the work opportunities I discussed with you last month?
transcript_json.translation: W: 我上个月和你讨论的那些工作机会呢？

transcript_json.text: Have you gone to those places of business to investigate whether any legitimate positions might be available for someone with your background?
transcript_json.translation: 你去那些单位打听过了吗，看你这种背景的人有没有正式职位可做？

transcript_json.text: M: Um, well...
transcript_json.translation: M: 呃，这个……

transcript_json.text: W: Look, Alan, if your heart is set on working in the art industry, you need to be more assertive and start talking with people.
transcript_json.translation: W: 听着，艾伦，如果你铁了心要进艺术行业，就得更主动些，开始跟人打交道。

transcript_json.text: Networking is key if you want to become a celebrity in the world of museums and galleries.
transcript_json.translation: 想成为博物馆和画廊圈子里响当当的人物，人脉是关键。

transcript_json.text: M: Time is a very precious commodity right now.
transcript_json.translation: M: 眼下时间太宝贵了。

transcript_json.text: My social life does not exist.
transcript_json.translation: 我的社交生活根本不存在。

transcript_json.text: I can barely keep up with my studies and thesis is due by the end of this year.
transcript_json.translation: 我连学业都快跟不上了，论文年底就要交。

transcript_json.text: When can I find time to research jobs when I have so much to do as it is?
transcript_json.translation: 我眼下要做的事已经堆成山，哪还有时间去找工作？

transcript_json.text: W: What you do now will determine your future options.
transcript_json.translation: W: 你现在做的，将决定你将来有哪些选择。

transcript_json.text: Now is the optimum time to put forth your best effort.
transcript_json.translation: 现在正是拿出全部努力的最佳时机。

transcript_json.text: M: I will take what you said into consideration.
transcript_json.translation: M: 你说的我会考虑。

transcript_json.text: The advice is much appreciated.
transcript_json.translation: 非常感谢你的建议。

transcript_json.text: M: Have you decided yet what your end of semester business project will be on?

transcript_json.text: W: Yes, how about you?

transcript_json.text: M: Yes, go on. You go first.
transcript_json.translation: M: 好，说吧。你先来。

transcript_json.text: W: I'm going to do it about beef.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我打算以牛肉为题。

transcript_json.text: M: Beef?
transcript_json.translation: M: 牛肉？

transcript_json.text: W: Yeah, beef.
transcript_json.translation: W: 对，牛肉。

transcript_json.text: I'm going to design a business case study for a cow farm that supplies beef for the domestic market.
transcript_json.translation: 我打算为一家给国内市场供应牛肉的养牛场设计一份商业案例研究。

transcript_json.text: M: Wow, that sounds very interesting and original.
transcript_json.translation: M: 哇，听起来很有意思，也很有新意。

transcript_json.text: Where ever did you get that idea?
transcript_json.translation: 你这主意是怎么想出来的？

transcript_json.text: W: I don't know, it just came to me I guess. But think about it.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我也不知道，大概就是突然想到的吧。不过你想想看。

transcript_json.text: Beef consumption has been rising strongly over the past 20 years.
transcript_json.translation: 过去20年牛肉消费一直在强劲增长。

transcript_json.text: As the economy continues to grow, consumer demand is expected to continue to increase, for the foreseeable future.
transcript_json.translation: 随着经济持续增长，在可预见的未来，消费需求预计还会继续上升。

transcript_json.text: And currently, most of the beef is imported, which brings with it added fees.
transcript_json.translation: 而且目前大部分牛肉靠进口，会带来额外费用。

transcript_json.text: So why not raise cattle here?
transcript_json.translation: 那为什么不在这里养牛呢？

transcript_json.text: M: Of course.
transcript_json.translation: M: 那当然。

transcript_json.text: Makes perfect sense.
transcript_json.translation: 太有道理了。

transcript_json.text: There's plenty of land out west, so if done right, it should be very profitable to raise our own cattle.
transcript_json.translation: 西部有的是土地，只要经营得当，我们自己养牛应该非常赚钱。

transcript_json.text: W: Exactly.

transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 1

transcript_json.text: Increased television time for young children has long been linked with poorer progress in some areas of development.
transcript_json.translation: 幼儿看电视时间过长，长期以来都被认为与某些发育领域的进步较慢有关。

transcript_json.text: One possible way to counter those negative effects is talking while watching the screen.
transcript_json.translation: 一个可能的化解办法是看电视时多交谈。

transcript_json.text: As a new study suggests, the more parents engaged in conversation with preschoolers during TV time, the more likely those children were to have higher curiosity levels when they reached kindergarten.
transcript_json.translation: 一项新研究表明，家长在看电视期间与学龄前孩子交谈越多，这些孩子上幼儿园时好奇心水平就越可能更高。

transcript_json.text: This was particularly true for children with socioeconomic disadvantages.
transcript_json.translation: 对社会经济处境不利的孩子来说尤其如此。

transcript_json.text: "Our findings reinforce the importance of parent conversation to promote early childhood development and curiosity," said lead author Prachi Shah at University of Michigan Health C.S. Mott Children's Hospital.
transcript_json.translation: “我们的发现进一步印证了家长交谈对促进幼儿发展和好奇心的重要性，”研究第一作者、密歇根大学健康C.S.莫特儿童医院的普拉奇·沙阿说。

transcript_json.text: Researchers assessed hours of daily television exposure and frequency of parent screen time conversation among 1,500 preschoolers.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员评估了1500名学龄前儿童每天看电视的时长，以及家长在屏幕时间与他们交谈的频率。

transcript_json.text: And then measured early childhood curiosity in kindergarten.
transcript_json.translation: 然后在他们上幼儿园时测量幼儿期的好奇心。

transcript_json.text: The study specifically focused on curiosity levels, which are associated with enhanced learning and higher academic achievement in reading and math at kindergarten.
transcript_json.translation: 这项研究专门关注好奇心水平，好奇心与幼儿园阶段更强的学习能力、更高的读写和数学成绩相关。

transcript_json.text: And behavioral developmental benefits, especially for children from families with lower socioeconomic status.
transcript_json.translation: 还有行为发育上的益处，对来自社会经济地位较低家庭的孩子尤其明显。

transcript_json.text: While many young children are now growing up with digital media exposure through mobile devices like tablets and phones.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然如今许多幼儿是伴随着平板电脑和手机等移动设备的数字媒体接触成长的，

transcript_json.text: Television remains a dominant screen activity, accounting for 72% of all screen time.
transcript_json.translation: 但电视仍然是占主导地位的屏幕活动，占全部屏幕时间的72%。

transcript_json.text: TVs are in 98% of all homes, keeping television exposure a relevant developmental context in young children.
transcript_json.translation: 98%的家庭都有电视，看电视因此仍是幼儿发展中一个重要的环境因素。

transcript_json.text: Excessive media exposure, including television, can displace exploratory activities such as play and parent child interactions, which are believed to be key to cultivating curiosity in kids.
transcript_json.translation: 包括电视在内的过度媒体接触，会挤占玩耍、亲子互动等探索性活动，而人们认为这些活动正是培养孩子好奇心的关键。

transcript_json.text: Our findings suggest the importance of parents finding opportunities to foster conversational exchanges in daily routines with their young children, including while watching television, Shah said.
transcript_json.translation: 沙阿说，我们的发现表明，家长要在日常生活中——包括看电视时——寻找机会与幼儿多进行对话交流，这一点很重要。

transcript_json.text: PASSAGE 2
transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 2

transcript_json.text: Humans are aspirational, goal seeking beings.
transcript_json.translation: 人类是有抱负、追逐目标的生物。

transcript_json.text: Each of us, according to research, has an inborn drive to acquire.
transcript_json.translation: 研究表明，我们每个人天生都有获取的驱动力。

transcript_json.text: The dark side of this drive to acquire is being mindlessly driven to possess more and more things and to socially compare our stuff with all the stuff other people have in their lives.
transcript_json.translation: 这种获取驱动力的阴暗面是：盲目地被驱使去占有越来越多的东西，并拿自己的东西和别人生活中的东西作比较。

transcript_json.text: So the question is, how do we ensure we tap into our drive to acquire in positive ways that will benefit our well being?
transcript_json.translation: 那么问题来了：我们如何确保以有益于幸福感的方式正面利用自己的获取驱动力呢？

transcript_json.text: One way is to become more intentionally aspirational.
transcript_json.translation: 一个办法是更有意识地怀抱志向。

transcript_json.text: To be intentionally aspirational includes consciously aspiring to be the person you need to be to succeed in your professional and personal life.
transcript_json.translation: 有意识地怀抱志向，包括自觉努力成为在职业和个人生活中取得成功所需要成为的那种人。

transcript_json.text: It also includes consciously aspiring to acquire things in your life that will positively impact your sense of well being.
transcript_json.translation: 也包括自觉地争取获得生活中能给你的幸福感带来积极影响的东西。

transcript_json.text: If you're not consciously, mindfully, and intentionally harnessing your inborn drive to acquire, you might be mindlessly pursuing all the wrong things.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你没有自觉地、用心地、有意图地驾驭这种天生的获取驱动力，就可能稀里糊涂地追求一堆错误的东西。

transcript_json.text: While your intentional, aspirational goals will include the pursuit of acquiring things that will increase your sense of well being, they ought to also include goals to help other people in your various life roles.
transcript_json.translation: 你有意识的志向目标除了包括追求能提升幸福感的东西，还应当包括在你扮演的各种人生角色中帮助他人的目标。

transcript_json.text: Your intentional, aspirational goals will also include striving to be your personal best, a person of good character, integrity, and trustworthiness.
transcript_json.translation: 你有意识的志向目标还应包括努力做到最好的自己，做一个品格良好、正直可靠的人。

transcript_json.text: Think about this from a practical rather than theoretical viewpoint.
transcript_json.translation: 从实际而非理论的角度想想这一点。

transcript_json.text: If you're not pursuing intentional aspirational goals, you have nothing to strive for.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你不去追求有意识的志向目标，你就没有奋斗的方向。

transcript_json.text: If you have nothing to strive for, you're putting yourself in the dangerous position of simply drifting through life, and you'll not be able to experience, live, and enjoy all that life has to offer.
transcript_json.translation: 没有奋斗的方向，你就会把自己置于浑浑噩噩混日子的危险境地，无法体验、感受并享受生活给予的一切。
