transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 1

transcript_json.text: It's revision time for exams and dissertations.
transcript_json.translation: 又到了备考和写论文的复习阶段。

transcript_json.text: The pressure is on, so you'll want all the help you can get to age your memory and raise your grades.
transcript_json.translation: 压力山大，所以你需要一切能帮上忙的办法来增强记忆、提高成绩。

transcript_json.text: As a nutrition expert, I want to say that eating well can make a real difference to your revision regime.
transcript_json.translation: 作为一名营养专家，我想说，吃得好真能给你的复习状态带来实实在在的改变。

transcript_json.text: So, what brain boosting food and drink would I recommend?
transcript_json.translation: 那么，我会推荐哪些健脑饮食呢？

transcript_json.text: Coffee can have numerous benefits.
transcript_json.translation: 咖啡有不少好处。

transcript_json.text: However, while coffee may make you more alert, Individuals can build up a tolerance, meaning this is short lived.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，咖啡虽然能让你更清醒，但人会产生耐受性，所以效果短暂。

transcript_json.text: Coffee can also increase blood sugar and eventually cause lack of focus and energy.
transcript_json.translation: 咖啡还会升高血糖，最终导致注意力不集中、精力不足。

transcript_json.text: It's also worth noting that people react differently to coffee.
transcript_json.translation: 还值得注意的是，人对咖啡的反应各不相同。

transcript_json.text: Some people can drink it at midnight and go straight to sleep, whereas others get feelings of anxiety after a small amount.
transcript_json.translation: 有人半夜喝了照睡不误，有人喝一点点就焦虑。

transcript_json.text: Also remember that coffee from a coffee shop may be stronger than coffee made at home, so stop drinking coffee by 2 p.m. and have a maximum of two cups of coffee a day.
transcript_json.translation: 还要记住，咖啡店的咖啡可能比家里做的更浓，所以下午两点后就不要再喝咖啡，每天最多两杯。

transcript_json.text: But be aware of your own reaction to it.
transcript_json.translation: 但要留意自己对咖啡的反应。

transcript_json.text: Whole grain foods will ward off hunger.
transcript_json.translation: 全谷物食品能抵御饥饿。

transcript_json.text: Examples include porridge and whole wheat bread.
transcript_json.translation: 比如粥和全麦面包。

transcript_json.text: Combining whole grain foods with protein will help keep your blood sugar levels balanced, which is essential for mood and concentration.
transcript_json.translation: 全谷物搭配蛋白质有助于保持血糖平稳，这对情绪和专注力至关重要。

transcript_json.text: Berries and nuts are a convenient and nutritious snack.
transcript_json.translation: 浆果和坚果是方便又营养的零食。

transcript_json.text: Blueberries, like many dark colored fruits and vegetables, can slow down brain damage and age-related decline.
transcript_json.translation: 蓝莓和许多深色果蔬一样，能减缓大脑损伤和与年龄相关的衰退。

transcript_json.text: Frozen berries are also a good choice.
transcript_json.translation: 冷冻浆果也是不错的选择。

transcript_json.text: They are usually cheap, last longer, and don't lose their nutrients when frozen.
transcript_json.translation: 它们通常便宜、保存更久，冷冻时也不会损失营养。

transcript_json.text: But flavored and coated nuts are less healthy, as they contain added oil, salt, and sugar.
transcript_json.translation: 但调味和裹衣坚果就没那么健康，因为含有额外的油、盐和糖。

transcript_json.text: Doctors often recommend taking vitamin supplements to top up on the nutrients you need.
transcript_json.translation: 医生常建议服用维生素补充剂来补足所需营养。

transcript_json.text: But I would say food should always come before supplements, and the key to getting as many nutrients as possible is to eat a varied diet, with lots of different colors such as frozen berries and dark green vegetables.
transcript_json.translation: 但我要说，食物永远比补充剂重要，想尽可能多地摄入营养，关键是饮食多样化、颜色丰富，比如冷冻浆果和深绿色蔬菜。

transcript_json.text: It's better to get everything you need from food and drink.
transcript_json.translation: 所需的营养最好都从日常饮食中获取。

transcript_json.text: For example, oranges contain not only vitamin C, which boosts the immune system, but also fiber and other components that you can't get packaged together in a tablet.
transcript_json.translation: 比如橙子不仅含有增强免疫力的维生素C，还有纤维和其他成分，这些在一粒药片里是无法同时获得的。

transcript_json.text: Don't forget to drink a proper amount of water, which can boost attention by almost 25%, and can elevate your mood as well.
transcript_json.translation: 别忘了喝适量的水，它能把注意力提高近25%，还能改善情绪。

transcript_json.text: Finally, don't skip meals.
transcript_json.translation: 最后，别不吃饭。

transcript_json.text: Eating regularly will help keep blood sugar balanced, and feed the brain with the fuel it needs.
transcript_json.translation: 规律进食有助于保持血糖平稳，为大脑提供所需的燃料。

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 2
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 2

transcript_json.text: A late Swedish academic has identified a worrying trend.
transcript_json.translation: 一位已故的瑞典学者发现了一个令人担忧的趋势。

transcript_json.text: Not only do many people across advanced economies have no idea that the world is becoming a much better place, but they actually even think the opposite.
transcript_json.translation: 在各个发达经济体中，许多人不仅不知道世界正在变得好得多，甚至以为恰恰相反。

transcript_json.text: This is no wonder, when the news focuses on reporting catastrophes, terrorist attacks, wars, and famines.
transcript_json.translation: 考虑到新闻总聚焦于报道灾难、恐怖袭击、战争和饥荒，这不足为奇。

transcript_json.text: Who wants to hear about the fact that every day some 200,000 people around the world are lifted above the two dollar a day poverty line?
transcript_json.translation: 每天全世界约有20万人摆脱日均两美元的贫困线，谁想听这种消息呢？

transcript_json.text: Or that more than 300,000 people get access to electricity and clean water for the first time every day?
transcript_json.translation: 还有每天有30多万人第一次用上电和清洁饮用水，谁想听呢？

transcript_json.text: These stories of people in low income countries simply don't make for exciting news coverage.
transcript_json.translation: 这些关于低收入国家民众的故事，实在算不上激动人心的新闻素材。

transcript_json.text: But as Rosling pointed out in his book Factfulness.
transcript_json.translation: 但正如罗斯林在其著作《事实》中指出的，

transcript_json.text: It's important to put all the bad news in perspective.
transcript_json.translation: 重要的是要正确看待所有这些坏消息。

transcript_json.text: While it is true that globalization has put some downward pressure on middle class wages in advanced economies in recent decades, it has also helped lift hundreds of millions of people out of poverty.
transcript_json.translation: 诚然，近几十年全球化给发达经济体的中产阶级工资带来了一些下行压力，但它也帮助数亿人摆脱了贫困。

transcript_json.text: If we really care about global welfare, globalization is the only way forward to ensure that economic prosperity is shared among all countries and not only a select few advanced economies.
transcript_json.translation: 如果我们真正关心全球福祉，全球化就是唯一的前进道路，才能确保经济繁荣为所有国家共享，而不只是少数几个发达经济体独享。

transcript_json.text: While some people glorify the past, One of the big facts of economic history is that until quite recently, a significant part of the world's population has lived under quite miserable conditions.
transcript_json.translation: 有人把过去美化得天花乱坠，但经济史上的一个重大事实是：直到不久之前，世界人口的相当一部分都生活在相当悲惨的境况中。

transcript_json.text: And this is true throughout most of human history.
transcript_json.translation: 在人类历史的大部分时间里，情况都是如此。

transcript_json.text: While there were many long lasting ups and downs, like the Great Depression or the recent Great Recession, the constancy of the long run growth rate is actually quite miraculous.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然有过许多长期的大起大落，比如大萧条或近年的大衰退，但长期增长率始终如一，其实相当了不起。

transcript_json.text: Low income countries, including China and India, have been growing at a significantly faster pace in recent decades, and are quickly catching up to the West.
transcript_json.translation: 包括中国和印度在内的低收入国家，近几十年增速明显更快，正在迅速追上西方。

transcript_json.text: A 10 percent growth rate over a prolonged period means that income levels double roughly every seven years.
transcript_json.translation: 长期保持10%的增长率，意味着收入水平大约每七年翻一番。

transcript_json.text: It is obviously good news if prosperity is more shared across the globe.
transcript_json.translation: 如果繁荣能在全球范围内被更均匀地分享，那显然是好消息。

transcript_json.text: While inequality within countries has gone up as a result of globalization, global inequality has been on a steady downward trend for several decades.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然全球化导致各国内部不平等加剧，但几十年来，全球范围内的不平等一直在稳步下降。

transcript_json.text: This is mostly a result of the improvement of hundreds of millions of people's living standards.
transcript_json.translation: 这主要是数亿人生活水平提高的结果。

transcript_json.text: In fact, for the first time ever since the Industrial Revolution, about half of the global population can be considered middle class.

transcript_json.text: We all know that the sense of smell is powerful.
transcript_json.translation: 我们都知道嗅觉很强大。

transcript_json.text: The delicious scent of bread, for example, can act like a time machine.
transcript_json.translation: 比如，面包的香气就像一台时光机。

transcript_json.text: One sniff can bring back a memory from many years ago.
transcript_json.translation: 一嗅就能唤起多年前的记忆。

transcript_json.text: Indeed, scent particles, in general, can revive memories that have been long forgotten.
transcript_json.translation: 的确，气味微粒总体上能唤醒早已被遗忘的记忆。

transcript_json.text: But why do smells sometimes trigger powerful memories, especially emotional ones?
transcript_json.translation: 但气味为什么有时会触发强烈的记忆，尤其是情感色彩浓的记忆呢？

transcript_json.text: The short answer is that the brain regions that handle smells, memories, and emotions are linked.
transcript_json.translation: 简短的回答是：大脑中处理气味、记忆和情绪的区域是相连的。

transcript_json.text: A scent is a chemical particle that floats in through the nose and into the region of the brain responsible for smell, where the sensation is first processed into a form that the brain can read.
transcript_json.translation: 气味是一种化学微粒，从鼻子飘入大脑中负责嗅觉的区域，在那里，这种感受首先被加工成大脑能读取的形式。

transcript_json.text: Brain cells then carry that information to the area of the brain where emotions are processed, and then to an adjacent area of the brain where learning and memory formation take place.
transcript_json.translation: 然后，脑细胞把这些信息带到大脑处理情绪的区域，再带到旁边负责学习和记忆形成的区域。

transcript_json.text: Sense are the only sensations that travel such a direct path to the emotional and memory centers of the brain.
transcript_json.translation: 气味是唯一能以如此直接的路径抵达大脑情绪和记忆中枢的感觉。

transcript_json.text: That results in an intimate connection between emotions, memories, and sense.
transcript_json.translation: 这就造成了情绪、记忆和气味之间的紧密联系。

transcript_json.text: Which is why memories triggered by sense are experienced as more emotional than those triggered by sight or sound.
transcript_json.translation: 这也是为什么气味触发的记忆，比视觉或声音触发的记忆情感色彩更浓。

transcript_json.text: Let's take a closer look at how those memories are activated.
transcript_json.translation: 我们再细看这些记忆是如何被激活的。

transcript_json.text: Usually, when a person smells something that's connected to a meaningful event in their past, they'll first have an emotional response to the sensation, and then a memory might follow.
transcript_json.translation: 通常，当一个人闻到与过去某件重要事情相关的东西时，会先对这种气味产生情绪反应，然后记忆可能随之而来。

transcript_json.text: But sometimes, the memory doesn't come to the surface.
transcript_json.translation: 但有时，记忆并不会浮现出来。

transcript_json.text: The person might feel the emotion of something that happened in the past, but won't remember what they experienced.
transcript_json.translation: 这个人可能感受到往事带来的情绪，却不记得自己经历过什么。

transcript_json.text: What causes this baffling phenomenon?
transcript_json.translation: 是什么造成了这种令人费解的现象？

transcript_json.text: The explanation is context.
transcript_json.translation: 答案是情境。

transcript_json.text: Imagine this scenario.
transcript_json.translation: 想象这样一个场景。

transcript_json.text: A person is walking down the street, smelling a scent that they first encountered decades ago, which activates an emotional response.
transcript_json.translation: 一个人走在街上，闻到几十年前初次接触过的气味，这激活了一种情绪反应。

transcript_json.text: If the person had first come across that smell in a very different context, it will be much more difficult to recover the associated memory, because the brain uses the context to give meaning to the information and find that memory.
transcript_json.translation: 如果此人当初是在截然不同的情境下第一次闻到这种气味，那么要找回相关记忆就会困难得多，因为大脑要靠情境来赋予信息意义并找到那段记忆。

transcript_json.text: The special nature of memories brought back by scents notwithstanding, they have the same drawbacks as other memories.
transcript_json.translation: 气味唤起的记忆虽然有其特殊之处，但也有和其他记忆一样的缺点。

transcript_json.text: They aren't always accurate, and they can change over time.
transcript_json.translation: 它们并不总是准确，还会随时间改变。

transcript_json.text: In fact, each time we remember something, that memory can become distorted.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，我们每次回忆某件事，那段记忆都可能被扭曲。

transcript_json.text: But, because of the strong emotional associations these memories evoke, people who remember something due to a scent are often convinced that the memories are accurate, even when they aren't.
transcript_json.translation: 但由于这些记忆唤起的强烈情感联想，因气味而想起某事的人往往坚信记忆是准确的，哪怕其实并不准确。

transcript_json.text: When a person tries to access a memory, their brains quickly examine everything stored in it to find the relevant information.
transcript_json.translation: 当一个人试图提取一段记忆时，大脑会快速检索其中存储的一切，以找到相关信息。

transcript_json.text: But as we age, many of us have difficulty retrieving memories.
transcript_json.translation: 提取记忆方面会有困难。

transcript_json.text: In a review published in the journal _Trends in Cognitive Sciences_ on February 11, researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories.
transcript_json.translation: 在 2 月 11 日发表于《认知科学趋势》期刊的一篇综述中，研究人员对这一现象的成因提出了解释。老年人的大脑把更多空间分配给了日积月累的知识，试图提取记忆时要翻找的材料也更多。

transcript_json.text: While this wealth of prior knowledge can make memory retrieval challenging, the researchers say it has its upsides—this life experience can aid with creativity and decision-making.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然这种丰富的既有知识会让记忆提取变得困难，但研究人员说它也有好处。这种人生阅历有助于创造力和决策。

transcript_json.text: Researchers Tarek Amer, Jordana Wynn and Lynn Hasher looked at several behavioral and brain-imaging studies, which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing information that is no longer relevant and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other, irrelevant memories along with it.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员塔里克·阿梅尔、乔丹娜·阮以及琳恩·哈舍这几位研究人员查看了多项行为学和脑成像研究。这些研究表明，老年人难以抑制那些已不再相关的信息，而且在搜寻某段特定记忆时，常常会把其他不相关的记忆一并提取出来。

transcript_json.text: The studies also showed that when given a cognitive task, older adults rely more heavily on previous knowledge than younger adults do.
transcript_json.translation: 这些研究还表明，在完成认知任务时，老年人比年轻人更依赖以往的知识。虽然研究人员主要关注

transcript_json.text: While the researchers focus primarily on the difficulties that these disorderly-crowded memories may pose, they also highlight a few situations in which these same memory patterns may be useful.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然研究人员主要关注这些杂乱拥挤的记忆可能带来的困难，但他们也强调了这些记忆模式可能派上用场的几种情形。

transcript_json.text: Evidence suggests that older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity as a function of enriched memories, the researchers write.
transcript_json.translation: 有证据表明，年长的成年人因记忆更丰富而保持了创造力，有时甚至有所增强，其他研究人员写道。

transcript_json.text: They further hypothesize that older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge when it comes to decision-making, where they can pull on their accumulated wisdom.
transcript_json.translation: 他们进一步推测，老年人也许能得益于自己的老年人可以调动自己积累的智慧，既有知识会让他们大受裨益。

transcript_json.text: There are at least four major problems with work in America today.
transcript_json.translation: 当今美国的工作至少存在四大问题。

transcript_json.text: First, work can be alienating.
transcript_json.translation: 第一，工作可能让人产生疏离感。

transcript_json.text: Workers are often not in control of how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the profits made from their work.
transcript_json.translation: 劳动者往往无法掌控自己怎样工作、何时工作、他们生产的商品和服务被如何处置，以及他们工作创造的利润被如何处置。

transcript_json.text: Second, workers are not paid the full value of their labor.
transcript_json.translation: 第二，劳动者没有得到与其劳动全部价值相称的报酬。

transcript_json.text: Real wages have not kept pace with productivity, driving economic inequality and a decline in labor's share of income.
transcript_json.translation: 实际工资未能与生产率同步增长，加剧了经济不平等和劳动收入份额的下降。

transcript_json.text: Third, people are time poor.
transcript_json.translation: 第三，人们的时间很匮乏。

transcript_json.text: In the U.S., full-time employees work an average of 8.72 hours per day despite productivity increases.
transcript_json.translation: 在美国，尽管生产率提高了，全职员工平均每天仍工作 8.72 小时。

transcript_json.text: Long working hours contribute to the feeling of time poverty, which has an adverse effect on psychological well-being.
transcript_json.translation: 72 小时。

transcript_json.text: Fourth, automation puts jobs and wages at risk.
transcript_json.translation: 第四，自动化使工作岗位和工资面临风险。

transcript_json.text: Technological innovation could in theory liberate people from the 40-hour workweek, but unless changes are made to the structure of work, automation will simply exert downward pressure on wages and further diminish work opportunities.
transcript_json.translation: 技术创新理论上可以把人从每周 40 小时的工作制中解放出来，但除非对工作结构做出变革，自动化只会对工资形成下行压力，并进一步削减就业机会。

transcript_json.text: So, what can be done to alleviate these problems?
transcript_json.translation: 那么，能做些什么来缓解这些问题呢？

transcript_json.text: There are competing visions of the best way to arrive at a solution.
transcript_json.translation: 对于最佳的解决之道，存在相互竞争的不同设想。

transcript_json.text: One vision is what's known as the post-work position.
transcript_json.translation: 其中一种设想就是所谓的“后工作”立场。

transcript_json.text: The post-work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time.
transcript_json.translation: “后工作”理论家认为，工作不应在我们的生活中占据中心位置，也不应占用我们那么多时间。

transcript_json.text: They assert that, although doing some work might be necessary, meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace.
transcript_json.translation: 他们主张，尽管干一些活可能是必要的，但意义、目标和社会价值存在于职场之外建立并维系的社区和关系之中。

transcript_json.text: Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，生活本身就应该被看作目的。

transcript_json.text: Recent studies show that self-control and persistence increase academic outcomes independent of IQ.
transcript_json.translation: 最新研究表明，自控力和坚持能提高学业成绩，且与智商无关。

transcript_json.text: Even our personal beliefs about effort can affect academic outcomes.
transcript_json.translation: 甚至我们个人对努力的看法也会影响学业成绩。

transcript_json.text: Children who think effort leads to achievement outperform those who believe ability is a fixed trait. Given the link between persistence and academic success, decisions about effort are particularly important in childhood, yet relatively little research has explored how young children learn what's worth the effort.
transcript_json.translation: 认为努力能带来成就的孩子，表现优于如何习得什么值得努力的研究还相对很少。

transcript_json.text: We all know that infants are keen observers of the social world.
transcript_json.translation: 我们都知道，婴儿是社会世界的敏锐观察者。

transcript_json.text: But they're not just idly watching.
transcript_json.translation: 但它们不只是漫无目的地看。

transcript_json.text: They are tiny learning machines.
transcript_json.translation: 它们是小小的学习机器。

transcript_json.text: They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples.
transcript_json.translation: 它们能从区区几个例子中归纳出因果关系、社会角色这类抽象概念。

transcript_json.text: Even a 15-month-old infant can outperform a high-level computer in such tasks.
transcript_json.translation: 就连 15 个月大的婴儿在这类任务上也能胜过高级计算机。

transcript_json.text: Could infants also make broad, generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort?
transcript_json.translation: 在努力这件事上，婴儿是否也能从几个例子中做出可广泛推广的推断呢？

transcript_json.text: If so, then maybe persistence isn't simply a character trait.
transcript_json.translation: 如果是这样，那么坚持也许不只是一种性格特质。

transcript_json.text: Maybe it's flexible and adaptable based on social context.
transcript_json.translation: 也许它会根据社交情境灵活调整。

transcript_json.text: To explore this question, we showed 15-month-old babies one of two things - an experimenter working hard to achieve two different goals or an experimenter who effortlessly reached each goal.
transcript_json.translation: 为了探究这个问题，我们给 15 个月大的婴儿看了两种情景之一——实验者努力达成两个不同的目标或者一位实验者轻松达成每个目标。

transcript_json.text: Then we introduced the baby to a novel music toy that seemed as if it could be activated by pushing a big button on top.
transcript_json.translation: 然后我们把一个新奇的音乐玩具拿给婴儿看，它看上去只要按下顶部的一个大按钮就能启动。

transcript_json.text: The button could be pressed down but didn't actually activate anything.
transcript_json.translation: 那个按钮按得下去，但其实什么也启动不了。

transcript_json.text: Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music.
transcript_json.translation: 我们避开婴儿的视线，用隐藏按钮打开音乐玩具，让他们听到玩具在放音乐。

transcript_json.text: We gave the babies the music toy and left the room.
transcript_json.translation: 我们把音乐玩具交给婴儿，然后离开了房间。

transcript_json.text: Then analysts who didn't know which condition each baby was in watched videotapes of the experiment and counted how many times babies tried to activate the toy by pressing the button. Across one study and a pre-registered duplication, babies who had seen an adult persist and succeed pushed the button about twice as many times as those who saw an adult effortlessly succeed.
transcript_json.translation: 随后，不知晓每个婴儿所处实验条件的研究人员观看实验录像，统计婴儿按按钮试图启动玩具的次数。

transcript_json.text: In other words, babies learned that effort was valuable after watching just two examples of an adult working hard and succeeding.
transcript_json.translation: 换句话说，宝宝们仅仅看了两例大人努力并获得成功的演示，就懂得了努力是有价值的。

transcript_json.text: Part of what's exciting about this finding is that the babies didn't just imitate the adult's actions.
transcript_json.translation: 这一发现令人兴奋的一点在于，婴儿并不只是模仿大人的动作。

transcript_json.text: Instead, they generalised the value of effort to a novel task. The experimenter never demonstrated pushing a button or trying to make music.
transcript_json.translation: 而是把努力的价值迁移到了新任务上。实验者从未示范过按按钮或尝试让玩具发声。

transcript_json.text: Instead, the babies learned from different examples of effortful actions that the new toy probably also required persistence.
transcript_json.translation: 婴儿是从不同的努力行为实例中学到，新玩具多半也需要坚持才能玩转。

If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it's likely that you're losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships and more.
transcript_json.translation: 如果长期迟到已经主宰了你的生活，成为你这个人身上的一个标志性特点，那你很可能正在错失工作机会、娱乐活动、友谊等等。

transcript_json.text: If you are showing up late to your own life, get organised, prioritise punctuality, and address any underlying causes.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你总是让自己的生活迟到，那就振作起来，把守时放在优先位置，并解决任何深层原因。

transcript_json.text: When you have to be somewhere, try to arrive fifteen to thirty minutes before you need to.
transcript_json.translation: 当你要去某个地方时，尽量提前 15 到 30 分钟到场。

transcript_json.text: If you always run late, that means you must be failing to account for something you always do. Anticipate that by giving yourself extra time to arrive.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你总是迟到，那说明你一定漏算了某些你每次都会做的事。针对这一点，多给自己留出在途时间。

transcript_json.text: Keep track of whether or not you actually do arrive early.
transcript_json.translation: 记录一下自己是否真的提前到了。

transcript_json.text: You might find that leaving early gets you to places exactly on time. Set two alarms. Set one alarm that lets you know it's time to drop what you're doing, and a second alarm that means you need to walk out the door. Obey the alarms. As soon as the first alarm goes off, stop what you're doing.
transcript_json.translation: 你也许会发现，早出发反而让你分秒不差地到达。设两个闹钟：第一个提醒你该放下手头的事了，第二个意味着你必须出门了。听从闹钟。一听到一响，就立刻停下手头的事。

transcript_json.text: If it's something you'll be coming back to, like a project for work, make a note to remind yourself where you left off. Grab everything you need and make sure you know how to get where you're going.
transcript_json.translation: 如果那是你之后还要继续的事，比如一个工作项目，就做个笔记提醒自己进行到哪儿了。拿上你需要的一切，并确保知道怎么去目的地。

transcript_json.text: Aim to be out the door and on your way before the second alarm rings. This will only work if you take the alarms seriously, so make sure you react as soon as you hear them.
transcript_json.translation: 力争在第二个闹钟响之前就出门上路。对待闹钟的前提下才管用，所以一听到闹钟就马上行动。

transcript_json.translation: 如果早晨对你来说很煎熬，那就尽量在前一晚把一切准备好。

transcript_json.text: That culture has carried down to the present day, he believes. Boston College professor Thomas O'Connor thinks a contributing factor is Boston's history as a city where each new group of immigrants was treated with suspicion and exclusion.

transcript_json.translation: 他认为，这让波士顿有了一种抱团排外和内敛的气质。

transcript_json.text: The idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture, he says. People will begin a conversation with someone they know, but not with a stranger.

transcript_json.text: By being snobbish about manners, proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy, he says. Some say that's just the way Boston is and that the city will never change.

transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 1

transcript_json.text: Pet dogs can often readily understand a wide range of their owners' commands and gestures.
transcript_json.translation: 宠物狗往往能轻松听懂主人的各种指令和手势。

transcript_json.text: But are these abilities inborn or are they exclusively learned through training?
transcript_json.translation: 但这些能力是天生的，还是完全靠训练习得的？

transcript_json.text: To find out, a new study examined whether stray dogs could understand human gestures.
transcript_json.translation: 为了找到答案，一项新研究考察了流浪狗能否理解人类的手势。

transcript_json.text: The study revealed that 80% of participating dogs successfully followed pointing gestures to a specific location despite having never received prior training.
transcript_json.translation: 研究显示，80% 的受试狗从未接受过任何训练，却能成功跟随指向手势找到特定位置。

transcript_json.text: The results suggest that dogs can understand complex gestures by simply watching humans.
transcript_json.translation: 结果表明，狗仅仅通过观察人类就能理解复杂的手势。

transcript_json.text: This could have implications in reducing conflict between stray dogs and humans.
transcript_json.translation: 这可能有助于减少流浪狗与人类之间的冲突。

transcript_json.text: Dogs were domesticated 10,000 to 15,000 years ago.
transcript_json.translation: 狗在 1 万到 1.5 万年前被驯化。

transcript_json.text: This means they are probably the oldest domesticated animals on the planet.
transcript_json.translation: 这意味着它们可能是地球上最古老的驯化动物。

transcript_json.text: Humans then bred dogs with the most desirable and useful traits so that they could function as companions and workers.
transcript_json.translation: 后来人类选择最理想、最有用的性状来繁育狗，使它们能充当伴侣和工作犬。

transcript_json.text: This resulted in domesticated dogs that are highly responsive to human commands and gestures.
transcript_json.translation: 这培育出了对人类指令和手势高度敏感的家养狗。

transcript_json.text: However, it was not clear whether dogs understand us through training alone, or whether this was an inherent ability.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，狗究竟是单靠训练理解我们，还是这是一种与生俱来的能力，此前并不清楚。

transcript_json.text: Why does this matter?
transcript_json.translation: 为什么这很重要？

transcript_json.text: Stray dogs are a common feature in cities around the world.
transcript_json.translation: 流浪狗是世界各地城市中的常见现象。

transcript_json.text: They may observe and occasionally interact with people, but such dogs have never been trained and are behaviorally “wild”.
transcript_json.translation: 它们可能观察人类，偶尔与人互动，但这样的狗从未受过训练，行为上是“野性”的。

transcript_json.text: Conflicts between stray dogs and humans are a problem.
transcript_json.translation: 流浪狗与人类之间的冲突是个问题。

transcript_json.text: Understanding how humans shape stray dogs' behavior may help alleviate this problem.
transcript_json.translation: 理解人类如何塑造流浪狗的行为，或许有助于缓解这个问题。

transcript_json.text: According to the researchers of the new study, stray dogs are intelligent creatures.
transcript_json.translation: 新研究的研究人员认为，流浪狗是聪明的生灵。

transcript_json.text: They closely observe humans and use their understanding of us to make a decision.
transcript_json.translation: 它们密切观察人类，并利用对人类的了解来做决定。

transcript_json.text: “Treating stray dogs with sensitivity and respect and giving them space,” the researchers assert, “can reduce much conflict.”
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员断言：“体贴并尊重地对待流浪狗、给它们留出空间，可以减少许多冲突。”

transcript_json.text: Think your refrigerator is just one big box of evenly cold air?

transcript_json.text: Not so!
transcript_json.translation: 冰箱上部不如底部冷，所以留给

transcript_json.text: The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top and everywhere in between.
transcript_json.translation: 普通冰箱内的温度其实从前到后、从下到上以及中间各处都有差异。

transcript_json.text: Because of this, food product placement within the appliance is far more important than you probably realize.
transcript_json.translation: 正因如此，食物在冰箱里的摆放位置远比你想象的更重要。

transcript_json.text: The whole purpose of the modern refrigerator is to slow the growth of bacteria, which thrive in temperatures from 4.4 to 60 °C.
transcript_json.translation: 现代冰箱的全部意义就在于减缓细菌繁殖，而细菌在 4.4 到 60 摄氏度之间大量滋生。 现代冰箱的全部意义就在于减缓细菌繁殖，而细菌在 4.4 到 60 摄氏度之间大量滋生。

transcript_json.text: As a result, refrigerators are typically set at or below that low end to protect foods against bacteria.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，冰箱通常就设定在那个下限或更低，以保护食物免受细菌侵害。

transcript_json.text: Although it might seem like time spent organizing the fridge will spoil your day, doing so will actually make it more user-friendly, easier to clean and food safety-conscious.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然整理冰箱似乎会占用你一天中的时间，但这样做实际上会让冰箱更好用、更易清洁，也更符合食品安全要求。

transcript_json.text: Those little bins on the inside of refrigerator doors are convenient, but they don't maintain a consistent temperature, so definitely refrain from putting perishable foods in there.
transcript_json.translation: 冰箱门内侧的那些小格虽然方便，但温度不稳定，所以千万别把易腐食物放在那里。

transcript_json.text: The top area is not as cold as the bottom of the fridge, so save it for the foods that don't need extra-chilly temperatures.
transcript_json.translation: 那些不需要特别低温的食物。

transcript_json.text: Store foods that are ready-to-eat or already cooked on the top shelf.
transcript_json.translation: 即食或已做熟的食物放在最上层。

transcript_json.text: The middle shelf is the most temperature-controlled part of the fridge, so place eggs here.
transcript_json.translation: 中间层是冰箱里温控最好的部分，所以鸡蛋放在这里。

transcript_json.text: Drinks and prepared foods can also live on the middle shelf if you run out of room up top.
transcript_json.translation: 如果上层放不下，饮料和预制食品也可以放在中间层。

transcript_json.text: The back of the bottom shelf is the coldest spot in the fridge, so store perishable dairy products here to keep them edible, longer.
transcript_json.translation: 最下层的里侧是冰箱最冷的地方，所以把易腐的乳制品存放在这里，让它们能吃得更久。

transcript_json.text: Never store foods with high water content here, because the water within them can and will freeze, effectively ruining them.
transcript_json.translation: 千万别把高水分食物放在这里，因为它们所含的水分可能而且必定会结冰，把它们彻底毁掉。

transcript_json.text: My current research is mainly looking at factors like stress and how would it affect our immune system.
transcript_json.translation: 我目前的研究主要关注压力之类的因素，

transcript_json.text: So the current projects that I am quite excited about are looking at older people and factors that are important to them.
transcript_json.translation: 以及它们会如何影响我们的免疫系统。

transcript_json.text: In one project, we are looking at hip fracture in older people, which is a common event, and we are trying to understand the impact of depression.
transcript_json.translation: 在一个项目里，我们研究老年人髋部骨折——这是常见事件——并试图弄清抑郁的影响。

transcript_json.text: Often people in hospital with a hip fracture develop depression, and these are the people that then go on to become feeble a lot more quickly than others.
transcript_json.translation: 因髋部骨折住院的人常常会患上抑郁，而这些人随后衰弱的速度会比其他人快得多。

transcript_json.text: They get infections; often, these infections lead to death.
transcript_json.translation: 他们容易感染；而这些感染常常导致死亡。

transcript_json.text: So we're trying to slow down that progression to feebleness.
transcript_json.translation: 所以我们正努力减缓这种走向衰弱的进程。

transcript_json.text: So if we can better understand how these factors interact, then we can actually start doing something about it.
transcript_json.translation: 如果我们能更好地理解这些因素如何相互作用，就能真正开始有所作为。

transcript_json.text: The impact that my research will have in Birmingham, first of all, is obviously for older people, because these are the people that are having hip fractures and developing depression.
transcript_json.translation: 我的研究在伯明翰的影响，首先显然是针对老年人的，因为发生髋部骨折并患上抑郁的正是这些人。

transcript_json.text: And we're trying to improve their health and their quality of life.
transcript_json.translation: 我们正努力改善他们的健康和生活质量。

transcript_json.text: But this isn't just a problem in Birmingham or even in the UK.
transcript_json.translation: 但这不仅是伯明翰的问题，甚至也不仅是英国的问题。

transcript_json.text: This is a problem globally.
transcript_json.translation: 这是一个全球性问题。

transcript_json.text: People are aging.
transcript_json.translation: 人口在老龄化。

transcript_json.text: There're a lot more people in the older generation who are living for longer, but not necessarily staying healthy for a large part of their lives.
transcript_json.translation: 老一代中长寿的人越来越多，但他们未必能在人生的大部分时间里保持健康。

transcript_json.text: So the last part of their life can often be full of ill health and we're trying to understand factors that can contribute to the quality of life later on.
transcript_json.translation: 所以他们人生的最后阶段常常疾病缠身，我们正试图理解哪些因素能改善晚年的生活质量。

transcript_json.text: I think the thing that excites me most about my research is that it feels real and relevant.
transcript_json.translation: 我觉得我的研究最让我兴奋的一点是，它让人觉得真实、切合实际。

transcript_json.text: Lots of academics are probably very excited about their research, but it might not be that relevant to those around them.
transcript_json.translation: 许多学者可能对自己的研究非常兴奋，但那项研究未必与身边的人有多大关系。

transcript_json.text: Whereas I feel that the work I do is relevant to everyone, because everyone is aging.
transcript_json.translation: 而我觉得我做的工作与每个人都相关，因为每个人都会变老。

transcript_json.text: Health is an issue for everyone, regardless of their age.
transcript_json.translation: 无论年龄大小，健康是每个人都要面对的问题。

transcript_json.text: And what I'm trying to do is understand the factors that affect health and how we can improve the quality of life and people.
transcript_json.translation: 我要做的是理解影响健康的因素，以及我们如何提升人的生活质量。

transcript_json.text: So that's one of the things that really excites me about it.
transcript_json.translation: 这就是让我对这项研究真正感到兴奋的原因之一。

transcript_json.text: One of the other things is rather than just taking one perspective — so rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist — we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints to actually look at the sort of different factors affecting health.
transcript_json.translation: 另一点是，我们不再只从一个视角出发——也就是说，不再仅从心理学家的视角看待衰老与健康——而是现在汇集了许多不同的技术和观点，来真正考察影响健康的各种不同因素。

transcript_json.text: Americans are obsessed with celebrity chefs.
transcript_json.translation: 美国人对明星大厨着迷。

transcript_json.text: We talk about them and try to eat like them.
transcript_json.translation: 我们谈论他们，还照着他们的样子吃。

transcript_json.text: But could we learn something more from them than recipes and techniques?
transcript_json.translation: 但除了菜谱和厨

transcript_json.text: According to Marketdata Enterprises, Americans spend nearly $10 billion a year on self-help and personal organization products.
transcript_json.translation: 艺技巧，我们还

transcript_json.text: The market is huge, partly because most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organization.
transcript_json.translation: 能从他们身上学

transcript_json.text: But cooking schools and professional kitchens do.
transcript_json.translation: 到别的东西吗？

transcript_json.text: Perhaps the principles of cooking organization can be extended to help even those of us who aren't top chefs.
transcript_json.translation: 烹饪组织管理的原则或许可以推广开来，帮到我们这些并非顶级大厨的人。

transcript_json.text: The system that makes kitchens function is called mise-en-place, or, literally, “put in place”.
transcript_json.translation: 让后厨高效运转的这套体系叫 mise-en-place，字面意思是“各就各位”。

transcript_json.text: It's a French phrase that means to gather and arrange the ingredients and tools needed for cooking.
transcript_json.translation: 这是一个法语短语，意思是把烹饪所需的食材和工具收集并摆放到位。

transcript_json.text: But for many professional cooks, the phrase means something deeper.
transcript_json.translation: 但对许多职业厨师来说，这个短语有着更深的含义。

transcript_json.text: Some cooks call it their religion.
transcript_json.translation: 有些厨师称之为他们的信条。

transcript_json.text: It helps them coordinate vast amounts of labor and material, and transforms the lives of its practitioners through focus and self-discipline.
transcript_json.translation: 它帮助他们统筹大量的劳力和物料，并通过专注和自律改变践行者的人生。

transcript_json.text: Students at the Culinary Institute of America view it as a way of life.
transcript_json.translation: 美国烹饪学院的学生把它视为一种生活方式。

transcript_json.text: It's a way of concentrating their mind to only focus on the aspects that they need to be working on at the moment, to kind of rid themselves of distractions.
transcript_json.translation: 它是一种让心智专注、只聚焦当下必须处理的环节的方式，可以说是摆脱各种干扰。

transcript_json.text: And it's a habit that some students carry with them even when they're not in the kitchen.
transcript_json.translation: 这是一种有些学生即使在厨房之外也保持的习惯。

transcript_json.text: They mise-en-place their life.
transcript_json.translation: 他们把自己的生活也“各就各位”。

transcript_json.text: They set up their books for class, they set up their chef whites, they shine their shoes, they know everything that they need every step of the day.
transcript_json.translation: 他们为上课备好书，备好厨师服，擦亮皮鞋，对一天中每一步需要什么了然于心。

transcript_json.text: Then how does one attain this level of organization?
transcript_json.translation: 那么，人如何才能达到这种条理水平呢？

transcript_json.text: The key to high level organization is the mindset.
transcript_json.translation: 高度条理化的关键在于心态。

transcript_json.text: Cooks can easily do 6 hours of preparation for a 3-hour dinner shift.
transcript_json.translation: 厨师为一场 3 小时的晚餐班次做上 6 小时的准备是常事。

transcript_json.text: Mise-en-place forces cooks to account for every minute of their time and every movement.
transcript_json.translation: “各就各位”迫使厨师对自己的每一分钟、每一个动作都心中有数。

transcript_json.text: “Every component of one single dish is in one single corner so their hand literally moves inches,” explains Dwayne Lipuma, an instructor at the Culinary Institute of America.
transcript_json.translation: “一道菜的每一种原料都放在同一个角落，这样他们的手真的只需移动几英寸，”美国烹饪学院讲师德韦恩·利普马解释道。

transcript_json.text: “Once students set up their station, I should be able to cover up their eyes.
transcript_json.translation: “学生一旦布置好自己的操作台，我就应该可以蒙上他们的眼睛。

transcript_json.text: And they should know that their knives are always here, their oil is always right here, their salt and pepper is always right here.”
transcript_json.translation: 他们清楚自己的刀永远在这个位置，油永远就在这儿，盐和胡椒也永远就在这儿。”

transcript_json.text: But practiced at its highest level, mise-en-place says that time is precious.
transcript_json.translation: 而修到最高境界时，“各就各位”告诉我们：时间宝贵。

transcript_json.text: Resources are precious.
transcript_json.translation: 资源宝贵。

transcript_json.text: Space is precious.
transcript_json.translation: 空间宝贵。

transcript_json.text: Your self-respect and the respect of others are precious.
transcript_json.translation: 你的自尊和他人的尊重同样宝贵。

transcript_json.text: Use them wisely.
transcript_json.translation: 你的自尊和他人的尊重都弥足珍贵。要明智地使用它

transcript_json.text: Isn't that a philosophy for our time?
transcript_json.translation: 们。这难道不是我们这个时代的一种处世哲学吗？

transcript_json.text: Why do we stop making goals for ourselves and stop progressing in life?
transcript_json.translation: 为什么我们会停止为自己设定目标、停止在人生中前进？

transcript_json.text: One reason is the belief that we should accept who we are and not constantly strive to improve ourselves.
transcript_json.translation: 一个原因是相信我们应该接纳自己，而不必不断努力提升自己。

transcript_json.text: The mistake we make with this is that whilst self-acceptance is imperative, it should actually be used as the basis for growth.
transcript_json.translation: 我们在这里犯的错误是：虽然自我接纳不可或缺，但它其实应当被用作成长的基础。

transcript_json.text: When we are not growing, learning and seeking improvements in our lives, we tend to stagnate, accepting what it is and stop believing we can be better.
transcript_json.translation: 当我们在生活中不再成长、学习和寻求进步时，我们就容易停滞不前，安于现状，不再相信自己能变得更好。

transcript_json.text: A key tool for creating goals and progressing is using our imagination.
transcript_json.translation: 设定目标、不断进步的一个关键工具，就是运用我们的想象力。

transcript_json.text: Yet as is so often the case, by the time we've reached midlife, we've stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve and feel quite negatively about goal-setting.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，情况常常是：人到中年时，我们已经不再梦想自己想要达成什么，对设定目标也相当消极。

transcript_json.text: Instead of feeling confidence, happiness and satisfaction from achieving our goals, we feel we are always falling short.
transcript_json.translation: 我们从实现目标中感受到的不是自信、快乐和满足，而是觉得自己总是达不到。

transcript_json.text: That leads to disappointment and we stop dreaming.
transcript_json.translation: 这带来了失望，于是我们不再做梦。

transcript_json.text: We stop imagining the life we'd like to have or the person we'd like to be, quickly finding ourselves shattered by the pain of our reality.
transcript_json.translation: 我们不再想象想要过的生活、想成为的人，很快便发现自己在现实的痛苦中一蹶不振。

transcript_json.text: Up until now, unless we work in the creative industry, we've found the idea of using “play” a bit childish.
transcript_json.translation: 直到现在，除非从事创意行业，我们一直觉得把“玩”当回事有点幼稚。

transcript_json.text: In the West, we are mostly operating from our heads, the rational mind, but it's beginning to be better understood, because using our imagination is actually one of the most powerful things we could ever do.
transcript_json.translation: 在西方，我们大多靠头脑、靠理性思维运转，但人们开始有了更好的理解：因为运用想象力其实是我们能做的最有力量的事情之一。

transcript_json.text: The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes and we're always adapting, whether we realize it or not.
transcript_json.translation: 我们因未达目标而恼火的问题在于：目标总在变化，而我们总在调整适应，不管我们自己是否意识到。

transcript_json.text: What happens, therefore, is that we end up feeling like we are never going to reach our goals.
transcript_json.translation: 结果就是，我们最终觉得自己永远无法实现目标。

transcript_json.text: And herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions and reasons for failure, dissatisfaction, and unhappiness.
transcript_json.translation: 这里正藏着最大的一个误区，也是失败、不满和不幸福的根源之一。

transcript_json.text: We measure against the goal rather than where we've come from.
transcript_json.translation: 我们以目标为标尺来衡量自己，而不是看自己已经走了多远。

transcript_json.text: Dan Sullivan calls this “the gap and the gain”.
transcript_json.translation: 丹·沙利文把这称为“差距与收获”。

transcript_json.text: We measure always against the goal, which we never feel we're reaching, rather than the gain.
transcript_json.translation: 我们总是拿目标——那个我们从未觉得够得着的目标——来衡量，而不是拿收获来衡量。

transcript_json.text: That is where we've come from.
transcript_json.translation: 收获就是我们已经走过的地方。

transcript_json.text: In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to, we see results.
transcript_json.translation: 衡量我们走过的路，而不是我们想去的远方，我们才能看到成果。

transcript_json.text: We see things we've taken for granted or not noticed.
transcript_json.translation: 我们看到那些自己一直视为理所当然或未曾留意的东西。

transcript_json.text: It's a simple, yet profound change in perception, and what I love about it is the power it has to instantly shift us up a gear.
transcript_json.translation: 这是一种简单却深刻的视角转变，而我喜欢它的地方在于，它有一种让我们立刻换挡提速的力量。

transcript_json.text: It's so, so simple, yet has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking.
transcript_json.translation: 它如此、如此简单，却能对我们的思维产生立竿见影的积极影响。

transcript_json.text: W: Today's special guest is Lord Blackwell, one of our country's most experienced and distinguished career diplomats.
transcript_json.translation: W: 今天的特别嘉宾是布莱克维尔勋爵，他是我们国家经验最丰富、最负盛名的职业外交官之一。欢迎您！

transcript_json.text: Welcome!
transcript_json.translation: W: 今天的特别嘉宾是布莱克维尔勋爵，他是我们国家经验最丰富、最负盛名的职业外交官之一。欢迎您！

transcript_json.text: M: It's my pleasure.
transcript_json.translation: M: 很荣幸。

transcript_json.text: W: Our audience will be most interested in learning about a career in the foreign service.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我们的听众最感兴趣的，是了解外交官这份职业。

transcript_json.text: However, before we talk about that, I'd like to ask you about the current developments hitting the news today regarding the Republic of Winopia.
transcript_json.translation: 不过在此之前，我想先问问您今天新闻头条上关于 Winopia 共和国的最新动态。

transcript_json.text: What can you tell us?
transcript_json.translation: 您能给我们讲讲吗？

transcript_json.text: M: I'm afraid I don't know much beyond what we've all seen on the news.
transcript_json.translation: M: 恐怕除了大家在新闻里看到的，我了解的不多。

transcript_json.text: It looks like the government of Winopia seems to be undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy, and an interim administration has been transitionally established until a head of state is agreed on.
transcript_json.translation: 看起来 Winopia 政府似乎正经历某种合法性危机，在各派就国家元首人选达成一致之前，已临时成立了一个过渡政府。

transcript_json.text: But my career work has mostly focused around the continental spheres of Europe and the Americas, and thus I've never been involved with Winopian relations.
transcript_json.translation: 但我的职业工作主要聚焦于欧洲和美洲大陆的事务，因此从未参与过与 Winopia 有关的关系工作。

transcript_json.text: It's for this reason that I don't know anything on this matter beyond what we can all read in the newspapers.
transcript_json.translation: 正因如此，除了大家都能在报纸上读到的，我对这件事一无所知。

transcript_json.text: W: Oh, I see.
transcript_json.translation: W: 哦，明白了。

transcript_json.text: M: Nevertheless, be rest assured that our expert envoys at our consulate there will be closely monitoring the situation, and I expect our bilateral relations with that country will not be affected.
transcript_json.translation: M: 尽管如此，请放心，我们驻当地领事馆的资深使节会密切关注局势，我预计我们与该国的双边关系不会受到影响。

transcript_json.text: W: So how does one get a career in foreign relations?
transcript_json.translation: W: 那怎样才能走上外交关系的职业道路呢？

transcript_json.text: M: There are many different paths one can take.
transcript_json.translation: M: 可走的路有很多条。

transcript_json.text: All diplomats have their own story.
transcript_json.translation: 每位外交官都有自己的故事。

transcript_json.text: But in my case, I got a degree in electrical engineering followed by six years' service in the air force.

transcript_json.text: Then I went to law school, and upon obtaining a degree in international law, I joined the diplomatic corps where I have been for 22 years.

transcript_json.translation: 此外，外交官的言谈论述必须非常清晰有力。

transcript_json.text: Whether it is defusing attention or enacting policy, people and communication skills are vital.
transcript_json.translation: 无论是化解矛盾还是推行政策，人际交往和沟通能力都至关重要。

transcript_json.text: One thing I've learned in a quarter-century of management is that there are ample gray areas in human behavior, and that there may not always be clear right-or-wrong solutions to employee disputes.
transcript_json.translation: 在四分之一世纪的管理生涯中，我学到的一件事是：人的行为存在大量灰色地带，员工纠纷未必总有明确的对错解决方案。

transcript_json.text: When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe.
transcript_json.translation: 当两个人对同一件事各执一词时，很难判断该信谁。

transcript_json.text: One such circumstance always comes back to me.
transcript_json.translation: 有一个这样的情形总在我脑海中浮现。

transcript_json.text: It happened years ago, and it's a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution.
transcript_json.translation: 那件事发生在多年前，这场冲突有多容易被忘掉，从一点就能看出来：我甚至不记得当初争执的是什么，但我清清楚楚记得解决方式。

transcript_json.text: Two talented young executives, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event, and it seemed likely we'd never get to the truth.
transcript_json.translation: 两位才华出众的年轻高管——其中一位由我管理——对同一件事的说法大相径庭，看来我们永远也查不到真相了。

transcript_json.text: We reached the deadlock, and the manager of the other individual said, "Here's something I learned from an excellent manager I once worked for.
transcript_json.translation: 我们陷入了僵局，另一位高管的经理说："这是我从曾经共事过的一位优秀经理那里学来的。

transcript_json.text: He used to say, 'When in doubt, assume positive intent.'"
transcript_json.translation: 他常说：“拿不准的时候，就假定对方出于善意。

transcript_json.text: And just like that, we had a path forward.
transcript_json.translation: ”就这样，我们有了前行的方向。

transcript_json.text: My counterpart and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter; quite likely there were elements of truth in both employees' stories.
transcript_json.translation: 我和对方经理一致认为，我们也许永远查不清事实真相；很可能两位员工的说法各有真实的成分。

transcript_json.text: We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further.
transcript_json.translation: 我们同意在今后留意他们的行为和关系，但不再进一步干预。

transcript_json.text: We assumed the best about both of them and moved on.
transcript_json.translation: 我们把他们俩都想得最好，然后翻篇了。

transcript_json.text: The result was that we were able to put the conflict behind us.
transcript_json.translation: 结果是，我们得以把这场冲突抛在身后。

transcript_json.text: In fact, their problems didn't recur.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，他们的问题没有再出现。

transcript_json.text: Over the years, this general approach has proved useful.
transcript_json.translation: 这些年来，这种大方向的做法已被证明管用。

transcript_json.text: Whenever the truth is obscure, assuming positive intent and agreeing to move on can be a constructive decision.
transcript_json.translation: 每当真相晦暗不明时，假定对方出于善意并同意翻篇，可以是一个有建设性的决定。

transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 2

transcript_json.text: For some Americans, going out to dinner is a treat, planned and budgeted for.
transcript_json.translation: 对一些美国人来说，下馆子是一种款待，要提前计划、留出预算。

transcript_json.text: For others, it's just a daily occurrence.
transcript_json.translation: 对另一些人来说，这只是家常便饭。

transcript_json.text: And that second group of people is becoming the majority as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining.
transcript_json.translation: 随着喜欢做饭的美国人越来越少，后一类人正成为多数。

transcript_json.text: In the early 2000s, researcher Eddie Yoon conducted a survey to ascertain Americans' attitudes to cooking.
transcript_json.translation: 21 世纪初，研究人员埃迪·尹做了一项调查，以摸清美国人对做饭的态度。

transcript_json.text: The survey found that 15% of Americans loved to cook, 50% said they hated to cook and 35% reported mixed feelings.
transcript_json.translation: 调查发现，15% 的美国人热爱做饭，50% 说自己讨厌做饭，35% 则心情复杂。

transcript_json.text: When Yoon conducted the same survey 15 years later, only 10% of respondents reported a love of cooking, 45% said they hated it and 45% had mixed feelings.
transcript_json.translation: 15 年后尹再做同样的调查时，只有 10% 的受访者表示热爱做饭，45% 说讨厌，45% 心情复杂。

transcript_json.text: Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing.
transcript_json.translation: 尹断言，做饭和缝纫类似。

transcript_json.text: As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing.
transcript_json.translation: 就在 20 世纪初，许多美国人还自己缝制衣服。

transcript_json.text: Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing; only a tiny minority still sew, and they do it mainly as a hobby.
transcript_json.translation: 如今，绝大多数美国人买衣服穿；只有极少数人还缝纫，而且主要是当爱好。

transcript_json.text: Yoon believes the number of home cooks will diminish in a similar fashion.
transcript_json.translation: 尹认为，在家做饭的人数也会以类似的方式减少。

transcript_json.text: Currently, the average American household spends over $3,000 per year on dining out.
transcript_json.translation: 目前，美国家庭平均每年在外就餐花费超过 3000 美元。

transcript_json.text: However, what people save in convenience, they lose in cash.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，人们图省事省下的力气，都要用多花的钱来换。

transcript_json.text: Take buying lunch on workdays for example.
transcript_json.translation: 以工作日买午饭为例。

transcript_json.text: People spend, on average, $10 per meal when they buy lunch.
transcript_json.translation: 买午饭时，人们平均每餐花 10 美元。

transcript_json.text: Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less.
transcript_json.translation: 而自己做午饭，花费会更少。

transcript_json.text: One survey found people only spend on average $6.30 when they bring lunch prepared at home.
transcript_json.translation: 一项调查发现，自带家中准备的午餐时，人们平均只花 6.30 美元。

transcript_json.text: Americans' growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of challenges for the grocery industry.
transcript_json.translation: 美国人越来越不愿意把时间花在厨房里，这预示着食品杂货行业将面临一大堆挑战。

transcript_json.text: It's likely to detrimentally impact family finances as well.
transcript_json.translation: 这也可能对家庭财务造成不利影响。

transcript_json.text: Every year, of the more than 2.5 billion bags checked onto flights worldwide, 26 million go missing — and of that 26 million, 1 million never make it back to their original owner.
transcript_json.translation: 恶劣天气和航班延误、目的地标签编码错误，还有人干脆忘记取走自己的一件行李，这些都是部分原因。每年，在超过两 5 亿件托运上飞机的行李中，有 2600 万件会失踪——而这 2600 万件中，又有

transcript_json.text: Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded destination tags and some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags are a few of the reasons.
transcript_json.translation: 恶劣天气和航班延误、目的地标签录入错误，以及有些人干脆忘了拿走自己的一件行李，都是其中一些原因。

transcript_json.text: But the number-one reason a bag ends up lost is that it has no ID tag, and airlines don't know to whom it belongs.
transcript_json.translation: 但行李最终丢失的头号原因是它没有身份标签，航空公司不知道它属于谁。

transcript_json.text: Transferring baggage from check-in to departure gates to arrival gates to baggage claim is a delicate piece of timing.
transcript_json.translation: 把行李从值机柜台送到登机口，再送到到达口和行李提取处，是一个需要精细拿捏时间的环节。

transcript_json.text: If the system moves too slowly, the bags won't make connecting flights.
transcript_json.translation: 如果系统运转太慢，行李就赶不上中转航班。

transcript_json.text: If it's too fast, the bags may make the connection but the passengers might miss the flight.
transcript_json.translation: 如果留的时间太短，行李或许能衔接上，乘客却可能误了航班。

transcript_json.text: Each airport has its own way of allotting how much time a bag needs to move in transit.
transcript_json.translation: 每个机场都有自己的办法来分配行李中转所需的时间。

transcript_json.text: Some airports have sophisticated automated systems, including scanners that read baggage labels, destination-coded vehicles that load and unload the bags without stopping, and sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate.
transcript_json.translation: 一些机场拥有精密的自动化系统，包括读取行李标签的扫描仪、不用停车就能装卸行李的目的地编码车辆，以及把行李分送到相应登机口的分拣机。

transcript_json.text: Even so, all that technology may not save your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt, making you the owner of a bag with no name.
transcript_json.translation: 即便如此，这些技术也可能保不住你的行李标签在传送带上被扯掉，让你成为一个"无名包"的主人。

transcript_json.text: Once a bag goes missing and the passenger files a claim, the bag is declared "mishandled" by the carrier.
transcript_json.translation: 一旦行李丢失、乘客提出索赔，承运方就会把这件行李登记为"处理不当"。

transcript_json.text: Mishandled refers to bags that have been delayed, lost, stolen or damaged.
transcript_json.translation: "处理不当"指的是被延误、丢失、盗窃或损坏的行李。

transcript_json.text: Most delayed bags are only one flight behind their owners and can be delivered within 24 hours.
transcript_json.translation: 大多数被延误的行李只比主人晚了一个航班，可以在 24 小时内送达。

transcript_json.text: The other bags are examined by airline employees for clues to their ownership and destination.
transcript_json.translation: 其余的行李则由航空公司员工检查，寻找关于其归属和目的地的线索。

transcript_json.text: If the mystery is solved, those bags are returned to their owners within four or five days.
transcript_json.translation: 如果谜团解开，这些行李会在四五天内归还给主人。

transcript_json.text: Bags with no destination code or identification tag are shipped to a central warehouse, and undergo a comprehensive baggage tracing process over the next 90 days.
transcript_json.translation: 没有目的地代码或身份标签的行李会被运往中央仓库，并在接下来的 90 天里经历一套全面的行李追踪流程。

transcript_json.text: Airlines inventory their mishandled baggage, and many use a database to match the contents with owners' descriptions.
transcript_json.translation: 航空公司会对处理不当的行李登记造册，许多公司还用数据库把行李内容与主人的描述进行匹配。

transcript_json.text: It takes about three months to go from "missing in action" to "irretrievably lost".
transcript_json.translation: 从"下落不明"到"彻底找不回来"，大约需要三个月。

transcript_json.text: Once that happens, the bags are donated to charity, sold at auction, or purchased by a company which sells them to the public.
transcript_json.translation: 一旦到了那一步，这些行李会被捐给慈善机构、拍卖出售，或被一家公司买下再转卖给公众。

transcript_json.text: So never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage.
transcript_json.translation: 所以，千万别把真正贵重的东西放进托运行李。

transcript_json.text: And make sure your name is on the bag, along with your phone number, so an agent can contact you.
transcript_json.translation: 并确保包上写有你的名字和电话号码，以便工作人员能联系到你。

transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 2

transcript_json.text: You've probably been with someone who ignored you while interacting with his or her smartphone.
transcript_json.translation: 你很可能遇到过这样的人：和你在一起时却只顾玩手机、冷落你。

transcript_json.text: And you've probably engaged in this behavior yourself.
transcript_json.translation: 而且你自己很可能也做过这种事。

transcript_json.text: In a recent survey, nine out of ten respondents said they'd used their smartphone during their most recent social activity.
transcript_json.translation: 在最近的一项调查中，90% 的受访者说他们在最近一次社交活动中用过智能手机。

transcript_json.text: There's also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful.
transcript_json.translation: 还有证据表明，这种行为对社交有害。

transcript_json.text: It can leave people less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions.
transcript_json.translation: 它会降低人们对面对面交流的满意度。

transcript_json.text: And it can generate feelings of resentment and jealousy.
transcript_json.translation: 它还会滋生怨恨和嫉妒的情绪。

transcript_json.text: Now, the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study exploring the reasons for these effects.
transcript_json.translation: 如今，《应用社会心理学杂志》发表了一项新研究，探讨产生这些效应的原因。

transcript_json.text: The study included 128 mostly female student participants.
transcript_json.translation: 该研究有 128 名以女生为主的学生参与者。

transcript_json.text: The participants watched a three-minute animation in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a conversation.
transcript_json.translation: 参与者观看一段三分钟的动画，其中两个卡通人物互动并交谈。

transcript_json.text: The conversation couldn't be heard but could be detected through mouth movements.
transcript_json.translation: 谈话听不到声音，但可以通过嘴部动作看出来。

transcript_json.text: Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video and then make judgments about the conversations and how they felt about their conversation partners.
transcript_json.translation: 参与者要把自己想象成视频中离镜头最近的那个人物，然后对谈话作出评判，并说出对谈话对象的感觉。

transcript_json.text: In one version of the experiment, the phone of the participants' conversation partner remained unused on the table throughout the conversation.
transcript_json.translation: 在实验的一个版本中，参与者的谈话对象的手机全程放在桌上，无人使用。

transcript_json.text: In another version, their partner's attention was quickly drawn to something on their phone and they spent the rest of the time interacting with their phone.
transcript_json.translation: 在另一个版本中，谈话对象的注意力很快被手机上的东西吸引，剩下的时间都在玩手机。

transcript_json.text: A third version involved the participants' partner alternating between periods of interaction with their phone and periods where they ignored their phone.
transcript_json.translation: 第三个版本中，谈话对象在玩手机和不用手机两种状态之间来回切换。

transcript_json.text: If you've experienced a similar situation, you probably won't be surprised by the results of the experiments.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你经历过类似情形，对这些实验的结果大概不会感到意外。

transcript_json.text: The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions.
transcript_json.translation: 参与者对社交互动中玩手机持负面看法。

transcript_json.text: The more it was present, the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the relationship.
transcript_json.translation: 手机出现得越多，他们对互动质量和关系质量的评价就越差。

transcript_json.text: The researchers believed that focusing on one's phone instead of the person one is with has this effect because it's seen as a form of social exclusion.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员认为，只顾盯着手机而不理身边的人之所以有这种效果，是因为它被视为一种社会排斥。

transcript_json.text: They assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school cafeteria.
transcript_json.translation: 他们断言，这种行为类似于人们别无选择只能独自在学校食堂吃饭的情形。

transcript_json.text: The twist is that this exclusion occurs while sharing a physical encounter and having a conversation.
transcript_json.translation: 特别之处在于，这种排斥发生在共处一地、进行交谈的时候。

transcript_json.text: Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants' sense of belonging, need for meaning and self-esteem.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员发现，这种行为对参与者的归属感、意义需求和自尊都有不良影响。

transcript_json.text: These negative effects are similar to those caused by traditional forms of social exclusion.
transcript_json.translation: 这些负面影响与传统形式的社会排斥所造成的相似。

transcript_json.text: The new findings are important because they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience.
transcript_json.translation: 新发现很重要，因为它细化了我们对日常经历中一个微妙而常见方面的理解。

transcript_json.text: This common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment even as we try to connect with others.
transcript_json.translation: 就在我们努力与他人建立联系的同时，这种常见行为也可能造成疏离的恶性循环。

transcript_json.text: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
transcript_json.translation: 问题 19 至 21 基于你刚才听到的录音。

transcript_json.text: Q19. What does the speaker say about using one's smartphone during a face-to-face conversation?
transcript_json.translation: Q19. 关于面对面交谈时使用智能手机，说话人说了什么？

transcript_json.text: Q20. How did the participants in the new study respond regarding phone use during social interactions?
transcript_json.translation: Q20. 新研究中的参与者对社交互动中玩手机作何反应？

transcript_json.text: Q21. What does the speaker say can result from the common behavior of using phones during face-to-face conversations?
transcript_json.translation: Q21. 关于面对面交谈时玩手机的常见行为，说话人说会导致什么？

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 3
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: More and more people travel for a variety of reasons.
transcript_json.translation: 出于各种原因出门旅行的人越来越多。

transcript_json.text: Many are tourists, but many venture forth on personal or professional business.
transcript_json.translation: 许多人是游客，但也有许多人因私事或公务出行。

transcript_json.text: Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find.
transcript_json.translation: 无论旅行的原因是什么，旅行者共同的抱怨是他们住到的千篇一律、缺乏人情味的住宿。

transcript_json.text: After spending five consecutive nights in five similar hotels, the business traveler may find it difficult to remember what happened from day to day, or even what towns were visited, and the tourist may get the mistaken impression that all cities are pretty much the same, at least as far as decoration, food and service are concerned.
transcript_json.translation: 连续五晚住五家雷同的酒店之后，商务旅行者可能很难记清每天发生了什么，甚至连去过哪些城镇都想不起来；游客则可能产生错觉，以为所有城市都大同小异，至少在装修、餐饮和服务上是如此。

transcript_json.text: To combat this sense of impersonal sameness, travelers are taking advantage of in-home hospitality or Bed and Breakfast arrangements.
transcript_json.translation: 为了对抗这种千篇一律的冷漠感，旅行者们开始利用住家式的款待，也就是"住宿加早餐"式安排。

transcript_json.text: B&Bs, I mean, Bed and Breakfast arrangements are private homes which offer lodging and breakfast in a very personalized, friendly setting.
transcript_json.translation: 民宿，我是说"住宿加早餐"式安排，指的是在非常个性化、友好的环境中提供住宿和早餐的私人住宅。

transcript_json.text: For decades, B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe, especially the British Isles.
transcript_json.translation: 几十年来，民宿一直是游览欧洲尤其是英伦诸岛的经典方式。

transcript_json.text: And in fact, they are not really a new idea in America.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，这在美国也并不是什么新鲜事物。

transcript_json.text: The tradition dates back to colonial times when inns were few and far between, and the weary traveler had to depend on the kindness of strangers for a meal and a bed.
transcript_json.translation: 这一传统可追溯到殖民地时期，那时旅店稀少，疲惫的旅人只能靠陌生人的好心解决一餐一宿。

transcript_json.text: But the revival of B&Bs as desirable accommodations is a fairly recent phenomenon.
transcript_json.translation: 但民宿作为理想住宿的复兴，是相当晚近的现象。

transcript_json.text: If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business.
transcript_json.translation: 如果经营民宿的想法让你动了心，在投入这一行之前有几个因素要考虑。

transcript_json.text: The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location.
transcript_json.translation: 第一个考虑是你的房产，不仅是房子本身，还有位置。

transcript_json.text: If you live near a famous historical site or in a popular destination, such as New York City or Washington, D.C., your home can be fairly simple, yet still do well as a B&B.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你住的地方靠近著名历史景点，或在纽约、华盛顿这样的热门目的地，你的房子可以相当朴素，却仍能把民宿经营得红红火火。

transcript_json.text: On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique or has facilities for the traveler, such as a private entrance, private bath or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you.
transcript_json.translation: 另一方面，如果你的房子在建筑上独具特色，或者有为旅客准备的设施，比如独立入口、独立卫浴或游泳池，人们可能愿意远道而来。

transcript_json.text: Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family.
transcript_json.translation: 另一个重要因素是你和家人的生活方式。

transcript_json.text: You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry and the bookkeeping involved.
transcript_json.translation: 你必须考虑：家里每个人是否真心喜欢接待客人，是否愿意一遍遍聊当地的景点和活动，是否有时间和精力应付额外的做饭、清洁、洗衣以及相关的记账事务。

transcript_json.text: The final consideration is a financial one, potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income.
transcript_json.translation: 最后的考虑是财务方面的：想做民宿房东的人，必须对收入机会抱有现实预期。

transcript_json.text: While B&Bs usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B&B.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然民宿的起步成本通常较低，但专家估计，房东要靠民宿谋生，至少得有 5 间房长期租得出去。

transcript_json.text: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
transcript_json.translation: 问题 22 至 25 基于你刚才听到的录音。

transcript_json.text: Q22. What does the speaker say travelers commonly complain about?
transcript_json.translation: Q22. 说话人说旅行者通常抱怨什么？

transcript_json.text: Q23. What is said about Bed and Breakfast arrangements?
transcript_json.translation: Q23. 关于"住宿加早餐"式安排，说了什么？

transcript_json.text: Q24. What is the first thing you have to consider if you want to start a B&B business?
transcript_json.translation: Q24. 如果你想开民宿，首先要考虑的是什么？

transcript_json.text: Q25. What does the speaker say potential B&B hosts must be realistic about?
transcript_json.translation: Q25. 说话人说想做民宿房东的人必须对什么抱现实态度？

transcript_json.text: Section A (Directions)
transcript_json.translation: Section A (Directions)

transcript_json.text: In this section, you will hear two long conversations. At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
transcript_json.translation: 在这一部分，你将听到两段长对话。每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

transcript_json.text: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
transcript_json.translation: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

transcript_json.text: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices, A, B, C and D. Then, mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
transcript_json.translation: 听到问题后，你要从四个选项 A、B、C、D中选出最佳答案，然后用一条直线在答题卡1上划掉对应的字母。

transcript_json.text: CONVERSATION 1
transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 1

transcript_json.text: W: I must say, I love our canteen!
transcript_json.translation: W: 说真的，我太喜欢咱们食堂了！

transcript_json.text: It's such a great meeting point!
transcript_json.translation: 真是个聚会的好地方！

transcript_json.text: M: Yeah, it really is, both for students and teachers. Shame about the food.
transcript_json.translation: M: 是啊，确实如此，对学生和老师都是。就是伙食差点意思。

transcript_json.text: W: What do you mean?
transcript_json.translation: W: 此话怎讲？

transcript_json.text: I think the food is fine.
transcript_json.translation: 我觉得饭菜挺好啊。

transcript_json.text: M: I would say the food is just OK, but the prices are absurd. Don't you agree?
transcript_json.translation: M: 要我说，饭菜还行，但价格贵得离谱。你不觉得吗？

transcript_json.text: W: I don't, actually.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我还真不觉得。

transcript_json.text: I personally think they're perfectly appropriate.
transcript_json.translation: 我个人觉得价格完全合理。

transcript_json.text: If it's overpriced, why does it get so frantically busy at lunchtimes?
transcript_json.translation: 要是真贵了，午餐时间怎么会挤成那样？

transcript_json.text: M: Hmm, you make a good point.
transcript_json.translation: M: 嗯，有道理。

transcript_json.text: I guess a lot of it is good value, maybe even most of it.
transcript_json.translation: 我猜很多东西确实物有所值，甚至大部分都是。

transcript_json.text: However, don't you think 6 bucks for a slice of apple crumble is beyond most students' budgets?
transcript_json.translation: 不过，一片苹果酥卖6块钱，你不觉得超出大多数学生的预算了吗？

transcript_json.text: W: Um, yes, desserts are overpriced. I'll give you that.
transcript_json.translation: W: 嗯，甜点确实贵得离谱，这点我承认。

transcript_json.text: To be honest, I've forgotten about those, as I never eat them.
transcript_json.translation: 说实话，我都忘了甜品这茬，因为我从来不买。

transcript_json.text: I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies.
transcript_json.translation: 我从来不太馋甜食，也不迷恋什么精致美食。

transcript_json.text: What I always go for is their scrambled eggs.
transcript_json.translation: 我每次必点的是他们的炒蛋。

transcript_json.text: They have such a great variety.
transcript_json.translation: 花样特别多。

transcript_json.text: M: Yeah, those are good.
transcript_json.translation: M: 是，那个不错。

transcript_json.text: They also come out really fast.
transcript_json.translation: 而且上菜特别快。

transcript_json.text: Actually, that's one of the best things about the canteen - the speed.
transcript_json.translation: 其实，这是食堂最大的优点之一——快。

transcript_json.text: If I fancy something more substantial than a sandwich, but I don't have much time for lunch, the university canteen is always a good option.
transcript_json.translation: 要是想吃点比三明治更顶饱的，午饭时间又紧，学校食堂永远是个好选择。

transcript_json.text: The kitchen staff work at such a brisk pace.
transcript_json.translation: 后厨员工干活特别麻利。

transcript_json.text: They really deserve to be complimented for it.
transcript_json.translation: 真该好好夸夸他们。

transcript_json.text: W: Totally, and it's such a great environment too.
transcript_json.translation: W: 没错，而且环境也特别好。

transcript_json.text: Like the entire building is beautiful.
transcript_json.translation: 整栋楼都很漂亮。

transcript_json.text: M: It is very nice.
transcript_json.translation: M: 确实很漂亮。

transcript_json.text: W: The massive glass windows make all the difference.
transcript_json.translation: W: 那些巨大的玻璃窗功不可没。

transcript_json.text: I think they're so cool.
transcript_json.translation: 我觉得特别酷。

transcript_json.text: Apparently, they did a massive renovation a few years ago.
transcript_json.translation: 听说几年前他们大装修过一次。

transcript_json.text: It cost them a pretty penny.
transcript_json.translation: 花了不小的一笔钱。

transcript_json.text: M: Yeah, I'm not surprised.
transcript_json.translation: M: 嗯，不意外。

transcript_json.text: It's a very versatile space, suitable both for eating and relaxing.
transcript_json.translation: 这是个非常多功能的空间，吃饭、放松都合适。

transcript_json.text: W: And for working.
transcript_json.translation: W: 还能工作。

transcript_json.text: M: You're right, working too.
transcript_json.translation: M: 对，还能工作。

transcript_json.text: I've used my laptop there once or twice.
transcript_json.translation: 我在那儿用过一两次笔记本电脑。

transcript_json.text: And there's always a group project or meeting going on at the far end.
transcript_json.translation: 而且最里面那头总有小组作业或会议在进行。

transcript_json.text: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
transcript_json.translation: 问题1到4基于你刚听到的对话。

transcript_json.text: Q1. What does the woman say about the food at the canteen?
transcript_json.translation: Q1. 关于食堂的饭菜，女士说了什么？

transcript_json.text: Q2. How does the woman feel about the canteen's sweet things or fancy delicacies?
transcript_json.translation: Q2. 女士对食堂的甜食和精致美食是什么态度？

transcript_json.text: Q3. What does the man say is one of the best things about the canteen?
transcript_json.translation: Q3. 男士说食堂最大的优点之一是什么？

transcript_json.text: Q4. What did the canteen undergo a few years ago?
transcript_json.translation: Q4. 几年前食堂经历了什么？

transcript_json.text: CONVERSATION 2
transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 2

transcript_json.text: W: Hi, Tony, today we're talking about how managers can get along better with young people at work.
transcript_json.translation: W: 你好，托尼。今天我们聊聊管理者如何与职场年轻人更好地相处。

transcript_json.text: We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic. That's not really justified though, is it?
transcript_json.translation: 我们常听说如今的年轻人缺乏职业道德。但这种说法其实站不住脚，不是吗？

transcript_json.text: M: Not really.
transcript_json.translation: M: 确实站不住。

transcript_json.text: In reality, young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation.
transcript_json.translation: 实际上，这个年龄段的年轻人和其他世代一样，形形色色、多面多样。

transcript_json.text: W: Yeah, but if you are struggling to work with young people in your workspace, what can you do?
transcript_json.translation: W: 话虽如此，但要是你在工作中就是和年轻人合不来，该怎么办呢？

transcript_json.text: M: Well, it's essential to connect with them to learn about their values.
transcript_json.translation: M: 嗯，关键是和他们建立联系，了解他们的价值观。

transcript_json.text: It's also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life.
transcript_json.translation: 同样重要的是，要认识到年轻人希望如何平衡工作与个人生活。

transcript_json.text: W: So they generally don't want to defer happiness in return for career advancement?
transcript_json.translation: W: 就是说，他们一般不愿意为了升职而推迟享乐，对吧？

transcript_json.text: M: Absolutely.
transcript_json.translation: M: 完全正确。

transcript_json.text: They are not willing to sacrifice their personal lives for their work lives and this leads people to equate that with an unwillingness to work hard.
transcript_json.translation: 他们不愿为工作牺牲个人生活，于是人们就把这等同于不肯努力工作。

transcript_json.text: W: Right.
transcript_json.translation: W: 对。

transcript_json.text: But that couldn't be further from the truth, could it?
transcript_json.translation: 但这完全不是事实，对吧？

transcript_json.text: M: Young people will work extremely hard during their defined work hours, but they expect to have their time off, like weekends and nights free from work.
transcript_json.translation: M: 年轻人在规定的工作时间里会非常拼命，但他们希望下班时间——比如周末和晚上——不被工作打扰。

transcript_json.text: W: So how should managers go about assessing young people's productivity?
transcript_json.translation: W: 那管理者该怎么评估年轻人的工作产出呢？

transcript_json.text: M: Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work, since someone can work for eight hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company.
transcript_json.translation: M: 一般来说，年轻人认为工作产出不该用工时来衡量，因为有人干满八个小时，对公司有意义的成果却几乎为零。

transcript_json.text: Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform.
transcript_json.translation: 相反，年轻人是用工作质量来衡量自己的产出水平的。

transcript_json.text: W: But we often hear that young people want to feel more than just being a part of a big machine.
transcript_json.translation: W: 但我们常听说，年轻人的希望不只是当大机器上的一颗螺丝钉。

transcript_json.text: Such a perspective can be hard to discredit, can't it?
transcript_json.translation: 这种看法很难驳倒，是不是？

transcript_json.text: M: It's important to legitimize their work.
transcript_json.translation: M: 重要的是让他们的工作得到认可。

transcript_json.text: Young workers want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large.
transcript_json.translation: 年轻员工想做对自己、对公司乃至对整个世界有意义的项目。

transcript_json.text: They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own.
transcript_json.translation: 他们必须感到有必要留在一家价值观与自己一致的公司里工作。

transcript_json.text: W: Thanks for your advice.
transcript_json.translation: W: 谢谢你的建议。

transcript_json.text: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
transcript_json.translation: 问题5到8基于你刚听到的对话。

transcript_json.text: Q5. According to the woman, what view about today's young people is not really justified?
transcript_json.translation: Q5. 按女士的说法，关于如今年轻人的哪种看法站不住脚？

transcript_json.text: Q6. What does the man say is important for managers to get along better with young workers?
transcript_json.translation: Q6. 男士认为管理者要和年轻员工更好相处，什么很重要？

transcript_json.text: Q7. How do young people measure their productivity levels according to the man?

transcript_json.text: Many restaurants are trying to persuade customers to eat more sustainably, moving away from environmentally unfriendly meat towards greener dishes.
transcript_json.translation: 许多餐厅正设法劝顾客吃得更环保，远离对环境不友好的肉类，转向更绿色的菜品。

transcript_json.text: Although it sounds counter-intuitive, restaurants which include specific vegetarian sections on their menus may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat, a new study suggests.
transcript_json.translation: 一项新研究表明，虽然听起来违反直觉，但菜单上单列素食专区的餐厅，可能反而在无意中鼓励顾客吃肉。

transcript_json.text: Behavioral scientist Linda Bacon, one of the study's authors, said, "Restaurants can have a positive impact on the environment by encouraging their customers to choose more plant-based food and less meat.
transcript_json.translation: 行为科学家琳达·培根是这项研究的作者之一，她说，餐厅鼓励顾客多选植物性食品、少吃肉，就能对环境产生积极影响。

transcript_json.text: However, our findings suggest that while certain restaurant menu designs can encourage some consumers to make pro-environmental food choices, they can have the opposite effect on others."
transcript_json.translation: 然而，我们的发现表明，某些菜单设计虽然能促使一些消费者做出环保的食物选择，对另一些人却会起反作用。

transcript_json.text: The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food and half of whom rarely ate it.
transcript_json.translation: 研究涉及750人，其中一半常吃素食，另一半很少吃。

transcript_json.text: No vegetarians were included.
transcript_json.translation: 受试者中不包括素食者。

transcript_json.text: They were given different menus and asked to choose a meal as if they were eating out with friends.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员给他们发了不同的菜单，请他们假装和朋友外出就餐来选一餐。

transcript_json.text: Placing vegetarian dishes in a separate section did not have a significant effect on the choices made by infrequent vegetarian food eaters.
transcript_json.translation: 把素食单列一区，对很少吃素食的人的选择没有明显影响。

transcript_json.text: But it did have a notable effect on the frequent eaters, lowering their chance of picking a vegetarian option by 65%.
transcript_json.translation: 但对常吃素食的人影响显著，他们选素食的可能性降低了65%。

transcript_json.text: The researchers also discovered that presenting a vegetarian dish as the chef's recommendation, or including a more appealing description of a non-meat meal, leads to a greater proportion of infrequent vegetarian eaters choosing a vegetarian option.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员还发现，把一道素菜标为主厨推荐，或者给非肉菜品写上更吸引人的介绍，能让更大比例的不常吃素者选择素食。

transcript_json.text: But again, these altered menu designs backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently, leading them to be less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.
transcript_json.translation: 但同样地，这些改动过的菜单设计在更常吃素的人身上适得其反，他们反而更不愿意选素菜了。
