transcript_json.text: Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors.
transcript_json.translation: 诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院一直在设法阻止致命的室外空气污染进入室内。

transcript_json.text: They found that if pollution is frozen to around -18°C in a condensing tube, the particles gather together and fall to the bottom, allowing fresh, clean air to pass through.
transcript_json.translation: 他们发现，如果把污染物在一根冷凝管里冷冻到零下18摄氏度左右，颗粒就会聚集起来落到管底，新鲜洁净的空气便能通过。

transcript_json.text: Their method was able to remove 99% of pollutants.
transcript_json.translation: 他们的方法能去除99%的污染物。

transcript_json.text: It is hoped that the work could pave the way for simple modification of air conditioning units so that they can also clean polluted indoor air.
transcript_json.translation: 人们希望这项工作能为空调机的简单改造铺路，让空调也能净化受污染的室内空气。

transcript_json.text: Outdoor air pollution in cities is a global problem, whether it be haze plaguing Calcutta or poor air impacting the health of children in London schools.
transcript_json.translation: 城市室外空气污染是个全球性问题，无论是困扰加尔各答的雾霾，还是影响伦敦学校孩子们健康的不良空气。

transcript_json.text: While there are some existing technologies to purify indoor air, they can be inefficient, expensive or produce harmful by-products.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然现有一些净化室内空气的技术，但它们可能效率低、成本高，或产生有害的副产品。

transcript_json.text: When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors.
transcript_json.translation: 室外空气质量差时，人们往往会待在室内更久。

transcript_json.text: But outdoor pollution also leads to indoor pollution, and people still suffer.
transcript_json.translation: 但室外污染也会导致室内污染，人们照样受罪。

transcript_json.text: It is estimated that pollution is linked to over 40,000 early deaths in Britain each year.
transcript_json.translation: 据估计，在英国，污染每年与超过4万例早逝相关。

transcript_json.text: Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences said, "We have shown in our experiments that simply by circulating polluted air through a small freezing chamber, we can remove most of the fine particles and gas pollutants.
transcript_json.translation: 中国科学院的潘纲教授说，我们的实验已经证明，只要让污染空气流经一个小型冷冻腔，就能去除大部分细颗粒物和气态污染物。

transcript_json.text: Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances in areas which might experience extremely poor air conditions.
transcript_json.translation: 我们的研究让在空气状况可能极差的地区给家用电器增加空气净化功能成为可能。

transcript_json.text: By controlling indoor air pollution and improving air quality in this way, this work could be greatly beneficial to public health."
transcript_json.translation: 通过这种方式控制室内空气污染、改善空气质量，这项工作将大大有益于公共健康。

transcript_json.text: Research recently carried out by my team suggests that fish may be self-aware.
transcript_json.translation: 我们团队最近开展的研究表明，鱼可能是有自我意识的。

transcript_json.text: A certain species of fish recently passed the well-known mirror test.
transcript_json.translation: 最近有一个鱼种通过了著名的镜子测试。

transcript_json.text: This is a test that demonstrates self-recognition in animals.
transcript_json.translation: 这是一项检验动物能否自我识别的测试。

transcript_json.text: Only a few animals, such as humans, apes, dolphins and some birds, can recognize themselves in a mirror.
transcript_json.translation: 只有少数动物能在镜子里认出自己，比如人类、类人猿、海豚和一些鸟类。

transcript_json.text: And only these animals, capable of self-recognition, will attempt to remove marks placed on their skin after noticing them in the reflection.
transcript_json.translation: 而且只有具备自我识别能力的这些动物，才会在镜中注意到身上的标记后，试图把它弄掉。

transcript_json.text: This ability suggests a level of higher intelligence and awareness.
transcript_json.translation: 这种能力意味着更高的智力和意识水平。

transcript_json.text: This is not shown by children until around 18 months.
transcript_json.translation: 儿童要到大约18个月大才会表现出这种能力。

transcript_json.text: Until now, no fish has demonstrated the ability.
transcript_json.translation: 在此之前，还没有鱼表现出这种能力。

transcript_json.text: But our experiments show the fish in question will scrape up against hard surfaces to remove marks placed on its body by our researchers after viewing itself in a mirror.
transcript_json.translation: 但我们的实验显示，我们研究的那种鱼在镜中看到自己后，会在硬物上蹭身体，弄掉研究人员标记在它身上的印记。

transcript_json.text: The behaviors we observe leave little doubt that this fish behaviorally fulfills all criteria of the mirror test as originally laid out.
transcript_json.translation: 我们观察到的行为几乎不容置疑：这条鱼在行为上完全符合最初设定的镜子测试的全部标准。

transcript_json.text: The fish in our study never attempted to remove the marks when no mirror was present or when the marks were just placed on the mirror.
transcript_json.translation: 我们研究的鱼在没有镜子时，或者标记只是画在镜子上时，从未试图去除标记。

transcript_json.text: Unmarked fish also did not attempt to remove marks from themselves when interacting with a marked fish on the other side of a window.
transcript_json.translation: 身上没有标记的鱼隔着玻璃与带标记的鱼互动时，也没有试图从自己身上去掉标记。

transcript_json.text: These results show either that fish are self-aware or that the mirror test, which is considered to be the gold standard test used to denote higher intelligence, may be flawed.
transcript_json.translation: 这些结果表明，要么鱼有自我意识，要么这项被视为衡量高等智力金标准的镜子测试本身可能有缺陷。

transcript_json.text: What is less clear is whether these behaviors should be considered as evidence that fish are self-aware, even though in the past these same behaviors have been interpreted as self-awareness in so many other animals.
transcript_json.translation: 不太确定的是，这些行为是否该被当作鱼有自我意识的证据，尽管过去同样这些行为在很多其他动物身上都被解读为自我意识。

transcript_json.text: Depending on your position, you might reject the interpretation that these behaviors in a fish satisfy passing the test at all.
transcript_json.translation: 取决于你的立场，你可能根本不认可“鱼有这些行为就算通过了测试”这种解读。

transcript_json.text: But on what objective basis can you do this when the behaviors they show are so functionally similar to those of other species that have passed the test?
transcript_json.translation: 但当它们表现出的行为与其他通过测试的物种在功能上如此相似时，你又有什么客观依据这样做呢？

transcript_json.text: Results from our research raise more questions than answers.
transcript_json.translation: 我们的研究结果引出的问题比给出的答案还多。

transcript_json.text: What if self-awareness develops like an onion, building layer upon layer rather than appearing all at once?
transcript_json.translation: 如果自我意识像洋葱一样一层层长成，而不是一下子出现呢？

transcript_json.text: Perhaps in order to explore self-awareness further, we should stop looking at responses to the mirror as a decisive test.
transcript_json.translation: 也许要进一步探索自我意识，我们就不该再把对镜子的反应当作决定性测试。

transcript_json.text: Only with a richer theory of the self and a larger test battery will we be able to determine all of the various levels of self-awareness, including where exactly fish fit in.
transcript_json.translation: 只有拥有更丰富的自我理论和更全面的测试组合，我们才能确定自我意识的各个层次，包括鱼究竟处在哪一层。

transcript_json.translation: 问题16到18基于你刚听到的录音。

transcript_json.translation: Q16. 关于著名的镜子测试，我们了解到什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q17. 说话人团队的研究表明，他们实验的那种鱼怎么样？

transcript_json.translation: Q18. 关于研究结果，说话人说了什么？

transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 2

transcript_json.text: Reading with a young child is important.
transcript_json.translation: 和幼儿一起阅读很重要。

transcript_json.text: But does it matter whether you read from an electronic book or traditional print?
transcript_json.translation: 但读电子书还是传统纸质书，有区别吗？

transcript_json.text: As any parent knows, small children are generally keen on screens.
transcript_json.translation: 任何当过家长的都知道，小孩子普遍喜欢屏幕。

transcript_json.text: So the finding from a new study that very young children enjoy electronic books more than printed picture books may not come as a huge surprise - but the following additional findings might: both parents and children behaved differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books.
transcript_json.translation: 因此，一项新研究发现幼儿更喜欢电子书而不是印刷绘本，这也许并不太让人意外——但接下来的补充发现可能就会了：读电子书和读印刷绘本时，家长和孩子的表现都不一样。

transcript_json.text: And the children who read the electronic books learned more.
transcript_json.translation: 而且读电子书的孩子学到的更多。

transcript_json.text: Previous studies of young children have suggested that electronic books, which incorporate extra features such as dictionaries and images that depict story events, may have advantages over print.
transcript_json.translation: 此前针对幼儿的研究表明，带有词典、故事场景配图等额外功能的电子书可能比纸质书更有优势。

transcript_json.text: In fact, multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains beyond what is provided by printed books.
transcript_json.translation: 事实上，多项研究发现，电子书对故事理解和词汇增长的帮助超过了纸质书。

transcript_json.text: But there's also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort in learning from electronic books, and that parents talk less about content when sharing such books.
transcript_json.translation: 但也有研究表明，孩子有时用电子书学习时投入的心智努力更少，家长陪读这类书时也更少谈论内容。

transcript_json.text: The study we're looking at today aims to give us a better understanding of how good electronic books are for young children.
transcript_json.translation: 我们今天来看的这项研究，目的是让我们更好地了解电子书对幼儿到底有多大好处。

transcript_json.text: For this study, researchers videoed children aged 17 to 26 months reading with one of their parents.
transcript_json.translation: 在这项研究中，研究人员拍摄了17到26个月大的孩子与父母一方共读的视频。

transcript_json.text: Each parent-child pair was randomly assigned to read either two educational electronic books or two printed books with the same content.
transcript_json.translation: 每组亲子被随机分配读两本教育类电子书，或两本内容相同的纸质书。

transcript_json.text: While the parent read the words in the printed books aloud, the electronic books had audio of voice actors reading the text.
transcript_json.translation: 纸质书由家长朗读文字，电子书则由配音演员朗读文字。

transcript_json.text: The researchers found that parents who read the printed books pointed more frequently to pages than parents who read the electronic books.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员发现，读纸质书的家长比读电子书的家长更频繁地指着书页。

transcript_json.text: But the opposite was true for the children.
transcript_json.translation: 孩子那边情况正相反。

transcript_json.text: Children who read the electronic books also commented more on the content and learned more new words than the children who read printed books.
transcript_json.translation: 读电子书的孩子比读纸质书的孩子更多评论内容，学到的生词也更多。

transcript_json.text: This greater learning is ascribed to greater engagement with the electronic books.
transcript_json.translation: 学得更多被归因于孩子对电子书的投入更强。

transcript_json.text: It's important to note that the electronic books in the study were simple.
transcript_json.translation: 值得注意的是，研究中的电子书很简单。

transcript_json.text: While they included background music, animation and sound effects, there were no other extra features.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然包含背景音乐、动画和音效，但并没有其他额外功能。

transcript_json.text: It's also important to note that there's research on older children, finding that electronic books don't always bolster learning.
transcript_json.translation: 同样值得注意的是，有针对大龄儿童的研究发现，电子书并不总是能促进学习。

transcript_json.text: Parents and educators need to beware.
transcript_json.translation: 家长和教育工作者需要当心。

transcript_json.text: Extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them; however, if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature.
transcript_json.translation: 电子书的额外功能也许能提高孩子的参与度，但如果这些功能不能把注意力引向教育内容，它们可能起不到辅助作用。

transcript_json.text: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
transcript_json.translation: 问题19到21基于你刚听到的录音。

transcript_json.text: Q19. What finding from the new study might come as a huge surprise?
transcript_json.translation: Q19. 新研究中哪个发现可能让人大吃一惊？

transcript_json.text: Q20. What do we learn about previous studies of young children reading electronic books?
transcript_json.translation: Q20. 关于此前幼儿读电子书的研究，我们了解到什么？

transcript_json.text: Q21. What extra features should be included in electronic books to bolster children's learning?
transcript_json.translation: Q21. 电子书应该加入什么样的额外功能来促进孩子的学习？

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 3
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: Let me be honest with you.
transcript_json.translation: 跟你说句实话吧。

transcript_json.text: If you're living your life full of regrets, you're wasting your time.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你活在一肚子悔恨里，就是在浪费自己的时间。

transcript_json.text: Why would you go through life regretting the very decisions that made you who you are today?
transcript_json.translation: 正是那些决定造就了今天的你，为什么还要一辈子为它们懊悔呢？

transcript_json.text: There are plenty of unfavorable decisions we've made, but does that mean we should regret them? No!
transcript_json.translation: 我们做过很多不利的决定，但这就意味着我们应该为它们后悔吗？不！

transcript_json.text: I've had many moments where I sit and think about all the things I wish I could have done differently.
transcript_json.translation: 我也有很多坐下来回想“要是我当初能换个做法就好了”的时刻。

transcript_json.text: However, just because things could be different, it doesn't necessarily mean they would be better.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，事情本可以有别的走向，并不意味着结果就会更好。

transcript_json.text: You don't have to continually be thinking of all your past decisions and whether or not you made the right one.
transcript_json.translation: 你不必一直惦记过去所有决定，纠结自己当初选得对不对。

transcript_json.text: You can't go back and change anything, so what's the point in worrying about it?
transcript_json.translation: 你又回不去改变什么，担心又有什么用呢？

transcript_json.text: Every single decision you've ever made, positive or negative, has made you the person you are today.
transcript_json.translation: 你做过的每一个决定，无论好坏，都造就了今天的你。

transcript_json.text: We want to go back and change parts of our past, but what would be the benefit of that?
transcript_json.translation: 我们想回到过去改变一些事，但那样做有什么好处呢？

transcript_json.text: We would have lost the valuable knowledge from the lessons we learned.
transcript_json.translation: 我们将失去从教训中学到的宝贵认知。

transcript_json.text: There are reasons you make the choices you do, and that tells us about who you are.
transcript_json.translation: 你之所以那样选择自有原因，而这也说明了你是谁。

transcript_json.text: So when it comes to any decision in life, be unapologetically yourself.
transcript_json.translation: 所以，面对生活中的任何决定，理直气壮地做自己就好。

transcript_json.text: Because at the end of the day, it was you who made that decision.
transcript_json.translation: 因为说到底，做那个决定的人是你。

transcript_json.text: With less time spent focused on regrets, you'll finally have time to focus on the more essential things in life.
transcript_json.translation: 少花时间纠结悔恨，你终于能腾出精力去关注生活中更重要的事。

transcript_json.text: In any situation, you grow more as a person with every decision you make.
transcript_json.translation: 无论什么境况，你做的每个决定都会让你成长一分。

transcript_json.text: Life is full of lessons to learn, so we can't let regret stop us from moving forward.
transcript_json.translation: 人生处处是功课，我们不能让悔恨挡住前进的脚步。

transcript_json.text: We don't know if we've made the right or wrong choice until after it's already been made, so it can be easy to start regretting your decision.
transcript_json.translation: 选择做出来之前，我们无从知道对错，所以人很容易开始后悔自己的决定。

transcript_json.text: But if the decision has already been made, what's the purpose of dwelling on it? There isn't one.
transcript_json.translation: 可如果决定已经做出，再纠缠于它还有什么意义？毫无意义。

transcript_json.text: All you can do is move forward.
transcript_json.translation: 你能做的只有向前走。

transcript_json.text: You can't let yourself sit there and worry about every past choice. We aren't all perfect.
transcript_json.translation: 你不能让自己坐在那里为过去的每个选择发愁。人无完人。

transcript_json.text: Whenever you make a decision, there will always be a possibility for regret later, but that's how life is supposed to be.
transcript_json.translation: 每当做出决定，日后总有可能后悔，但生活本就如此。

transcript_json.text: You will make poor decisions in life - we all do - but it's what you do with the lessons learned that matters.
transcript_json.translation: 人生中你总会做出糟糕的决定——谁都一样——重要的是你如何对待从中吸取的教训。

transcript_json.text: Think about every decision you've ever made.
transcript_json.translation: 想想你做过的每一个决定。

transcript_json.text: Were they always the best? Of course not.
transcript_json.translation: 它们永远都是最优选择吗？当然不是。

transcript_json.text: But look at how far you've come since then.
transcript_json.translation: 但看看从那时起你已经走了多远。

transcript_json.text: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
transcript_json.translation: 问题22到25基于你刚听到的录音。

transcript_json.text: Q22. What should we do with the unfavorable decisions we've made?
transcript_json.translation: Q22. 对于做过的那些不理想的决定，我们该怎么办？

transcript_json.text: Q23. What does the speaker say about every single decision we've ever made?
transcript_json.translation: Q23. 关于我们做过的每一个决定，说话人说了什么？

transcript_json.text: Q24. What is life full of according to the speaker?
transcript_json.translation: Q24. 按说话人的说法，人生充满了什么？

transcript_json.text: Q25. What is said to be of real importance when we make poor decisions in life?
transcript_json.translation: Q25. 人生中做出糟糕决定时，真正重要的是什么？

transcript_json.text: CONVERSATION 1
transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 1

transcript_json.text: M: Welcome to "Business Matters".
transcript_json.translation: M: 欢迎收看《商业要事》。

transcript_json.text: Today we have invited career development consultant Lucy Williams to talk about how to get ahead at work.
transcript_json.translation: 今天我们邀请了职业发展顾问露西·威廉姆斯，来聊聊如何在职场获得晋升。

transcript_json.text: Hi, Lucy.
transcript_json.translation: 你好，露西。

transcript_json.text: Many of us never seem to get promoted.
transcript_json.translation: 我们很多人似乎一直得不到晋升。

transcript_json.text: Why is that?
transcript_json.translation: 这是为什么呢？

transcript_json.text: And what can we do about it?
transcript_json.translation: 我们又该怎么办呢？

transcript_json.text: W: One mistake people make is to limit communication only to their bosses.
transcript_json.translation: W: 人们常犯的一个错误是只跟自己的上司交流。

transcript_json.text: It's important to expand your network and include your co-workers.
transcript_json.translation: 拓展你的人际网络、把同事也包括进来很重要。

transcript_json.text: M: But some of our co-workers are less senior to us.
transcript_json.translation: M: 可有些同事的职级比我们低。

transcript_json.text: Is it really necessary to connect with them?
transcript_json.translation: 真的有必要跟他们建立联系吗？

transcript_json.text: W: It's important not to underestimate your colleagues.
transcript_json.translation: W: 重要的是不要低估你的同事。

transcript_json.text: Sometimes a job title might not clearly demonstrate the influence they may have.
transcript_json.translation: 有时候，一个职位头衔并不能清楚体现他们可能拥有的影响力。

transcript_json.text: M: Now many of us think that working hard creates a good impression, but this isn't always true, is it?
transcript_json.translation: M: 我们很多人都以为努力工作会留下好印象，但这并不总是对的，对吧？

transcript_json.text: W: That's right.
transcript_json.translation: W: 没错。

transcript_json.text: We should avoid trying to take on too much work and constantly staying late, just to show that you are committed.
transcript_json.translation: 我们应该避免为了表现自己敬业，就包揽太多工作、还总是加班到很晚。

transcript_json.text: M: I see.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我明白了。

transcript_json.text: So setting expectations too high at the beginning can make us look bad if we don't maintain them.
transcript_json.translation: 所以如果一开始把期望定得太高，之后又保持不住，就会让我们显得很差。

transcript_json.text: W: Yeah, it's better to make sure you are putting in quality time instead of just a large quantity of time.
transcript_json.translation: W: 是啊，最好确保你投入的是高质量的时间，而不只是大量的时间。

transcript_json.text: And these efforts can easily be demonstrated by the results we achieve.
transcript_json.translation: 而且这些努力很容易通过我们取得的成绩体现出来。

transcript_json.text: M: What about helping others at work?
transcript_json.translation: M: 那在工作中帮助别人呢？

transcript_json.text: Should you try and go beyond your normal responsibilities and offer to help people with their projects?
transcript_json.translation: 应该主动超出自己平时的职责范围，帮忙做别人的项目吗？

transcript_json.text: W: Extend your assistance to those who need it, but only as long as your own work will not go unattended.
transcript_json.translation: W: 可以向需要帮助的人伸出援手，但前提是你自己的工作不会因此被耽误。

transcript_json.text: If someone can benefit from your assistance or advice, help them out to gain their respect and trust.
transcript_json.translation: 如果有人能从你的帮助或建议中受益，就帮他们一把，以此赢得他们的尊重和信任。

transcript_json.text: M: But it goes without saying that you shouldn't act like a know-it-all, otherwise you'll appear arrogant.
transcript_json.translation: M: 但不言而喻，你不能表现得无所不知，否则会显得傲慢。

transcript_json.text: W: Absolutely.
transcript_json.translation: W: 完全正确。

transcript_json.text: Be humble, and you'll get a lot of time later on to show your genius.
transcript_json.translation: 保持谦逊，以后有的是时间让你展现才华。

transcript_json.text: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
transcript_json.translation: 问题1至4基于你刚刚听到的对话。

transcript_json.text: Q1. What are the speakers mainly talking about?
transcript_json.translation: Q1. 对话双方主要在谈论什么？

transcript_json.text: Q2. What does the woman say is one mistake people make?
transcript_json.translation: Q2. 女士说人们犯的一个错误是什么？

transcript_json.text: Q3. What does the woman advise people to do in their work?
transcript_json.translation: Q3. 女士建议人们在工作时要怎么做？

transcript_json.text: Q4. Why does the man say one should not act like a know-it-all?
transcript_json.translation: Q4. 男士为什么说人不能表现得无所不知？

transcript_json.text: CONVERSATION 2
transcript_json.translation: CONVERSATION 2

transcript_json.text: W: I think we first need to decide how to divide up the presentation responsibilities.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我想我们首先得决定怎么分配展示任务。

transcript_json.text: From what I recall, the presentation consists of five parts, not including the introduction and conclusion.
transcript_json.translation: 据我回忆，这个展示一共有五个部分，还不包括引言和结论。

transcript_json.text: That would mean altogether, we need to allocate seven parts between the two of us.
transcript_json.translation: 也就是说，我们俩总共要分七部分。

transcript_json.text: M: So, we have the abstract, background research, the project design, the results and the discussion portions.
transcript_json.translation: M: 那就是摘要、背景研究、项目设计、结果和讨论这几个部分。

transcript_json.text: As the abstract section only applies to the article, we needn't include it in the presentation.
transcript_json.translation: 由于摘要只用于文章，我们不必把它放进展示里。

transcript_json.text: How would you suggest we dole out the rest?
transcript_json.translation: 剩下的部分你建议怎么分？

transcript_json.text: W: How do you feel about handling the background bit?
transcript_json.translation: W: 你来负责背景那部分怎么样？

transcript_json.text: In this way, we can both discuss the part of the project that we devoted most of our time to.
transcript_json.translation: 这样我们俩都能讲讲自己投入时间最多的那部分项目。

transcript_json.text: M: Hold on a minute.
transcript_json.translation: M: 等等。

transcript_json.text: You want me, the one who did the bulk of the task, to also do the majority of the presentation?
transcript_json.translation: 你是想让我这个干了大部分活的人，也来做展示的大部分内容？

transcript_json.text: The background research which was so meticulous took more than a month.
transcript_json.translation: 那项极其细致的背景研究花了一个多月。

transcript_json.text: W: OK.
transcript_json.translation: W: 好了好了。

transcript_json.text: OK.
transcript_json.translation: 好了。

transcript_json.text: I get it.
transcript_json.translation: 我懂了。

transcript_json.text: Quit your moaning.
transcript_json.translation: 别抱怨了。

transcript_json.text: I appreciate the rigorous work ethic you applied to the research, but not the sarcasm that comes up every time I mention it.
transcript_json.translation: 我欣赏你做研究时严谨的工作态度，但我可受不了我每次一提这事你就阴阳怪气。

transcript_json.text: What do you think would be a fair arrangement?
transcript_json.translation: 你觉得怎样安排才公平？

transcript_json.text: M: I think the best arrangement would be to split the research into two parts: before-1980 and afterward.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我觉得最好的安排是把研究分成两部分：1980年以前和1980年以后。

transcript_json.text: I would take the before-portion and you would be assigned the after-1980, leaving the project and results.
transcript_json.translation: 我负责前面那部分，你负责1980年以后的，剩下项目设计和结果。

transcript_json.text: I volunteer to describe the project.
transcript_json.translation: 我自告奋勇来讲项目设计。

transcript_json.text: But as I struggled a bit with the statistics in the results section, how about you handling that?
transcript_json.translation: 不过结果部分里的统计我有点吃力，要不你来负责那部分？

transcript_json.text: W: That's agreeable to me.
transcript_json.translation: W: 我没问题。

transcript_json.text: I propose we both handle the discussion section in parts along with the question and answer afterward, leaving only the introduction and conclusion.
transcript_json.translation: 我提议讨论部分我们俩分段一起讲，之后的问答环节也一样，这样就只剩引言和结论了。

transcript_json.text: M: I will take responsibility for the conclusion and put you in charge of the introduction.
transcript_json.translation: M: 我来负责结论，引言就交给你了。

transcript_json.text: This will make it so that we alternate presenting, so as to avoid sounding monotonous to the audience.
transcript_json.translation: 这样我们就能轮流上台讲，免得听众听着单调。

transcript_json.text: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
transcript_json.translation: 问题5至8基于你刚刚听到的对话。

transcript_json.text: Q5. What does the woman say they first need to do?
transcript_json.translation: Q5. 女士说她们首先需要做什么？

transcript_json.text: Q6. Why does the man refuse to handle the background part?
transcript_json.translation: Q6. 男士为什么拒绝负责背景部分？

transcript_json.text: Q7. What does the woman urge the man to stop doing?
transcript_json.translation: Q7. 女士敦促男士别再做什么？

transcript_json.text: Q8. Why does the man suggest he present the conclusion and the woman do the introduction?
transcript_json.translation: Q8. 男士为什么建议自己讲结论、女士讲引言？

transcript_json.translation: Section B，题目说明。

of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.

transcript_json.text: PASSAGE 1
transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 1

transcript_json.text: Makeup can do more than just change your appearance-it can also alter others' perceptions of you, for better or for worse.
transcript_json.translation: 化妆能做的远不止改变你的外表——它还能改变别人对你的看法，或好或坏。

transcript_json.text: According to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland, although both men and women perceive women who wear makeup as being of a higher status, men associate makeup with prestigious, positive qualities, while women view other women wearing makeup as being dominant and a potential threat.
transcript_json.translation: 苏格兰斯特灵大学的新研究发现，虽然男性和女性都认为化妆的女性地位更高，但男性会把化妆与声望高、正面的特质联系起来，而女性则把其他化妆的女性看成强势、有潜在威胁的人。

transcript_json.text: The research showed that men and women both rated the faces with cosmetics as being more attractive, but only women rated made-up faces as being more dominant, while only men rated made-up faces as being higher in prestige.
transcript_json.translation: 研究显示，男性和女性都认为化了妆的脸更有吸引力，但只有女性认为化妆脸更显强势，也只有男性认为化妆脸声望更高。

transcript_json.text: A follow-up study investigated the root cause behind these differences in perception, and found that female-on-female jealousy seemed to be the main cause of the differences in perception.
transcript_json.translation: 一项后续研究探究了这些认知差异背后的根源，发现女性之间的嫉妒似乎是造成这种认知差异的主要原因。

transcript_json.text: Women rating women with makeup said they would be more jealous of them and thought they would be more attractive to men than their non-makeup wearing counterparts.
transcript_json.translation: 给化妆女性打分的女性表示，她们会更嫉妒这些人，并认为她们比不化妆的女性对男人更有吸引力。

transcript_json.text: Cosmetic products are good for more than just giving you a pretty face.
transcript_json.translation: 化妆品的好处可不只是给你一张漂亮的脸。

transcript_json.text: It can be particularly useful for women to understand how wearing makeup alters others' perceptions of them in situations where they are trying to gain others' trust and admiration.
transcript_json.translation: 在女性想赢得他人信任和赞赏的场合，了解化妆会如何改变别人对她们的看法尤其有用。

transcript_json.text: At a job interview, knowing whether the hiring committee will consist of men or women might influence a female candidate's decision about wearing makeup.
transcript_json.translation: 在求职面试时，知道招聘委员会由男性还是女性组成，可能会影响女性应聘者是否化妆的决定。

transcript_json.text: Whether the interviewers will view her as attractive, dominant and prestigious can affect the interviewers' actions and perhaps the outcome of the interview itself.
transcript_json.translation: 面试官是否会把她看成有魅力、强势、有声望的人，会影响面试官的行为，甚至可能影响面试本身的结果。

transcript_json.text: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
transcript_json.translation: 问题9至11基于你刚刚听到的短文。

transcript_json.text: Q9. What can makeup do according to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland?
transcript_json.translation: Q9. 根据苏格兰斯特灵大学的新研究，化妆能起到什么作用？

transcript_json.text: Q10. How did both men and women rate the faces with cosmetics in the new research?
transcript_json.translation: Q10. 在这项新研究中，男性和女性对化妆面孔的评价有何共同点？

transcript_json.text: Q11. Why does a female candidate need to know the gender of the hiring committee members?
transcript_json.translation: Q11. 女性应聘者为什么需要知道招聘委员会成员的性别？

transcript_json.text: PASSAGE 2
transcript_json.translation: PASSAGE 2

transcript_json.text: You may have seen advertisements trumpeting methods of changing a habit that require absolutely no willpower whatsoever.
transcript_json.translation: 你可能见过一些广告，大肆宣扬那些完全不需要意志力的改变习惯的方法。

transcript_json.text: But can you really change a bad habit or create a good one without willpower?
transcript_json.translation: 但你真的能在没有意志力的情况下改掉坏习惯或养成好习惯吗？

transcript_json.text: To answer this question, we first have to ask: "What is willpower?" Most people, sadly, think of it only as the ability to clench their teeth and resist attractive temptations.
transcript_json.translation: 要回答这个问题，我们得先问："什么是意志力？"遗憾的是，大多数人只把它理解为咬紧牙关抵抗诱人诱惑的能力。

transcript_json.text: In this view, willpower means self-denial and no fun.
transcript_json.translation: 照这种看法，意志力就意味着自我克制、毫无乐趣。

transcript_json.text: No wonder people hope to make changes without it.
transcript_json.translation: 难怪人们希望不用它也能做出改变。

transcript_json.text: I define willpower as "using only the thought of your motivators to control your actions." Let's say your motivators are "prevent diabetes" and "reach a healthy weight".
transcript_json.translation: 我把意志力定义为"只靠想着自己的动力来控制行为"。比如说，你的动力是"预防糖尿病"和"达到健康体重"。

transcript_json.text: So if you are at the all-you-can-eat buffet, you think about your motivator-avoid diabetes through weight loss-and you take small portions and avoid the dessert table.
transcript_json.translation: 这样，如果你在随便吃的自助餐厅，就会想着你的动力——通过减重预防糖尿病——于是你会少拿一点，并且不去碰甜点台。

transcript_json.text: So, amazingly enough, willpower begins with a thought-a bright idea-some way to improve your life or contribute to others.
transcript_json.translation: 说来神奇，意志力始于一个念头——一个好点子——一种改善你的生活或造福他人的方法。

transcript_json.text: This bright idea is your motivator.
transcript_json.translation: 这个好点子就是你的动力。

transcript_json.text: Doctor Walter Mischel, an expert on willpower skills, uses the expressive term "a burning goal".
transcript_json.translation: 意志力技能专家沃尔特·米歇尔博士用了一个很形象的说法："炽热的目标"。

transcript_json.text: Whether you call it a motivator, a burning goal, or a bright idea, this idea is the force behind your willpower.
transcript_json.translation: 不管你叫它动力、炽热的目标还是好点子，这个念头都是你意志力背后的力量。

transcript_json.text: What sort of bright ideas-motivators-make for effective willpower?
transcript_json.translation: 什么样的好点子——也就是动力——能造就有效的意志力呢？

transcript_json.text: In fact, any goal that you value strongly counts.
transcript_json.translation: 实际上，任何你非常看重的目标都算数。

transcript_json.text: The list may include good health, self-respect, a better future for your family, a personal mission and being a role model for your child.
transcript_json.translation: 这个清单可以包括：健康的身体、自尊、家人更好的未来、个人使命，以及成为孩子的榜样。

transcript_json.text: All these can certainly drive a positive change.
transcript_json.translation: 这些当然都能促成积极的改变。

transcript_json.text: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage
transcript_json.translation: 问题12至15基于你刚刚听到的短文

transcript_json.text: Q12. What methods do some advertisements trumpet about changing a habit?
transcript_json.translation: Q12. 一些广告宣扬什么样的改变习惯的方法？

transcript_json.text: Q13. What does the speaker define willpower as?
transcript_json.translation: Q13. 说话人把意志力定义为什么？

transcript_json.text: Q14. What may sound amazing enough as regards willpower?
transcript_json.translation: Q14. 关于意志力，什么事听起来够神奇的？

transcript_json.text: Q15. What does the speaker say may make for effective willpower?
transcript_json.translation: Q15. 说话人说什么可能造就有效的意志力？

transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 1

transcript_json.text: For many pregnant women, understanding what seafood is safe and healthy and what should be avoided because of mercury concerns comes with a lot of worrying.
transcript_json.translation: 对很多孕妇来说，弄清哪些海鲜安全健康、哪些因为汞的问题应当避开，是一件让人操碎了心的事。

transcript_json.text: In part, that's because the federal government's advice on the matter, first issued in 2004, has long been criticized as vague.
transcript_json.translation: 这部分是因为联邦政府2004年首次发布的有关建议，长期以来一直被批评过于模糊。

transcript_json.text: That guidance has included advice on how much seafood to eat, and which species pregnant and breastfeeding women should avoid over concerns about mercury contamination.
transcript_json.translation: 该指导意见包括应吃多少海鲜，以及出于对汞污染的担忧，孕妇和哺乳期女性应避开哪些鱼种。

transcript_json.text: But critics say the government advisory has done more harm than good, scaring many pregnant and breastfeeding women away from eating seafood altogether.
transcript_json.translation: 但批评人士说，政府的建议弊大于利，吓得许多孕妇和哺乳期女性干脆不吃海鲜了。

transcript_json.text: The problem is real.
transcript_json.translation: 这个问题是真实存在的。

transcript_json.text: According to a spokesman for the Food and Drug Administration, or FDA for short, the agency analyzed fish consumption data from more than 1,000 pregnant women in the US and found that 21 per cent of them ate no fish whatsoever in the previous month.
transcript_json.translation: 据美国食品药品监督管理局（简称 FDA）的一位发言人称，该机构分析了美国1000多名孕妇的鱼类消费数据，发现其中21%的人在此前一个月完全没吃鱼。

transcript_json.text: And those who did eat fish consumed far less than recommended by the dietary guidelines.
transcript_json.translation: 而那些吃鱼的人，食用量也远低于膳食指南的建议。

transcript_json.text: Some 50 per cent ate less than two ounces a week and 75 per cent ate less than four ounces.
transcript_json.translation: 约50%的人每周吃鱼不到两盎司，75%的人不到四盎司。

transcript_json.text: This week the FDA issued an update to the advice, listing more than sixty species in a chart that ranks fish as A Best Choice, Good Choice and Choices to Avoid.
transcript_json.translation: 本周，FDA发布了这份建议的更新版，用一张图表列出了60多个鱼种，把它们分为最佳选择、不错的选择和应避开的种类。

transcript_json.text: The goal is to make it easier for mothers-to-be to feel confident about the type of seafood they include in their diets.
transcript_json.translation: 目的是让准妈妈们更容易对饮食中海鲜的种类感到放心。

transcript_json.text: The new advice recommends consumers choose a variety of fish to eat, and it comes with an easy-to-understand illustration of what an appropriate portion size should be-four ounces for an adult and two ounces for children aged four to seven.
transcript_json.translation: 新建议提倡消费者吃多种多样的鱼，还配有一份通俗易懂的图示，说明合适的食用量是多少——成人四盎司，4至7岁儿童两盎司。

transcript_json.text: And while expectant mothers have long been warned to stay away from shark and four other particular types of fish from the Gulf of Mexico, now there are three new species on the list of what to avoid.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然准妈妈们长期以来一直被告诫要远离鲨鱼和墨西哥湾另外四种特定的鱼类，但现在应避开的名单上又新增了三个鱼种。

transcript_json.text: But not everyone is thrilled with the new advice.
transcript_json.translation: 但并非人人都为新建议感到高兴。

transcript_json.text: Critics say the new advice doesn't always agree with the agency's own scientific findings.
transcript_json.translation: 批评人士说，新建议并不总是与该机构自己的科学结论一致。

transcript_json.text: While mercury is of great concern when people are talking about pregnant women and seafood, it's not the only factor contributing to anxiety.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然谈到孕妇和海鲜时汞是最大的顾虑，但它并不是引发焦虑的唯一因素。

transcript_json.text: The FDA maintains that its final consumption recommendations were based on thorough scientific analysis.
transcript_json.translation: FDA坚持认为，其最终的食用建议是基于全面的科学分析做出的。

transcript_json.text: Agency spokesman Cassell says the FDA believes their recommendations will increase confidence, not uncertainty.
transcript_json.translation: 该机构发言人卡塞尔说，FDA相信他们的建议会增强人们的信心，而不是增加不确定性。

transcript_json.text: But critics disagree.
transcript_json.translation: 但批评人士不这么认为。

transcript_json.text: They think the FDA's advice is not based on the evidence in its own detailed report, and so it confuses everyone.
transcript_json.translation: 他们认为 FDA 的建议没有以其详细报告中的证据为依据，结果把大家都搞糊涂了。

transcript_json.translation: Q16. 关于联邦政府的海鲜安全建议，说话人说了什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q17. 美国食品药品监督管理局本周做了什么？

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 2
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 2

transcript_json.text: I know you're busy with work, but you also need to take some time off to recharge those batteries.
transcript_json.translation: 我知道你工作忙，但你也得抽空休个假，给自己充充电。

transcript_json.text: So, should you plan one big vacation for the year, or should you take multiple short vacations throughout?
transcript_json.translation: 那么，你是应该一年安排一次长假，还是全年分散地休几个短假？

transcript_json.text: Quantity can sometimes beat quality.
transcript_json.translation: 数量有时也能胜过质量。

transcript_json.text: First and foremost, regardless of how you use your vacation days, you need to be using them, and soon.
transcript_json.translation: 首先也是最重要的，不管你怎么用这些假期，你都得把它们用掉，而且要尽快。

transcript_json.text: The longer you put off your time off, the worse you're making things for yourself.
transcript_json.translation: 你把休假拖得越久，对自己的伤害就越大。

transcript_json.text: One 9-year-long study published in Psychosomatic Medicine suggests not taking at least one vacation a year may increase your risk of mortality due to heart disease.
transcript_json.translation: 发表在《心身医学》上的一项长达9年的研究表明，一年连一次假都不休，可能会增加你死于心脏病的风险。

transcript_json.text: So, not only are you killing your joy, you're possibly killing yourself.
transcript_json.translation: 所以，你不光是在扼杀快乐，还可能是在慢性自杀。

transcript_json.text: Give yourself a break, folks.
transcript_json.translation: 各位，让自己歇歇吧。

transcript_json.text: When you should take those breaks, however, depends on a few factors: how many days you have available to use, what activities bring you joy, whether you have a family or not, and other variables come into play.
transcript_json.translation: 不过，什么时候休这些假取决于几个因素：你有多少天可用的假期、什么活动能给你带来快乐、你有没有家庭，还有其他各种变量。

transcript_json.text: Because of that, there's no perfect formula that works for everyone, but there are still a few things everyone can try to shoot for.
transcript_json.translation: 正因如此，没有一个对所有人都适用的完美公式，但仍有一些目标是每个人都可以努力争取的。

transcript_json.text: We know that in terms of maximizing relaxation, you should aim for vacations that range somewhere between 7 and 11 days long.
transcript_json.translation: 我们知道，要想让放松效果最大化，假期长度应该定在7到11天之间。

transcript_json.text: That gives you enough time to let go of your stress at work, completely loosen up, and achieve full-on calm.
transcript_json.translation: 这样你就有足够的时间放下工作压力，彻底放松下来，达到完全的平静。

transcript_json.text: That above-mentioned study also recommends you space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once.
transcript_json.translation: 上面提到的那项研究还建议你把假期均匀地分散开，而不是一次性把假期全用完。

transcript_json.text: Eight days might sound like a lot for someone who only gets 10 days of vacation a year.
transcript_json.translation: 对一个一年只有10天假期的人来说，8天听起来好像很多。

transcript_json.text: But if you frame them with weekends, you can manage two evenly spaced 8-day vacations a year.
transcript_json.translation: 但如果把假期和周末拼起来，你一年可以安排两个间隔均匀的8天假期。

transcript_json.text: If you have 14 days of paid leave, that's almost three separate 8-day vacations you can use to split your year into thirds.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你有14天带薪年假，那差不多能休三个独立的8天假期，把一年分成三份。

transcript_json.text: As tempting as it might be to use all your days to take one long summer break, your overall goal should be to achieve the perfect balance between length plus joy and frequency.
transcript_json.translation: 尽管把所有假期拿来休一个夏日长假很诱人，但你的总体目标应该是在长度加快乐与频率之间取得完美平衡。

transcript_json.text: Vacation frequency is important because planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to.
transcript_json.translation: 休假频率很重要，因为全年安排多个假期意味着你总有所期待。

transcript_json.text: Planning things and the anticipation that comes with it tend to make us happier.
transcript_json.translation: 做计划以及随之而来的期待往往会让我们更快乐。

transcript_json.text: If you only take one long vacation every year, the excitement builds much more slowly and seems so far off that it can actually lead to feelings of despair.
transcript_json.translation: 如果你一年只休一次长假，兴奋感积累得慢得多，而且显得遥遥无期，甚至可能导致绝望的情绪。

transcript_json.translation: 问题19至21基于你刚刚听到的录音。

transcript_json.translation: Q19. 关于完全不休假的人，说话人说了什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q20. 这项长达9年的研究建议人们在规划假期时怎么做？

transcript_json.text: Q21. Why is vacation frequency important according to the speaker?
transcript_json.translation: Q21. 根据说话人的说法，为什么休假频率很重要？

transcript_json.text: RECORDING 3
transcript_json.translation: RECORDING 3

transcript_json.text: Autonomous cars that can take over from drivers if they are tired or caught in the heat of an argument are being developed in Sweden.
transcript_json.translation: 瑞典正在研发一种自动驾驶汽车，当司机疲劳或陷入激烈争吵时，它可以接替司机驾驶。

transcript_json.text: Researchers working as part of the European Union's €77 billion research program are developing sensor-based systems that monitor whether a driver is distracted, anxious or tired.
transcript_json.translation: 作为欧盟770亿欧元研究计划一部分的研究人员，正在开发基于传感器的系统，监测司机是否分心、焦虑或疲劳。

transcript_json.text: If a driver is not in a fit state to be on the road, the car automatically takes control of the wheel to prevent accidents.
transcript_json.translation: 如果司机的状态不适合开车，汽车就会自动接管方向盘，以防发生事故。

transcript_json.text: Doctor Anna Anund from the Swedish National Road and Transport Research Institute, who is leading the project, said a driver's state can be measured using a number of sensors, including heart rate monitors and eye sensors, which track where a driver's gaze is.
transcript_json.translation: 领导该项目的瑞典国家道路与运输研究所的安娜·阿努德博士说，司机的状态可以通过多种传感器来测量，包括心率监测器和追踪司机视线方向的眼睛传感器。

transcript_json.text: She said the aim was to really make sure that the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way, so we can take into consideration the driver's state, and so we do not give control to a driver who is under pressure of fatigue, stress, anxiety, and so on.
transcript_json.translation: 她说，目的是真正确保从司机到车辆的切换以安全的方式进行，这样我们就能把司机的状态考虑进去，不会把控制权交给一个正承受疲劳、压力、焦虑等的司机。

transcript_json.text: According to data from the European Commission, Sweden has the safest roads in the EU, with the UK a close second.
transcript_json.translation: 根据欧盟委员会的数据，瑞典的道路安全程度在欧盟位居第一，英国紧随其后。

transcript_json.text: However, the number of road accidents in both has largely levelled out since 2010.
transcript_json.translation: 然而，自2010年以来，两国的道路交通事故数量都基本趋于平稳。

transcript_json.text: Driver fatigue is thought to be responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes across the EU, although there are certain times of the day when more accidents happen.
transcript_json.translation: 据认为，司机疲劳是整个欧盟多达五分之一车祸的肇因，尽管一天之中有些时段事故更多。

transcript_json.text: At 6:00 a.m., for example, drivers are said to be 20 times more likely to have an accident than at 10:00 a.m.
transcript_json.translation: 例如，据说早上6点司机发生事故的可能性是早上10点的20倍。

transcript_json.text: While most experts agree driverless technology should help bring down accident numbers in the long term, some have questioned whether it is safe.
transcript_json.translation: 虽然大多数专家都认为无人驾驶技术长期来看应该有助于降低事故数量，但也有人质疑它是否安全。

transcript_json.text: The researchers have said the technology they are developing is seeking to bridge the gap between Level 3 on the autonomy scale, in which drivers have to be ready to take control of the car at any point, and Level 4, in which driving is automated.
transcript_json.translation: 研究人员表示，他们正在开发的技术试图弥合自动驾驶等级中3级与4级之间的差距：3级要求司机随时准备接管车辆，4级则实现了自动驾驶。

transcript_json.text: Daniel Ruiz, the chief executive of the UK's connected and autonomous vehicle programme Meridian, said: "there is a strong debate going on about how it is possible to make a Level 3 car completely safe." Despite advances in technology, we still have some way to go in shifting public sentiment.
transcript_json.translation: 英国网联自动驾驶汽车项目 Meridian 的首席执行官丹尼尔·鲁伊斯说："关于如何才能让3级汽车完全安全，目前存在激烈的争论。"尽管技术不断进步，但在转变公众情绪方面我们仍有很长的路要走。

transcript_json.text: With an increase in attention-grabbing accidents recently, drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to.
transcript_json.translation: 随着近来骇人听闻的事故增多，司机们现在认为自动驾驶汽车不如以前安全了。

transcript_json.translation: 问题22至25基于你刚刚听到的录音。

transcript_json.translation: Q22. 研究人员在瑞典在做什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q23. 据安娜·阿努德博士说，研究人员的项目旨在做什么？

transcript_json.translation: Q24. 据认为什么造成了整个欧盟五分之一的道路交通事故？
